name: Cologne
description: Miraculously, while most of the city's Old Town was turned to rubble, the Cathedral survived, and today this utterly magnificent masterwork of medieval Gothic architecture still hovers above the roofs of the city. Begun in 1248 and the finishing touches only put to its gigantic twin towers in 1880, after an interval of over two centuries, this UNESCO-protected building is overwhelming in its scale and beauty. A whole host of church treasures dating back to the 4th century is on view in the medieval sacristan crypt, while behind the high altar the Shrine of the Three Kings, the relics of the Biblical Caspar, Melchior, and Balthasar rises up in medieval golden splendour. The Church of Great St. Martin and the Old Town Hall in the Old Town have their riches too. As do many of Cologne's forty-odd museums, such as the City Museum or Museum Ludwig dedicated to modern art.

name: Hacienda Yaxcopoil
description: Hacienda Yaxcopoil was founded in the 17th century, first as a cattle ranch, and later, a henequen plantation. At its height, the grand estate covered 22,000 acres and was considered one of the most important in the Yucatan. Shifting politics and economics caused the estate to fall into decline, and today, it is less than 3% of its original size. Yaxcopoil is one of the few haciendas that has been preserved in its original condition, right down to its elegant 19th century furnishings. Surrounding the main house, you'll find storehouses, a school, hospital, store, workshop, and some housing for some of the workers - everything this semi-isolated estate would need to run. Along with offering insights into the Colonial and Industrial era's, Yaxcopoil has its own Maya museum exhibiting artifacts uncovered at the nearby ruins. For more information, please visit yaxcopoil.com

name: Lendava
description: Lendava (formally Dolnja Lendava) is a countryside town in easternmost Slovenia. The town features the 12th century Lendava Castle situated on a hill above the city center. The castle also has a museum and gallery. In addition, there is a Jewish synagogue, a church, theaters, and a concert hall. For relaxation, the town also has a thermal spa, "Terme Lendava" with unique oil fossil water containing healing properties. Lendava offers something for everyone, whether you're searching for culture or comfort.

name: Antofagasta
description: Antofagasta is a historic port city in northern Chile known for its mining heritage, captivating natural monuments, pristine beaches, and vibrant street life. Explore its historical treasures by journeying into the mysteries of the saltpeter offices, once bustling hubs during the early 20th century, now transformed into captivating "ghost towns." For astronomy enthusiasts, Antofagasta provides access to the pristine night skies of the Atacama Desert, home to some of Chile's finest astronomical observatories. Take time to visit the nearby beaches, featuring soft white sands and gentle waters. One notable attraction is the La Portada Natural Monument, a striking rock formation resembling a white arch, positioned where powerful waves collide with the cliffs. Antofagasta proudly displays its affluence and heritage through its picturesque center, Plaza Colon, and continues to do so along Avenida Arturo Prat. This bustling, pedestrian-only street spans multiple blocks, offering an array of restaurants, shops, and lively street performances.

name: Chawton
description: Jane Austen's House Museum occupies the 17th-century house where Jane Austen spent the last eight years of her life, and produced most of her major works, including Pride and Prejudice. After Austen's sister died in 1845, the house was used as worker housing until 1947 when Jane Austen's House Museum was established. Today, visitors will find a collection of the Austen's personal effects and furnishings, including music books with pieces transcribed by Jane, a Clementi pianoforte, and a Hepplewhite bureau-bookcase containing several of her works. There are also three pieces of jewelry owned by the author, including a turquoise and gold ring that had been sold at auction to American singer Kelly Clarkson. Because of its historic importance, the British government placed an export ban on the ring, and the museum was able to purchase it with the help of a £100,000 anonymous donation. Throughout the year, the museum also hosts special events to further appreciation of Jane Austen, and to encourage new writers. For more information, please visit jane-austens-house-museum.org.uk

name: Mitzpe Ramon
description: Mitzpe Ramon literally translates to "Ramon Lookout" for its location at the edge of the Ramon Crater. Built in 1951 to house workers constructing Highway 40, the town was long considered a dusty backwater. But the spectacular desert scenery and laid back atmosphere has been attracting artists and free-thinkers, who have helped turn the it into a creative destination. In the Spice Route Quarter in particular, old hangars and warehouses have been converted into hip cafes, handicraft shops, and artist studios, including the space of the revolutionary Adama Dance Company. At the literal edge of town, perched on a cliff overlooking the Ramon Crater, the Mitzpe Ramon Visitor Center offers an unforgettable view of the world's largest box canyon, and details the formation of the makhtesh. Part of the exhibition is the Ilan Ramon Memorial, which honors Israel's first astronaut, who died in the 2003 Columbia Disaster, and loved the Ramon Crater.

name: Elbasan
description: Settled by the ancient Illyrians, Elbasan flourished for centuries thanks to its position on the Roman Via Egnatia. After helping spread Christianity to the region, the city was abandoned until the 15th century when it was rebuilt by the Ottomans, and remained a center for Islam in Albania even after their independence. Today, visitors these different phases in the castle district, where the old city walls, the ruins of the older Roman and Byzantine fortifications, as well as the 15th century Royal Mosque and 16th century Orthodox Church of St. Mary all stand side-by-side. As one of the country's cultural capitals, the city is also home to several unique museums. In the home of Alexander Xhuvani, visitors can learn about the life of this key figure in Albania's national revival. Nearby, the School Museum walks visitors through the country's unique educational development, while the Ethnographic Museum is preserves the city's traditional way of life.

name: Alta Gracia
description: Declared a World Historical Heritage in 2000, the estancia in Alta Gracia showcases the harmonious fusion of European and native American influences, evident in its architecture and art. Visitors can explore the well-preserved rooms, revealing the daily lives of past inhabitants. The estancia served as a center for agriculture and cattle production, supporting religious and educational institutions. The Jesuits left their mark on every corner, from the blacksmith's workshop to the flour mills, providing a glimpse into their organized and productive lifestyle. The adjacent temple, Our Lady of Mercy, boasts colonial Baroque architecture, adorned with intricate woodwork and gold leafing. The journey continues to the Tajamar, the province's oldest dam, supplying water to nearby estates and powering flour mills. Alta Gracia also honors the revolutionary icon, Che Guevara, whose childhood home is now a museum. The Casa del Che provides insights into his early life through exhibits and photographs, offering a nuanced view of the man behind the legend.

name: Marianske Lazne
description: Dissolutes, dukes, writers and poets refreshed themselves with Marianske Lazne's curative spa waters throughout the Nineteenth Century/ Perhaps most famously Goethe, who, heartbroken by a moody Baroness, composed his Marienbad Elegy here. Its romantic colonnades, pavilions, cafes, and snug hotels, all promote light-heartedness and enjoyment of the moment. Though there are plenty of spots to compose a heart-rending poem too, if the mood takes you. The Ambrose Spring, the 'Spring of Love' perhaps, or the Rudolph Spring whose water can be drunk directly from the wooden pavilion. If verse composition eludes you try the inspirational Singing Fountain in the town's iconic Colonnade. Designed by academic architect Pavel Mišík, the fountain, embedded with coloured lights, plays its jets of water to a varied program of classical and contemporary music.

name: Provins
description: With its high walls and even higher towers, its easy to see Provins is special. In the 13th century, Provins was one of the European centers of commerce, regularly hosting important fares since the town was located on a commercial crossroads. The newly-gained wealth was reinvested into the town, local real-estate, and its fortifications. The good times don't last forever, and when war and plague befell the city in the 14th century, it fell into a slump. Not much has changed since then, so today, visitors can take a trip to past centuries and admire the medieval walls or the stunning 13th-century architecture throughout the small town of Provins.

name: Gyumri
description: Gyumri rose above adversity and became a sanctuary for Armenian refugees fleeing the horrors of the Armenian Genocide after World War I, transforming it into a place of rich cultural heritage and historical significance in the region. Renowned for its traditional architecture and vibrant history, Gyumri has nurtured numerous talented artists, athletes, and musicians over the years, and is considered the home of Armenian comedy. The city's charm lies in its traditional neighbourhoods and the cozy streets where you'll encounter hidden cafes and historical buildings made from rare volcanic black and red tuff rock. Visit the Black Fortress, also known as Sev Berd, constructed by Russian Emperor Nicholas I using black volcanic tuff. Explore the old Kumayri district situated in the heart of the city, which dates back to the 5th century and boasts enchanting architecture. Sample some of the delectable local cuisine and immerse yourself in the cultural tapestry of Gyumri.

name: Larissa
description: At first glance, it would be difficult to guess the age of Greece's 4th largest city. Its name, however, gives a clue - Larissa was a nymph in Greek mythology. Upon closer inspection, the city's two ancient theaters, both of which are of great archeological importance, point toward a city that predates most of human civilization. Visitors in Larissa can learn about the ancient theatres, and the city's long history, in the local archeological museum. A stop in Larissa isn't all about ancient history though - visitors can also enjoy a stroll through the Alkazar park or sip a coffee in one of the city's great cafes.

name: Chiavari
address.addr1: 16043 Chiavari, Metropolitan City of Genoa, Italy
description: A pre-Roman necropolis from the 7th century BC was uncovered in Chiavari and reveals the town's rich history. Built under the Via Aurelia, a Roman road project commissioned by C. Aurelius Cotta in 241 BC, the town has enjoyed an active fishing trade, lace industry, abundant olive farms, and even the invention of the iconic Chiavari chair in the years following. Chiavari hosts a fascinating mix of architecture, from the Tuscan-Gothic style, Palazzo di Giustizia (Palace of Justice), to the Ancient- Roman inspired Cattedrale di N. S. dell'Orto (Shrine of Our Lady dell' Orto). Walk along the seafront's pebbled beach or roam through the "carrugi" into the historic center that dates from the Middle Ages. Participate in the city's routine by dining in family owned restaurants or window shop the many boutiques.

name: Nara
description: Having served as Japan's capital during the Nara period from 710 to 794, Nara boasts an illustrious past as the seat of the Emperor. It is adorned with a collection of eight remarkable temples, shrines, and ruins. Together with the Kasugayama Primeval Forest, these sites form the UNESCO-listed Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara. Nara Park, a serene expanse in the city's northeast, holds a special allure with its lush greenery and over 1,500 freely roaming deer. These deer, believed to be sacred messengers, offer an interactive and unique experience for visitors. Among Nara's captivating attractions, Todaiji Temple stands out with its towering wooden architecture and the awe-inspiring Great Buddha statue cast in black bronze. Isuien Garden, a 17th-century masterpiece, provides a peaceful oasis with its meticulously designed landscapes and breathtaking views of Todaiji temple. For art enthusiasts, the Nara National Museum houses a diverse collection of cultural treasures, and the picturesque Mount Wakakusa offers panoramic vistas of the city's scenic beauty.

name: Kamakura
description: Located less than an hour south of Tokyo, the city of Kamakura was once a political capital of Japan, standing alongside Kyoto and Nara. Today, it draws visitors with its rich heritage and natural attractions. Historical landmarks in the city include Tsurugaoka Hachimangū, the city's principal shrine around which Kamakura developed, and the 13th-century Great Buddha of Kamakura, which is both a symbol of the city and the second-largest Buddha in Japan. The area is also adorned with other beautiful traditional temples and shrines, such as Hasadera and Zeniarai Benten Shrine. Kamakura is renowned for its seasonal festivals. Centered around Tsurugaoka Hachimangū are the Kamakura Festival in April — a celebrated week-long event with dancing and traditional performances — and the Reitaisai in September, which showcases the samurai art of horseback archery. Komachi-dori Street offers a mix of traditional restaurants, trendy cafes, confectioneries, souvenir shops, and upscale kimono stores. For a taste of local flavors, try the city's favorite Cheese Korokke or Matcha and Purple Sweet Potato Ice Cream.

name: Luneburg
description: The need to pickle and preserve large amounts of herring caught in the Baltic Sea led to a high demand for salt in the region, and thus, prosperity for Luneburg. However, as overfishing led to the decline of the town in the 16th century, virtually all new construction ceased. Coupled emerging from World War II unscathed, the town has managed to maintain its medieval character. Today, Luneburg is a lively university town rumored to boast the highest concentration of pubs in Germany. But clues to the town's salty past can still be seen when touring the historic Am Sande square or shopping in the town center. The Alter Kran, a crane standing at the former Ilmenau docks, is one of Luneburg's most famous landmarks and speaks to the town's legacy. Between its breweries, spas, museums, and gardens, this medieval salt town has something for everyone.

name: Portoviejo
description: Originally a coastal city, Portoviejo was moved 30km inland in 1628, 93 years after it's founding, to a better protected site after repeated attacks from native populations. Located on a river of the same name, Portoviejo is the economic and agricultural centre of the Manabí Province. The city's older neighbourhoods are home to a large amount of colonial-era architecture, and the central park has lush grass and flower beds full of colour, as well as many palm trees. The local motto "Portoviejo rises - When there's a will there's a way" was never more appropriate than when it had to recover from the 2016 earthquake, as well as earlier economic setbacks of the 1980's and 90's. The modern city has great infrastructure with a great variety and quality when it comes to modern conveniences. You can also buy pretty much anything from the large flea market in the downtown area.

name: Sendai
description: Discover the vibrant city of Sendai, your gateway to the scenic Tohoku Region. Despite being near the epicenter of the 2011 earthquake, Sendai stands strong, welcoming visitors to explore its captivating attractions. The city's resilience shines through, with most tourist spots reopening shortly after the disaster. Experience the allure of Matsushima, renowned for its picturesque bay adorned with pine-covered islets, one of Japan's three most stunning vistas. Known as the "City of Trees" or "Forest City," Sendai's streets are lined with towering green trees that transform into golden hues during autumn and are illuminated enchantingly in winter. Uncover the legacy of Date Masamune at Aoba Castle, where the powerful feudal lord's history lives on. Explore the Sendai City Museum to admire his iconic black armor that reportedly inspired Darth Vader's attire. Delve into Sendai's unique festivals, including the Sendai Tanabata Festival, celebrating an ancient tale of star-crossed lovers.

name: Qatif
description: Nestled along the shores of the Persian Gulf and atop a petroleum field, this city has struck black gold. But it's not just about the oil. This oasis city has grown into one of Saudi Arabia's agricultural marvels, producing an array of dates, alfalfa, rice, fruits, and vegetables. Feeling peckish for some authentic Saudi produce? Swing by Khamee's market. Wander through the bustling lanes of the traditional markets, such as the Thursday Market "Suq Alkhamees" and "Suq Waqif," where you might stumble upon folksy handicraft. Feel like a walk along the shore? A promenade awaits. Need a relaxing bath, Ottoman-style? Abu Loza's Bath is just a splash away. History aficionados are welcome to check out sites in and around Qatif such as archaeological remains of Qasr Darin, Qal'at al-Qatif's ancient castle ruins, or Tarut Castle. Lastly, the Al-Qatif oasis is a living postcard showcasing traditional human settlement, farming, and a complex irrigation system.

name: Mina Clavero
description: Nestled within the enchanting Traslasierra valley, Mina Clavero beckons with its natural wonders and vibrant experiences. Flowing from the majestic Sierras Grandes, the Mina Clavero river's cold and crystalline waters carve a path through the city, forming golden beaches and inviting natural riverside retreats. This haven is a playground for outdoor enthusiasts. With 14 kilometers of sandy and rocky beaches, the river sets the stage for trekking, horseback riding, and thrilling ATV excursions. Embark on 4x4 crossings through diverse mountain roads, each offering a different level of exhilaration. eyond its natural allure, Mina Clavero boasts a robust tourist infrastructure. Immerse yourself in local gastronomy and partake in the lively entertainment scene, including a casino, bingo, and captivating street shows. Discover the scenic wonders that make Mina Clavero not just a destination but an exhilarating journey into Argentina's natural marvels.

name: Marwell Zoo
description: Nestled in the scenic Hampshire countryside near Southampton, Marwell Zoo offers an unforgettable adventure for animal lovers and families alike. Marwell Zoo prides itself on its conservation efforts and immersive exhibits. Wander through the lush landscapes and encounter majestic Amur tigers, elegant giraffes, and the rare Grevy's zebras. The Lemur Loop allows visitors to walk among these playful primates, while the Tropical House offers a vibrant journey through a rainforest, teeming with exotic birds, frogs, and reptiles. For a unique perspective, hop on the Marwell Zoo road train or take a leisurely stroll through themed areas such as the Roof of the World, which features snow leopards and red pandas. The zoo's expansive enclosures ensure that the animals have plenty of space to roam, mirroring their natural habitats and providing visitors with a sense of their wild environments.

name: Hardwick Hall and Gardens
description: Built at the end of the 16th century, Hardwick Hall was one of the first examples of English Renaissance architecture. The prodigy house mostly escaped modernization, with conscious preservation efforts taking place since the 19th century. Today, a guided tour brings the rich history of this opulent manor to life, and showcases the large collection of embroideries, many of which date back to the 16th century, and lavish furnishing, many of which are original and listed in an inventory dating from 1601. The manor grounds were redesigned in the 1870s, with serene grass paths lined with yew and hornbeam hedges leading to the grounds' 4 areas: the orchard, lawn, nuttery, and herb garden. Featured in the BBC documentary 'Britain's Best Buildings', Hardwick inspired the Main Exhibition Building at the Philadelphia Centennial Exhibition of 1876, and stood in for Malfoy Manor in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 1. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/hardwick

name: Merano
address.addr1: Merano, Province of Bolzano - South Tyrol, Italy
description: Merano is part of the South Tyrol region, where more than half of the population are German speakers. Although located within Italy's borders, Germany's language and culture lives and breathes in this wealthy city. German sausage and beer can be easily found as you saunter through the streets. Surrounded and protected by mountains, Merano is most known for its great climate and therapeutic programs. With health and well-being at the core of the city, don't forget to see the Art Nouveau building, which houses a health center as well as the city's many galas and upscale events. At last, it is more than necessary to visit the statue erected for South Tyrol's most notable freedom fighter, Andreas Hofer, in front of the main train station.

name: Destileria La Rojena
description: In 1795, Jose María Guadalupe de Cuervo received the first official charter from the King of Spain to produce tequila commercially, and the Destileria La Rojena has been producing the agave liquor ever since. Today, the historic hacienda is a jewel of colonial architecture with colorful buildings, columned courtyards, and neo-Baroque details. But it's inside where the magic really happens as agave piña are cooked, pressed, and processed using a blend of traditional techniques and modern machinery. On a guided tour, you'll be able to admire both the beautiful architecture and the rich history behind the world's best-selling tequila - and, of course, taste some for yourself. Bookings must be made in advance at https://www.mundocuervo.com/eng/la-rojena-distillery/

name: Meseta de Cacaxtla Flora and Fauna Protection Area
address.city: Meseta de Cacaxtla Flora and Fauna Protection Area
description: The eco-reserve, spanning nearly 200 square miles, stands as one of the largest and most diverse ecosystems in Mexico. Situated in the state of Sinaloa, the protected area borders the Pacific Ocean to the west and stretches into the foothills of the Sierra Madre mountains. Its wide-ranging ecosystems include sandy beaches, rugged ocean shorelines, exploratory tide pools, estuaries, inland ponds, and dry-tropical deciduous forests. It houses a myriad of animal species including hundreds of unique birds, reptiles, amphibians, boars, and even wild jaguars! This protected area falls within the Sinaloan dry forests ecoregion, incorporating areas of deciduous thorn scrub and lush mangroves. Although independent exploration of Meseta de Cacaxtla is an option, many visitors opt to traverse this eco-reserve accompanied by local tour operators.

name: Coatepec
address.region: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
description: Located in the Mexican state of Veracruz, Coatepec was named as a Pueblo Magico (a government designation where investment takes place to facilitate a "magical" experience). Named "the coffee capital of Mexico", the ideal climate in the region and the local fertilizer that is produced creates the great bean to roast and a scrumptious roast to wake up to! Other than its coffee, this city is a splash of colour. Visit the Church of San Jeronimo to admire the colourful architecture and the local flair in Spanish colonial architecture. Just walking through any street in this town will mesmerize you with its inviting colours and its sleepy ambiance. Another beloved trait of this town is its food. Its consistent climate facilitates the best quality of fare from Tamales to Gorditas to Enfrijoladas, among others! If you want an exciting escape from a bustling city, to just kick back with a cup of joe, then Coatepec is the place for you!

name: Angeles City
description: Angeles City was founded in 1796 by Don Ángel Pantaleón de Miranda, his wife, and a few followers, and within a century was made the seat of the Philippine government. Today, the city center, is known for its fine hotels, restaurants, and malls, while Fields Avenue has made it a destination for nightlife lovers, particularly because of its countless go-go bars. The city also has a wealth of historic monuments, like the Santo Rosario Church. Despite its beautiful Baroque facade, the church has a dark past, being built using slave labor, and used as an execution site by the Spanish. Then there's the Kamikaze East Airfield, which serves as a reminder of the Japanese occupation, and to promote international friendship. For a sampling of Philippine history and culture, the Nayong Pilipino Clark has recreations of some of the country's most important monuments, and a slew of museums dedicated to everything from Philippine money to textiles.

name: Artvin
description: Situated along the Çoruh River in Northern Turkey, just a stone's throw away from the Black Sea, Artvin is associated with its natural beauty. It is nestled amidst majestic mountains and serene crater lakes, offering a perfect setting for avid trekkers to indulge in the purest forms of nature. Notable attractions around Artvin include the Artvin Glass Terrace, offering a breathtaking view of the Hatila Stream, and Borcka Karagol Nature Park, a must-visit destination for its stunning panoramic views. Artvin's diverse population has significantly shaped its vibrant history, rich culture, and unique culinary traditions. Located near several centuries-old castle ruins, the city also provides a tantalizing glimpse into the region's storied past.

name: Phuket
description: One of the oldest settlements in Thailand, Phuket was a relatively small port until the early 1900s. Attracting businessmen and merchants from China, Portugal, and even the Arabian Peninsula, Phuket flourished as a vibrant trade center in the 20th century. Today, the old town is lined with distinctive Sino-Portuguese buildings, giving a glimpse into the city's proud past, while hip coffee shops, conceptual galleries, and boutique hotels are popping up to cater to the recent influx of artists and musicians. From this increasingly cosmopolitan city, it's easy to head out to the island's beautiful beaches, lush jungle, or go island hopping in Thailand's most picturesque coastal landscape.

address.addr1: Кањон Матка, Street 1;Village Matka, Village Matka 1000, Macedonia (FYROM)
description: When the Treska River was dammed, it transformed Matka Canyon into a scenic lake. The hiking trails around its perimeter offer great views, and the opportunity to see some of the endemic species that evolved here during the last glacial period. The area is dotted with caves, which visitors can tour. Perhaps most impressive is the concentration of medieval monasteries. The Monastery of St. Andrew's was built in 1389 and contains some impressive frescos. Perched on a cliff overlooking the lake, the Monastery of St. Nicholas Shishovski offers spectacular views of the lake and its surroundings. Nearby is Matka Monastery, which dates from the 14th century, and houses 15th century frescoes.

name: Knysna
description: Every year, travelers pass through the town of Knysna while touring the Garden Route - a 200 km stretch of coastline which is heralded for its beauty. However, those are misguided who do not stop to experience Knysna in its stunning natural setting. A plethora of beaches, forest hiking trails, and scuba diving sites give the more nature-oriented travelers a wide range of colorful options for their active holiday. Those who prefer culture trips have their choice of township tours and high-quality restaurants, and do not miss the oyster bars - the availability of high quality, fresh oysters are one of Knysna's most famous features, with a yearly Oyster Festival to showcase the product.

name: Abbotsford House
description: Abbotsford House was built by Sir Walter Scott using proceed from his illustrious writing career - first as a small villa, with many later additions using sculptured stones from ruined castles and abbeys transforming it into a sprawling Romantic mansion. An integral part of Scottish history, and keen history, Scott filled his home with an impressive collection of historic artefacts. Among the impressive collection of arms and armour, visitors can find Rob Roy MacGregor's gun, Mary Queen of Scots' crucifix, Claverhouse's pistol, and the Marquis of Montrose's sword, though the Scottish Crown jewels he rediscovered are on display at Edinburgh Castle. His library, containing over 9000 rare volumes has also been preserved. Surrounding the house, the Regency-style gardens were also laid out by Scott, and offer fantastic views of the house's unique architecture while providing a colorful and fragrant place to relax. For more information, please visit scottsabbotsford.com

name: Mount Etna
address.addr1: Funivia dell'Etna - Stazione Arrivo Parco dell'Etna, Nicolosi, Piazzale Rifugio Sapienza, 95030 Nicolosi CT
description: At 3329 meters high, Mt. Etna is the largest mountain south of the Alps, not to mention the largest volcano in Europe, and one of the most active in the world. While the near constant activity has devastated the surrounding settlements over the centuries, it's also created fertile, soil in which vineyards and orchards thrive. The mountain is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its surreal and varied landscape, and the invaluable scientific information it provides. Nature lovers can experience otherworldly deserts of black lava, beech wood forests, lush vineyards, or snow-capped peaks. Get just close enough to marvel at this natural wonder, or hop aboard the funicular (around 16.00€ p.p) to ride partway up the slope. Those with hiking ambitions should add more time to their stop to explore the network of trails and waystations, where you'll be treated to the volcano's amazing landscape as well as spectacular views of Sicily and the Mediterranean. Please inform your driver what you'd like to do on your visit. Sometimes it's even possible to see lava flowing! Please note: the mountain's altitude makes it quite cold, and as it's still active, access will sometimes be closed off for public safety.

name: Comitan
description: Originally a Mayan settlement known as Balún Canán, the Spanish built their own city atop the site, and renamed it Comitan. As the city grew over the centuries, it managed to preserve its colonial core and quaint atmosphere, which has made it a popular vacation destination among Mexican nationals. The colonial churches are particularly charming, such as the 17th century Templo de Santo Domingo, with its Moorish-inspired architecture and peach-colored facade. The towering Templo de San José is an unusual blend of Neo-Gothic and Baroque, done up in a whimsical white, while the vivid orange Iglesia de San Caralampio sits atop a checkered brick staircase. For those looking to dive deeper into the city's history, the free Museo de Arqueologico de Comitan exhibits a small collection of Mayan artefacts, while the Casa Museo Doctor Belisario Domínguez honors the life of the early 20th century doctor after whom the city is named.

name: Rila Monastery
description: Founded in the 10th century, Bulgaria's largest monastery played an important role in restoring Bulgarian faith and national identity during Ottoman rule in the 18th and the 19th centuries. Today, the monastery stands as a work of art, with its exterior decorated with bold stripes and vibrant polychromatic frescoes. Inside, the dynamic decoration continues, with every inch covered with colorful frescoes, and ornate gilding taking up an entire wall. For UNESCO, the monastery's importance to the Bulgarian national identity and its wealth of artwork made it an easy choice as a World Heritage Site.

name: Cathedral of Gloucester
description: Founded as a 7th century abbey, the current Cathedral of Gloucester was built by the Normans in the 12th century, with several revisions made over the years. Today, this stupendous Cathedral is a stupendously preserved survey of medieval architecture. Inside, visitors will find Norman pillars supporting stupendous vaulted ceilings, and some singular medieval relics, such as the ornately carved tomb of Edward II, and some of the country's finest stained glass windows - including one with the oldest depiction of golf. The cathedral's cloisters with their fan-vaulting and stained glass windows are particularly magnificent. Harry Potter fans will be in heaven as the cloisters served as several Hogwarts locations, such as where Harry and Ron hid from the troll, where the words 'The chamber of secrets has been opened' appeared, and that red door? It was the entrance to the Gryffindor common room.

name: La Escondida
description: La Escondida was originally constructed in 1959 as a small inn and restaurant to welcome travelers from near and far. Because of its secluded location in the trees, it was difficult for owner Don Eduardo to initially attract business. Eduardo embraced the hidden location and began dotting the landscape with magical creatures that one might find in a woodland fairytale. Gnomes, trolls, fairies and more have taken over the area and create a magical atmosphere. Today, the eclectic enclave welcomes guests to the restaurant for a cup of tea and a walk through the grounds. Keep your eye out for the giant chef statue at the roadside entrance to signal you're getting close to hidden haven. Be sure to check the opening hours!

name: Benagil
description: The world-renowned poster child of the Algarve coast, the natural grotto with its occulous and secluded beach should be on every visitor's 'must-see list'. Depending on your dedication, there are multiple ways to view the cave, and the coastline. The driest is a short walk, which allows you to view the cave from above. To see as much of the coast as possible, boat tours from praia de Benagil will zip visitors through a series of coastal caves. For those looking to get their feet wet, it's also possible to rent kayaks and paddle over to the cave. An additional advantage of going under your own power is that you can actually stand on the beach and take your time enjoying this natural wonder.

name: Suncheon
description: Suncheon is the largest city in Jeollanam-do, renowned for its popular ecological park, Suncheon Bay. This unique region boasts coastal wetlands, freshwater streams, vast fields of picturesque reeds, and a diverse wildlife population. The bay is divided into two parts, the Wetland Reserve and the National Garden, connected by the "Sky Cube" train. The Wetland Reserve showcases dense reed fields attracting rare bird species, and a hike to the hilltop offers panoramic views of the wetlands, a truly rewarding experience. For K-drama and movie enthusiasts, the Suncheon Open Film Location is a must-visit attraction. Comprising three villages representing different eras from the 1950s to the 1970s, it has been featured in numerous Korean films, making it a dream destination for fans. For history buffs, Seonamsa, a historical temple dating back to 529 BC, offers a glimpse into the city's rich history and culture. The temple, restored to its 11th-century glory, invites visitors to explore its exquisite surroundings and indulge in a traditional Korean tea service at a nearby tea house.

name: Siena
description: The medieval city of Siena is most famous for the Palio, a bareback horse race that has been held in the city square twice a year since the 16th century. Outside of the race, the city is an alluring mixture of medieval architecture and Tuscan tradition. The main square is dominated by the early 14th century Palazzo Pubblico and its soaring tower. This historic building still houses the city's municipal offices, and welcomes visitors to learn more about the town's history in the Civic Museum. If you're up for a rewarding challenge, you can climb the 500 steps to the top of the tower for wonderful views of Siena and its surroundings. Also in the square is Siena's stunning Gothic cathedral, which is one of the finest in the country with its painted facade and interior filled with beautiful Renaissance frescoes. Of course, being in Tuscany, it's also a great place to sip one some wine and sample the region's cuisine.

name: Gubbio
description: Settled since the Bronze Age, Gubbia was an important city for the Umbrians, and the Iguvian tablets discovered here in 1444 constitute the largest surviving text in the Umbrian language. After being conquered by the Romans in the 2nd century BC, it maintained its prominence, as its Roman theatre, the second-largest left in the world, can attest. The city's medieval center was the result of a 14th century boom, as embodied by the magnificent Palazzo dei Consoli. Reminiscent of a castle-in-miniature, palace overlooks an amazing hanging square, and the Praetorian Palace. The Ducal Palace houses an exact reproduction of the duke's study of the duke, as the original exhibited at the Metropolitan Museum in New York. After wandering the town's cobbled streets, past its many medieval monuments, be sure to sit down to enjoy one of Gubbio's famous pasta dishes with truffles, which are produced in strict compliance with ancient techniques.

name: Montepulciano
description: Montepulciano is renowned for its pork, cheese, "pici" pasta, lentils, and honey, but it's known worldwide for its wine. Connoisseurs consider its Vino Nobile among Italy's best. The city, full of elegant Renaissance palaces, ancient churches and hidden corners, boasts vast panoramas all over the wonderful Val d'Orcia and Val di Chiana valleys that surround it. It has one of the most intact and architecturally unified historic centres of any Italian town: within its walls, no major building work has taken place since 1580. Piazza Grande is the heart of Montepulciano and the setting for its main events, including the Bravio delle Botti barrel racing contest held in August every year and much more. Just be prepared to share the town: Montepulciano has received great attention following the filming of the vampire saga Twilight sequel New Moon here and has seen a notable increase in visitors.

name: Desierto de los Leones
description: Mexico's first national park is haunted by the abandoned Desierto de los Leones convent, the ruins of which add a historic air to the stunning natural surroundings. While Desierto de los Leones is neither a desert, nor filled with lions, the stunningly overgrown plants, flowers, and shrubs add an element of whimsy and are reminiscent of a mythical past. Ideal for a moment of reflective mediation, the peaceful surroundings are what attracted this area to the Spanish monks. Eventually being abandoned in 1810, this convent and the areas surrounding it, are filled with all kinds of wildlife and even legends about the supernatural. Make sure to bring a jacket, as the cool misty environment only adds to the calming atmosphere of the convent. And, beware of rattlesnakes!

name: Wloclawek
description: Włocławek's history stretches back over 3000 years, through local tribes, Romans, and ambitious European empires. With such a long history, it's home to some singular sites. One of the most important is Copernicus Square, dedicated to when Nicolaus Copernicus studied at the cathedral school, where he built the sundial that's on the Cathedral Basilica. To see his work, head to the Basilica Cathedral of the St. Mary Assumption, a gothic cathedral built between 1340-1411. It is one of the country's oldest and highest churches, and filled with some breathtaking artwork, including the oldest stained glass windows in Poland. St. Witalis Curch is the oldest building in Włocławek, dating back to 1330, and home to some beautiful Polish 15th century paintings. For those looking something more recent, the Marina won many architectural competitions and offers a pleasant place to relax by the river.

description: Saint Paul de Vence embodies French charm with its markets and local wines, art galleries, the famous Folon Chapel, the Grande Fountaine, and countless other intrigues. But it was the 20th century that gave the town its artistic identity characterized by its dozens of art galleries and the world-renowned Foundation Maeght art museum. The town is famously known for the many artists who lived in or visited St-Paul; some of whom are buried in the cemetery at the village's southern end. It is suggested by the locals to come during the off season, as the cobblestone lanes become crowded during summer, as the town is a visitor's favorite!

name: Ubeda
description: Founded in the 9th century, intensive trade made Ubeda one of the most important cities in the region. During the 15th and 16th centuries, it received an influx of aristocratic families, who erected lavish homes and palaces. Today, many of these monuments still survive, making Ubeda the best place in Andalucia to admire Renaissance architecture. The Plaza Vázquez de Molina is entirely surrounded by buildings from the 16th century, forming one of the most important collections of Renaissance buildings in all of Europe. The 16th century Sacred Chapel of El Salvador, with its magnificent Plateresque doorways and reredos by Alonso de Berruguete is a pristine example of the city's Renaissance heritage. Also facing the square is the Church of Santa María de los Reales Alcázares. Built in the 13th century on the site of an old Arab mosque, it combines centuries of artistic styles, including a 16th century cloister.

name: Limoges
description: Built on the site of a Roman Augustoritum, by the Middle Ages the town had become a flourishing artistic centre, starting with an important school of medieval music composition. It later mastered enamels on copper, and in the 19th century, porcelain. Two centuries late, the town is the world-renowned capital of French porcelain. In the former Bishop's palace, visitors will find a fine collection of the renowned porcelain alongside Impressionist paintings. The palace gardens are spread out over scenic terraces, allowing visitors to simultaneously enjoy the botanical garden and views of the river. Dominating the town, the Saint-Etienne cathedral is a gorgeous example of Gothic art, particularly its Flamboyant Gothic portal. In the picturesque old town, along with charming half-timbered houses, visitors will find the 15th century Saint-Aurélien chapel, and the cafe-lined Motte square with its beautiful 19th century covered market hall.

name: Arlington Row
description: Arlington Row in Bibury was built in 1380 as a monastic wool store, but in the 17th century, the buildings were converted into a string of cottages for the town's weavers. Today, the string of cottages are one of the most photographed sights in the Cotswolds, being preserved by the Royal Academy of Fine Arts, and appearing in everything from Bridget Jones' Diary to UK passports. In fact, the street is so picturesque that resident Peter Maddox's 'ugly little yellow car' was vandalized in 2017 for 'ruining' pictures of the street. This in turn prompted a headline-making parade of yellow cars, which passed through the village in support of Peter's plight.

name: Mahebourg
description: Situated along the picturesque southeastern coast of Mauritius, Mahebourg exudes an irresistible charm that captivates visitors with its blend of history, culture, and natural beauty. Wander through the vibrant streets of Mahebourg and discover a tapestry of colonial-era buildings, colorful markets, and bustling waterfront promenades. Visit the iconic Mahebourg Waterfront, where traditional wooden boats bob gently in the harbor against a backdrop of azure waters and palm-fringed shores. History enthusiasts will delight in exploring the town's many museums and historical sites, including the National History Museum, which offers insight into the island's fascinating past through interactive exhibits and artifacts. For nature lovers, Mahebourg serves as a gateway to some of Mauritius' most stunning natural attractions, including Blue Bay Marine Park, renowned for its crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral reefs teeming with marine life. Embark on a snorkeling or glass-bottom boat excursion to immerse yourself in the breathtaking underwater world that lies just beyond the shore. Indulge in the local cuisine at one of Mahebourg's charming waterfront restaurants, where you can savor fresh seafood delicacies and Creole specialties while enjoying panoramic views of the Indian Ocean.

name: Cuetzalan
description: Nestled high in the foothills of the Sierra Norte region, Cuetzalan was named a "Pueblo Magico" for its warm climate, historic significance and beautiful views. One of its many unique qualities is the preservation of Mesoamerican culture, most notably the Flying Dancers, reserved as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. This is an ancient ritual where performers dance around a 30 metre high pole and climb on top of it flying around it attached to ropes. One person stays on top of the pole, while simultaneously playing a flute, beating a drum and dancing. This is an unforgettable experience that truly shows the village's pride for culture. Other sights include the beautiful colonial church of Cuetzalan, the pyramids of Yohualichan and the La Cascada de las Brisas waterfalls.

name: Kazanlak
description: Settled since around 6,000 BC, the area near Kazanlak was home to ancient Thracian kings, and is still home to their tombs. This ancient necropolis is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its exceptionally elaborate murals depicting Thracian funerary traditions. Because of the fragility of the 2,500 year-old paintings, an exact replica of the tomb was made for visitors to see the architecture and artwork. Centuries ago, the Damask rose was brought to Bulgaria, and has since developed into its own unique strain. Visitors can head to the Museum of Roses to learn about the cultivation and production of rose oil through photographs, documents, and exhibits.

name: Huasco
description: Whether you love swimming, sailing, surfing, diving, fishing, or simply strolling by the seaside, Huasco is the perfect retreat that welcomes outdoor enthusiasts year-round. Among its notable strands include Playa Granda, nestled within the city, Tres Playitas (Three Little Beaches), and Baratillo Beach to the north of Huasco. The historic Church of San Pedro stands as a testament to the town's maritime heritage, harking back to its days as a fishing village, while the Esmeralda Fort presides over the bay with a touch of historical intrigue. Huasco offers cultural and educational experiences as well, with attractions like the Municipal Library, housed in a century-old building that once served as the old station. Nearby, you'll find Huasco Bajo, an ancient indigenous settlement turned rural village amid olive groves. For those intrigued by the region's natural wonders, Bahía Guacolda, located in the south, presents a striking landscape marked by rocky terrain, cacti, and a dusting of iron ore. With its enticing beaches, historical sites, and vibrant natural beauty, Huasco is a magnet for those seeking outdoor adventure and relaxation along the Chilean coast. Photo by Yastay, CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Poti
description: With a history spanning over 26 centuries, Poti is a city filled with fascinating stories and architectural marvels. Its unique city plan and stunning heritage buildings have earned it the nickname "Little Paris". Exploring Poti means strolling through its walkable streets adorned with beautiful buildings and street art, while immersing oneself in its vibrant market and savoring delciious meals at its excellent restaurants. The iconic Poti Lighthouse, with its red-and-white candy-striped exterior, stands as a prominent landmark and top attraction. Ascend its spiral iron staircase to reach the open viewing deck, which provides panoramic views of the Rioni River estuary and a sprawling cemetery. Marvel at the eo-Byzantine Poti St. Virgin Cathedral, modeled after Istanbul's Hagia Sophia, making it the only cathedral of its kind in Georgia, and the 70 buildings with Cultural Heritage status. Discover Poti, where history, maritime charm, and cultural heritage intertwine along the captivating Black Sea coast.

name: Sukhothai
description: Sukhothai was the capital of the eponymous kingdom which flourished in the 13th through 15th centuries. This era of peace allowed art, architecture, and language to flourish, and what developed here in Siam's first capital laid the foundations for Thailand's first kingdom. Today, Sukhothai Historical Park offers visitors 190 ruins spread across 70 square kilometers in a splendid display of art and architecture from the 'dawn of happiness'. The historic city is divided into 5 zones, the most popular being the central zone, which encompasses the ruins of the royal palace and the royal temple, Wat Mahathat. With its giant Buddha, lotus-bud chedi, and reflecting pond the Wat Mahathat is the park's poster child. The park is so big that those looking to see all the major sites should hop on a guided tram tour. The Ramkhamhaeng National Museum is also worth visiting if you'd like to see artifacts including stucco relief images, Buddhas, Hindu deities, and ceramics unearthed in the area.

name: Sale
description: Founded in the early 11th century, Salé was like a sister to Rabat for most of its history, even serving as a pirate port in the 17th century. So notable was the pirate presence here that Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe was imprisoned by the 'Salé Rovers'. Salé's medina is the perfect place to explore on foot, and easy to spot thanks to its bright orange walls. Wandering the narrow streets, you'll find plenty of traditional houses with intricately adorned windows and doors. Since Sale's not a main tourist attraction, the souk here is much more pleasant. The 12th century Great Mosque here is one of the most beautiful in the country, but is closed to non-muslims. The 14th century Medersa, however, is open to anyone and features jaw-dropping mosaics and carvings.

name: Valladolid
description: Founded by the Spanish Conquistador Francisco de Montejo in 1543 at a lagoon called Chouac-Ha, Valladolid was moved to its current location in 1545 because of mosquitos. Despite being one of the largest cities in Yucatan, Valladolid has a laid-back atmosphere and preserves both its Colonial and Mayan roots. At the heart of the city, dominating the main square is the Iglesia de San Servacio, which was built in 1706 after the Bishop Pedro De Los Rios Reyes ordered the destruction of the original 16th-century cathedral. The Convent of San Bernadino de Siena is another notable Colonial landmark, which is filled with colorful frescoes dating back to the 16th century. For Mayan culture, don't miss the Casa de los Venados, which exhibits the Mexico's largest private collections of pre-colonial art. But the top activity here is just wandering the streets, starting with the colorful Calzada de Los Frailes, to enjoy the atmosphere.

name: Gulu
description: Gulu was once the focal point for the destabilizing Lord's Resistance Army in 1990's, but since their defeat in the late 2000's the city has rebounded strongly. You might consider just passing through Gulu but it would be a shame to miss out on this bustling and friendly city. It's a pleasant stop with plenty of relaxed spots to hang out at, and with the amount of NGOs in the area the locals are used to welcoming visitors. Check out the various craft markets for paintings, wood carvings, and fabrics made by talented local artisans. It's also worth visiting the Taks Cultural Centre and peruse an art exhibition or a cultural performance. There's a restaurant there serving local cuisine. All proceeds go towards youth training. As for landmarks, the best maintained (possibly oldest) is the impressive red brick St. Joseph's Cathedral, which was once visited by Pope John Paul II.

name: Rio de Janeiro
description: The second largest city in Brazil and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Rio welcomes more visitors than almost anywhere else in the Southern Hemisphere. Start your trip at the top of the world, side by side with Christ the Redeemer! The panoramic views atop this world wonder allow you to gaze across the entire city and Sugarloaf Mountain. Jutting out from the shore, this forested peak is accessible by cable car and offers sweeping vistas while you enjoy a bite in one of the elevated cafés. On the coast, you'll find what Rio is perhaps most famous for, Copacabana Beach! This exotic stretch of paradise, with white sands and calming waters, entices millions of visitors every year. While the beach is great for football, further in the city is where dreams are made and legends are born. Superstars like Zico, Romario, and Ronaldo plied their trade on concrete courts throughout the city, before earning their place at the famous Maracana Stadium. In this tropical cityscape, the setting sun gives rise to samba. The party is especially in full flow during the Carnival! This festival fills the streets with music, colors, and dancing, all building to the pinnacle at its exciting epicenter, the famous Sambodromo stadium!

name: Bellagio
description: Lake Como and its cities feature contemporary art and monuments, decadent museums, lavish resorts, and the famous George Clooney. Throughout history, Como has remained a getaway for aristocrats and the wealthy. Even today, the common attraction is to ride the ferry or take a river cruise to marvel at all the luxurious villas and homes of famous actors, designers, musicians, and billionaires. On the main street Via Giuseppe Garibaldi, one might find all of Bellagio's treasures - from local food to leather. All of the neighboring alleys have plenty of shops featuring jewelry, silk, and perfumes!

name: L'Aquila
description: According to local legend, the city of L'Aquila was constructed when the Holy Roman Emperor, Frederik II, combined 99 valley villages to form the regional capital. The legend is memorialized by the 99 jets that make up the 13th century Fontana delle novantanove cannelle. Sitting in a valley surrounded by tall, snow-capped mountains, the has a traditional Italian feel in an alpine setting. The historic center is a maze of narrow streets lined with Baroque and Renaissance buildings, opening onto elegant piazzas. The Basilica of San Bernardino, built in 1472, has an elegant Renaissance façade, and contains the monumental tomb of its patron saint. The 16th century Spanish fort overlooking the town has been home to the National Museum of Abruzzo since 2016. For travelling gourmets, particularly those who like some heat, nearly every regional dish is seasoned with local peperoncino chilies.

name: Agadir
description: Agadir was founded by Portuguese merchants in the 15th century to develop trade links with Saharan caravans. The settlement did well until the 1760s when trade was diverted to Essaouira, and needed to be completely rebuilt after a devastating earthquake in 1960. Today, the old town is covered by the grassy knoll beneath the kasbah. Amazingly, the 16th century kasbah itself survived the quake, and now stands as the oldest building in the city, where visitors can enjoy medieval architecture and stupendous views of the coast. But it's the beautiful stretch of white sand, calm waters, and 300 sunny days a year that have made Agadir Morocco's prime beach resort. Even if you don't want to get your feet wet, a broad promenade provides a great place soak up some sun.

name: Tullamore Dew
description: Founded in 1829, Tullamore Dew's production was moved to Midleton in the 1950s. However, in 2014, production returned to Tullamore after the construction of a state-of-the-art distillery and visitor center. While the distillery might be new, a visit immerses visitors in the history of whiskey, from grain to glass, thanks to multimedia presentations and expert guides. On a tour of the Distillery House, you'll meet the Tullamore D.E.W. Distillery Ambassador, learn about the production process, and even try you hand at making a blended whiskey. As an added bonus for whiskey aficionados, the distillery offers the opportunity to buy a range of Tullamore products, including the Old Bonded Warehouse Release which is only available in the visitor centre. For more information please visit https://www.tullamoredew.com/en-gb/visit-us/

name: Lecco
description: Settled by the ancient Celts, this scenic lakefront city was once a Frankish frontier town. In the 10th and 11th centuries it received significant attention from the Holy Roman Emperor, first to crush a rebellion, and again to free it from the church. The lakefront promenade offers visitors a scenic starting point before exploring the rest of the city. The best views in the city are offered from atop the belltower, which requires an advanced booking. Below it, the Basilica of Saint Nicholas houses medieval frescoes within its neo-classical facade. While the Church of Santa Maria has a simple facade, it's one of the city's oldest churches, and has an impressive baroque interior. The city also has some impressive villas from the 18th and 19th centuries. The Villa Manzoni is now a museum dedicated to Alessandro Manzoni, a 19th century author who was born here.

name: Kuala Lumpur
address.addr1: Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
description: Malaysia's capital of Kuala Lumpur, or KL as it's often called, was only founded in the mid 19th century as a small mining settlement. In 1886 a railway line allowed it to rapidly develop, and in 1896, Kuala Lumpur was made the capital of the Federated Malay States. Today, KL is the largest city in Malaysia, where the country's Malay, Chinese and Indian communities have created a colorful feast for the senses. Glinting skyscrapers and giant shopping malls dwarf the city's vibrant mosques and colonial manors. While Kuala Lumpur reveres its heritage, it's also an ambitious modern city, as the riverbank-regeneration project and 1,483 foot tall Exchange 106 tower can attest. The favorite local pastimes are shopping and eating, so to do as the locals do, take to the streets on foot to discover the city's more village-like aspects, incomparable street food, and friendly traditional coffee shops - you can always pop into a mall to cool off.

name: Konopiste
address.addr1: The Konopiste Castle, 256 01 Benešov, Czech Republic
description: This Baroque-revamped Gothic fortification belonged to the Archduke Franz Ferdinand d'Este, whose assassination in Sarajevo ignited the First World War. Gloomy remembrance is not the order of the day at Konopištĕ and its environs however. The castle stands at the wooded lip of an extensive lake ideal for long bracing walks, while the castle's own belt of gardens and lawns invite more serene strolling. Tours of the castle interior are of course available, including Franz Ferdinand's private apartments, and his collections of antique furniture, Italian paintings, Gothic sculptures, hunting trophies and armoury are seriously impressive. But what's so appealing about Konopištĕ is the atmosphere of its lake-side location. Walking around the lake's wooded shore and looking back at the castle's tree-cushioned towers, reflecting perhaps on the fate of ordinary mortals and Archdukes can be a stilling, calming experience.

name: St Mary the Virgin in Saffron Walden
address.addr1: Church Path, Saffron Walden CB10 1JP, UK
address.city: St Mary the Virgin in Saffron Walden
description: Dating back to the 13th century, St. Mary the Virgin in Saffron Walden received a makeover in the Perpendicular style in 1450, courtesy of John Wastell, the master mason behind Cambridge's King's College Chapel. Today, it's the largest 'non-Cathedral' church in Essex, and its neo-Gothic spire the tallest in the region. Stepping inside, visitors first notice the cavernous dimensions and fine stained glass windows, but a closer look reveals a wealth of historic elements. A keen eye will notice elements from the church's previous lives, such as a fragment of a Saxon Market Cross in the South Porch, and the 13th century carvings in the North Aisle. Of the church's artefacts, the 16th century tomb of Thomas Audley is particularly noteworthy. A farmer who rose to become Lord Chancellor of England and supporter of Henry VIII, Lord Audley was the 3rd third richest man in England when he died.

name: Imbros Gorge
description: Before the road between Chania and Hora Sfakion was built, the Imbros Gorge mule trail was the only connection between the two towns. During World War II thousands of overwhelmed Allied Troops used the protection of the gorge's deep walls to withdraw. The only four soldiers with weapons sacrificed themselves holding off a German attack on the retreating column. Today, the Imbros Gorge is one of the most popular hikes in Crete, partly as a pilgrimage for the troops' descendants, but also because of its rugged beauty and ease of access. After entering the gorge at Imbros, the walls gradually narrow, until you reach the Stenada, where the sides are only 1.6m apart, but 300m high. From here, the gorge begins to widen again until you reach the village of Komitades at its base. There are quite a few tavernas here where you can have lunch to refuel.

name: Akagera National Park
description: Named after the grand river that flows through it, Akagera National Park is home to a splendor of African wildlife, including lions, leopards, elephants, buffalos, zebras, giraffes and various antelopes. Over 500 bird species also make this a popular destination for keen birdwatchers. See the wildlife up close by joining a guided walk or taking a boat safari on Lake Ihema to spot hippos and crocodiles lurking in the water. The 1,100 square kilometers of parkland is replete with stunning landscapes and natural beauty, with rolling hills, vast grasslands and wetlands. Akagera National Park is an important site for conservation in Rwanda and plays a vital role in protecting the country's biodiversity, making it a popular destination for ecotourism. Take the opportunity to explore Rwanda in all its natural beauty and learn about the importance of conservation at this incredible attraction.

name: The Royal Air Force Museum London
address.addr1: Grahame Park Way, London NW9 5LL, UK
address.city: The Royal Air Force Museum London
description: Opened in 1972, the Royal Air Force Museum London began with 36 aircraft housed in a World War I aerodrome. Over the years, the museum accrued more planes, and more space, and now has over 100 warplanes from the past 100 years housed in 5 hangers. Here visitors will discovered the evolution of aircraft and the RAF, from the Sopwith Camel to the Eurofighter Typhoon, and see rare relics, such as one of the 2 surviving Vickers Wellingtons, and iconic RAF planes like a Spitfire that flew in the Battle of Britain. Along with the aircraft are exhibitions about the vital work of the ground crews, and personal artefacts ranging from RAF airmen. All this history is brought to life through fascinating audiovisual installations, and visitors can even get into a simulator to take to the (virtual) skies! For more information, please visit www.rafmuseum.org.uk

name: Victoria Harbour
description: Victoria Harbour was built in the shadow of Dunbar's ruined medieval castle in the 1840s. The castle ruins are now home to over 600 nesting kittiwakes - the most accessible colony in Britain. At the opposite end of the harbour is an 18th century fort and battery, built to defend the town against the privateers who stalked the area during the American War of Independence. Today the battery is a seaside park, amphitheatre, and art space. This well-protected harbour is a safe-haven for a lively commercial fishing fleet that frequently lands shellfish - meaning Dunbar's a great place to enjoy some seafood. Sammy, the resident seal is often seen patrolling the harbor in hopes of the fishermen giving him a fresh fish supper.

name: Stockwood Discovery Centre
description: The Stockwood Discovery Center tells the story of the local people while keeping environmentally friendly principles in mind. Stepping into the Discovery Center, visitors will uncover the region's history, from prehistoric times to the days of the Stockwood House and the Farley estate. Among its collections, visitors will find geological and archaeological artefacts, like the medieval Wenlok Jug, as well as rural crafts, and the UK's largest collection of Mossman carriages. Outside, visitors have the rare opportunity to enjoy the work of acclaimed artist Ian Hamilton Finlay in a classical garden, while the Period Gardens reflect the country's changing gardening styles. For more information, please visit lutonculture.com/stockwood-discovery-centre

name: Glen Coe
description: An extinct supervolcano carved out by a glacier, Glen Coe is perhaps one of the most geologically distinctive areas in the Scottish Highlands. Filmmakers have been aware of Glen Coe's distinctive beauty for decades, and fans might recognize the chasm once spanned by the Bridge of Death in Monty Python and the Holy Grail, and three sets were built in Clachaig gully for Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. The site just across from the Clachaig Inn is the most notable as it was used in subsequent Harry Potter films. Even if you're not a Potter-head, Glen Coe's walking trails still bring visitors through some of Scotland's most dramatic landscapes.

name: Malang City
description: Nestled in a highland region, Malang City enjoys a cool and pleasant climate and is bursting with natural beauty and captivating landmarks. Marvel at a stunning waterfall backdrop and engage in the unique experience of sky cycling across a suspended rope at Coban Rais. For art enthusiasts, the Hotel Tugu Malang stands out as an extraordinary showcase of Asian art and antiquities including ancient ceramics, jade carvings, porcelain, wood carvings and even a complete facade of a Chinese temple. Exploring the streets of Malang reveals a treasure trove of colonial architecture, with Jl Besar Ijen or 'millionaires' row' lines with elegant whitewashed mansions from the Dutch era. Adding to the charm of Malang are the Kampung Warni Widi neighborhoods, where originally ramshackle houses have been transformed into whimsical, multicolored communities and are one of the city's most popular attractions.

name: Jekyll Island, GA
description: The story of Jekyll Island, GA, spans millennia. From Native American tribes to European conflict, and an elite private member's club, centuries of stories have elevated it into a beloved holiday destination. The dazzling Driftwood Beach is a stunning spectacle and photo opportunist's dream, with sun-bleached driftwood, gentle waves and beautiful sunsets. The Georgia Sea Turtle Center is a must for wildlife lovers, and offers a great opportunity to learn about these endangered animals. Take to the Wanderer Memorial Trail to learn the story of America's last known slave ship, The Wanderer, located along the banks of the Jekyll River. For more of the island's history, the former Jekyll Island Club, an exclusive, private winter retreat intended only for the country's elite. The 30 historic structures offer a look how the upper crust, like William Rockefeller, lived.

name: Grand Canyon Village, AZ
description: The Grand Canyon Village can trace its roots back to the end of the 19th century. Many of the buildings in the historic district were built by the Santa Fe Railroad Company in the early 20th century, and designed by Mary Colter, one of the country's first and foremost female architects. The log train depot is one of the last buildings of its kind in the country, and is still in use! While Mary Colter's Hopi House has been offering Native American crafts since it was built in 1904. The historic district leads right to the edge of the canyon, where you can take in the amazing views from Mary's Lookout Studio, or the home photographic studio of the Kolb brothers - the first Grand Canyon's pioneering photographers. Of course, the highlight is the hiking trail (or bus if you're not up for a walk) along the rim of the Grand Canyon.

name: Lienz
description: The Roman city and open-air museum of Aguntum is located just outside the town and offers fascinating insights into town life in the first and second centuries. In Lienz itself the town's main square, the Hauptplatz is full of charm, with its palm trees and cafe terraces. The Town Hall is located in the Lieburg, a twin onion-domed pocket-sized castle built in the early 17th century. For the bigger variety visit Lienz's landmark Bruck Castle, dating from the 13th century, set on a mixed-forest hill overlooking the town. Apart from fabulous views the castle – named after the bridge at its foot - is a beautifully preserved building dedicated to the region's rich artistic and cultural heritage. Its art collection covers half a millenium of paintings and sculpture, including the biggest public collection of East Tyrolean Expressionist painter Albin Egger-Lienz, born near the town of his hyphenated name.

name: Carcassonne
description: Originally an Iron Age fortification, the Romans expanded the site into a proper settlement. From then on, the fortified hilltop was continuously expanded by its rulers until the Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659. Like many towns in the region, Carcassonne's Cathars were targeted by the Albigensian Crusades, and expelled from the city when it surrendered. After being demilitarized by Napoleon, the town fell into disrepair, almost being demolished. Fortunately, a campaign to save the town brought in architect Eugène Viollet-le-Duc, one of the founders of the modern science of conservation, who expertly restored the fortifications to their former glory. Thanks to these efforts, visitors are able to explore the ramparts, the Château Comtal, the Cour du Midi remains of a Gallo-Roman villa, the Inquisition Tower, Gothic basilica, and the torture chamber at the Exposition.

name: Cotswold Wildlife Park and Gardens
address.addr1: Cotswold Wildlife Park and Gardens, Bradwell Grove, Burford OX18 4JP, UK
description: The origins of the Cotswold Wildlife Park and Gardens date back to 1804 when William Hervey had the current manor house built and planted a great number of trees in the park, including the 40 meter tall wellingtonia that can still be seen from miles away. In 1969 the house's owner opened the gardens to the public, and a year later, the Wildlife Park was founded. Today, the landscaped parkland and gardens are home to over 260 species, ranging from penguins to lions and rhinos. Visitors will also find one of the UK's largest reptile collections, and a variety of other indoor exhibits, like the Tropical House with its free-roaming sloths, bats, and birds. The stupendous gardens are equally as exotic, where visitors can find everything from cannas to wisteria. For more information, please visit cotswoldwildlifepark.co.uk

name: Cardiff
description: Settled since 6000BC, modern Cardiff began when William the Conqueror built a castle on the site of an old Roman fort in the 11th century. For much of its history, Cardiff was a relatively small settlement, and it wasn't until the 1830s, when John Crichton-Stuart began building the docks that Cardiff would develop into a city worthy of being called a capital (a title granted in 1955). Today, Cardiff is a refreshing mix of old-and new. Head to Cardiff Castle to see the Norman keep before stepping into the lavish Victorian neo-Gothic palace with its amazing apartments. The National Museum isn't just home to world class art and natural history exhibits - it's a staple in Doctor Who! In fact, many scenes from the Doctor and Torchwood were shot in Cardiff. The revitalized waterfront is watched over by the bright red Pierhead building, while the rest of the bayside is filled with modern shops and cool cafes.

name: Akureyri
description: While the area was originally settled by the Vikings in the 9th century, Akureyri wasn't recognized as a permanent settlement until 1778. While the town took decades to grow from its original population of 12, word of the excellent port and fertile lands eventually attracted more settlers. Today, it's the largest and most important settlement in northern Iceland. Perhaps the most iconic landmark is Jólagarðurinn, a bright red cabin covered with candy where it's always Christmas. For more traditional cabins, you can head a few kilometers outside of town to see the 19th century Laufás turf homes. Nature lovers can see nearly every plant native to Iceland (plus plenty of foreign species) at the Arctic Botanical Gardens or take a whale-watching trip. If you're hungry, Akureyri has a soft spot for junk food like their signature cheese burger with the french fries between the buns. Afterward, enjoy Iceland's best ice-cream at Brynjuís.

name: Mexiquillo Natural Park
description: Located in Nayarit, San Blas is a charming beach town known for its fishing, agriculture and titillating tourism. It was founded in the 16th century and used to protect against pirate attacks during the colonial era, making it a historically significant destination to step back in time. As you approach San Blas, you'll be greeted by a tropical jungle featuring plantations of coconut, pineapple, banana, mango, coffee, sugar, cane and papaya. Natural arches formed by the dense jungle welcome you to this friendly town, where the central garden is adorned with sailfish sculptures and opens up to artisanal stalls. Peruse sculptures of marlin fish and crocodiles, as well as clay handicrafts and vibrant paintings, before heading to the fort of San Blas for an impressive panoramic view of the town. San Blas boasts 30 kilometers of pristine, untouched beaches, including Los Cocos and the famous Matanchen Bay, lined with palm trees and hammocks to relax in. Fresh catches like snook, snapper and mackerel are caught right on the beaches and prepared to perfection.

name: Sayil
description: First settled around 800 AD, Sayil was a short-lived Mayan city that flourished for a short time before it was abandoned around 1000 AD. At its peak, it was home to an estimated 10,000 people, and based on the architecture, had close ties with Uxmal. The city's impressive monuments suggest it was ruled by its own royal dynasty whose wealth was likely based on agricultural holdings. Despite being partly-ruined the Grand Palace, is surprisingly lavish. Built on three tiers it has more rooms than any other Mayan palace, and features some excellent friezes on each floor of the facade. From here, paths lead to the remains of a residential areas and a temple pyramid known as the El Mirador. Not far from El Mirador is Sayil's crowd-pleasing stele - the well-endowed fertility god Yum Keep.

name: Saint Denis
description: Saint-Denis, the capital city of Réunion Island, is a vibrant and culturally rich destination nestled between lush green mountains and the azure waters of the Indian Ocean. Visitors to Saint-Denis can explore its historic streets lined with colonial-era buildings, elegant mansions, and colorful markets. The city's bustling markets, such as the iconic Saint-Denis Market, offer a feast for the senses with a vibrant array of fresh produce, spices, handicrafts, and local delicacies. Cultural enthusiasts will delight in Saint-Denis' numerous museums, galleries, and cultural centers, which showcase the island's diverse history, art, and traditions. The Léon Dierx Museum, housed in a beautiful colonial building, features an impressive collection of artworks by local and international artists. Nature lovers will find plenty to discover in the surrounding areas, with nearby attractions such as the picturesque Jardin de l'État, a lush botanical garden brimming with exotic flora, and the scenic La Montagne hiking trail offering panoramic views of the city and coastline.

name: Maribor
description: Tucked in between wine-growing hills and the Pohorje Mountains, Maribor is the second largest city in Slovenia and the capital of region Štajerska (Slovenian Styria). In its center grows the oldest vine in the world (over 450 years). Stop by the Old Vine House, a temple of wine tradition and culture, for viticulture exhibitions and excellent wines. Just north of the river Drava, wander the Old Town to enjoy the charming historic architecture and monuments like Castle Square (Grajski Trg), the Main Square (Glavni trg), the Maribor Cathedral (with observation tower), the Maribor Synagogue, as well as art galleries and theaters.
