name: Chapeco
description: Welcome to Chapecó, where vibrant culture and natural beauty converge to create an unforgettable experience. Step back in time at the Chapeco Cathedral, an architectural marvel with Franciscan design. The cathedral's two 40-meter towers form a cross, and a prayer grotto at the rear adds a touch of spirituality. Standing tall and proud since 1981, O Desbravador monument pays homage to Chapeco's early pioneers. Crafted by artist Paulo de Siqueira, the sculpture of a gaucho triumphantly holding an axe and laurel branch symbolizes the spirit of exploration. For nature enthusiasts, Eco Parque is a haven of tranquility. Immerse yourself in serene nature trails, surrounded by lush eucalyptus trees. Arena Condá, Chapecoense Football Association's home ground, stands as a testament to the city's resilience. This state-of-the-art stadium, with a capacity for 25,000 spectators, has become an emblematic symbol.

name: Pompeii
address.addr1: 80045 Pompeii, Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy
description: In 79 AD, waves of volcanic runoff and ash buried Pompeii, one of Ancient Rome's most active and splendid cities. The speed and magnitude of the event left the city frozen in time, preserved as it was. Excavations of the ancient metropolis have revealed some of the most significant insights into Roman art, customs, trades, and the brick-a-brack of everyday life. Walking the 2000-year-old streets reveals a wealth of architectural styles. Pompeii didn't segregate its neighborhoods based on income, so you'll find affordable apartments are next to lavish villas. The city's best-preserved home is the House of the Vetti, where you can admire richly frescoed entertainment rooms, and a central courtyard where a pool is surrounded by a formal garden. The city enjoyed an abundance of water, and used an aqueduct-fed reservoir to supply everything from public fountains to a street-cleaning system. Tickets are not included and often sell out, so we strongly recommend booking yours in advance at https://www.ticketone.it/en/artist/scavi-pompei/

name: Daytona Beach, FL
description: Perched on the edge of the Atlantic Coast, Daytona Beach is best known as America's Spring Break capital. Every year, countless merry-makers descend on this 23-mile stretch of white sand to revel in the sea and sun. But there are plenty of other cultural attraction to enjoy. Check out the Museum of Arts and Sciences to learn about Florida's Cuban heritage, the largest Coca-Cola collection in the United States, and see a vast Floridian fossil gallery. Daytona Beach is also the racing capital of America, with the headquarters of NASCAR, IMSA, and home to the Daytona International Speedway. Even if there isn't a race, you can still join a tour of the famous course. For a spot of golf, this city has got you covered, with two 18 hole courses and picturesque views. A beach city with more than its beach to offer, you will be sure to have lots of fun, no matter who you are!

name: Lorca
description: From Paleolithic times the town of Lorca has hosted a wide array of cultures and settlers, as can be seen from the numerous archaeological sites - from the Roman milestone, to the post-Reconquest Espolón and Alfonsina towers. The city was extensively damaged by a major earthquake in 2011, and later won the Europa Nostra Award for working to conserve its heritage with the restoration of six of the churches in its historic centre. Visitors to Lorca can also view the gate that granted passage through the wall that once surrounded the city in the 10th century, numerous churches and convents dating from different periods between the 15th and 18th centuries, and an array of stunning baroque palaces and stately homes. Whatever your interests, a visit to Lorca is sure to be one for the books.

name: Leon
description: Originally a Roman settlement, Leon changed hands several times during the Middle Ages. This ancient capital has been the center of civility for centuries, with 24 kings before its neighbor Castile even had laws. While most of its pre-Reconquest landmarks were destroyed by war, it still delivers a healthy dose of history. The massive Gothic Cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Often compared to Chartres, it might lack the size of its French counterpart, but its 1,200 square meters of stained glass create a stunning swirl of color unique in Spain. Nearby, the 11th century San Isidoro is built into the old city walls and set the mold for Northern Spain's Romanesque aesthetic. Part of the Roman Temple to Mercury it was built on is still preserved behind the basilica. Next to it, the Royal Pantheon and Treasury contain some exceptional 12th century frescoes illustrating New Testament, hunting and pastoral scenes.

name: Rouen
description: Situated on the Seine, it's no wonder Rouen developed into one of France's most important ports. A major Roman holding, when the Vikings settled here in the 10th century, Rouen became Normandy's capital. For centuries after, the city was closely tied to the English - William the Conqueror often held court her, and Richard the Lionheart's heart physically belongs to the city. After she was captured, Joan of Arc was tried in Rouen and burned alive in its central square. Today, the former Bishop's Palace now houses a museum in her honor. Next door is the towering Gothic cathedral, made famous by Monet, with its incomprehensibly detailed facade. Throughout the 'City of 100 Spires' cobbled streets visitors will find traditional half-timbered houses, quaint cafes, and many impressive museums, such as the Musee des Beaux-Arts, where visitors will find works from Monet to contemporary local artists.

name: Gori
description: Deriving its name from the word 'Hill', Gori is a city built upon undulating terrains, with a history dating back to the early Bronze Age. Most famous internationally as the birthplace of Joseph Stalin, complete with an infamous museum, Georgian locals associate Gori with its iconic citadel, the Gori Fortress, that is located on top of a hill. Despite suffering damage during the 2008 Russo-Georgian War, Gori is now a safe and intriguing destination. Visitors can explore the old town's charming streets and marvel at the Virgin Mary Cathedral. For a rewarding experience, climb up the Gori Fortress for a breathtaking panoramic view. The region is also renowned for its crisp, juicy apples – a must-try when in Gori.

name: Turin
description: Torino possess entertainment and pleasure for everyone. From the many trendy cafes to exquisite art galleries, Torino is full of passion. Its rich history is displayed in the diverse architecture that is scattered all over the city. The Winter Olympics of 2006 helped spark the city to revitalize its image and kickstart its love of art and architecture into the 21st century. Even a walk through the chic tree-lined streets toward the bridge of Emmanuel Vittorio is sure to wow the senses as you take in the atmosphere. The Egyptian Museum of Turin also has the largest collection of Egyptian art outside Egypt acquired by Napoleon. Take some time to grab a gelato whilst in Piazza Castello and take a tour of the National Museum of Cinema in Turin!

name: Kurume
description: Nestled in Fukuoka Prefecture, Kurume seamlessly blends vibrant urban living with the tranquil embrace of its surrounding nature. A gastronomic paradise, the city is the birthplace of tonkotsu (pork broth) ramen and is celebrated for other delicacies like yakitori (grilled meat on a stick), Chikugo udon, gyoza, and darumu and senpoko (organ meat delicacies). Its esteemed sake breweries rival Kobe's Nada and Kyoto's Fushimi, with the annual "Sakagura-Biraki" event in February or March drawing sake enthusiasts. Beyond its culinary delights, Kurume dazzles with its flourishing fruits and vibrant blooms. Explore Bairinji Gaien Park, Kurume Camellia Garden, and the Chikugo River's floral splendor. Don't miss out on sampling the local fruits - from succulent grapes and strawberries to the sweet persimmons, pears, and figs. The city's historical charm shines at landmarks like Suitengu Shrine and Daihonzan Naritasan Kurume Temple. For a memorable present, consider the Kurume Kasuri, an iconic indigo cotton craft.

name: Tikal
description: Tikal was one of the largest and most powerful of the ancient Mayan kingdoms during the 1st millennium AD, and some of its buildings date back to the 4th century BC. Like the rest of the Mayan empire's lowland cities, Tiak was completely abandoned at the end of the 10th century. Though the site was never fully lost to local knowledge, but official archaeological expeditions didn't begin until the second half of the 19th century. Today, the ruins are perhaps the most iconic in Guatemala. The steep pyramids towering above the lush jungle aren't just a beautiful sight for history lovers, Star Wars fans will get a kick out of the view from atop Temple IV - this is the same jungle panorama where we see the 'Falcon arrive at the rebel base on Yavin IV. It's recommended you buy a guide book or arrange for a guided tour to fully appreciate the site's history. Entrance tickets are 150 GTQ and are cash only. There are no ATMs on site, so be sure to take out money in advance. For more information, please visit www.tikalnationalpark.org

name: Elvas
description: Built as the first line of defense on the Spanish border, Elvas spent centuries defending Portugal's independence. The advanced defensive system successfully withstood sieges by the Spanish in 1659, 1711 and 1801, only falling to the French in 1808. Today, the city's mixture of Islamic and Medieval walls, ring of walls from the 17th century, plus forts built up through the 19th century are a UNESCO World Heritage site. Before even entering the town, visitors are greeted by the 17th century Aqueduct, with its 843 arches. Once you breach the perimeter walls, the city's cobbled streets offer a bounty of sights, including the Moorish medieval castle, scenic Square of Santa Clara, and squat cathedral.

name: Carthage
description: A Phoenician colony established in the 9th century B.C, Carthage developed into the capital of the Punic empire, and was the only threat to ancient Rome. After being destroyed and rebuilt following the Third Punic War, Roman Carthage served as the empire's premier city in North Africa, and remained in use until the invading Arabs razed in 692. This destruction means the ruins aren't in the best shape, but their historic importance is palpable. Along with the ruins of Roman baths, temples, and theatre, there are some fascinating reminders of the original Phoenician city, such as the Tophet - a religious sanctuary where people sacrificed their first-born children. A small niche is believed to be the burial place of princess Elissa, better known as Dido, the founder of Carthage. Be sure to stop by the National Archaeological Museum to gain a better understanding of the site and see the many artefacts unearthed here.

name: Wismar
description: Wismar passed into Sweden's possession following the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 and remained under its rule for centuries. During this time, the city became a center of artistic innovation and contributed to the development of Brick Gothic architecture in the Baltic region. Today, visitors can enjoy the outcome of this influential period, including sites such as the Archdeacon's House, the Church of St. Nicholas, and a partition's house known as the Old Swede. These structures can be found surrounding the city's huge marketplace along with the region's iconic gabled houses. Attention is easily drawn to the center of the market square, however, where the Wasserkunst, a wrought-iron fountain imported from Holland in 1602, stands as a focal point. Just a short walk from the square, movie enthusiasts can take advantage of a photo opportunity with the Wassertor, a brick gateway featured in the classic horror film Nosferatu.

name: Annecy
description: Founded by the Romans, Annecy was a court of the Counts of Geneva from the 10th century, and was made the regional capital under the Counts of Savoy in the 15th.Thanks to their patronage, this alpine town developed into the 'Venice of the Alps'. Running through the city is the River Thou, one of the shortest rivers in the Europe at 3.5 kilometers, most of which is in the canals running through the city. Visitors can enjoy a stroll through the well preserved old town, marveling at its beauty. Sitting in the middle of a canal, the Palais de l'Ile dates back to the 12th century. Once a court house and prison, inside visitors can learn about its architecture and heritage. Overlooking the town, the Château d'Annecy, once home to the Counts of Geneva, now houses a museum with exhibitions of Art and History of the area.

name: Rovinj
description: Rovinj is located on the northern Adriatic Sea and is coastal Istria's star attraction. The city is often characterized by its variety of stone and rocky beaches. The heart of Rovinj is its old town, which has protected since 1963. The old town is perched on an elevated peninsula surrounded by Venetian houses and the majestic Cathedral of St. Euphemia. The Baroque church sits on a hill and contains the remains of St. Euphemia, the patron saint of the city. A variety of of artistic styles such as Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, Romanesque, and Neoclassical elements can also be found spread across the old town. Many restaurants, cafes, and clubs have also taken root in Rovinj along with its growing popularity as a tourist destination.

name: Savona
description: Savona is an important seaport in the Liguria region in northwestern Italy. It has characteristic narrow streets, markets, cafes, promenades, piazzas, and a plethora of Art Nouveau architecture. One of Savona's most celebrated inhabitants, Christopher Columbus, farmed land in the area while recounting his journey. His residence, located just a few kilometers from the city, is available to visit. One of Savona's most acclaimed attractions is Cappella Sistina, a famous cathedral built in the 1480s by Pope Sixtus IV. Its ornate detailing and renovated late Baroque style attracts visitors from all around the world. Another notable town monument is the Priamar fortress, built in 1542. The fortress was used as a prison during the majority of the 19th century. Today, it houses Savona's Archaeological Museum. In addition to its diverse architecture, Savona prides itself on its history and tradition, hosting many festivals throughout the year.

description: The site consists of the Trakošćan Castle, the building next to the castle, the park and forest park (with a lake). The castle's architecture is made up of Gothic, Neo-gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque elements. It features historic collections on display including: the knight's room, the hunting room, the music salon and study room of Julijana Erdödy (the first Croatian woman to gain the title of academic painter), and other smaller collections as well. There is also a firearms collection on display, dating back to the 15th-19th century.

name: Yeongju
description: Yeongju is a city embraced by scenic landscapes and a nostalgic ambiance—the perfect destination to delve into Korean culture and history. Well-known series such as "Love Rain", "Moonlight Drawn by Clouds," and "Jeong Do-Jeon" have been filmed in Yeongju, due to its romantic and historic setting. Visit Sosu Seowon, the country's oldest Neo-Confucian academy, established during the Joseon Dynasty. The reconstructed Buseoksa Temple, dating back to 1376, also deserves a visit, holding the distinction of being the second oldest surviving wooden building in Korea. For food enthusiasts, Yeongju is a haven for delectable beef dishes, especially renowned for its hanwoo beef. Local restaurants cater to the palate of hanwoo lovers, offering a delightful culinary experience. Indulge in the local delicacies of tteokboki, jjeolmyeon, and bread rice cakes. With its rich historical legacy, breathtaking landscapes, and gastronomic delights, Yeongju beckons travelers to embark on a captivating journey of cultural immersion and scenic marvels.

name: Zihuatanejo
description: Until very recently, Zihuatanejo was not much more than a sleepy fishing village, home to locals going about their routine in relative peace and isolation. Everything changed in the 1970s, when the Mexican government chose to build a resort nearby, and the tourism industry blossomed overnight (also likely thanks to its feature at the end of the movie "The Shawshank Redemption"). Zihuatanejo is now the third most-visited place in the country. If you choose to stop here, bring your bathing suit! You'll have the choice to take a leisurely stroll down the Paseo del Pescador (Fisherman's Path) or go for a dip at one of the three main beaches: Playa La Madera, Playa La Ropa, or Playa Las Gatas.

name: Sarajevo
description: Sarajevo is the capital and largest city of Bosnia and Herzegovina. After facing near annihilation in the 1990's, the city today is considered one of the most interesting in all of Europe. Often referred to as "little Jerusalem", Sarajevo is famous for its rich religious diversity and fascinating history. On a single street, you'll find a Catholic church, an Orthodox Church, a synagogue, and many mosques coinciding with one another. The restored city center has an architectural mixture of Ottoman and Austro Hungarian buildings. There are many oriental shops, giving the center a village-like atmosphere. The Bosnian Historical Museum, the most important museum in Sarajevo, depicts the impact of nearly four years of war (from 1992-1995). Perhaps the most significant sight of the city's past is the Latin Bridge. In 1914, Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife crossed the bridge in an open car and were consequently shot and killed by Gavrilo Princip. This act sparked a war between Serbia and Austria-Hungary, and (due to the web of alliances in Europe) led to the First World War.

name: Lovcen
description: The views from Montengro's highest peak are breathtaking, and the Lookout restaurant is a great place to dine with a view. For those looking to go even higher, a 10 minute walk to the peak rewards visitors with the best views in the country and the chance to see the mausoleum of Njegoš. This resting spot was actually his last wish, to be peacefully placed at the top of the mountain in the chapel that he designed. After multiple exchanges in regime, territory, and power, his chapel was demolished, body removed, and later rebuilt and returned. Now, a mausoleum stands at the top of the mountain for Njegoš who was both a ruler and one of the most ambitious and esteemed poet-philosophers of the Serbian, Yugoslavian, Montenegrin histories.

name: Bridgetown
description: Bridgetown, referred to as The City or Town by locals, is the country's capital and its most populated city with over 100 thousand residents. The city's character manifests in its British colonial architecture juxtaposed with a laid-back West Indian ambiance. A must-visit in this historic city is the UNESCO-recognized Barbados Garrison, which was once the most significant military headquarters in the British colonies. Beach lovers will delight in Carlisle Bay, a natural harbor graced with picturesque stretches such as Pebbles Beach and some of the island's most luxurious resorts. The Carlisle Bay Marine Park is a popular sport for scuba divers eager to discover shipwreck relics scattered across the seabed. For architectural admirers, the Parliament Buildings, constructed from coral limestone in the 19th century, showcase neo-Gothic splendor. They house governmental offices, the National Gallery, and the Parliament Museum. And this is just a glimpse of what Bridgetown has in store!

name: Puerto Plata
description: A stone's throw from where Christopher Columbus established the first European settlement in the New World, Puerto Plata was designed by Columbus and his brother, and settled within a few years of Santo Domingo. As one of the oldest cities in the Americas, there's plenty of history to discover. The city itself was razed in 1863 and rebuilt, with its historic downtown exhibiting the largest collection of Victorian style houses in the Caribbean. Watching over it is the 16th century San Felipe Fortress, which along with great views, presents military artifacts from the 18th and 19th centuries. But if panoramic views are your thing, you'll want to make a bee-line to the cable car, which will whisk you to a mountain top 2,650 feet above Puerto Plata's lush landscape. Then, of course, there are the many nearby white sand beaches where you can bask in the Caribbean sun or take to the sea windsurfing or kiteboarding.

name: Porto-Vecchio
description: Porto-Vecchio may mean "Old Port", but the town on the French island of Corsica is very much in vogue. What began as an ancient Roman settlement was later preserved by the Genoese and has since become a teeming center of boutiques, cafes, bars and restaurants perched above a modern marina. Take a stroll through the Place de République, Porto-Vecchio's main square, where a lively restaurant and bar scene will lure you in with tasty French and Corsican cuisine. During the high season, the square transforms into a hub for lovers of nightlife. After sipping on a spritz in the afternoon, grab your towel and head to one of the many beaches along Porto-Vecchio's north and south. Take a dip in turquoise waters with a backdrop of luscious mountains at perhaps the most famous beach on the island, Palombaggia. For a historic detour, take in the ruins of the old citadel, the Bastion de France, or revel in the nineteenth century Roman style facade of the St Jean-Baptiste church.

name: Graz
description: Graz is often overlooked as most visitors head for Vienna, but makes an ideal destination for a stop by, particularly with the abundance of attractions on offer in the Old Town, where everything is located close together and easily manageable. Escape from reality by wandering the well-kept cobblestones of the pedestrianized streets packed with secret courtyards and alleyways that belong to another world. The food stalls tease the senses with delicious smells while the colorful restaurants and cafes all contribute to the atmosphere of an ancient quarter alive with modern-day people. Known for its friendliness and hospitality, there are few places in Europe that can rival the Old Town in full swing. Graz doesn't feel like a typical tourist destination as the Old Town is transformed by both visitors and locals to generate a pulsating, vibrant, and historical experience that few cities of this size can equal.

name: Gorlitz
description: Although Gorlitz has provided the setting for many famous movies over the years (Grand Hotel Budapest, Inglourious Basterds, and The Monuments Men to name just a few), it is the fabulous Peterskirche Gorlitz with its mighty twin towers that takes the accolades. The church majestically sits on a hill overlooking the River Neisse within the town walls and both the interior and exterior are an inspiration. This Gothic church, which could easily pass for a cathedral, is an object of extraordinary beauty. The Romanesque doorway adorned with spooky gargoyles hiding beneath the branches of the arch, the luminous fifteenth-century gothic interior, and the organ from 1703 with its mind-blowing sound effects, all add to an incredible visitor experience. Feel free to stop, take a seat in a pew and just look up at the incredible ceiling to add to the sense of wonderment that makes a visit to this church a truly memorable occasion.

name: Liverpool
description: Founded by King John in 1207, Liverpool remained a relatively unimportant port for until the 18th century. As nearby Chester's river silted over, Liverpool grew rapidly, made rich from trade with the West Indies. By the turn of the 20th century, Liverpool was 'the New York of Europe', having attracted immigrants from across the continent, and grown accordingly. In the 1960s, the city was swept up in the 'Mersey beat' sound, giving birth to The Beatles, and making the city a pilgrimage site for their fans. Today, visitors can see photos and memorabilia in McCartney's former home, or head to Albert Dock where the band's career is documented at the aptly named Beatles Story. While down at the UNESCO-listed waterfront, visitors are treated to 18th and 19th century landmarks, and a slew of fascinating museums, such as the Maritime Museum, International Slavery Museum, and Tate Gallery.

name: Khama Rhino Sanctuary
description: The Khama Rhino Sanctuary was established in 1992 to both save the disappearing rhinoceros and restore a once vibrant ecosystem. This community effort has successfully transformed the 8585 hectare reserve into a haven for wildlife. The black and white rhinos, which they've successfully bred to repopulate other parts of the country are the stars of the show, but the 30 other animal species, and over 230 types of bird that have resettled the park are equally amazing to see. For more information, please visit www.khamarhinosanctuary.org.bw

name: Hluboka nad Vltavou
description: Visitors never forget their first breathtaking vision of Hluboká. Similar in appearance to the world-famous Windsor Castle in England, the castle is surrounded by beautiful royal gardens and the English Park lined with ancient oak trees where visitors are free to stroll and soak up the grandeur of this Baroque masterpiece. The castle has a different feel than many others in the region — the darker paneled rooms with carved decorations are an outstanding feature while the guided tours show the castle as a living and functioning building with the furniture still in place in the dining rooms, library, and bedrooms. The incredibly detailed kitchen, complete with an ovens room and a baking room, provides visitors with a fascinating glimpse into the life of its royal and aristocratic residents. No visit to nearby České Budějovice is complete without stopping by at the wonder that is Hluboká.

description: Surrounded by heavily terraced hillside and breathtaking scenic views, Chivay is the gateway to the Colca Canyon in the Colca Valley. This market town is known for producing top-quality handmade products from Alpaca wool and embroidered accessories like bags and purses. The main square, Plaza de Armas de Chivay, is the heart of the town and boasts epic mountain views to be enjoyed from the gardens or one of the surrounding restaurants. If you're visiting in the evening don't miss the Planetarium & Observatory, open daily during April-December from 6:30-9:30 PM, for views of star constellations and the Milky Way. Enter the Colca Canyon with a stroll over the Inca Bridge, or for a more relaxing visit you can unwind with a drink in the La Calera Thermal hot springs, set in the slopes of the mountains.

name: Subotica
description: The vibrant colors and outstanding architecture of the city is due to its once importance and wealth during the Austro-Hungarian empire. Today this abundant city is filled with activities for all, from spas to the sights and sounds of various religious structures. Take a gander at the Cathedral of St. Teresa of Avila or the Synagogue. Have a sip of wine at the Winery Zvonko Bogdan before you enjoy the beauty of the government buildings: City Hall and the City Library. This multicultural city draws visitors in for its artwork and well preserved history. Near the border of Hungary, Subotica is a great place to rest on the way to your destination.

name: Akancho Akankoonsen
description: Nestled beside the serene Lake Akan, Akancho Akankoonsen beckons with its enchanting blend of onsen tranquility and the rich cultural tapestry of the Ainu, Hokkaido's indigenous people. For hiking enthusiasts, Akan boasts numerous trails, each revealing unique wonders, such as the intriguing "Bokke" spots, where mud volcanoes release steam from the earth. The Bokke Nature Walk, a 1.5 km loop path along the lakeside, allows for easy access to witness this natural spectacle. Immerse yourself in the heart of Ainu culture at Ainu Kotan, a vibrant Ainu community just a block away from the main street. Home to approximately 120 Ainu people, Ainu Kotan showcases traditional craft shops, museums, and theaters, providing an authentic glimpse into Ainu's distinctive heritage. Explore the mystical Lake Kaminoko Pond, known as "The Child of God" in Ainu legend, and venture to Kawayu Onsen, a hot spring town renowned for its acidic waters believed to promote metabolism. The Akan-Kohan Eco-Museum Center delves into the ecosystem and topography of the Lake Akan Onsen area, featuring the iconic Akanko Marimo and showcasing the diverse fauna inhabiting the region.

Originally under Austrian rule but left defenseless, Italy and Austria battled it out for many years until the Italians conquered. The Alps ignored the imaginary lines of France, Switzerland, Austria, and Italy. But each country's set of Alps brings their own charm. Cortina d'Ampezzo makes its home in the Dolomites Alps and leaves visitors basking in its 120 km of natural beauty and year-round snow. Abundant in snow of various intensities, the Dolomites Alps have been home to the Women's World Cup and to Olympians all over the world. Hop on the free ski bus and venture through the mountains!

name: Muara
description: Originally inhabited by a small community of Malay fishermen, Muara now serves as the country's primary deep-water port and holds strategic significance as part of the Maritime Silk Road. It connects the Chinese coast to Singapore, India, Kenya, and Europe, paying a vital role in maritime commerce. One of the main attractions in Muara is Muara Beach, a picturesque stretch along the South China Sea coastline. With its clear white sands and a length of approximately one mile, the beach offers a serene and inviting environment for visitors, featuring amenities such as picnic areas, a children's playground, and facilities for changing and restrooms. On weekends, food and drink stalls cater to the needs of beachgoers. Enjoy a game of volleyball or beach football at the Muara Beach Recreational Park nearby, and visit the war memorial located on the beach, honoring the amphibious assault carried out by the Australian Army during the Battle of Brunei in 1945.

name: Eltz Castle
description: Sat snugly on a 200-foot rock spur in the middle of a dense forest, Eltz was originally comprised of three castles as per the custom of the times and was shared by three families in order to ease costs. When two of the these merged in 1815, the castle structures were combined, with two parts now open to the public and the third still lived in today by the owning family. This breathtakingly picturesque castle is accessible to visitors through short tours that last less than an hour. The tour takes visitors around many of the castle rooms and provides a glimpse into the life of German nobility during medieval times. The superb Gothic chapel is a must see and many of the castle's 80 rooms are crammed with centuries-old furniture, art, and weaponry, much of it decorated with the Eltz family crest (as they've lived here for over 800 years, maybe a bit of hoarding can be forgiven). The castle is reachable from a nearby parking, located 10 minutes away on foot.

name: Consuegra
description: Settled since Roman times, Cosuegra's historic countryside has been famous since the 16th century. Today, Cosuegra's windmills are the best examples in the country, with 5 of them still retaining their complete mechanisms. One has been restored and In the distance, the 12th century castle beckons visitors to explore its halls, and get an alternative view of the giant windmills. The city center also offers its own attractions, such as the Renaissance town hall in the scenic Plaza de España square. If the windmills are still on your mind - look up!

name: Hyeres
description: Settled by the Greeks in the 4th century BC, Hyères is a resort-town with substance. In the 18th century, English aristocracy in search of warm weather flocked to the village, then came artists such as Leo Tolstoy, Rudyard Kipling, and DH Lawrence, and in 1892, Queen Victoria herself. However, as the village was built on a hilltop, it eventually fell out of favour as vacationers looked to Nice and St. Tropez instead. Fortunately, that means the bougainvillea-lined streets are free for visitors to explore without masses of other tourists. A resort-town in spirit, the 3 'remarkable gardens', panoramic vistas, and many cafes and restaurants serving fresh seafood just beg visitors to slow down and relax.

name: La Quemada Archeological Site
description: Located in the state of Zacatecas, this enthralling archaeological site, whose name translates to 'The Burning', sits right on the fringes of ancient civilizations. Over the years, researchers have endeavored to trace La Quemada's cultural roots, flirting with affiliations to a myriad of regional cultures including the Toltecs, Teotihuacán, Purépecha, and the Chichimeca. Yet, the site retains its enigma. Estimated to have flourished between 300 and 1200 A.D., the origins and extent of occupation at La Quemada remain shrouded in mystery. Spread across three distinct complexes, the site's attractions include an impressive array of masonry platforms. These architectural marvels served as the bedrock for grand structures that once soared into the sky. The site is a treasure trove of ancient ceremonial buildings, boasting over 50 patio platforms and more than a dozen pyramid structures, some crafted with impressive intricacy. Complement your journey through time with a visit to the site's museum. Open daily from 10 am to 5 pm, it serves as a comprehensive guide, detailing the parts of the site's history scientists have managed to uncover.

name: Portovenere
description: An ancient Roman fishing community, it's supposedly named after a temple to Venus that once stood on fortified promontory where the church of Peter the Apostle stands today. An interesting architectural amalgamation, the church's original structure dates back to the 5th century, while the sections with black and white banding is from the 13th. Architecture fans will also want to visit the Romanesque church of St. Lawrence, erected in 1098 on the site of ancient temple dedicated to Jupiter, and of course the 12th century walls surrounding the city. Literature lovers can stop by Byron's Grotto, where local legend says Lord Byron meditated and drew inspiration. Of course, as a seaside Italian village, relaxing with some fresh local food would suit every visitor's travel tastes.

name: Playa Carrizalillo
description: At only 300 meters long, Playa Carrizalillo proves that great things come in small packages. Descend the 160 steps to find golden sands, blue waters, colorful umbrellas, and straw-thatched huts framed by tropical trees. Lounge on the beach, take a drip in the water, or snorkel the colorful coral reef. For budding surfers, you can rent a board (around 150 MXN per hour) or sign up for a lesson with a local (around 500 MXN for 2 hours, including the board) to take advantage of the two beginner-friendly breaks.

name: Al Duwadimi
description: Known interchangeably as Ad Dawadimi or Al Duwadimi, Dawadmi presents a vibrant tapestry of community life. Among Dawadmi's prominent attractions, the King Abdulaziz palace stands as a beacon of history and architectural grandeur. Delve into the town's past, which traces back to its foundation in the latter half of the twelfth century Islamic era. From ancient farms and wells to rich historical effects, Dawadmi's roots run deep. Explore historical sites like the Plateau Protoplasm, Bakri plateaus, and the pools of Takhfah and pilgrimage route wells. Marvel at the inscriptions in the Thlan, Musikrh, Zaana, and Khanoukh mountains, as well as the sparkling Blonde settlements that stretch for over 20 kilometers southwest. As you traverse the breathtaking landscapes of Dawadmi, you'll encounter megalithic monuments, marble quarries, and granite clips that whisper tales of ages past.

name: Al Khobar
description: With its southern suburbs facing the picturesque Half Moon Bay, Al Khobar is renowned as a resort town, featuring pristine beaches and resorts. As the sun sets over the city, watch it come alive with a bustling atmosphere around some of the largest malls in the kingdom, including the Mall of Dhahran and the al-Rashid Mall. Explore the historic Suwaiket Street, where you can immerse yourself in the charm of the city's oldest markets. Al Khobar takes pride in its artistic and architectural scene, with notable landmarks such as Prince Ibn Jalawy Park and Eskan Park. The architectural wonder of the King Fahd Causeway, a 24 kilometer, 4-lane landbridge connecting Saudi Arabia with Bahrain, stands as a testament to engineering brilliance. See the Khobar Water Tower stand tall over the city and visit Corniche Al Khobar for a seafront promenade that offers a plethora of restaurants serving up diverse international flavors. Immerse yourself in a delightful fusion of natural beauty, cultural richness and culinary delights in Al Khobar.

name: Brussels
description: As the creators of world-famous characters, Tintin, Lucky Luke, and the Smurfs, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the people of Brussels love their comics! So much so, that the city has more comic strip artists per capita than anywhere else in the world! Taught in local art schools and commemorated in museums and galleries, this art form even covers entire streets! Head to Marolles, Sainte-Catherine, and other neighborhoods around the city and gaze up at the countless murals depicting cuttings from your favorite comic strips! Not only famous for comics, Brussels was the home of renowned artists such as René Magritte and Jacques-Louis David. Their works are exhibited around the city, the former celebrated with his own museum! Design is in full force in Brussels; the city is bestowed in architectural monoliths. Just step into Grand Place, considered to be the most beautiful square in the world, and admire the eclectic architecture including the square's crown jewel, the marvelous Brussels Town Hall. Don't forget to stop by Mannequin Pis. This humorous little statue is iconic in Belgian heritage, almost as much as their sweet treats and golden ales!

name: La Fortuna
description: Costa Rica is famous for its abundant wildlife, flourishing forests, and varied terrain. Nowhere can you see that more than around La Fortuna. The area was once dedicated solely to agriculture and the extraction of rubber. Now it is one of the country's most important destinations for tourism and conservation. For animal lovers, close encounters are not hard to come by. Just stay close to the trees in Sloth's Territory, keep your eyes on the sky at Proyecto Asis, or take to the Bogarin Trail to get face to face with Mother Nature's exotic species including sloths and toucans! Thrill seekers are treated to an array of adventure sports here in La Fortuna. Weaving chasms, cascading waterfalls, and the Arenal white-water rapids provide the perfect setting to go ziplining, canyoning, rafting, and more! After all that, it's time to wind down at some of the gems of the Alajuela Province. Hot springs and thermal pools are scattered along the Tabacón River. These natural spas are sure to bring a soothing and peaceful end to an action-packed day.

name: Otavalo
description: The vibrant town of Otavalo is famous for its daily indigenous markets where the locals sell handmade and mass-produced textiles, primarily made of wool. The Plaza de Ponchos is the heart of the action where you can expect to see vendors selling everything from homewares to clothing to fashion accessories in brilliant, vivid colours. For a larger event visit on a Saturday when the markets spill into neighbouring streets as merchants from nearby towns and villages set up shop. Top tip: don't be scared to barter, it is expected especially if purchasing multiple items! For a little history about the textile industry of Otavalo there is the Museo Viviente Otavalango, a textile factory where Otavalos were once forced to work under harsh conditions. If you prefer nature to shopping, the Peguche Waterfall just outside of town offers a picturesque escape to unwind in tranquil surroundings.

name: Lugo
description: Visitors can walk along the top of the 2,117-metre, uninterrupted circuit of 3rd century walls, complete with 71 towers and 10 gates, and a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000. The bridge over the Minho is also of Roman origin, though many repairs over the centuries have effaced its Roman character. Probably founded by Celtic inhabitants of the region and dedicated to Lugos, a pan-Celtic God of light, oaths, and art, Lugo was later conquered by the Romans in 13 BC before being found deserted in the middle of the 8th century. The area is now home to almost 100,000 inhabitants and features a rich history, from it's 12-century cathedral, 18th-century Baroque-style City Hall, and the remains of a Roman bath at the edge of the Minho river.

name: Arbeia Roman Fort
address.addr1: Baring St, South Shields NE33 2BB, UK
description: Founded around 120 AD, the Roman Fort at Arbea guarded the main sea route to Hadrian's Wall, eventually becoming the main maritime supply fort for the wall, and was the site on the only permanent stone-built granaries in Britain. The fort was abandoned when the Romans left Britain in the 5th century, but not without the fort serving as the Roman Emperor's HQ for the Scottish invasion, a major base for the Roman army, having hosted troops from around the empire, and it's said to be the birthplace of the Northumbrian King Oswin. The fort has been brought back to life through a faithful reconstruction, and filled with cultural events. Visitors can learn about the ancient Romans and their rule over Britain, as well as see gladiator battles, falconry displays, reenactments, storytelling. For more information, please visit arbeiaromanfort.org.uk

name: Cascada el Aguacero
description: The Cascada el Aguacero looks like something out of a fairy tale - a bit of Rivendell in Mexico. Here, the La Venta river drops 75 meters over the edge of a forested river canyon, streaming through the lush jungle. The water bounces off moss-covered outcrops on the way down, enveloping the area in a refreshing mist - there's even a small cave in the cliff face where you can see the falls from a completely different perspective. To experience this amazing sight you have to be willing to work for it - it's about 700 steps to reach the base of the river canyon.

name: Ivano-Frankivsk
description: Ivano-Frankivsk was founded in 1662 by Andrzej Potocki as a castle to defend against the Crimean Tatars. The city grew in importance over the centuries, and flourished as a trade and crafts center. The West Ukrainian People's Republic, which only existed from 1918 to 1919 even used Ivano-Frankivsk as its capital. The heart of the city is its old Market Square, surrounded by charming historic houses. However, Ivano-Frankivsk is unique in that it has the only modernist Town Hall in Ukraine, which now houses the tourist information center (the first in the country), and a small museum. Nearby, visitors will find the Late Baroque Orthodox Cathedral - a former Armenian Church with an opulently ornamented interior. The Church of Virgin Mary is the oldest building in the city, and was originally the burial vault for the Potocki family. Today it houses an art museum exhibiting everything from Galician icons to works from Italian painters.

name: Sankt Gilgen
description: Sankt Gilgen deserves to be on every nature lover and film buff's to-do list. This is where the iconic opening scenes to 'The Sound of Music' were filmed — and who can forget those? The connection with music doesn't stop there, though. The village is also the birthplace of Mozart's mother, his grandfather and is where his sister lived following her marriage. Even though he never actually stayed there, the history of picturesque Sankt Gilgen is inextricably connected to Mozart, Austria's favorite son. The shimmering azure waters of Lake Wolfgangsee provide an ideal location to feel the cool, clean air and to spend a few moments watching the paragliders as they swirl around the mountain peaks before heading off into the clouds. Whether taking the short gondola ride to the mountain top or simply meandering a mountain trail from the village, the views and ambience of Sankt Gilgen present every visitor with an unforgettable mountain paradise.

name: Ajaccio
description: Along with palm trees and brightly colored architecture, the open-vista boulevards of Ajaccio are filled with the undeniable presence of a revered historical figure. Napoleon was born in Ajaccio in 1769 and the port city celebrates its favorite son at every opportunity. Statues of the leader in military poses tower over squares and palaces, and the museum Maison Bonaparte, houses in his ancestral home, is a veritable goldmine for history lovers. For the art appreciators, the Fesch Palace (built by Napoleon's maternal uncle) hosts one of France's largest collections, right after the Louvre Museum in Paris. Contemplate masterpieces by Poussin, Botticelli, and Titian before enjoying drinks and fresh seafood by the harbor. Stroll through the vibrant market on Foch Square between April and October for local delicatessen, regional cheeses, wines and jams, or follow the Chemin des Crêtes path for spectacular views across the Mediterranean. And, of course, don't leave without having a splash in one of the many astonishing beaches surrounding Ajaccio.

name: Castelsardo
description: While the area's been settled since prehistoric times, Castelsardo proper can trace its origin to a medieval castle built by the Doria family of Genoa. The picturesque town grew around this medieval nucleus, its colorful houses spilling down the hillside to the vibrant waters of the Mediterranean. Starting at the Piazza del Novecentenario, work your way up the narrow streets to the Castello dei Doria. It's an uphill climb, but well worth it for the spectacular views. Plus, you get to explore the 13th century fortifications. Inside the walls, you'll find both the 14th century church of St. Mary and 17th century Castelsardo Cathedral. And down in the cathedral crypt you'll find a small museum showcasing its most precious treasures including frescoes Andrea Lusso. After taking in the view and history, you can cool off at the beach, or refuel with some of Castelsardo's signature cuisine like lobster alla castellanese (a sauce made with lobster eggs).

name: Monte Alban Archaeological Site
description: Founded around 500 BC, the Monte Alban Archaeological Site quickly grew into one of the largest cities in Mesoamerica, and was the first capital of the Zapotec empire. However, after being inhabited for 1500 years, this once thriving metropolis quickly lost influence and was ultimately abandoned after the ruling class decentralized their power into dozens of smaller city states. Monte Alban's vast central plaza is lined with a ball game court, and tremendous temples, tombs, and bas-reliefs, offering a survey of Oaxaca's pre-Classic and Classic periods. At the colossal Building H, a staircase leads to a temple and two tombs, and is where the famous jade mask of the Bat God was found. Pay attention to the carved tombstones in the Los Danzantes building, which are strikingly similar to Olmec art. Before leaving, make sure to explore Tomb 7, which was the site of the richest archeological hoard ever discovered in Mexico (the artifacts are on display at the Museum of Oaxacan Cultures in the Santo Domingo cultural center).

name: Chiang Mai
description: Founded in 1296, Chiang Mai was the capital of the Lanna Kingdom until the 18th century, and remained a princely seat until 1939. Today, it's the second largest city in Thailand, with the feel of a modern metropolis, but also firmly rooted in the past. The Old City is still contained within the original walled and moated boundaries, and home to over 30 Buddhist temples, some of which are as old as the city itself - Wat Chiang Man was where King Mengrai lived while the city was still being constructed. However, the city's most famous landmark isn't even in the city: Doi Suthep, is a mountain about 12 km away that's crowned by the 13th century Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, offering travellers stupendous views and beautiful architecture. The other key Chiang Mai experience is its food, particularly khao soi.

name: Florence
description: Florence, the capital of the region of Tuscany, is located on the banks of the Arno River. The city was founded by the Romans in the 1st Century B.C. It boasts sculptures, churches, palaces and many other important monuments. Florence's historic center has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982. The Duomo, Florence's cathedral, is one of the most striking monuments in the city center. Climb the Duomo or its bell tower for a spectacular view of the city. The walkable city has over 80 museums and medieval back alleys and shopping streets to explore. Discover your inner artist while strolling the medieval streets and enjoying Italy's best gelato!

name: Sousse
description: Founded as a trading post in the 11th century BC, Sousse's strategic position involved it in a slew of ancient wars, including Caesar's Civil War, when Julius famously tripped getting off a boat, grabbed a handful of dirt, and exclaimed "I have you now, Africa!" Sousse's UNESCO-listed medina, surrounded by 9th century walls, has been unchanged for centuries, and its colorful streets offer visitors a glimpse at traditional Tuisian life. The 9th century Great Mosque is a fort-like structure, modelled after the Roman-infulence mosque in Kairouan. Towering above the old town, the 9th century ribat is a rare surviving example of a medieval Aghlabid fortification. For those looking for the best view in town, the tower of the 9th century kasbah is not only 50 meters taller than the ribat, but is also one of the oldest towers in North Africa. For those wanting a closer look at the city's rich history, the exceptional archaeological museum houses the country's second largest collection of antiquities.

name: Kumasi
description: Kumasi, Ghana's beating heart, pulsates with rich Ashanti heritage and infectious energy. Nicknamed the "Garden City," wander through vibrant streets adorned with blooming jacarandas and bougainvillea. Immerse yourself in the legendary Kejetia Market, a sprawling maze of stalls bursting with colorful textiles, handcrafted pottery, and the aroma of exotic spices. Delve into the Ashanti Kingdom's legacy at the Manhyia Palace Museum, where opulent artifacts whisper tales of warriors and kings. Witness the awe-inspiring Golden Stool, a symbol of Ashanti unity, and be captivated by the intricate goldwork that adorns it. Kumasi isn't just a history buff's paradise. Unwind in the verdant haven of Rattray Park, a haven of lush greenery amidst the urban buzz. Mingle with locals over steaming cups of Ghanaian coffee, or catch a pulsating live drumming performance that will set your soul on fire.

name: Birgu
description: With a rich history steeped in maritime, mercantile and military activities, Birgu has evolved into a prominent showcase of Maltese tradition, exuding medieval nostalgia through its narrow winding streets and converted townhouses. History lies in its fortified walls, with notable attractions such as the Inquisitor's Palace, once the seat of the Inquisition in Malta from 1571 to 1798. Today, it has been transformed into a museum showcasing Malta's national museum of ethnography collection, featuring the palace's chapel, library, dungeons, and courtyard. Visit the Notre Dame Gate, built in 1675 and standing as a historical gateway in Birgu, offering a magnificent view of the island from its terrace and roof. Along with all its historical grandeur, the city has witnessed a modern revival with the establishment of wine bats, elegant restaurants and a bustling waterfront, breathing new life into this small city.

name: Spokane, WA
description: Spokane is a great place to orient yourself into the rugged environment, sustainable living and the last metropolitan point before entering the great wilds of Washington State. With some of the most impressive architecture in the Western United States, you can walk through the city's diverse neighborhoods to get a sense of the changing eras. A leader among western cities for parks, Spokane has a whopping 87 parks, with one of the most beautiful being the Riverfront Park (built during the World Expo 1974) and the Manito Park and Botanical Gardens. To get a great fill of a quaint but buzzing city, history, and nature, Spokane is your place.

name: Oruro
description: The vibrant city of Oruro is famed for its annual carnival, Carnaval de Oruro, which takes place in February or March and sees the indigenous locals dance for the devil to appease him for stealing his precious metals. Filled with lavish costumes, traditional dancing and outlandish parades, everything about the carnival is colourful and it's not to be missed! Oruro is a mining city, primarily for tin, copper and silver. You can learn more about the industry at the Museo Sacro, Folklórico, Arqueológico y Minero where you'll descend to the underground for a history of the trade brought to you by actual miners. The museum is attached to the Santuario de Virgen de Socavón, the church for worship of the 'Virgin of the Mineshaft'', patron saint of the miners. Her monument stands some 45 metres high in another part of town, offering striking views of the city and its surroundings.

name: Jena
description: Jena is one of those places dripping in history and it shows. Contemporary twenty-first century buildings stand next to medieval churches while parks are just a short walk away and mountains surround the cityscape. Whatever your taste, Jena has something for everyone. The city is condensed and its large number of parks quickly becomes apparent while even walks to experience the nature of the region remain close by. And there are plenty of medieval buildings if that's your thing. Regardless of how is from the unmistakable futuristic looking Jen-Tower that soars into the sky. Once at the top, the viewing platform offers sublime panoramic views of the entire city, the hills and the valley beyond, which make the trip in the elevator to the top and the small entrance fee a sure thing.

name: Hell-Fire Caves
address.addr1: Church Ln, West Wycombe, High Wycombe HP14 3AH, UK
description: The Hellfire Caves were excavated in the mid-17th century as part of Sir Francis Dashwood's ambitious project to alleviate local poverty by mining chalk to construct a nearby road. Dashwood then had the mines transformed into a network of halls and chambers to use as a meeting place for his infamous Hellfire Club - an exclusive club where members of high society could partake in all manor of immoral acts. The chambers include a banquet hall, and Franklin's Cave (named for Dashwood's friend, and Hellfire guest, Benjamin Franklin). The tunnel ends with the 'Inner Temple', reached by crossing a stream known as the River Styx, where the club held their lecherous meetings. Today a series tableaus illuminate some of the supposed-goings on, but the truth is lost in the annals of history. For more information, please visit hellfirecaves.co.uk. Photo by ian freeman under CC BY-SA 3.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hellfire_Caves_-_panoramio.jpg)

name: Opatija
description: Opatija is located in western Croatia. It lies at the center of the Riviera with an impressive 12 km long coastal promenade. Opatija was the most fashionable resort during the Austro-Hungarian empire. Today, the laidback town is home to various grand spa hotels. It also has many green areas, including well-kept parks and beaches to relax in and enjoy. A multitude of cultural and entertainment events are held in town throughout the year. Sveti Jakov, a Benedictine church complex situated in the town center, is one Opatija's most notable sights. Also worth exploring is The Croatian Museum of Tourism. The permanent exhibition houses relics from the late 19th and 20th centuries. Opatija's temperate climate, grand spa hotels, and various historical monuments continue to make the town a top destination spot today.

name: Aachen
description: Built around 800, the cathedral is of global importance in terms of the history of its art and design, and offers an impressive example of church architecture. The cathedral contains the final resting place of Charlemagne and is where German emperors were crowned for over 600 years. The amazing octagonal domed cathedral resembles a crossroads of the times and reflects the different cultures and the evolution of European religion, politics and history. There are many different aspects of the cathedral that are not often seen in any other cathedral built after the thirteenth-century. The relics that are still contained in the cathedral today led to it becoming a major European pilgrimage site while over 30 German kings were crowned there prior to 1531. Few cathedrals in the world are more solemn and majestic than Aachen's and even fewer make such a deep impression on those who experience this imperial gem.

name: Santa Ana
description: Santa Ana was founded by the Mayans, but like the rest of the region, was conquered by the Spanish in the 16th century. A relatively small settlement that didn't gain the status of 'town' until 1812, the early 20th century saw Santa Ana become the most prosperous city in the country thanks to its coffee industry. Today, the city is considered one of the most beautiful in Latin America thanks to the opulent monuments erected with this wealth. The main attractions are the intricate Neo-Gothic cathedral and the National Theatre - a Neo-Baroque beauty filled with murals, stucco, and gilt. Santa Ana's historic center is home to nearly 400 buildings, making the area worth exploring outside of these main monuments. If you need a break from sightseeing, duck into one of the city's many cafes, comedores, or pupuserias for some local fare, and just watch the world go by.

name: Oradour-sur-Glane
description: On June 10th 1944, shortly after the Allied landings in Normandy, German troops rounded up the entire population of this quiet village. The men were brought to cattle sheds and mowed down with machine guns, while the women and children were locked in the church and burned alive. The SS then set fire to the rest of the town in an apparent attempt to hide their crime, and despite a trial at Bordeaux, were never brought to justice. After the war, Charles De Gaulle had the burnt out remains preserved to remind future generations of the atrocities of war. Above the entrance to the village, a sign reads "Souviens-Toi" — "Remember." In order to spread the site's stirring message to as many as possible, it's free to enter and free to roam.

name: Hegra
description: Designated as Saudi Arabia's inaugural World Heritage property, the Hegra Archaeological Site is an awe-inspiring tableau of the Nabataean civilization. Boasting an exceptional collection of well-preserved monumental tombs adorned with intricate facades dating from the 1st century BC to the 1st century AD, the site provides a vivid glimpse into the architectural and artistic prowess of the Nabataeans. Among the 111 grand tombs, 94 are embellished, and alongside these, you will find 50 pre-Nabataean inscriptions and captivating cave drawings. Al-Hijr is a living testament to the ingenuity of Nabataean culture and stands as an outstanding example of their hydraulic mastery, with an array of water wells and channels. The site immerses you in the narrative of the ancient inhabitants of AlUla, revealing their customs and way of life. While wandering among these impressive structures, you'll come across tombs dedicated to various figures, from healers to military leaders, each marked by distinct stylized carvings and symbols.

name: Bern
description: Founded by the Duke of Zähringer in 1191, Bern was made a free imperial city by the Holy Roman Emperor, Frederick II following the duke's death. While the city flourished, a major blaze in 1405 destroyed many of the original wooden buildings. These were gradually replaced by half-timbered houses the characteristic sandstone buildings that still grace the Old Town today. Within the UNESCO Heritage Site, visitors can wander the 6 kilometers of arcades, shopping, or just soaking in the local architecture. Among the many fountains and historic towers is unique, visitors can find an elevated Rose Garden, which sits above the Bear Park, home to the city's heraldic beast. Bern's 15th-century Gothic cathedral is the tallest in Switzerland and for those undeterred by heights, a viewing platform in its 101-meter tower offers the best views of the old town.

name: Uxmal
description: According to Maya chronicles, Uxmal was founded around 500 AD by Hun Uitzil Chac Tutul Xiu, and ruled over by his descendants for generations. For a time, Uxmal was the most powerful city in western Yucatán, and dominated the Northern Maya area alongside its ally, Chichen Itza. Around the 12th century, the arrival of Toltec invaders and fall of Chichen Itza caused the city to fall into decline, though colonial records show it remained inhabited into the 16th century. Unlike many Mayan cities, Uxmal was not laid out geometrically - rather, its buildings are positioned according to astronomical phenomena. The buildings follow the Puuc architectural style, with smooth, curved stone bases and highly decorated upper levels, exemplified by the 35-meter-tall pyramid, topped with an ornately decorated temple. At the Governor's Palace, a 320 foot long mosaic showcases the culture's intricate artwork through a series of 103 stone masks of the rain god Chac.

name: Concepcion
description: Founded in 1773, the little town of Concepcion hasn't changed much over the centuries. It's dirt streets are still lined with Colonial-era buildings, and you'll still see horse-drawn carts rolling behind scooters often overladen with multiple riders. At the heart of the main street is a towering statue of Maria Auxiliadora, which has a small viewing platform at its base. From here you walk towards the river and stop by the Museo Municipal del Cuartel de la Villa Real. Housed in a 19th century barracks, this small museum exhibits Triple Alliance War relics as well as indigenous artefacts. While you're walking around town, you'll probably notice the locals' exceptionally laid-back and sociable nature, so if you want a real taste of Concepcion life, stop by a cafe, order a terere (an iced mate drink), and relax.

name: Hopa
description: Nestled in Artvin Province of Northeast Turkey, Hopa is a captivating coastal town. It's located on the eastern edge of the Turkish Black Sea, close to the Georgian border. With its azure sea, lush natural landscapes, and historic architecture, Hopa effortlessly wins over visitors. This town offers a unique, intimate exploration of Turkey, away from the typical tourist trails. Key attractions include the verdant Çamburnu Nature Park, the serene Hopa Port for leisurely coastal walks, and a myriad of charming old houses scattered throughout the city. Hopa's culinary scene is a delightful fusion of Black Sea and Georgian cuisine, with a special emphasis on fresh seafood - certainly not to be missed. The bustling Hopa Bazaar is the perfect place to hunt for souvenirs or local delicacies. To top it all, Hopa hosts an array of cultural festivals during the summer.

name: Chikin Ha
description: Surrounded by lush jungle, Chikin Ha is a small ecological park that preserves the region's natural and cultural history through its three sacred cenotes. The eponymous Cenote Chikin Ha is a favourite among cave divers as a fold in the earth opens up into a beautiful underwater cave system. Even if you're not here diving, it's still a beautiful place to swim, or just dip your toes for a natural fish foot spa experience. In vivid contrast to the cool cave waters, Cenote Xtabay is almost entirely open to the sun. These clear, blue waters are teeming with life, with lily pads gracing its surface and turtles and fish grazing its bottom. Finally, there's Taak-Bil-Ha, where a life-filled island is surrounded by sacred waters. Chikin Ha also offers a guided tour where you can learn more about Mayan culture and even experience a traditional ritual inside one of the caves!

name: Christchurch
description: A newly bustling city, Christchurch is exploding with dining, art, nightlife, and activities. There's something for everyone, whether you prefer shopping, outdoor adventure, or consider yourself a foodie, Christchurch will not disappoint. For starters, you can venture around the lush parks, either by bike or by foot, and marvel at the stunning scenery. Then wander to the city where the street art will catch your eye at every corner. The Salt District is the place to be for wining and dining, as it is dominated with restaurants and bars with comfort food, as well as unique tastes sure to excite the palate. Then stroll the downtown area and find cute little boutiques as well as interesting galleries that make you shop til you drop!

name: Parndorf Outlet
description: Open daily except for Sundays, Parndorf delivers. Dedicate some time to explore some of the world's most iconic brands, such as Gucci, Prada, and Armani. Parndorf offers more than just shopping; they have great food selections, golf weekends, live music, and more. There are also quite a few options for the kids and family too! There are activities and professional caretakers to mind your children while you take some 'me' time browsing through the latest selection of Karl Lagerfeld and Diesel. Just 30 minutes from Vienna and Bratislava, leave some space in your luggage to take home a few discounted gems! Please note that the outlet center is closed on Sundays.

name: Killarney
description: In the Middle Ages, Killarney was renowned for its monastery on Innisfallen Island. Founded by St. Finian the Leper in the 7th century, the Irish High King Brian Boru was educated here, and its monks spent 300 years writing the Annals of Innisfallen, a chronicle of Ireland's early history. Killarney's natural surroundings made it a popular tourist destination the mid 18th century, and even today, walking through the beautiful Killarney National Park remains the most popular activity in town. The 15th century Ross Castle lake is a pleasant place to stroll, and one of the popular walking trails here brings you past prehistoric copper mines. Ross Castle is also the launching point for boat tours of the lake, including trips to the famed Innisfallen Island during the summer. In the town center, you can appreciate the elegance of Killarney House and Gardens, or the fine Gothic Revival architecture on the 19th century St. Mary's Cathedral.

name: Genoa
description: Dating back to at least the ancient Etruscan civilization Genoa has been a port city since its conception. A medieval maritime powerhouse, the city remains Italy's largest and busiest port, but behind that layer of industry is one of Italy's most grandiose cities. The birthplace of Christopher Columbus, Genoa's Old Town is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with Renaissance and Baroque palaces lining its 16th and 17th century 'new streets'. Of the 100 or so palaces in the city, many are open to visitors with the Palazzo Reale taking the cake for decadence. Still containing many of its original furnishings and art, this 17th century looker even has its own version of the Hall of Mirrors. Along with having one of the largest historic centers in Europe, Genoa boasts a slew of world-class museums, and the largest aquarium on the Mediterranean. And, of course, you'd be remiss not to indulge in the local cuisine, which is hands down some of the best in the country.

name: Pietermaritzburg
description: Pietermaritzburg was founded by the Voortrekkers in 1837, and has since grown into the provincial capital. Despite its growth, Pietermaritzburg has preserved its past, with plenty of Victorian and Edwardian buildings lining the pedestrian lanes. Most notable is the city's iconic red-brick city hall. Perhaps an even more grand reminder of the city's Victorian past is the KwaZulu-Natal National Botanical Garden, which is home to many species brought from the Northern Hemisphere by European colonists. The dramatic avenue of London Plane Trees is a favourite among photographers. Animal lovers will want to visit Butterflies for Africa, where you can enjoy the company of butterflies, birds, monkeys, and other creatures.

name: Playa del Carmen
description: Placed between tourism Goliath, Cancun, and renowned retreat, Tulum, 'Playa' visitors are afforded a plethora of activities, attractions, and excursions. Remarkable theme park, Xcaret, and modern-day paradise, Cozumel, are just a stone's throw away. The town is bookended by the revered Caribbean Sea and the lush rainforests of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, both of which spoil the area with a bounty of cenotes, coral reefs, and wildlife to discover. On arrival, head to the center of town and stroll down Avenida Quinta (5th Avenue). This pedestrian-only street is a hotspot for restaurants, bars and boutiques. Here, you'll get a real taste of Mexico, with authentic food tours and traditional cooking classes, and at night, this corridor comes alive as bars and clubs open out to the street for una gran fiesta! In need of tranquility, away from the crowds? Look no further than Punta Esmeralda. Make your way along the beach and you'll find this serene alcove on the shore, fringed with palm trees and accompanied by a small natural pool called 'Cenotito'. From the seafront, snorkels, jet skis, and diving tours are all available at your leisure. A trip of a lifetime, in Playa del Carmen!

name: Dilijan
description: Nestled within the scenic Dilijan National Park, Dilijan is a captivating destination that offers a harmonious blend of natural beauty, rich cultural heritage, and rejuvenating experiences. Known as the Armenian Switzerland or Little Switzerland, the town is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts. Trails wind through the forested mountains and reveal breathtaking vistas, serene alpine lakes, and centuries-old monasteries. Take a rowing boat out onto Parz Lake or have a relaxing picnic by the lakeside. Visit Old Dilijan, the town's historic district, where a well-preserved enclave showcases traditional Armenian architecture, craftsman's workshops, a gallery, and a museum. Strolling along the cobblestoned Sharambeyan Street is like stepping back in time, with nooks and crannies and local artisanal stores to explore. Dilijan beckons you with its enchanting landscapes, healing mineral springs, and cultural treasures, promising an unforgettable experience.

name: Dolores Hidalgo
description: Dolores was little more than a provincial town before Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla stamped his mark on the settlement. His legacy to the town was the setting up of a ceramics industry, which remarkably still exists and supports half the population over 200 years later. But his legacy to the nation is far more remarkable as it was here in 1810, from his church, that he issued a call to arms to overthrow "bad government" in the name of King Charles IV, who's crown had been usurped by Napoleon Bonaparte. A decade of rebellion culminated in the birth of an independent Mexico. That momentous history can be explored today by visiting the Hidalgo House Museum, his former mansion, the Museum of Independence, Father Miguel's church (Our Lady of Sorrows) fronted by the beautiful town square. This is one of Mexico's most important "Magical Towns" and should not be missed.

name: St. Catherine's Monastery
description: St. Catherine's Monastery dates back to around 330AD when the Byzantine empress Helena had a small chapel and a fortified refuge built beside what was believed to be THE burning bush. In the 6th century, Emperor Justinian I ordered a monastery built, which now attracts pilgrims and history lovers from around the world. In the 6th-century Church of the Transfiguration, you'll find an astounding array of ornamentation, from a gilded 17th-century iconostasis to the amazing 6th-century mosaic of the Transfiguration. Outside, you can see the descendent of the original burning bush, and maybe bestow marital happiness on yourself by drinking from the Well of Moses. For many, the highlight is the Monastery Museum, which exhibits Byzantine-era icons, precious chalices and crosses, ancient manuscripts, and it's prized possession: the Codex Sinaiticus, the world's oldest near-complete bible. The monastery's library, the oldest and second largest in the world, contains an incredible collection of illuminated bibles and manuscripts, including a hand-written copy of the New Testament. Please note: as an active monastery, conservative dress is required (no shorts, and women must cover their shoulders). It's possible to climb mount Sinai, but appropriate footwear is required, and you will want to add additional time to your stop.

name: El Romerillo
description: Located about halfway between San Cristobal de las Casas, and the major town of Tenejapa, the tiny Mayan settlement of El Romerillo doesn't even show up on the map. Its inhabitants are entirely indigenous, and entirely without internet. Being an indigenous settlement, the Romerillo is in typical Chiapas Maya style, which means giant wooden crosses colored in shades of blue with pine branches hanging from them. Below these, the graves are recognized by their humble mounds and more modest-sized wooden crosses, among which livestock can often be seen grazing.

name: Chetumal
description: While the Maya had a city known as Chetumal, this pre-Columbian capital was likely today's Santa Rita in Belize. Mexico's modern Chetumal wasn't established until 1898 as a port town, and was populated by settlers from Belize invited by the town's founder. Today, the laid-back capital of Quintana Roo is a popular home base for travellers looking to explore the nearby Mayan ruins, or continue on to Belize. But hidden among the busy port and thatch-roofed beach bars is the state's largest and most comprehensive Mayan museum. For those who'd rather spend their time outdoors, the Boulevard de Bahía is the longest promenade in the Yucatán Peninsula, and offers great views of the Bay of Chetumal.

name: Minoan Palace of Phaistos
description: The Minoan Palace of Phaistos is the second most important Cretan archeological site after Knossos and a model example of the Minoan civilization. Phaistos, a city-state that existed from 6000 BC to the 1st century BC, was the religious and spiritual center of southern Crete. Most of the buildings located on the site today belong to the Neopalatial period (1700 - 1450 BC), in part because the area was destroyed by earthquakes and rebuilt several times. Some of the site's most important structures are the monumental entrance to the palace, the Treater Court, and the Tripartite Shrine. Fun fact: one of the items uncovered during excavations in the site's northern part was the Faistos Disc, an important artifact from the Minoan Bronze Age (now on display in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum). The disc is famous for the symbols it is covered with, which have baffled archaeologists for decades. The site also includes a bookshop with thematic literature and a canteen. The opening hours depend on the season, and entrance fees range from 4 to 8 EUR. A note for visitors with limited mobility: touring the site might be challenging due to stairs and hilly geography.

name: Fjadrargljufur Canyon
description: The 2 kilometer-long Fjadrargljufur Canyon formed at the end of the last Ice Age when waters from a retreating glacier etched their way into the soft sedimentary rock. Today, a gentle stream lies at the bottom of the 100-meter-deep canyon, its rocky walls now covered in green moss. Despite its raw beauty, the canyon remained relatively unknown until it appeared in Justin Beiber's "I'll Show You" music video, and Jon Snow's first dragon flight in Game of Thrones. After skyrocketing in popularity, the Environment Agency of Iceland stepped in to ensure this delicate environment isn't damaged (Beiber fever has officially been blamed). Now visitors follow a trail leading along the side of the canyon where you're treated to increasingly beautiful views, culminating in a viewing platform for a stunning vista over the whole area.

name: Ouro Preto
description: Founded in the late 17th century, Ouro Preto was the center of the Brazilian Gold Rush and one of the largest cities in the Americas. Today, Ouro Preto is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its wealth of Baroque architecture. Start your visit at the Praça Tiradentes, the airy square in the heart of the old town, where you'll find the former municipal palace (now the Museu da Inconfidência) and the Rococo Igreja da Nossa Senhora do Carmo holds the last works of Brazil's beloved Aleijadinho. Of the many colonial churches scattered around town, the Igreja de São Francisco de Assis is the finest. Designed by Aleijadinho with murals by Mestre Ataíde, it's one of the "Seven Wonders of Portuguese Origin in the World". You can also delve in to the source of Ouro Preto's wealth by touring one of the many gold mines, like the Mina Chico Rei or Mina Velha.

name: Basel
description: Settled since antiquity, Basel's position along the Rhine at the meeting point of the French, German, and Swiss borders solidified its status as an important trade and transportation hub, often making it the site of international peace negotiations and meetings. Today, it's still retained that station, with visitors flocking from all over the world to attend its ART Basel festival. Home to the country's highest concentration of museums, visitors have over 40 options, ranging from the world famous Basel Art Museum, to the Museum of Cultures, or the museum devoted to the iron sculptor Jean Tinguely. At the heart of the city's historic old town, visitors can enjoy the the large market square, faced by the vibrant red sandstone town hall and the late Romanesque-Gothic cathedral.

name: Viborg
description: The town of Viborg was a major center for Danish politics and religion starting as early as 800, and at its core was the Viborg Cathedral. Built in the 1100's, it has had quite an unfortunate history as it has been ravaged by several fires, the latest of which was in 1726. Due to its combustibility, it has required many reconstructions. Its modern day construction, built in 1876, is an accurate example of Romanesque architecture from its original inception. However, not every section of the cathedral was completely destroyed. The oldest section of the cathedral is the crypt which is home to a granite coffin, dating back to the 12th century, which is impressively cut from one stone. Today the interior is decorated with biblically themed frescoes by Danish artist Joakim Skovgaard.
