name: Hamad Town
description: Hamad Town has a heart-warming history of welcoming immigrants to its community, ever since being established in 1984 as a 'housing town' for those unable to afford skyrocketing prices in other parts of the country. In 1990, during the Gulf War, Bahrain opened its doors to Kuwaitis seeking refuge from the conflict. The result has been cultural diversity in a lively town, also renowned for its twenty-two roundabouts. Such is the significance of them that the number of the nearest roundabout is often incorporated into residential addresses. Visit the old marketplace known as Souq Waqif, where merchants would stand along the roads and sell their goods to passers-by. Today, the bustling market offers an intriguing collection of antiquities, traditional garments and unique souvenirs. Motorsport enthusiasts will find delight in the proximity of the Bahrain International Circuit, a world-famous Formula One race track located in Sakhir, just a short drive from Hamad Town. Hamad Town is not only a residential hub but also a destination that offers a glimpse into Bahrain's cultural heritage and provides exciting experiences for both residents and visitors alike.

name: Le Havre
description: Founded in the 16th century by Francis I, France's second largest port has been used for everything from cod fishing to a military staging ground, which made it a military target. During World War II, it was all but destroyed by Allied bombing, and rebuilt by. Auguste Perret with concrete. In recognition of his visionary application of the medium the city was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Perret, a mentor to Le Corbusier, personally designed St. Joseph's church, which serves as a monument to the 5000 civilians who died during the bombing. The sombre interior is illuminated by countless stained glass windows, which run the length of the church's hollow, 107 meter tower. Visitors can walk along the waterfront, to see the port launched the Impressionist movement before heading to the Museum of Modern Art, which is home to one of the largest collections of the French impressionist art, including works by Monet, Dubuffet, Renoir, Degas, and Matisse.

name: Goderdzi Resort
description: Goderdzi, renowned as one of Georgia's premier ski resorts, beckons visitors with its long ski runs and stunning natural beauty. Its snow-capped peaks provide the perfect backdrop for skiers, snowboarders, and winter enthusiasts alike. But Goderdzi's allure isn't confined to the colder months! In the summer, the resort transforms into a vibrant hub of activities, offering hiking, cycling and horseback riding adventures, and even the thrill of paragliding. Additionally, visitors can sample the local curative mineral spring waters, lending a rejuvenating touch to their holiday. Lastly, the local fossil forest is another memorable attraction.

name: Herceg Novi
description: Herceg Novi is situated on the slopes of Mt. Orjen at the entrance to the Bay of Kotor. The coastal town was founded in 1382 by King Tvrtko I and has been ruled by many throughout the ages. Herceg Novi emulates a botanical garden, with lush tropical flowers and rare fauna. The city center, Stari Grad, is adorned with winding streets and buildings that date back to the 1300's. The most notable town monuments are the Forte Mare fortress and the tower clock. Herceg Novi's lush promenade depicts many rare plants, including mimosa trees and banana trees. Revel in this charming coastal town's beaches, rich flora, and turbulent history.

name: Purmamarca
description: Purmamarca is a picturesque little town nestled in Northern Argentina's Jujuy region. It is located in the Quebrada de Humahuaca, which was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO, and it's easy to see why - Purmamarca is a destination worth a visit not only because of its distinct culture, cuisine, and traditions, but also because of its dramatic surrounding landscape. The town is surrounded by the Hill of the Seven Colours, whose unique color range is a product of geological processes that took place over millions of years. The landscape is believed to offer the most beautiful view 45 minutes after dawn. The people of Purmamarca embrace their indigenous heritage and way of life that has gone back thousands of years, with their annual celebrations attracting tourists from all around the world. Visitors can also check out artisan stands with artwork, tapestries, clothes, or pottery, or simply wander around to look at the town's colonial architecture and even play with goats and llamas. Since Purmamarca is a tourist-oriented town, booking a tour at the visitors' center is pretty easy. But, if you want to take in the beauty of the landscape at your own pace, driving around the area is the way to go! Important note: it is not recommended to visit the Jujuy region during bad weather, especially during or right after heavy rain.

name: Maringa
description: Maringá, a hidden gem in the heart of Northern Paraná, boasts the distinction of being the third-largest city in the state. Dive into Maringá's cultural tapestry with a visit to the Calil Haddad Theater, the largest in the region, hosting regular shows that captivate audiences. Grevíleas Park offers a serene retreat, while the Helenton Borba Cortes History and Art Museum, nestled within the Calil Haddad Theater, preserves the city's rich heritage through an exquisite collection. Marvel at the modernity of the Maringá Cathedral, an architectural wonder inspired by Sputnik, standing tall at 124 meters and ranking as the tallest monument in South America. Explore the lush expanse of Ingá Park, a former forest reserve dedicated to scientific research and education. Maringá's enchanting Plaza Pio XII, also known as Praça do Cogumelo, features a mushroom-shaped water tower, providing a vantage point for breathtaking city views and mesmerizing sunsets. Don't miss the Japanese-Brazilian Festival in August, celebrating Maringá's rich Japanese heritage, with the city hosting the third-largest population of Japanese descendants in Brazil.

name: Oaxaca de Juarez
description: While the Oaxaca valley has been inhabited for thousands of years, modern-day Oaxaca de Juarez was established in 1521 by Spanish conquistadors searching for the source of the Aztec's gold. Since then, the city has grown to become the state capital, but despite its size, still retains its historic charms in its UNESCO-listed town center. Many of the city's 1,200 historic monuments were built low with thick walls to withstand the many earthquakes that rock the region while still being richly adorned. While the central square is lined with charming arcaded buildings hosting open-air cafes, the pride of Oaxaca is the 16th century Templo de Santo Domingo, which has a beautiful baroque facade, and an interior that's entirely covered in swirling gilded reliefs and painted figures. The adjoining monastery now houses one of Mexico's best museums with exhibits covering everything from pre-Hispanic artefacts to traditional cuisine, and the cloisters now surround a botanical garden dedicated to local flora.

name: Linderhof Palace
description: The palace and the surrounding park form one of the most artistic and stylistically nineteenth-century structures that can be viewed today. This royal residence is the only palace that the "Mad King" lived to see completed and the one he spent the most time residing in. Decorated in the Rococo style, gilding, tapestries and ornate embellishments can be found everywhere. The sound of visitors' jaws dropping are often heard when discovering that this world of fantasy and flamboyance includes an illuminated artificial grotto surrounding a small lake, on which floats a shell-shaped boat surrounded by garlands of flowers. In addition to the palace, there are beautiful formal gardens with a fountain in the center fed by a made-made waterfall which cascades down the mountainside. Although just as decadent, Linderhof is the smallest of Ludwig's creations and tours take just thirty minutes, making it the ideal stop-off on any journey.

name: Antibes
description: An important ancient Greco-Roman port city, Antibes long-served as the gateway to Gaul. After the fall of Rome, Seigneur Rodoart fortified the town against barbarian attacks, which allowed to to weather the entirety of modern history. In the 19th century, wealthy people from all over the world discovered its innate beauty and built glorious summer mansions here. This in turn inspired many of the great artists to visit this pretty harbour city. Today, you can follow a trail that takes in the sites painted by such artists as Dameron, Boudin, Monet, Meissonier, and Picasso. Picasso was especially prolific during his short stay at the 14th century Grimaldi Castle, and left many of his works there. His widow later added to the collection, leaving the Musée Picasso with one of the finest collection of his works in the world.

name: Canterbury
description: Originally settled by Celtic tribes, Canterbury began its journey to international fame at the end of the 6th century, when Saint Augustine converted King Ethelbert to Christianity. Since then, the city's identity was closely tied to the Church, with the infamous murder of Archbishop Thomas Becket, and Chaucer's 'Canterbury Tales' cementing its name in history. The 14th century Gothic Cathedral is the Mother Church of the Anglican Communion, where visitors can see the shrine dedicated to Thomas Becket, and the very spot he was murdered in the 12th century. It's also possible to join a guided tour to learn about the Cathedral's history and visit its cloisters and Chapter House. The Canterbury Tales is a museum dedicated to Chaucer, where visitors can learn about the life and times of the author. The Canterbury Roman Museum preserves the city's ancient heritage - and the UK's only in situ mosaics.

name: Perugia
description: Founded by the Etruscans around the 6th century BC, the city was legendary amongst Roman authors by the time it was assimilated into the Republic. Sitting 1,640 ft above sea level, the old town is partly surrounded two sets of walls. The medieval wall is still largely intact, and has several entrances, such as the Cassero di Porta Sant'Angelo. The inner, Etruscan wall, was built using massive boulders. A few remains of the Roman era still survive, including an amphitheatre outside Porta Marzia, and what is likely a mausoleum under St. Peter's bell tower. The Piazza IV Novembre, with its magnificent Maggiore Fountain, is the best way to experience the essence of the city. Facing the square is the 13th century Palazzo dei Priori, which houses the National Gallery of Umbria, while the facade of the Cathedral of San Lorenzo boasts the pulpit where Saint Bernardino used to preach.

name: Cordoba
address.region: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
description: Córdoba in the Veracruz State is a picturesque testament to Mexico's former colonial fervour. Acting as a trading post between Mexico City and Coast. Spain's financial interests were protected in Cordoba, and you can see this in the atmosphere of the city. Cordoba is also the site of the Treaty of Cordoba, which established Mexican independence from Spain. The well-preserved historic centre retains the same layout as it had during the Spanish Colonial period. Relax at the shady 21 May Park, the main plaza of the city that is surrounded by shops, cafes and restaurants. Famed as a coffee centre, you can visit the Coffee Museum of Cordoba to learn more about the brew that you enjoy! For a night of culture, you can dress to the nines and attend a show at the Teatro Centenario Pedro Diaz.

name: Coromandel
description: With the discovery of gold in the town in 1852, Coromandel began to flourish while also preserving its historic values. This historical town is now loved by talented artists who have moved there specifically for what the place has to offer. Excellent restaurants using locally sourced food add to the charm of the town, and a range of hiking trails nearby beautiful scenery are what excite and entice many visitors. Spend the day or a few hours participating in the arts and crafts, learning about the mining history, indulging in delicious cuisine, or taking a dip at a gorgeous nearby beach. This town has it all.

name: Glymur Waterfall
description: At 198 meters tall, Glymur Waterfall held the title of highest cascade in the country until 2011 when climate change caused the Vatnajökull glacier to melt, and create the 240 meter Morsárjökull. For Glymur Waterfall, the attraction isn't just in the waterfall's height, but the stunning natural beauty. To reach the falls, visitors follow a hiking trail that will bring you across rocks and fields, through caves, along a cliff, and across a river. This relatively challenging hike is amazing in itself, but the final view of the falls plummeting into a narrow, moss-covered canyon is truly one of the greatest natural spectacles in Iceland. The hike to the falls is fairly long, and difficult in some places, so appropriate footwear is required, and the stop is not recommended for those with mobility issues or small children.

name: Baguio
description: Established in 1900 as the only US hill station in Asia, Baguio has since become the "Summer Capital of the Philippines" thanks to its cooler climate. The heart of Baguio is the sprawling Burnham Park, a feature from the original US plan for the city. Surrounding a man-made lake, a walking path leads you past everything from a skating rink to a rose garden and orchidarium. Camp John Hay, the original R&R facility for American military personnel, which is now something of a country club. But Baguio's claim to fame is it is the first and only UNESCO City of Culture in the Philippines. The Panagbenga Flower Festival every February sees it come alive with colorful festivities, but the BenCab Museum, dedicated to Filipino National Artist Ben Cabrera, showcases his work, that of different artists, and indigenous artefacts year round.

name: Queenstown
description: Queenstown is just one of those places where you don't even know where to begin to explain what there is to do. Whether you are interested in adventure activities, dining, or a day at the spa for relaxation, this town has it all. You could start with the skyline Gondola high above Queenstown to take in a panoramic view of the city, the surrounding mountains and the stunning lake. If you're feeling like you need an adrenaline rush, why not paraglide back down to the city afterwards? We understand if maybe paragliding isn't your thing, so instead you could go relax at one of the many spas and soak in a hot pool overlooking the Tolkien-esque landscape. Need a bite to eat? This town has around 150 diverse restaurants cafes offering international cuisine and award winning wine. For the thrill seeker or perhaps for one trying to conquer their fears, bungee-jumping is a very popular activity here where you can plummet down towards the earth in one of the most beautiful landscapes in the world. Of course there are more relaxing adventures such as hiking or bike riding along one the many extensive trails offered in the area.

name: Putre
description: Backed by the Taapaca volcanic complex, and surrounded by terraced plantations, the little town of Putre is the perfect place to get acclimated to the high Andean altitude, especially if you're on your way to the Lauca National Park. While it doesn't look like much, take a walk down O'Higgins Avenue, which is bisected by a mountain stream. Some of the humble-looking homes have preserved carved stone portals and window sills from the 17th century. From here head to the main square, which is clean and open, offering some nice views of the surroundings and Putre's main landmark: its historic church. Built in 1670 with some 19th century restorations, this charming national monument exhibits some local cultural influence, like a nave made from adobe.

name: Mont Saint Michel
description: In the 8th century, the bishop of the nearby hilltop town of Avranches had a vision where the Archangel Michael told him to build a church atop the island just out to sea. Only accessible when the tidal change permits, from the 10th century onwards, with the help of the Dukes of Normandy, followed by French kings, a major Benedictine abbey developed on the Mont-Saint-Michel. Eventually the island became a symbol of France, for even when the English had taken the rest of Normandy, they never conquered this fortified isle. Visitors can enjoy a walk up through the old town to reach the medieval engineering marvel that is the abbey church. With not enough level ground, huge crypts were constructed to create a level base for this medieval skyscraper.

name: The Sculpture Park
description: Spread over 10 acres of woodland, the Sculpture Park has over 600 sculpture by over 200 artists positioned amongst the trees, lakes, streams, and walkways. Listen to the chirping of birds while contemplating an abstract sculpture on your way through the 2 mile walking path. Specializing in modern and contemporary work, the park's collection is an exciting mixture of styles and materials. Apart from its size, the Sculpture Park is unique in that its ever-changing exhibits are all for sale! For more information, please visit thesculpturepark.com

name: Mount Nebo
description: According to the Bible, Moses scaled Mount Nebo for a glimpse of the Land of Canaan after leading the Israelites through the desert for 40 years, and though he could see it, God said he would not enter. It's also said that the prophet Jeremiah hid the tabernacle and the Ark of the Covenant in a cave in the mountain. To commemorate Moses, a Byzantine church and Monastery were built at the very top of the mountain in the 4th century, and today, a modern chapel and museum protect its beautiful mosaic floors. From the top of the mount you can take in the Biblical view of the Promised Land that - on a clear day it's even possible to see Jericho and Jerusalem!

name: Naples
description: Although Naples is one of the oldest cities in Italy, it looks quite young. Naples has touches of old architecture and charm but the heart of the city has plenty of high rises, and tall building complexes because it was the most bombed Italian city in World War II. Even with recent rebuilds, Naples has beautiful opera and theatre houses. From the popular film Eat, Pray, Love, Julia Roberts travels to Naples to try some of the original wood fired Neapolitan pizza. Take a visit to the Piazza del Gesu or one of the many popular churches just a stone's throw from the main train station. Naples port is one of the busiest of Italy so be sure to watch all the cruise ships go in and out while you enjoy a gelato on the promenade.

name: Treskavec Monastery
description: Founded in the 12th century, on top of the 1422 meter Mt Zlato, the hilltop has been a sacred site since antiquity. In the middle ages, the monastery was visited by the Serbian Emperor, who commented that 'life of the monks is nothing less that the life of those living on Mount Sinai or the Holy Mount of Athos'. The 14th-century Church of Sveta Bogorodica, built on the site of a 6th-century basilica, is lined with vivid frescoes, including a rare Child Jesus. Earlier Roman remains are preserved inside, along with graves, inscriptions and monks' skulls. Following a fire, the site is under reconstruction, but openly offers its ancient artwork and commanding views to visitors.

name: Hierve el Agua
description: From a distance, Hierve el Agua appears to be a massive waterfall pouring over a rocky cliff face. Once you get closer, however, you'll see it's actually a flowing curtain of calcified stone. Literally meaning "the water boils", this strange stone structure was formed over thousands of years as the mineral-rich waters from two pools at the top of the cliff trickled down the side of the rock face, depositing minerals in their wake. That's right - Hierve el Agua is essentially an enormous stalactite. The pools themselves were revered by the ancient Maya, and their fossilized irrigation channels are still visible, though many visitors are more interested in soaking in the panoramic views from this natural infinity pool. Please note: the park hours are inconsistent, so it's recommended that you call ahead of time to ensure they'll be open for your visit.

name: Rethymno
description: Rethymno has a rich history with a blend of Venetian and Cretan cultural heritage dating back to the Minoan era, as evidenced by its fortifications and archaeological cites, as well as Ottoman influence. Visitors can take a stroll through the lively central square and try the local cuisine, guaranteed to enjoy the walk: the narrow cobbled streets of the old town are lined with Venetian-style buildings. The Fortezza castle, which dates back to the 16th century, is one of the city's most notable landmarks and provides stunning views of the surrounding area. The city is also home to the impressive Rethymno Archaeological Museum, displaying artifacts from the Minoan era. Seaside lovers can enjoy a relaxing day at the long sandy beach of Rethymno or pay a visit to the Venetian port and harbor. Adventure seekers can go rafting or canyoning in the surrounding mountains or take a boat tour to see the famous Elafonisi Beach. Rethymno is nestled away from more touristy places like Chania – it is a pearl in the rough waiting to be discovered.

name: Waitomo
description: Known by local Māori since the 18th century, the Waitomo caves were first "formally" explored in 1884, and have been cherished as a natural treasure ever since. To this day, many of the guides are direct descendants of the Maori chief who originally explored the cave. The cave system is split into two levels, with the upper, dry passageways exhibiting fantastic stalactites, stalagmites, and other cave formations. A river runs through the lower level, so tours take place on a boat, from which you'll be able to admire the galaxies of glow worms and drift through "The Cathedral" - the largest chamber in the system. There are also a number of unique experience for the more adventurous, like "Black Water Rafting", tubing, and underground abseiling and zip-lining. Regardless of your activity of choice, you should book in advance at https://www.waitomo.com

name: Arachova
description: Thanks to its proximity to Athens and Delphi, Arachova is a popular choice for anyone trying to escape the hectic Greek cities. During the winter, it acts as a gateway for Greeks on their way to hit the nearby ski slopes. In the summer, the fresh mountain air, amazing views, and charming narrow streets are their own reward. Whichever season you find yourself in Arachova, the town's cozy bars and restaurants are a way to enjoy local cuisine.

name: Potenza
description: Founded by the Romans, the city has been rebelling against authority since the Roman defeat at Cannae in 216 BC. In 1137, the city, along with Pope Innocent II and Emperor Lothair II, attempted to overthrow their Norman rulers. Over the centuries, they rebelled against nearly every authority that held control over the city. Interspersed with the rebellions, the city was frequently damaged by strong earthquakes, most recently in 1980. Despite all of this, the city's historic center has managed to preserve monuments dating back to the Romans. Visitors can still see the cathedral's 12th century rose window and apse, or the impressive art collection at the 12th century, Romanesque Church of San Michele Arcangelo. To dig further into the region's history, the National Archaeological Museum and the Provincial Archaeological Museum exhibit artefacts from the area's pre-Latin cultures.

name: Aosta
description: The center of the Salassi people in proto-history, they were slaughtered and enslaved by the Romans in 25 BC, a victory memorialized by a triumphal arch still standing outside the city wells. By 11 BC, the military settlement the Romans had established had developed into the capital of the Empire's Grey Alps province thanks to its strategic position at the confluence of two rivers and two mountain passes. Today, the streets of Aosta's old town still follow the Roman city planning, and the Roman ruins have been incorporated into the city. The walls and two gates are still preserved, and if you keep your eyes open, you'll see buildings that are built on Roman foundations. The facade of the Roman theatre still stands today, and the Forum is annexed to the 11th century cathedral, which still bears an Ottonian fresco on the ceiling.

name: The Mall
description: The Mall is smaller than many other outlets, with only around 20 shops. However, instead of the usual high street and obscure European brands, The Mall only offers top designer labels, such as Alexander Mcqueen, Armani, Burberry, Coach, Fendi, Giorgio Armani, Gucci, Lanvin, Salvatore Ferragamo, Stella McCartney, Tod's, and Versace. Even Prada has a large shop nearby! For more information, please visit https://www.themall.it/en/outlet-italy/homepage.html

name: Locorotondo
description: Founded around the 11th century as under the jurisdiction of the Benedictine monastery of St. Stephen in Monopoli, the town became the estate of feudal lords for 500 years, ushering in an increase in population, housing development, and the construction of the walls and castle. The town's last feudal lords, the Dukes of Martina Franca, remained in Locorotondo until the beginning of the 19th century. The town has a handful of landmarks, such as the 18th century Mother Church of St. George the Martyr, with its 14th century bas-reliefs, and the Romanesque church of Our Lady of Greece, but its true beauty lies in the historic centre's labyrinth of white-washed alleys. The houses are topped with unusual pitched roofs called "cummerse", a feature typical of the historical centre of Locorotondo. From the city's perimeter, visitors can enjoy views of the countryside, dotted with trulli dwellings, interspersed to facilitate the development of vineyards.

name: Ek Balam
description: Ek Balam was a thriving Mayan city dating back to the 1st millennium BC. Around the start of the Common Era, it was the regional capital and remained inhabited up until the arrival of the Spanish in the 16th century. Today, the site consists of around 45 buildings, with many dating from around the 8th to 11th centuries. Unlike other Mayan cities, the intricate decorations on the building were made from plaster, rather than carved into stone, allowing for the artisans to create some of the most intricate motifs found in the Yucatan. The facade of the ruler Ukit Kan Leʼk Tokʼs tomb, for example, is styled like the open maw of a jaguar. The tomb sits atop a pyramid that's 150 meters long and 30 meters high- one of the largest Mayan structures in the Yucatan!

name: Chanthaburi
description: Occupied by the French at the end of the 19th century, Chanthaburi received waves of Vietnamese immigrants during the as they fled anti-Catholic persecution and communist rule in their home country. Even today, a significant number of Chanthaburians are Vietnamese, though it's still easy to see the influence the French and Chinese had on the city. The standout landmark is undoubtedly the neo-Gothic cathedral, which is the largest in the country, and houses a Virgin Mary statue encrusted with 200,000-500,000 gems donated by the local congregation. If you happen to be in town on the weekend, you might see the city's booming gem trade in action at its market. Leaning out over the river, the old town has been carefully revitalized, allowing visitors to admire its historic charms, snack on some traditional sweets, or pop into a trendy coffee shop.

name: Schonau am Konigssee
description: Loved by travelers from around the world, there are few places in the world more charming than Schonau am Konigssee. A visit to the lake where the water is so clean you can drink it is an essential part of any trip to the region. Three huge mountains surround the crystal-clear waters and where the gushing waterfalls and the green slopes provide a stark contrast to the barren mountains. A trip on one of the boats that glide silently across the Fjord-like waters provides the opportunity to witness the serenity of the Alps. Listen while a flugelhorn is blown amid the incomparable calmness of the lake and be prepared to be astounded by the echo as it makes its way around the mountains. Then you'll understand why so many people consider Schonau am Konigssee to truly be a place like no other. If you plan on enjoying the boat ride, we suggest increasing your stop time to 3 hours.

name: Vejer de la Frontera
address.addr1: Plaza de España, 16, 11150 Vejer de la Frontera, Cádiz, Spain
description: One of the favourite spots in Vejer is the Plaza de España, where a visitors and locals can relax near a beautiful spouting frog fountain covered in ceramic tiles, surrounded by palms. It's a perfect place to enjoy a pint of cerveza with tapas and just watch the world go by. From there, it only takes around minutes of walk up the hill to the Moorish castle, its ramparts affording magnificent panoramic views across the town and down to the coastline. On a good day, one can see as far as the Atlantic Ocean and Morocco. Just below the castle, there is the Estatua de la Cobijada, a statue of a woman sporting a covering that was traditional until less than a century ago.

name: Château de Cheverny
description: In France's Loire Valley, Château de Cheverny is a perfectly preserved artifact of classical Louis XIII architecture. Its rigid symmetry is softened by elegant domes and bell towers. Built between 1604 and 1635, the château has remained in the Hurault family for six centuries, preserving its original splendor. Inside, you'll be transported back in time through opulent rooms adorned with 17th-century tapestries, rare paintings, and intricately carved woodwork, including the grand Arms Room and a dining hall depicting scenes from Don Quixote. It was also the real-life inspiration for Tintin's Marlinspike Hall, featuring a dedicated exhibition to the book series.

description: Audley End House and Gardens were originally a medieval Benedictine monastery, which was replaced by a massive mansion by Thomas Howard, the Lord Treasurer, primarily for entertaining King James I. Howard reputedly spent £200,000 creating a home fit for the king, which likely played a role in his embezzlement conviction. After being purchased by King Charles II, it was being returned to the Earls of Suffolk in 1701 and gradually reduced. Though the mansion is now about ⅓ its original size, the interiors are still a jaw-dropping exposé of noble life, with the ornately decorated Great Hall giving way to amazing apartments, and a well-to-do nursery. Throughout the year, the Victorian Service Wing comes to life, giving visitors a look into traditional meals. Visitors can also enjoy a stroll through the extensive grounds, bisected by a river, or learn about heritage produce in the organic Kitchen Garden. For more information, please visit http://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/audley-end-house-and-gardens/prices-and-opening-times

name: Vaduz
description: Tiny, mountain-locked Liechtenstein is one of the richest countries in the world, and it shows in the capital's spotlessly clean streets. Hugging the banks of the Rhine in an alpine valley, Vaduz is crowned by the Crown Prince's turreted castle. The town centre mixes old and new, with tax-free luxury-goods stores sidled up alongside classical architecture. An unmissable opportunity for competitive travelers, the only way to get a passport stamp is to visit the Liechtenstein Center in person. For the truly dedicated, the Postage Stamp Museum shows off the country's postal history, and lets visitors buy stamps and postcards to show off to their friends. The Royal Family has one of the oldest and most comprehensive private collections in Europe, and house it in a modern museum. To get a true taste of Liechtenstein's culture, a tour and tasting at the Prince's winery should be on every visitor's to-do list.

name: Caaguazu
description: Situated on the northern end of the Caaguazú mountain range, 500 metres above sea level, this youthful and vibrant city is famous for it's moniker "The Capital Of Wood". It's previously large logging operations may be a thing of the past but it's legacy in woodcraft still lives on with many expert carpenters selling their wares on the final approach to the city centre. Here you can view and purchase high-quality furniture, toys, housing for pets, and other assorted wooden products. Also worth checking out is the Immaculate Conception Church. In 2008 the facade was adorned with three huge murals, a total of 60 square metres, by the artist Jorge Aguirre. The church is fronted by a pleasant paved and grassy area, and it is strikingly lit at night so that the beautiful paintings can be enjoyed throughout the whole day.

address.addr1: Jazirat Al Hamra, United Arab Emirates
description: Al Jazirah al Hamra was a small village that primarily subsisted off of pearl fishing. A series of territorial disputes between Sheikhs put the town in limbo, and in 1968, it was abandoned en masse. While the official reason is that the townsfolk accepted an offer from Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan to move to Abu Dhabi, many UAE citizens believe there was another reason for the exodus: the town is haunted by djinn. During the day, the abandoned village is a fascinating place to wander to get a glimpse at traditional Emerati life - keep an eye out for the coral used in construction. Other visitors come thrill-seeking, hoping to experience the chill hand of the village's spectral inhabitants.

name: Ponce
description: Ponce, Puerto Rico's second-largest city, was once the island's main metropolitan center, a status which has bestowed the city with a wealth of culture. Head to the public square for the one-of-a-kind Lion Fountain, the mayor's residence, and the magnificent Cathedral of Our Lady of Guadalupe. And the iconic old fire station which has been converted into a museum. From the plaza, you can also take a trolley up to the Castillo Serralles, the former residence of the producers of Don Q rum, which is now a museum dedicated to the history of the sugar and rum industries. Or visit the Ponce Museum of Art, the best art museum in the entire Caribbean. And if indigenous culture is more your thing, the Tibes Indian Ceremonial Center is the largest and the most important archaeological find in the West Indies. Of course, you can also enjoy plenty of sun and fun in Ponce. Take a stroll along the boardwalk, La Guancha Paseo Tablado, and grab a drink or bite to eat at one of the many bars and restaurants while taking in the view of the Caribbean Sea. The pier here is also the departure point for the weekend ferry to Caja de Muertos (Coffin Island or Dead Box Island).

name: Ostrava
description: Founded in the 13th century, Ostrava has the beautiful squares and historic buildings you'd expect from a medieval European city, like the Old City Hall, the Academia Bookshop – a converted Habsburg-era cafe – and the Golden Crown pharmacy in Masaryk Square. The Art Deco New City Hall, crowned by a glass and metal tower is the Czech Republic's version of the Empire State Building, providing magnificent views of the city and the surrounding landscape. However, Ostrava's most emblematic monument is the Lower Vítkovice industrial complex. Built in the early 19th century, this tentative UNESCO site has been converted into a cultural center, with its gasometer now a concert hall, and the blast furnace part of a tour that brings visitors atop a 60-metre-high tower via industrial elevator. At the Landek Mining Museum, visitors will find the world's largest exhibition of mining technology, and can even take a guided tour of the original coal seams.

name: Orange
description: Founded during the rule of Augustus in the 1st century, Orange once resembled a miniature version of Rome, with similar public buildings - just on a smaller scale. Besides the compact historical center, with its narrow streets, picturesque ancient squares and a hilltop park, the main attractions are surely the two UNESCO World Heritage Sites - the Roman theatre and Triumphal Arch. The theatre is described as the most impressive of its kind, it seats 9000 and features a 37-metre-high stone backdrop to the stage with niches, columns and a statue of Augustus. It takes about 20 minutes to get from the theatre to the massive three-arched Triumphal Arch, standing majestically over the city.

name: Thirsk
description: Though it's been settled since around 500 BC and mentioned in the Domesday Book (twice!), Thirsk has passed through history essentially unnoticed. Today, the town has been gaining publicity for its quiet charm. The heart of Thirsk is still its cobbled market square, dominated by its clock tower, and the site of Saturday and Monday markets. If you stop by the award winning Tourist Information Centre, they'll help you find the Blue Plaque Trail, which brings you to 20 buildings marked for their important architecture or residents. At the Skeldale House, former home of vet and author Alf Wright, you can journey back to the 40s to learn about veterinary science in the only center of its kind in the UK.

name: Yokohama
description: As Japan's second-largest city, Yokohama promises an unforgettable experience full of waterfront strolls and cup noodle museum explorations. Explore the lively Chinatown, indulge in diverse cuisine, and wander through the charming Sankei-en Garden, a historical gem with tranquil tea houses and picturesque landscapes. Marvel at well-preserved historic buildings and stand in awe of the Yokohama Landmark Tower, Japan's second-tallest building. Experience the world's first ramen museum, the Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum, a culinary journey through regional ramen varieties. Dive into rich cultural experiences, from mesmerizing art shows to live jazz performances in the city's energetic atmosphere. The Sankeien Garden, once owned by silk merchant Tomitaro Hara, offers a serene escape featuring bridges, waterfalls, bamboo forests, and ponds, while echoing the beauty of ancient Japan. Immerse yourself in the garden's peaceful ambiance.

name: Valparaíso
description: Once the most important port on the Pacific coast of South America, Valparaiso expanded rapidly through the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The opening of the Panama Canal in 1914 put a dampener on Valparaiso's unimpeded expansion, but also left the city with a jumble of narrow streets, endless stairways and funiculars, and a historic seaport all crowded by humble homes and lavish mansions.Your itinerary here could basically be just one point: "Walk around". Follow one of the paseos (walks), like Paseo Yugoslavo, Paseo Atkinson or Paseo Gervasoni for a sampling of the city's villas, views, and famous street art. Ride whichever funicular you come across, and scale whatever staircase grabs your eye. The city's uninhibited atmosphere has been attracting artists for over a century, and lit-lovers won't want to miss a visit to the home of Nobel-winning author Pablo Neruda. And as Chile's second-largest city, you'll have no shortage of cafes, restaurants, art galleries, and museums where you can rest your feet.

name: Guernica
description: Officially founded in 1366 at an important trading crossroads, the town is an integral part of Basque culture - during the Middle Ages, Basque leaders would meet at the Biscayan Assembly House to make important community decisions, and even today, the Basque president takes his oath under the Guernica Tree. Inside, visitors can admire paintings of the Lords of Biscay, or the giant stained glass depicting the Guernica Tree and the history of the assemblies. The Santa Maria church, begun in 1418, wasn't completed until 1715, so exhibits various architectural styles. While it's considered one of the region's best examples of Gothic architecture, the highlight might be the Walcker organ from 1889 inside. At the center of town is the interactive Peace Museum, which exhibits extensive photographic and audiovisual testimonies from the infamous bombing in hopes of educating visitors about the history of Guernica and the importance of peace.

name: Dunkirk
description: Today, Dunkirk is a picturesque coastal city with a nice historical center. However, as depicted in Christopher Nolan's new film, in May 1940 the city was transformed into a battlefield. Out-manned and out-gunned, Allied forces fell back to the beaches of Dunkirk in a harrowing retreat under heavy fire. While over 300,000 British, French, and Dutch troops managed to evacuate, over 30,000 were left behind and forced to surrender. Today, you can visit the infamous Dunkirk beach and imagine the excruciating moments the young men went through as they waited to be picked up. In the nearby museum, you can learn everything there is to know about the 1940 British evacuation bearing the codename "Dynamo".

name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
address.addr1: Victory Gate, HM Naval Base, Portsmouth PO1 3LJ, UK
description: The Portsmouth Historic Dockyard has been in use by the Royal Navy since the 15th century, has welcomed visitors to experience Britain's illustrious seafaring history for over a century. The historic buildings, many of which date back to the 18th century, house a variety of attractions, such as the Royal Navy Museum, the Boatbuilding and Heritage Skills Center, and the Mary Rose Museum, dedicated to King Henry VIII's favourite warship. Visitors can then experience the evolution of the warship by stepping on to the historic ships berthed in the dockyard. The HMS Warrior, built in 1860, was the world's first iron-hulled, armoured battleship, and the largest and most powerful warship of the Victorian Age, while the HMS M33, a veteran of the Battle of Gallipoli, is a floating museum dedicated that disastrous campaign. Or get your sea-legs on what's probably the world's most famous warship, the HMS Victory, the flagship commanded by Horatio Nelson at the Battle of Trafalgar. For more information, please visit www.historicdockyard.co.uk

name: Vukovar
description: The Baroque city of Vukovar, situated along the Danube River, is one of the worst destruction sites of the Croatian-Serbian war. It's the only city in Europe almost completely destroyed since WWII. Although many devastated buildings still remain, the city is slowly rebuilding itself to become stronger than it was before. A large cross located where the Vuka enters the Danube serves as a memorial to symbolize those who lost their lives during the war. Numerous museums can also be found within the city, the most notable being the The Vukovar Municipal Museum. The newly restored museum is situated in a Baroque castle and houses an extensive collection of medieval artifacts and war facts from the 1990's conflict. The city also holds many cultural events each year. Vukovar serves as a place of resilience and peace as it continues to recover from its painful past.

name: Comalcalco
description: Comalcalco was founded at least as early as the 6th century BC, and peaked around the 6th century AD. Because of its strategic location on the Mezcalapa River, Comalcalco was an important link in trade between the Yucatán and the Gulf Coast and the highlands of Chiapas and Guatemala. Located in Tabasco's largest cacao production area, it was likely involved in growing and distributing this precious commodity. Unlike most Mayan cities, Comalcalco was built from bricks rather than blocks of limestone, which were held together by an oyster-based mortar. The bricks' irregular sizes imply that they were hand-cut from lengths of clay, but what makes them truly unique is that many had designs painted, etched, or molded on their backs. After admiring the stupendous pyramids, palaces, temples, and tombs, the onsite museum is well-worth a visit to learn more about the site, and see the famous ornamented bricks up close.

name: Poznan
description: One of the country's oldest cities, Poznan is considered by many to be the birthplace of the Polish state. The Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul (commonly known as Poznan Cathedral) was Poland's first cathedral and where Catholicism was introduced to the country in 968. The Cathedral retains pride of place on Ostrów Tumski (Cathedral Island), celebrated as the spot on which Poznań was founded. Although Poznan's Old Town was severely damaged during WWll and the soviet rule that followed, it has been beautifully restored. The Royal-Imperial Route is a walk that runs through the heart of the city, allowing visitors to appreciate the most important and historic parts of Poznan with ease. Poznan City Hall, the Raczyński Library and the Collegium Minus of Adam Mickiewicz University are all architecturally unique and visually striking. Stary Rynek (the Old Town Market Square) is one of the finest in Europe and is lined with cafes and restaurants.

name: Maras Salt Mines
description: The Maras Salt Mines haven't changed much since the Incas created them over 1,000 years ago. The 3,000 pools built into the hillside produce pink salt, bath salt, and flavored salt, and yields around 150 kilograms per month. Through the simple process of evaporation and other primitive harvesting techniques, the farmers bag the salt and sell it in local markets. Due to the cost of shipping the heavy salt in such a remote area, you won't be able to purchase it anywhere else. The thousands of pools provide a stunning geometric landscape along the mountain side, which will be a for sure unforgettable view.

name: Karnak
description: Karnak was begun under the rule of Senusret I in the Middle Kingdom was continuously updated and expanded into the Ptolemaic period 1000 years later. The resulting temple complex is considered one of the grandest building projects of Ancient Egypt, with nearly every pharaoh of significance adding their own touches to the kingdom's most revered sanctuary. The largest and most important section of Karnak is the Great Temple of Amun, where you'll find colossal statues, detailed reliefs, and monolithic gates. In the 5,000 square meter Great Hypostyle Hall, one of the wonders in the world, row upon row of pillars, as well as the walls, abaci, and architraves are covered with intricate inscriptions, some of which still have their original coloring. This, of course, is just one part of the temple complex, and there are countless other amazing ancient constructions to discover. At night, the temple brings the history of ancient Phoebes to life through an illuminating sound and light show that adds an extra dimension to the experience.

name: Everglades National Park
description: Located in the southern tip of Florida, Everglades National Park is the largest tropical wilderness in the United States, and unlike any other ecosystem on the planet. In the 1940s, Marjory Douglas led a successful campaign to make the Everglades a National Park, and to preserve it from any human intervention. Thanks to her, you can experience the everglades in its natural states, as it has been for time immemorial. Take a boat tour through the expanse, and find alligators, herons, frogs and other animals that frequent this unique haven. For a hiking trip, there are several trails with varying difficulty. The Anhinga Trail is a family-friendly trail where you can experience the beauty of the Everglades on an easy half-mile walk.

name: Paris
description: Where to start with Paris? A blanket of white marble, green grass, and the occasional, world-renowned landmark. You don't have to look far to find something iconic; across every enamored park and behind every Haussmannian house, stands the face of France, the Eiffel Tower. Ride the elevator to the top for the glorious metallic lookout point, where the whole city lies below. Admire the grand spiderweb of walkways, guiding infatuated visitors over the River Seine, through the Arc de Triomphe, along the Champs-Elysees and across Place de la Concorde; halting in awe before the world's largest museum and bearer of lady Mona Lisa, The Louvre. Exploring this sculptured streetscape may seem like a daunting task. Fear not, as in Paris, charming cafés and bakeries bestow each avenue. You can rest in elegance before heading further afield to Notre Dame, Monte Martre, Sacré-Cœur, or even out to the Palace of Versailles. The world of Paris is your oyster and you won't want to miss a thing!

name: Mount Olympus
description: The Troodos Mountains are certainly one of the natural treasures of Cyprus, covered with pine forests, wildflowers, and scenic hiking trails. Many of the range's sights are named after Greek gods, such as Mount Olympus, which is Cyprus' highest point at over 6,000 feet. To experience the beauty of these mountains, one sure way is to hike on the Artemis Trail that runs around Mount Olympus. Named after the goddess of the wilderness, the trail stretches for a bit over 4 miles. Starting from the parking lot, the route is marked and runs through a pine forest and a precipice, and offers panoramic views of almost every area of Cyprus. A few tips: the hike is relatively easy although it is recommended to bring comfortable hiking boots. Bring water, snacks, and sunscreen. Most importantly, take advantage of every viewpoint on the route!

name: Korce
description: A small settlement in the 13th century, modern Korce's history began in the 1480s when it was redeveloped by Sultan Mehmet II's son-in-law. Korce grew quickly at the turn of the 20th century, and today is the 6th largest city in Albania. At the heart of the city is the Cathedral of the Resurrection, the largest Orthodox church in the country, which was built on the site of an older church destroyed during the Communist regime. Spread out behind the church is Korce's old town, a pleasant tangle of cobbled streets lined with French villas and traditional townhouses - the perfect place to sip some Turkish coffee and soak in the atmosphere. The city's rich culture is well-preserved in its slew of first-rate museums, including the Education Museum, which is housed in the first Albanian school building, and the exceptional National Museum of Medieval Art.

name: Positano
description: Positano was an important port for the ancient Greeks and Phoenicians, and prospered under the Amalfi Republic during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. However, unlike other nearby towns, Positano wasn't a hot holiday destination for 19th century intellectuals. Rather, it was an essay by John Steinbeck for Harper's Bazaar that brought the poor fishing village to the attention of the world's jet setters. A maze of steep lanes and stairs wind their way past pastel colored houses, cafes, galleries, and upscale boutiques down to Positano's renowned Marina Grande beach. Nearby, is the unmissable Church of Santa Maria Assunta, with its colorful majolica tile dome, lavish Rococo interior, and legendary 13th century Byzantine black Madonna icon.

name: Kicevo Monastery
description: When the 14th century Holy Mother of God Immaculate monastery burned down in 1558, the monks escaped through underground tunnels. Today, the structure is one of the finest monasteries in the country. Of its many icons, some of which date back to the middle ages, the miraculous 'Flying Virgin' is the most famous. According to legend, it was sent away on multiple occasions, but would fly back to its place in Kicevo Monastery. The monastery's 19th century church is the largest of its kind in the country. Within the church, visitors will find exceptional frescoes, an opulent iconostasis, and even rare books like the 14th century The Four Gospels and 15th century The Psalter. The other section of the church, the one without frescoes, was a Muslim sacral space that has been preserved from the Ottoman era.

name: Villa General Belgrano
description: Primarily shaped by German immigrants, along with Swiss, Italian, and Austrian families, Villa General Belgrano resonates with the Alpine and Bavarian spirit. Strolling along San Martín Avenue reveals the influence in architecture, gastronomy, and a profusion of craft beer, epitomized by the renowned Oktoberfest celebration. The heart of the town, José Hernández Square to El Sauce Stream's bridge, is a living canvas of German charm. Here, German-style architecture, diverse shops, restaurants, and craft beer bars beckon visitors. The square, once the venue for Oktoberfest, now retains its allure year-round, adorned with welcoming arches, a brewer statue, and a colossal beer barrel. The Clock Tower, an iconic German-style edifice, serves as the Tourist Office, offering a wealth of information on the Calamuchita Valley. Nearby, the Historical Museum and Cultural Center unveil the city's narrative through artifacts, documents, and photographs. For the adventurous, Cerro de la Virgen's trail, though challenging, rewards with panoramic views of the valley.

name: Fulda
description: The medieval city of Fulda with its cobbled streets, winding streets, small squares and lovingly restored half-timbered houses is the ideal place for a relaxing stroll. However, if you're looking for a true feel of the city and to experience the influence of religion on the region, then pay a visit to Fulda Cathedral, the burial site of St. Boniface and regarded as the jewel of the city. The current structure was built in the 1700s and is regarded as a baroque architectural masterpiece, similar to St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Although smaller in size and lesser in grandeur, the cathedral's interior is actually reminiscent of St. Peter's. The body of St. Boniface, along with that of King Conrad I of Germany — whose successors would later become Holy Roman Emperors — is interred in the crypt. For those interested in religion or architecture then a visit to this iconic cathedral will not disappoint.

name: The Forth Bridge
description: Built in 1890, the Forth Bridge was a groundbreaking feat of engineering when it opened. Spanning 2,529 meters it was the largest bridge of its kind in the world, and remains one of the longest to this day. Along with its sheer scale, the bridge also set the precedent for using 'mild steel' in large construction projects, and its distinctive design is the epitome of the industrial aesthetic. To put the bridge's size into perspective, imagine 6 Eiffel Towers laid end-to-end! Travellers can stop to admire this unique structure from several viewing points, and learn more about the bridge's history at the Queensferry Museum.

name: Monastir
description: Founded on the ruins of the Punic–Roman city of Ruspina, Monastir was an important Islamic bastion before the city transformed into a fishing port, and more recently, a beach resort town. The well-preserved Ribat of Monastir, built in the 7th century, is one of the oldest Arabic fortresses in North Africa. Originally built to defend against the attacks of the Byzantine fleet, it's better known as a filming location for the miniseries Jesus of Nazareth, and Monty Python's Life of Brian. The watchtower offers panoramic views of the coast and town, while the former prayer hall is now an Islamic Arts Museum. Monastir is notably the birthplace of Habib Bourguiba, the founder of modern Tunisia, who's remembered by both the Habib Bourguiba Mosque, and his grand mausoleum. Monastir's medina has been carefully restored, and while it's lost much of its down-at-the-heel attitude, its souk streets are overflowing with shopping opportunities.

name: Esporles
description: Nestled within the UNESCO-protected Serra Tramuntana mountains, Esporles is a tranquil haven just 20 minutes from Palma, effortlessly blending authentic Mallorcan charm with international appeal. The heart of Esporles, Calle Joan Riutort, meanders along a gentle stream, flanked by imposing Spanish Plane trees and traditional stone architecture. The village is a harmonious blend of townhouses in the center and more expansive properties farther afield, ranging from classic Mallorcan villas to contemporary gated residences. Esporles offers a year-round lifestyle intertwined with agricultural rhythms, making it a haven for wine and olive enthusiasts drawn to the fertile terrain. The village's quaint main street, Carrer de sa Rectoria, hosts a beloved Saturday market, while off the beaten path, narrow lanes reveal picturesque stone houses with panoramic valley views. Enchanting Esporles, untouched by mass tourism, exudes an authentic Mallorcan character. Residents revel in the simple pleasures of a tobacconist, pharmacy, and a handful of boutique shops along the majestic Carrer de sa Rectoria. The Neo-Gothic church stands tall at the village's western edge, a testament to Esporles' rich medieval history.

name: Pakse
description: Founded in 1905 as a French administrative outpost, Pakse served as the capital of the Kingdom of Champasak until 1946 when the Kingdom of Laos was unified. Today, Pakse is the second largest city in Laos, spanning the confluence of two rivers. This idyllic setting combined with more metropolitan comforts make Pakse a great place to explore on foot or by bike. There aren't many colonial-style buildings left despite Pakse's pedigree, but the grandiose Chinese Society Building in the town center, and the former Palace of Prince Boun Oum Na Champasak across the river are both exemplary. For those looking to delve deeper into the region's history, the Champasak Historical Heritage Museum houses some great relics, including 7th century Buddha head. While out exploring, be sure to take time to head to the Golden Buddha across the Lao-Japan Friendship Bridge for panoramic views of the city.

name: Rhodes City
description: Rhodes, a captivating gem nestled in the Aegean Sea, effortlessly blends ancient allure with modern charm. Immerse yourself in the echoes of antiquity as you wander through the cobbled streets of Rhodes Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Here, medieval walls guard a labyrinth of narrow alleys, adorned with Byzantine churches, Ottoman mosques, and elegant Venetian mansions. The Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights of Rhodes stands as a testament to the island's storied past, showcasing intricate mosaics and imposing architecture. Dive deeper into history at the Archaeological Museum of Rhodes, where artifacts spanning millennia reveal the island's fascinating past. Beyond its historic core, Rhodes beckons with sun-kissed beaches that fringe its rugged coastline. From the bustling shores of Elli Beach to the secluded coves of Anthony Quinn Bay, there's a sandy haven to suit every traveler's taste. Crystal-clear waters invite snorkelers and divers to explore vibrant marine life, while waterfront tavernas offer a taste of local delicacies and refreshing drinks.

description: Named after Sir Gerald Herbert Portal, the British Consul General of Zanzibar who came to Uganda in the 1890s to formalise the protectorate over the country, Fort Portal has transformed from a colonial stronghold to a dynamic town that's the perfect base from which to explore the amazing surrounding area. The Tooro Botanical Gardens, were established in 2001, and replaced 100 acres of eucalyptus trees with indigenous species, and are a great place to sample Uganda's natural diversity. The city is also famous for its tea plantations, so be sure to take the time for a fresh cuppa.

name: Kaysersberg
description: In the 13th century, the fortified settlement of Castrum Keisersberg was established along the route that connected the Rhine plain and Lorraine. By the 14th century, Kaysersberg had become a free imperial city, though gradually fell into obscurity after passing to the French in the 17th century. Today, traditional half-timbered houses still line the river that runs through the town. Much of the town dates from the 16th century, including the fortified stone bridge spanning the Weiss river. The Church Sainte-Croix was built between the 13th and 15th centuries, and has retained its Romanesque facade. After enjoying the historic towers, ramparts, and mansions, visitors can sit down at a cafe to enjoy the town's signature wine: Tokay, which is believed to have been brought from Hungary in the 16th century.

name: Wadi Rum
description: Carved into the sandstone and granite rock, Wadi Rum is the largest valley in Jordan. The quintessential desert landscape with scorching days and freezing nights, this unforgiving environment has somehow been inhabited since prehistory. The awe-inspiring landscape is best known for its connection with British officer T. E. Lawrence, who was here on several occasions during the Arab Revolt of 1917–18, and much of Lawrence of Arabia was filmed here. When Matt Damon was filming the Martian here, he said it was "like nothing I've ever seen anywhere else on Earth", which might explain why it's been a filming location for Sci-Fi movies including Star Wars: Rogue One, and the upcoming Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker, and perhaps most telling, as Arrakis in the 2020 Dune movie.

name: Wilmington, DE
description: Founded by the Swedish in 1638, Wilmington is one of America's oldest cities. It remained relatively small until the 19th century, when it became the leading producer of iron ships and gunpowder during the Civil War. DuPont was founded here as a gunpowder manufacturer, and the family's lavish manors (yes plural) are easily some of Wilmington's top attractions. Nemours Mansion, built in 1909 by Alfred I. du Pont as a gift for his second wife, Alicia, is styled as a French Chateau and filled with rare 18th-century French furniture. Then there's Winterthur, the palatial home of Henry Francis DuPont. The 175 room mansion houses one of the greatest collections of Americana, and is surrounded by magnificent grounds. The Delaware Museum of Natural History and Delaware Museum of Art are some of the best cultural attractions in the state. If you want a break from the city, the Russell W. Peterson Wildlife Refuge is right downtown, but feels worlds away.

name: Durango
description: For the Spanish, Durango is a hub for fans of the outdoors thanks to the exceptional hiking and biking trails that criss-cross the surrounding area. While the natural surroundings are gorgeous, you'll want to dive into the town's historic center, which is so full of monuments that it was declared a National Cultural Site. The church of Santa Ana is a Baroque beauty, while the church of María Uribarri houses a Gothic interior and huge portico with wooden cover. Even the Town Hall is exceptional with an unusual porch of seven half-point arches, and outstanding paintings decorating the last two floors. However, the city's most precious architectural gem is the 15th century Kurutziaga Cross, which is covered in Biblical imagery. While strolling through the streets of one of the Basque's most precious settlements, be sure to stop for some of their exceptional tapas.

name: Ronda
description: Settled in the 9th century BC, Ronda was officially named a city under the reign of Julius Caesar. The scenic setting, and many landmarks made the town popular with the Romantics, attracting the likes of Alexandre Dumas, Ernest Hemingway, and Orson Welles. The 18th century 'New Bridge' straddles a 100 meter ravine, and offers spectacular views of the surrounding countryside. In the city proper, you can find one of the country's oldest bull-fighting rings. The Mondragon palace, originally built in 1314 by the Moorish King Abomelik, was later used as the primary residence for Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand. Inside you'll find a fascinating museum devoted to Ronda's rich history, with exhibits including Roman and Moorish tombs. For a unique view of the city, the stunning Cuenca Gardens follow a series of terraces on the ledges of the Tajo river.

name: Sant'Antonino
description: Perched like an eagle's nest over the hillsides of Balagne, Sant'Antonino is one of the small villages that dots the gorgeous landscape of inland Corsica. It is also one of the oldest villages of the island, founded in the 9th century and flourishing later in the 16th century when the inhabitants turned it into a veritable garden. Olive trees, vineyards, almond trees, wheat and barley have been cultivated on the land for centuries, and as families prospered from the reaping, 75 houses were built into the rock of the main settlement. Stepping into the maze-like cluster of attached houses is like stepping back in time. Outside of the village center, the Church of the Annunciation has stood proudly since the 11th century and neighbors the Chapel de Confrérie. Trek to the top of the village to the ruins of old fortifications and take in the uninterrupted view of the Balagne region, and don't forget to stop at the ancient bread oven and wine press.

name: Kobuleti
description: Kobuleti is a small resort town in western Georgia, situated on the eastern coast of the Black Sea. It is renowned for its mild subtropical climate, ionized maritime air, bright sunshine, warm sea, and the friendliness and hospitality of its locals. The town's main beach is sandy with beautiful views of the town's verdant landscape - pine trees, eucalypts, bamboo, cypress groves, and date and cocoa palms. The resort's peak season spans four months from June to September, when tens of thousands of both Georgian and foreign visitors flock here to enjoy all that Kobuleti has to offer. Although the history of the town dates back to the Bronze Age, Kobuleti has gained recognition for its healing properties over the past few decades: visitors have been drawn to its therapeutic environment to treat respiratory and other ailments. The town also has several attractions to offer during the off-season. Just a short drive from the town, Petra Fortress stands as a relic of Ancient Lazica and is among Georgia's most significant Roman-era archaeological sites. Moreover, Kobuleti serves as the gateway to the Kobuleti Managed Reserve, a part of Georgia's UNESCO World Heritage-listed Colchic Rainforests and Wetlands.

name: Moore Town
description: Moore Town is a tiny but significant historic town located in the highlands of eastern Jamaica. It is home to the descendants of independent communities of former runaway slaves known as Maroons. The Maroons, brought from West and Central Africa, established the settlement to rebel against the expanding plantation system of the British. Their heritage is rich and diverse, with traditional religious ceremonies, a UNESCO-protected language and drumming style, and a unique political structure that includes a system of communally-held treaty lands. The town offers visitors a chance to learn about the rich history and heritage of the Maroons and witness the unique practices that have been passed down for generations. It's a great opportunity to get a deeper understanding of Jamaica's rich cultural heritage. Finish off your cultural immersion with a dip at the beautiful Nanny Falls right outside of town.

name: Kars
description: Kars is a city in northeast Turkey on the border with Armenia. Having been a part of Armenia for many centuries, the city has sparked the interest of the Ottoman and Russian empires before finally being reclaimed by the Turks in the 1920s. As a result, the unique blend of Turkish, Armenian, Georgian, Kurdish, and Russian cultures has come to define Kars. The city's most prized gem is the 12th-century Castle of Kars, also known as the Citadel; perched atop a rocky hill, the castle offers great views of the cityscape. Other points of interest include the 18th-century Stone Bridge, and the Armenian Church of the Apostles, a sacred monument converted into a mosque in 1993. Visitors are welcome to pay a visit to one of the bustling tea houses, where one can savor the taste of strong tea complemented by the sweet delight of baklava. To enrich your experience, extend your exploration beyond the city limits to the ancient city of Ani. Just a short distance from Kars, Ani was once an Armenian capital that rivaled Constantinople in power and grandeur, and now stands as a UNESCO-listed site.

name: Willemstad
description: Nestled in the heart of the southern Caribbean Sea, Willemstad, the vibrant capital of Curaçao, beckons with a rich tapestry of history, culture, and architectural marvels. The city's UNESCO-designated historic center unfolds in four distinct quarters, each contributing to its unique allure. Punda, established in 1634, exudes colonial elegance with its pastel-hued Dutch colonial buildings lining the waterfront of Sint Anna Bay. Across the bay lies Otrobanda, a cultural hub founded in 1707, offering a delightful contrast of vibrant streets and lively ambiance. Discover the enchanting Scharloo and Pietermaai Smal quarters, where historical gems like the Curaçao synagogue, the oldest surviving synagogue in the Americas, weave tales of a bygone era. The city's iconic Queen Emma Bridge, a floating marvel, connects the Punda and Otrobanda districts, periodically separating to allow vessels to pass. Willemstad, invites you to unravel its captivating narrative, where each street and square whispers tales of a city that has stood the test of time.

name: Twin Beach
description: As its name implies, Twin Beach is two beaches: Nacpan and Calitang Beach, which form a sort of curved "X". With no electricity and only accessed by a dirt road, the only development here are a few fishing villages, and a few beachfront amenities. While of course you can swim, no visit to the Twin Beach would be complete without a walk down to the lookout point where you can see the two beaches meet and diverge, and a fresh-cooked meal at the beachfront restaurant.

name: Nenagh Castle
description: Nenagh Castle was built in the 13th century by Theobald FitzWalter, and would serve as the seat of the Butler family for the next two hundred years. The 17th century proved especially cruel to the castle, with it being captured and burned on several occasions, ultimately falling into ruin by the end of the century. In the 19th century, the circular keep was restored, with a crown of crenelations and clerestory windows added to transform it into a belltower for a cathedral that was never built. Today, visitors can climb the 101-step spiral staircase to reach the top of the tower for some fantastic views of the area (just watch your head!). While there are information panels on each floor of the keep, the town offers free guided tours for those looking for additional insights into the castle's history. For more information, please visit www.nenagh.ie/places-of-interest/details/nenagh-castle

name: Lanhydrock House and Garden
address.addr1: Lanhydrock House and Garden, Treffry Ln, Bodmin PL30 5AD, UK
description: Lanhydrock House was first built in the 17th century as a fortified estate, complete with a garrison of Parliamentary forces. In 1881, a major fire ravaged the building, leaving only one wing intact, so the damaged wings were rebuilt in the Victorian style. World War I was a pivotal time for the estate's owners, with 4 of 5 sons enlisting themselves, earning 2 Military Crosses and a Victoria Cross between them. The parents and daughters devoted themselves to fundraising and nursing, with the youngest forsaking her life in high-society and instead establishing a nursing home where she worked until her death. Over 50 of the estate's stupendous rooms are open to the public, including the 17th century 'Long Gallery', with its remarkable plastered ceiling, rare book collection, and Steinway piano, or visitors can learn about the family's role in the war through their preserved artefacts and belongings. Surrounding the house are carefully manicured formal gardens and acres of pleasant parkland.

name: Gorizia
description: This charming, small city is located at the confluence of the Isonzo and Vipava valleys. Gorizia was separated into two cities during WWII when the international border ran through the city. Today, the diverse landscapes and pleasant Mediterranean climate make Gorizia an ideal resort. The star of the city is the Gorizia Castle, situated on a hill in the center of town. The castle was built in the 11th century and restored in the 1930's. It offers stunning views of the city with a view of the Alps in the background. This quiet destination is not overrun by tourists, making it the perfect area to relax and enjoy nature's beauty.

name: Bayreuth
description: This North Bavarian city is well known for its association with the German composer Richard Wagner, who lived in Bayreuth from 1872 until his death in 1883 and the world famous Bayreuth Festival where only Wagner's works are performed. However, Bayreuth offers so much more than Wagner. The simple charm of the town's historic houses and public buildings provide the perfect contrast with the rococo parks, fountains, artificial grottos and tree-lined avenues. The Baroque style city center contains an attractive pedestrian area with spacious town squares, numerous street cafés and over 400 specialty shops where time can easily slip by if you're not careful when whiling away the hours. Whether it's the UNESCO listed Margravial Opera House, browsing unforgettable buildings where the aristocracy once lived, or even simply checking out the huge range of shopping close at hand, Bayreuth has something to cater for every taste.

name: Ribe
description: This medieval town came into existence in the 8th century, making it the oldest still-inhabited town and Denmark, and even Scandinavia. This charming town has a seamless blend of history and modern facets. From the art, restaurants, museums, and viking artefacts, the atmosphere is truly one of a kind. Don't miss the beautiful cathedral in the center of town, for a small fee, you can climb the tower and view the lush surroundings, including the river running through the town. No other view screams medieval charm making it the perfect photo op! Then explore the viking center and learn about the life and times of the Ribe vikings from 'vikings' who can tell you themselves! Before leaving town, you can't forget to try a beer from Ribe Bryghus and some of the local dishes that have been enjoyed for centuries.

name: Nijmegen
description: Founded in the 1st century as a Roman military settlement, the city has been continuously inhabited ever since, earning it the distinction of the oldest city in the Netherlands. However, during World War II, the city has bombed and shelled by both sides, destroying many of the city's historic monuments, with ambitious city-planners taking care of many others. Fortunately, the historic core pulled through, leaving a pleasant neighborhood near the water for visitors to explore. At its heart, the Great Market is lined with historic buildings, such as the sixteenth-century weighing hall that is now a restaurant. The market also grants access to St. Stevenskerk, with a 15th century Latin school along with the 13th century St. Church. The Waal River is Europe's busiest waterway, meaning visitors can walk across the Waalbrug bridge to watch the constant stream of barges and ferries roll by.

name: El Totumo Mud Volcano
description: According to legend, the El Totumo Mud Volcano used to spew molten lava until a clever priest poured holy water into the caldera, turning it into a more benevolent mud bath. Though it might look like an unassuming pile of dirt from afar, climbing the stairs to the rim reveals a 15-foot-wide pool of naturally heated, mineral-rich mud where you can enjoy a therapeutic bath. Once you're done with your mud spa, head down the slightly-slippery exit stairs to rinse off in the nearby lagoon - the local women will make sure you're scrubbed clean and baby-soft.

name: Jaca
description: Nestled between Pyrenees mountains, man has been enjoying Jaca's stunning natural views since pre-Roman times. This long history is remember by the city's numerous remarkable structures, such as the 11th century Romanesque cathedral, the local Benedictine monastery, and of course, the Church of Santiago. While the city's known for its religious monuments, these are overshadowed by its huge citadel with a pentagonal design, a textbook example of 16th-century military architecture. With its beautiful surroundings, and equally beautiful architecture, it's no wonder the city is nicknamed "the pearl of the Pyrenees".

name: Soave Castle
description: The Soave Castle, or Castello Soave, is situated on top of a high hill overlooking the surrounding area. This beautiful, well-preserved fortress was built in the 10th century to protect the area against Hungarians. Today, it serves as the setting for medieval pageants and cultural events. Castello Soave consists of a drawbridge, massive tower, and three walls that form three different sized courts. There is also a small museum within the castle grounds. Soave Castle's most impressive feature is the Mastio, which is believed to be a former prison and torture chamber based on the amount of bones found there. Many interesting artifacts can be found in the castle, including lovely 14th century frescoes and medieval furniture. For a beautiful view of the surrounding vineyards and hills, don't forget to take a trip to the top of Soave Castle's imposing tower.

name: Suwon
description: Traditionally renowned as the 'City of Filial Piety,' Suwon continues to showcase its historical charm, attracting day trippers from Seoul with its well-preserved city walls and other captivating sites. One of Suwon's standout attractions is the UNESCO-listed Hwaseong Fortress, initially erected in 1796 by King Jeong-jo. Explore its restored splendor, strolling through the vast parade square where families often fly kites and ride bicycles. For those seeking a unique dining experience, the Tasting Museum awaits in a century-old Hanok building, serving delectable fusion cuisine, pasta, wines, and more. Signature dishes such as Porcini Risotto, Eggplant Ragu, and Tomahawk Steak tantalize taste buds. Near the scenic Suwoncheon Stream stands the Hwahongmun Gate, an architectural marvel with its distinctive seven arched watergates, strategically designed to regulate the water flow. Adjacent to the gate, the picturesque Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion entices visitors, providing breathtaking views of Suwon's surroundings. A stroll to the Yeongyeon Pond area offers a different perspective of the pavilion's beauty. Whether exploring ancient fortresses or indulging in fusion delicacies, Suwon promises an enriching experience for all who venture within its charming streets.
