name: Banaue
description: The Banaue Rice Terraces were created as early as 2000 years ago by indigenous tribes using little more than their bare hands. In the following centuries, little has changed. The paddies are still irrigated by an ancient system in the rain forest above and villagers still subsisting on their rice harvest. To combat the worms, rodents, and other pests that can destroy the steps, locals use the same herbs and religious rituals as their ancestors - no pesticides here. Sometimes called the "Eighth Wonder of the World", it's said that if all the terrace steps were put end-to-end, they would circle half the planet. Today, tourism plays a major role in the survival of the terraces, with locals offering tours and homestays - the income from which helps them care for the delicate steps. While you can simply stop here to enjoy the view, making the demanding trek up and down the terraces with a guide is an immersive look into this timeless way of life.

name: Dougga
description: Settled since 2000 BC, Dougga was the capital of an important Libyco-Punic state before being conquered by the Romans. While the town was exceptionally wealthy, it also experienced an early decline. Historians at first thought Dougga was a major religious site for the disproportionate number of temples, but it turns out the wealthy residents erected them as thanks for their good fortune. The most impressive is the 2nd century Capitol, dedicated to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva, which is preserved within a Byzantine-era fort. Along with the twenty temples, the cobbled streets lead visitors to a circus for chariot racing, a large villa, several baths, two triumphal arches, and a theatre that could seat practically the entire town. Near the theatre is Douga's only Christian monument - a 5th century church with a small, sarcophagi-packed crypt. South of the main town you'll find Tunisia's finest pre-Roman monument - the Libyco-Punic Mausoleum, dating from the 2nd century BC.

name: Ostend
description: Ostend began as a medieval fishing village, and by the 18th century had become such an important port that the British and Dutch stepped in to shut down Ostend's international trade company. After World War II, the city rose from the ashes and established itself as Belgium's premier seaside resort. The city's attracted everyone from Lord Byron to Albert Einstein to Marvin Gaye, but its most famous resident was painter James Ensor, whose influential works are now showcased in his former home and atelier. For art connoisseurs, the Mu.ZEE exhibits contemporary artists alongside some of the biggest names in Belgian art history. Visitors can also get their sea-legs on one of the city's floating museums. On the Amandine, visitors will learn about the gruelling lives of fishermen who braved the frigid North Atlantic, while the three-masted Mercator is a preserved piece of Belgian history. And of course be sure to indulge in the city's famous fresh seafood!

name: Alexandroupoli
description: Founded in the 19th century by fishermen, their village became an important crossroads when a railroad station was built, even becoming a stop on the legendary Orient Express in 1897. Today, fishing is still a major part of the regional capital's identity, regularly holding an exciting "fish auction" in its fish market. Visitors can enjoy a pleasant stroll along the waterfront promenade before stopping to enjoy some fresh seafood and ocean views. The city also has a wealth of neo-classical buildings thanks to its 19th century boom. Housed in one, the Ethnological Museum of Thrace covers Thrace's folk culture and customs from the 18th century to the 1970's through a variety of exhibits, ranging from traditional clothing to a sesame-oil press.

name: Monterosso al Mare
address.addr1: Strada Provinciale 38, 112, 19016 Monterosso al Mare SP, Italy
description: Cinque Terre is a string of five islands along Italy's Mediterranean coast. Monterosso al Mare is the last, but according to visitors, the best. Part of this is because unlike the pebbly beaches elsewhere on the coast, Monterosso has a sizable, sandy beach. And, of course, it still has Cinque Terre's signature pastel architecture. Visit the medieval castle and San Francesco church in Monterosso's old town after you wander through the town's famous lemon and olive groves.

name: Al Bahah
description: Located in the Hejaz region of western Saudi Arabia, Al Bahah might become the next major tourist hotspot in the country. Often referred to as "The Garden of Hejaz" due to its lush natural beauty and pleasant climate, Al Bahah is set against the dramatic granite slopes of the Shada Al-Asfal mountains. The city boasts a rich heritage, with numerous stone fortresses, known as qasaba, scattered throughout. Additionally, the Dhee Ayn Village, also known as the "marble village", is located about 15 miles southwest of Al-Baha and is definitely worth a visit. Built atop a small marble mountain, even the road leading to the village is a sight to behold, dotted with several historical stone and slate towers. Another highlight is the city's renowned honey production. In fact, Al Bahah proudly hosts an annual international honey festival. So, dive in and explore this hidden gem before it becomes a bustling tourist hub!

name: Olomouc
description: The centre of Olomouc is the largest historic preservation zone outside of Prague and therefore boasts numerous historic and religious buildings. However the one held in the highest regard is the Holy Trinity Column, a UNESCO World Heritage site and biggest Baroque sculpture in the Czech Republic. Built in 1754 by local citizens and craftsmen, the column is seen as both a celebration of the Catholic Church and of Olomouc itself. The monument stands 115ft high and is topped by a gilded statue of the Holy Trinity. The most prominent church in Olomouc is Saint Wenceslas Cathedral, founded in 1107 and situated in the compound of the Olomouc Castle. The Cathedral has undergone many renovations throughout its history, resulting in many different architectural styles on display, from a Romanesque crypt to a Gothic cloister to Baroque chapels. Olomouc is also home to the Moravian Theatre, the Moravian Philharmonic and the second oldest university in the Czech Republic.

name: Krems an der Donau
description: Enjoyable eating and drinking, an atmospheric historical centre, rivers of top-quality wine from local vineyards and a couple of unexpected museums attract the tourist to Krems an der Donau. Krems is the ideal place for a relaxing stroll, stopping by the churches and museums, walking along the banks of the Danube and sampling the local tipples as you go — although no visitor should depart without first experiencing the legendary Marillenschnaps, the apricot brandy that the city is renowned for. With all this history, it may appear that Krems is dominated by the past. In reality, the city is also home to contemporary art and culture which play an important role in the city by adding variety and energy to public areas. One such example of this is the 'Arts Mile' containing the Caricature Museum, Kunsthalle Krems, the Lower Austrian Literature Center and various other cultural and diverse institutions.

name: Oranjestad
description: Oranjestad, literally translating to "orange city", lies on the southern coast of Aruba, and is a bustling harbor city that blends modernity and antiquity. Initially established in 1796 and known for raising and exporting horses to neighboring Curaçao and Jamaica, the city developed with Dutch Colonial architecture and has seen its old buildings and houses transform into colorful landmarks, such as the green "stadhuis" of the City Hall. Shoppers are spoilt for choice, with a mix of international luxury retailers, diverse boutiques, and dazzling jewelry stores. For a dose of history, take a visit to Fort Zoutman, the National Archaeological Museum, and the Willem III Tower, which was once a lighthouse and public clock tower. Nature enthusiasts will enjoy the nearby Renaissance Island, a 40-acre cay with private beaches, known for its stunning wildlife, including flamingos. Explore other attractions such as the marina, where sailboats, fishing charters, and cruise ships dock, and get a glimpse of the city's entertainment and leisure district, filled with restaurants, cafes, clubs, lounges, bars, and casinos.

name: Nordlingen
description: About 15 million years ago, a large meteor crashed into Bavaria, leaving a huge crater, and forming micro-diamonds due to the impact's immense pressure. In 898, the town of Nordlingen was established, built using the local, diamond-laced stone. Today' it's one of only three towns in Germany with an intact city wall - a landmark visitors can still walk along to this day. Filled with half-timbered houses and historic buildings, the symbol of the town is the 15th century St. George's Church, and its belltower 'Daniel'. It's estimated the stone used to make the church contains 5000 carats of diamonds. After admiring the beautiful baroque altar, topped by a 15th century crucifix, visitors can scale the tower for views of the crater, and the town below - a sight used in Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory.

name: Aranjuez
description: The area was acquired by the Order of Santiago in 1178, but Aranjuez didn't rise to prominence until the 15th century when it was made a royal site by Ferdinand and Isabella. In the 16th century, King Philip II ordered the construction of the royal palace. The town was reserved solely for nobility until the 18th century, when it was extensively redesigned. Today, Aranjuez offers visitors a wealth of beauty and history to explore. A walk through the Royal Palace is an opulent experience, combining Rococo, Elizabethan, Chinese and Moorish decor. The surrounding gardens were modeled on Versailles, and are filled with flowers, trees, fountains galore, and the splendid Casa del Labrador, all of which have transformed nature into another room of the palace. The city's Old Quarter is an Artistic Monument in its own right that's well-worth exploring for its Baroque town planning and noble architecture.

name: Hondarribia
description: While a small fishing village today, this sea-front town was an important stronghold from the Middle Ages through the French Revolution. Though town was captured by the French, the Treaty of Basel was signed before they could destroy the walls and castle that still stand in the historic quarter today. While admiring the town's historic architecture and colorful facades, visitors should keep an eye out for one more thing: Basque restaurants. In recent years, the village has attracted some of the best Basque chefs, making it perhaps the single best place to sample their signature cuisine. Hondarribia is overflowing with great restaurants, some of which have received a Michelin star, but almost any are going to be a pleasure for your palette.

name: Salamanca
description: Dating back to antiquity, the Carthaginians conquered the city in the 3rd century B.C. It then became a Roman settlement, and fell under Moorish control until the 11th century. While there are still some relics from its 2000 year history, such as the Roman bridge, the city's greatest assets are thanks to its famous university. Founded in the 12th century, shortly after the Christian reclamation, the university complex consists of buildings in Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque styles, constructed from the 15th to 18th centuries. But the city's landmarks aren't limited to the university, the round, romanesque San Marcos Church, 16th century palaces, and Plaza Mayor, with its galleries and arcades, are worth cutting class for.

name: Valence
description: Founded by the Romans, the southern city of Valence has developed into a listed City of Art and History, filled with monuments for visitors. For many, the marked paths along the city's canals, shaded by poplars and willows is a serene way to spend the day. Walking through the city, visitors are treated to an architectural timeline, starting with the 11th century Cathedral of St. Apollinaire, embellished with polychrome decorations, while the 16th-century House of Heads, marks the transition from Gothic to the Renaissance. The Museum of Valence, Art and Archaeology, is housed in the former episcopal palace next to the cathedral. An exciting mixture of old and new, modern art and architecture meet with historic relics, while the belvedere offering one of the best views in the city.

name: Cahors
description: Originally a Celtic settlement, after being conquered by the Romans, Cahors became a thriving urban center. In the Middle Ages, the city began a slow decline, and it became infamous because its bankers charged interest on loans. According to the Church, this was a sin - one the city became synonymous with. It even garnered the contempt of Dante, being pooled with the legendary Sodom for its wickedness. Today, the city, with its cobbled streets and half-timbered houses is anything but wicked. The UNESCO-listed Valentré bridge was built in the 14th century, and has an eleborate construction legend, which has earned it the nickname 'Devil's Bridge'. The charming old town is dominated by the 12th century Saint-Etienne cathedral. Nearby, the elaborate Olivier-de-Magny garden is lined by beautiful mansions. The city is famous for its red wine, which been produced since before Bordeaux even had a wine industry.

name: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal
address.addr1: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, Station Rd, Trevor Basin, Wrexham LL20 7TG, UK
description: Completed in 1805, the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal was intended to provide water to the planned Ellesmere Canal - a man-made waterway that would have connected Liverpool to the Welsh coal fields. Designed by Thomas Telford, the 18 kilometer long stone, wrought iron, and cast iron structure was not only a feat of engineering, but also a masterpiece of creative genius that has inspired similar projects all over the world. Narrow boats have been travelling down the aqueduct's canal since its inception, and today, its possible for visitors to book a ride on one. For those who'd prefer to go at their own pace, there's also a walking path next to the canal. Regardless of which option you opt for, expect stupendous views of the Welsh countryside from atop the engineering marvel.

name: Lang Son
description: The towering karst peaks that line the border between Vietnam and China has made the city of Lang Son the site of countless military engagements. Perhaps most famously, the destruction caused by the Chinese in 1979 was shown to international journalists as proof of Chinese aggression. In the hills overlooking this booming border town, you can still find a fortress dating back to the 16th century. Accessed by a long flight of stairs, an imposing wall blocks the pass between two cliffs while offering stupendous views of the region's dramatic landscape. Today, a colonial-era citadel still stands in the mountains above this booming border town. Alternatively, is the Nhi Thanh cave, which is actually a network of grottoes that have been used as Buddhist chapels since the 18th century.

name: City of Bath
description: Settled since the Neolithic Age, the ancient city of Bath was aptly named after its famous hot springs, which made the city a popular destination for the ancient Romans. During the 18th and 19th centuries, the city was rebuilt and remodelled in the elegant Georgian Style, and spread over the surrounding hills to create a 'garden city'. Jane Austen lived in Bath between 1801 and 1806, and though she apparently never liked the city, she used it as the setting for 2 of her novels. Bibliophiles can head o the Jane Austen Centre, where guides in period costume and a Regency tearoom bring her era to life. The grand Georgian architecture, particularly at the Circus and Royal Crescent, made Bath the destination for 18th century society. The Roman Baths are another unmissable attraction, giving visitors a look back in time, and providing a unique vantage of Bath's stunning Gothic Abbey.

name: Panajachel
description: Panajachel was founded by the Spanish in the 16th century after they and their Kaqchikel allies defeated the Tz'utujils. Following the Spanish conquest, Franciscans established a church and monastery on the lake, and the city of Panajachel grew around it. Today, "Pana" as it's often called is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country. Santander Street is the main tourist-centered thoroughfare, lined with handicraft stalls, bars, and restaurants. Calle Principal (Main Street) is more local-focused with the village market, and the striking 16th century Church of St. Francis of Asisi. Head down to the waterfront and you'll see why the city and surrounding area is so popular. Soak in the spectacular panoramic views of the San Pedro, Tolimán and Atitlán volcanoes across the lake, or if you want to get your feet wet, rent a kayak or paddleboard.

name: Sheikh Zayed Mosque
description: Designed by Syrian architect Yousef Abdelky, the Sheikh Zayed Mosque took 11 years to construct. The resulting 30 acre complex was worth the wait, as it's not only the largest mosque in the country, but an absolutely amazing monument that's rated as one of the world's top landmarks on Tripadvisor. The design blends styles from around the world, including taking inspiration from Persian and Indo-Islamic mosques, with Moorish arches and classical Arab minarets. The elegant individual decorative elements, such as the calligraphy covering the dome, and dainty flowers creeping up the columns complement the complex's scale. It's also home to the world's largest carpet, which took over 1,000 knotters 2 years to complete, and the world's largest chandelier, and the world's largest marble mosaic. Visitors are welcome to explore on their own, or join a free guided tour, though appropriate attire is required in both cases.

name: Glamis Castle
description: Dating back to the 11th century, Glamis Castle was given to the Lyon family in 1376, and has been their home ever since. The castle underwent several revisions, with much of what stands today dating back to the 17th century. Glamis' long history has given it plenty of time to collect its fair share of legends, from the murder of King Malcolm II, to a secret chamber inhabited by a monstrous creature. Said by Sir Walter Scott to be 'somewhat too near to the dead', enthusiastic and knowledgeable tour guides bring the secrets of one of Britain's most haunted castles to life. Today, the castle is still inhabited by the Earl and Countess of Countess of Strathmore and Kinghorne, and walking through the richly decorated rooms, it's readily apparent that Glamis isn't a museum but a fabulous family home.

name: Ohrid
description: Built mostly between the 7th and 19th centuries, Ohrid is one of the oldest human settlements in Europe, and its 10th century monastery is the oldest Slav monastery in the world. Housing over 800 Byzantine-style icons, its collection is second only to Tretiakov Gallery in Moscow. The Old Town's architecture is the best preserved ancient urban architecture in the Balkans. From the 10th century fortress on the hilltop visitors can see the whole of Lake Ohrid. Walking down through the cobbled streets, a cornucopia of churches and traditional restaurants beckon to passersby before giving way to lakeside cafes and deckchairs.

name: Salzburg
description: Salzburg is picture book Austria and no visitor should miss out on the view of the Old Town's kaleidoscope of domes and spires, the imposing castle fortress and the stunning alpine scenery of the mountains that lie beyond. The Old Town is a place where time easily slips by as you wander and wander. Check out Mozart's birthplace and soak up the grandeur of the churches and monumental squares that appear one after the other. The city also rewards those who are prepared to look slightly further afield. Meander the narrow side streets accompanied by the classical music that seems to waft from each window and stop by one of the city's café's to sample the mouthwatering cake and coffee. Let Salzburg work its charm on you to leave you with an unforgettable memory as you absorb its incredible skyline, the ever-present music and its thousand-year-old history.

name: Cala Figuera
description: In the southeast of Mallorca, Cala Figuera is a postcard-perfect fishing port, cradled by the crystalline waters of Caló d'en Boira and Caló d'en Busques. History whispers through Cala Figuera's narrow streets, with remnants dating back to 1306. The watchtower, Torre d'en Beu, erected in 1569 to fend off pirates, stands as a testament to the region's maritime heritage. The lack of sandy beaches spared Cala Figuera from overdevelopment, preserving its authentic allure. As the sun caresses white-washed facades and olive-green shutters, the town unfolds its maritime tapestry. From the 19th-century houses to the petite church-turned-restaurant La Petite Iglésia, Cala Figuera narrates its story through stone and sea. The scenic harbor is a photographer's paradise, capturing the essence of Mallorca with every frame. The turquoise waters, framed by cliffs and pine-draped terraces, create a canvas of serenity. Hiking trails along the coastline offer panoramic views, while Sa Torre d'en Beu, a 16th-century watchtower, stands sentinel against the backdrop of azure skies.

name: Five Sisters Zoo
description: The Five Sisters Zoo is home to 180 species of mammals, birds, and reptiles from around the world. Here you can come face-to-face with crocodiles, meerkats, otters, owls and and a variety of other exotic animals. As part of their mission to support animal welfare, the Five Sisters also provides a home to bears and lions rescued from the circus. Visitors can stroll along the nature trail to see Muntjac Deer, Barbary Sheep, Polecat, farm animals, Coati, and the Wildlife Pond, chill with capybaras and tapirs, or meet the cold-blooded residents in the Reptile House. With free keeper talks, as well as handling sessions and lemur feeds (for an extra fee), the Five Sisters has plenty of fun learning opportunities for animal lovers of all ages. For more information, please visit fivesisterszoo.co.uk

name: Villa de Leyva
description: While the Spanish founded Villa de Leyva in 1572, the area has been inhabited since the Pre-Herrera period, 3000 years ago. The town has remained largely unchanged since Colonial times, and its main square one of the largest in South America. Surrounded by white-washed buildings, and watched over by a charming church, the 14,000 square meter plaza is the perfect place to admire the town's historic buildings, backed by rolling hills. On the outskirts of town, is the El Infiernito archaeological site. A Muisca astronomical observatory and religious site, the Spanish were so affronted by the phallic statues that they called the place "Little Hell". Also nearby Villa de Leyva is the Casa Terracota, an unusual, two story home built entirely from clay (there aren't even supports), that the owner likes to call the largest piece of pottery in the world.

name: Garmisch-Partenkirchen
description: This valley town was two separate entities for centuries, with the older Partenkirchen dating back to around 15 AD. Periodic outbreaks of bubonic plague, and crop failures raised valley tensions, leading to a witch hunts. Between 1589–1596, over 10 percent of the population was burned at the stake or garroted. Werdenfels Castle, where the trials took place, became an object of superstitious terror and was dismantled in the 17th century. Its stones were used to build the baroque St. Martin's church. This replaced the nearby Gothic church, parts of which predated Christianity. The towns were joined by Adolf Hitler for the 1936 Winter Olympic games, and the stadium is open to the public. To best experience classic Bavaria, take a walk down cobblestoned Ludwigstrasse, with its vibrantly painted buildings and cozy shops.

name: Herzliya
description: Herzliya was founded in 1924 as a humble farming community, with 101 houses and 35 cowsheds. The settlement grew rapidly, being named a city when its population reached 25,000 in 1960. Today, its one of Israel's most affluent cities and a tech industry hub, hosting Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon offices. The city's laid-back affluence makes it an attractive alternative to Tel Aviv, offering every modern amenity without the hustle-and-bustle. For most people, the main attraction is the beach, which is clean, has a lifeguard, and if you're so inclined, a good area for surfing. The area around the beach is dotted with trendy restaurants, with the modern marina complex offering a pleasant place to stroll while scouting the eateries that line its boardwalk. If you need to escape the heat, collection at the Herzliya Museum of Contemporary Art criminally overlooked, offering cool AC and even cooler art.

name: The Great Hall
description: The Great Hall is all that remains of the once mighty Winchester Castle - a fortification founded by William the Conqueror in the 11th century and demolished following the English Civil War. Built by Henry III in the 13th century, it's considered one of the finest surviving aisled halls of that era. Today, the Great Hall offers visitors a look into Winchester's rich history through its architecture and museum. Commanding one wall of the Great Hall is the legendary Round Table, a 13th century reproduction of King Arthur's fabled furniture. Measuring 5.5 meters across and weighing 1,200 kg, the table was like made by King Edward I for a 'Round Table Tournament' held to celebrate his daughter's betrothal. The table's artwork, depicting the names of the legendary knights, was added in 1522 by Henry VIII for Holy Roman Emperor Charles V's state visit - that's Henry himself sitting in Arthur's seat above a Tudor rose.

name: Curepipe
description: Curepipe, Mauritius, epitomizes a harmonious blend of historical charm, scenic beauty, and vibrant culture. Nestled within Curepipe is the stunning Trou aux Cerfs, a dormant volcano that has transformed into a verdant crater lake. Visitors can ascend to the rim of this natural wonder and marvel at panoramic vistas of the surrounding landscapes, dotted with tropical foliage and cascading waterfalls. For those eager to delve into the town's rich history, Curepipe boasts an array of colonial-era architecture and heritage sites. Wander through its charming streets adorned with Victorian-style buildings, or explore the iconic Curepipe Botanic Gardens, where rare indigenous flora flourishes amidst tranquil ponds and winding pathways. Art enthusiasts will find solace in Curepipe's vibrant cultural scene, with galleries showcasing the works of local artisans and craftsmen. Additionally, the town's bustling markets offer a glimpse into Mauritian life, with colorful stalls brimming with spices, textiles, and handicrafts. Food lovers will be delighted by Curepipe's culinary offerings, from authentic Creole dishes to international fare served in charming cafes and restaurants. Savor exotic flavors and aromatic spices as you dine al fresco, soaking in the town's relaxed ambiance.

name: Tobati
description: Upon entering the town of Tobati, visitors are welcomed by three massive stone faces that have been skillfully carved into the cliffside. These particular Guaraní residents have long since passed but their story still prevails. They are believed to be the first settlers in the area and tell a tale of an indigenous town overtaken by Jesuit missionaries. The Jesuit influence is seen in the many Jesuit-Guarani statues and works of art. Today, Tobati is renowned throughout Paraguay for its woodworking, ceramics and sculptures. The main church in Tobati contains a wooden relic of the Virgin Mary said to be carved by a Guarani convert to Christianity who was pursued for his conversion. He was to be put to death when caught, but as he prayed to the Holy Mother, his pursuers overlooked him so he carved the statue to glorify her for her protection

name: Tonsberg
description: The city of Tonsberg dates back over a thousand years and is bursting with rich cultural heritage. Explore the remnants of its past at the Tønsberg Castle, a medieval fortress perched on a hill overlooking the town and the fjord, offers stunning panoramic views and insights into the region's history. Nearby, the Oseberg Ship Museum displays a remarkably well-preserved Viking ship, showcasing Tønsberg's connections to this legendary era. Tønsberg's coastal location adds to its charm, with beautiful beaches, marinas, and waterfront promenades. Enjoy leisurely strolls along the harbor, take boat trips to nearby islands, or partake in water activities such as sailing, kayaking, and fishing. Discover The World's End" in Færder National Park with its beautiful archipelago and unique coastal landscape, and for the best view of the city, visit the Castle rock tower for panoramic views.

name: Banska Stiavnica
description: This serene, untroubled town is the oldest mining town in Slovakia and was once known as 'Silver Town' as it sits on the Theresa Vein – a vast silver deposit discovered in the Middle Ages. There are many medieval sights to see around the town, from the sixteenth-century Old Castle, complete with medieval jail, through to Holy Trinity Square with its red Baroque sandstone Plague Column, which always seems to shine whatever the weather. To delve into what put the town into the history books all those years ago, then a trip to the Slovakia Open Air Mining Museum is a must. The museum offers a close to one-mile long tour where visitors can learn about the technical aspects of mining while descending deep into the earth. There is an underground exhibition which features the original motor from the mine shaft engine. Visitors are also provided with hard hats, coats, and lamps which, of course, provide an unmissable photo opportunity itself.

name: Lucerne
description: Beginning as a Benedictine monastery around 750 AD, the city proper didn't begin to develop until 1178, when Lucerne became independent from Murbach Abbey. In the 14h century, Lucerne was one of the four original cities to form the Swiss Confederacy, which put an end to Austrian rule. Following this victory, the city flourished, and was a popular place to settle in the 16th and 17th centuries. Today, its 17th century Jesuit church is regarded as Switzerland's first sacral Baroque building. Many of the buildings in the car-free old town are decorated with frescoes, as exemplified in the picturesque 'Weinmarkt' square. The town's defensive wall has been almost perfectly preserved, with only one tower not in its original state. The 14th century Chapel Bridge was constructed as a part of the city's fortification system, and is now the symbol of the city.

name: Villabassa
description: Dating back to the 19th Century, Villabassa has always been a haven for health and wellness. It is home to Italy's first outdoor kneipp Spa adventure village. This village has amusement for everyone, from mud baths, to dew treading, and arm and foot baths as well. Children step in a treasure trove of adventure with climbing trees, and slides. There's even knowledge to be had about plants and wildlife on the botanical trail. The open air inhalatorium, where people inhale nature's natural medicine, is the first of its kind in Italy. The Kurpark also offers tons of biking and hiking trails as well as recreation courts and outdoor BBQ. Once your mind is clear and centered, be sure to find the S. Stefano parish church for its beautiful altarpiece.

name: Nagano
description: Nagano, a captivating city nestled in the Nagano Prefecture, promises a plethora of attractions and experiences. Whether you're drawn by the allure of the famous Snow Monkey Park, the thrill of scaling breathtaking mountains, or the relaxation of authentic hot springs, Nagano has it all. With Lake Kizaki offering water activities and world-class ski resorts for skiing enthusiasts, your adventure is limitless. Set against the backdrop of majestic peaks and the confluence of the Chikuma River, Japan's longest, Nagano exudes natural beauty. The renowned 1400-year-old Zenko-ji temple stands as a National Treasure and an integral part of Nagano's history. Developed around this temple, Nagano grew from a temple town into the vibrant city it is today. Zenko-ji temple, dating back to the 7th Century, holds immense significance as it houses Japan's first Buddhist statue, the 'hibiutsu'. While the original statue is hidden, a replica is displayed to the public once every six or seven years during the Gokaicho ceremony. Another marvel is Matsumoto Castle, an elegant six-story castle dating back to 1592. As one of Japan's designated national treasures, it boasts stunning views of the Japanese Alps through its narrow windows.

name: Ayacucho
description: Founded by the Spanish in 1540 as San Juan de la Frontera de Huamanga, Simon Bolivar gave Ayacucho (literally "Dead Corner") its name after seeing the casualties of the last battle of the Peruvian War of Independence. In the 1980s, death again came to the region when the Shining Path, a Communist revolutionary group, used Ayacucho as its base of operations. Today, the city is slowly gaining outside attention again, and its colorful colonial buildings make the streets worth wandering. At the center of town, you'll find the Main Plaza, with its statue of Simon Bolivar, which is surrounded by buildings from the 16th and 17th centuries, including the impressive cathedral. Ayacucho's relative isolation has lead to a proud culture with its own distinctive crafts, cuisine, and some of the country's most unique festivals.

name: Tule Tree
description: With a trunk measuring 42.0 m (137.8 ft) around, the Tule Tree is the thickest tree in the world. In fact, it's so large that scientists had to run DNA tests to confirm it was a single specimen and not multiple trees grown together. For the Montezuma cypress to reach such a size, scientists estimate it is between 1,200 and 3,000 years old. Local tradition holds that it was planted around 1400 years ago by a priest of the Aztec wind god, and its location on an indigenous sacred site supports this theory. Along with its impressive girth, it's the gnarled trunk that has earned it the nickname "The Tree of Life", for the knots are said to be shaped like lions, jaguars, elephants, and untold other creatures.

name: Sant Jordi de ses Salines
description: Sant Jordi de ses Salines is the closest village to the airport in Ibiza, in close vicinity to the thrumming nightlife of other hotspots but far enough to escape it all. Its prime location in the Natural Park lends it access to three of the most famous beaches of Ibiza - Playa d'en Bossa, Es Cavallet and Salinas. The village is emanated by a spiritual feel with the presence of an imposing 15th century church, built for workers of the Salinera. The urban center buzzes with bars and restaurants that quickly get packed, while a second-hand flea market bustles in the old horse racing hippodrome. Browse through books, Indian jewelry, local food products and clothing as the jubilant beat of bongo drums rouse excitement in the markets. On Saturday evenings from July to August, enjoy a classic film with Spanish subtitles in the village square for free, while sipping on a digestif.

name: Thun
description: First settled around 2,500 BC, the Thun of today dates back to the 12th century. The Gothic castle dominating the town was constructed by the Dukes of Zähringen between 1180 and 1190. While its exterior exudes medieval power, the interior museum is all about medieval pomp. Here, visitors can marvel at the splendidly restored Knights Hall from the 12th century, or visit the historical museum, which exhibits artifacts from prehistory, medieval objects, as well as weapons and uniforms from the 18th and 19th century. In the medieval town center, visitors can enjoy the historic architecture built up to the banks of the Aare River, and visit the old wooden bridge, which sometimes has surfers riding its runoff, the town church with its tower dating back to about 1330, and the 16th century town hall.

name: Easby Abbey
description: Easby Abbey was founded in 1152 Roald, Constable of Richmond Castle, for Premonstratensian canons rather than monks. These white-clad clergymen lived in a community at the abbey, but also undertook preaching and pastoral work in the region. During the Middle Ages, the abbey was frequently targeted by Scottish raids, and was damaged in 1346 when the English army lodged there on its way to the Battle of Neville's Cross. Following Henry VIII's dissolution of the monasteries in the 1530s, the abbey was abandoned and fell into ruin. Today, the abbey ruins are free to explore, making for a pleasant, history-filled walk, with signposts giving more information about the abbey's past. At the nearby parish church you can find murals dating back to the 13th century.

name: Udine
description: The attractive university town of Udine has two small medieval canals flowing through its center. Its many cultural and architectural sights include Udine's Castle and Piazza Liberta'. The castello (castle) is a large 16th century palazzo which now holds the town's museums. A climb to the top of the hill is rewarded with one of the best panoramic views of the city. At the foot of the castle hills is Piazza Liberta', a beautiful Venetian-style square representing the heart of Udine. The historical center of town has many pleasant wine bars, open-air cafes, and restaurants with local cuisine.

name: Taranto
description: Established as a Greek colony by the Spartans in 706 BC, the ancient city was built over, leaving only a few ruins behind. At the end of the 19th century, a channel was dug to allow military ships to enter the harbour, transforming the old city into an island. Crossing the famous Swing Bridge, the streets of old Taranto feel lost in time - they've maintained the same layout since 967. The 10th century Cathedral of San Cataldo has maintained some of its original Byzantine mosaic floor tiles. Defending the harbour is the Aragonese Castle, also of Byzantine origin, which was reconstructed in the late 1400's by Ferdinand II of Aragon. Visitors enter the castle via a raised walkway before exploring the battlements, towers, and chapel. Just across the way in new Taranto, the former Convent of San Pasquale Alcantarini houses the National Archaeological Museum, which is renowned for its extensive collection.

name: Grutas de Cacahuamilpa
description: Grutas de Cacahuamilpa National Park was established as a National Park in 1936 and contains 90 large salons within its extensive cavern network. The massive, illuminated caves hold fascinating formations carved by nature from limestone; formations which give name to each of the rooms. There's a 'goat' salon, a 'throne' salon and a 'sleeping woman' salon to name just a few, each so-called for the interpretation of their unique concretions. The cave system is still live, meaning that water from the ground still filters into it through the two underground rivers constantly evolving the formations through erosion of the limestone. Tours of the cavern system run every hour and last for approximately two hours. If you prefer to remain above ground, the park has a botanical garden where you can learn about the native flora, rock-climbing options for adventurous visitors, or a tranquil natural swimming pool if you prefer to relax.

name: Argao
description: The little town of Argao remains mostly untouched by tourism, its seaside resorts catering to visitors looking to get away from the crowds. But the town center is worth exploring as well. The early 19th century Argao City Hall is the oldest municipal building in Cebu, and is an excellent example of a 'bahay na bato' - a building with a stone ground level and wooden upper story. Even older is the late 18th century St. Michael the Archangel Church, which features some intricate carvings on its facade, and colorful murals depicting scenes from the Bible on its ceilings. The church even still has a pulpit, and a pipe organ from the Spanish-era. If you're feeling peckish, be sure to stop at a bakery to try the town's torta, which is widely considered the best in Cebu. Made with coconut wine and cooked over coconut husks, these little cakes are best enjoyed with a cup of bittersweet hot chocolate.

name: Timgad
description: Founded by Roman Emperor Trajan around 100 CE, Timgad was a beacon of Roman culture on the plains of Algeria. Its 10,000 inhabitants were housed on a perfectly planned grid, with all the typical Roman amenities, like temples, bathhouses, a public library, markets, theater, and forum. Timgad's peaceful and prosperous existence was brought to an end in the 5th century when it was first sacked by the Vandals, and then destroyed by the Berbers. After a short Christian rebirth, the Arab invasion in the 8th century finished off Timgad for good. Preserved by the sands of time, Timgad offers an amazing look at Roman life. Not only will you see the last surviving ruins of a Roman library in North Africa, but if you scale the theater, you get a bird's eye view of the perfect city plan. Before entering the archaeological site, be sure to visit the museum to see artifacts and mosaics unearthed here!

name: Saint-Florent
description: Pleasure boats gently bob in the water and fresh seafood is served along the promenade of Saint-Florent's gorgeous marina, on the north-west gulf of Corsica. The city is nestled between the towering mountains of Cap Corse and the beachy Agriates desert, making for a spectacular view from any vantage point. After treating yourself to a gelato at the port, stroll into the Old Town centered around the Place Doria, where you can gather with locals to enjoy an espresso and join a game of petanque. A walk from town to the promontory will lead you to the 17th century citadel, built by the Genoese for the battle of control over Mediterranean waters. Saint-Florent is just a 10-minute drive from Corsica's best vineyards in Patrimonio, where the clay and limestone hills produce unique flavors that have put the region on the map for wine connoisseurs. Beaches of fine white sand near-unrivaled in the Mediterranean will beckon you for a day in the sun after wining and dining.

name: Albacete
description: The capital of the Castilla-La Mancha province is relatively young, dating back to only the 13th century or so. During Spain's most contentious years, the little village stayed loyal to the crown, and was richly rewarded for it. In 1888 it became the first provincial capital to receive electric street lights. Today, the city is famous for its festivals and non-stop nightlife, though its landmarks attest to its historical roots. The city's tourist office is housed in the Posada del Rosario, which offers a mix of Gothic, Mudejar, and Renaissance styles, along with helpful information about the city. The Catedral de San Juan Bautista was built over the course of five centuries, and now offers a smorgasbord of styles including a Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and Neo-Gothic. The Plaza de Altozano provides the opportunity to taste some local delicacies, including a wide array of pork dishes, and for the more adventurous, caracols.

name: Zahara de la Sierra
address.addr1: 11688 Zahara de la Sierra, Cádiz, Spain
description: Climbing up a forested hillside, this scenic town began as a Moorish outpost due to its strategic position between Ronda and Seville. The town has preserved its medieval labyrinthine urban layout, making it a scenic place to stroll through the narrow streets. Up the hill, the original 13th century castle was restored, with the remains of the medieval village still tucked behind its walls. The quaint town centre is surprisingly well-stocked with attractions, including the Santa María de la Mesa Church, the San Juan de Letrán Chapel, the Clock Tower and the Palominos Bridge.

name: Kilkenny
description: Kilkenny was founded in the 6th century as an ecclesiastical settlement, and was the site of Ireland's first witch trial in 1324. Between 1642 and 1649, Kilkenny was the home base for the Irish Catholic Confederation, which helped instigate the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland. Things have since settled down, and today the city is famed for its well-preserved architecture. Kilkenny's massive medieval castle is open to visitors to explore on a self-guided tour, and it's grounds are a popular destination for locals and tourists alike. Across town is the 13th century St. Canice's Cathedral, which is notable for its size, beautiful stained glass windows, and round tower - one of only two in all of Ireland that visitors can climb. Between these two landmarks is a jumble of cobbled streets and historic buildings known as the "Medieval Mile". For beer lovers, Kilkenny is home to Smithwicks, Ireland's oldest brewery, which is open to visitors on a guided tour.

name: Novara
description: Founded by the Romans, the town was sacked and destroyed several times during its early years, only to come back stronger than ever. Thanks to its long history, the city offers visitors architecture from the medieval period through the 19th century. This exemplified in the Piazza della Repubblica, which is home to historic buildings, the Town Museum and the Novara Museum of Modern Art. The Broletto is a picturesque group of buildings including the Town Hall, and a 15th century arcaded building with a courtyard. Dominating the piazza, the 19th century cathedral was built in the neo-classical style in homage to an ancient temple that stood on the site. Inside, visitors can enjoy Renaissance artwork, mosaics, cloisters, and medieval frescoes from the earlier 12th century church. Opposite the cathedral is the city's oldest building: a 5-6th century baptistry, home to some ancient frescoes depicting scenes from the apocalypse.

name: Vicuna
description: Vicuña is the main town in the sunny and colorful Elqui Valley, renowned for producing pisco, Chile's signature brandy. This inviting town boasts a picturesque main square dominated by the medieval-style Bauer Tower. Numerous cafes around the square offer Pisco Sour, and ice cream shops serve delightful flavors. Opposite the square, the Church of Mary's Immaculate Conception stands proudly, recognized as one of the most beautiful temples in Chile's Near North. Vicuña also features artisan markets, such as Aldea Elquina and Pueblito de Artesano, where visitors can purchase locally-crafted items and souvenirs. Don't miss the House of Culture and the Public Library, hosting art exhibitions, lectures, and cultural forums throughout the year. A unique attraction is the Mount Mamalluca Astronomical Observatory, located 9 kilometers north of the city center: it showcases some of the world's clearest skies, offering a memorable nighttime experience (reservations are required). Lastly, Vicuña celebrates its connection to the renowned Chilean poet, Gabriela Mistral, through a dedicated museum.

name: Cenote Las Mojarras
description: The Yucatan's famous cenotes come in all shapes and sizes, and the open-air Cenote Las Mojarras could easily be mistaken for a lake.Surrounded by jungle and completely exposed to the sun, the water is much warmer and more life-filled than you'll find in an underground cenote - in fact, Las Mojarras is a species of resident fish. Along with swimming in the refreshing water, the cenote offers a range of activities, from a rope bridge and zipline to ATV tours. If all that fun works up an appetite, there's a palapa restaurant on site where the local Maya prepare traditional food in an outdoor earth oven.

name: Nizwa
description: As Oman's capital in the 6th and 7th centuries, Nizwa is deeply connected to the country's Islamic roots. Even in the 1950s, Nizwa was so fiercely religious that British explorer Wilfred Thesiger's Bedouin guides wouldn't let him enter the city. Since then, Nizwa has warmed to outsiders and become the second most visited site in the country. It's still home to some of Oman's most renowned mosques, including the 9th century So'al Mosque. The main landmark for most visitors is the 17th century fort, which showcases traditional architecture while providing great views of the town and surrounding area. Adjacent to the fort is the Nizwa Souq, which is one of the most important in the country, offering everything from dates and spices to some of Oman's finest silver jewelry and curved daggers. North of the Old Town is the Falaj Daris Park, which is the best place to see Oman's UNESCO-listed falaj irrigation system.

name: Feira de Santana
description: Feira de Santana represents a fusion of history, culture, and commerce, making it a dynamic and significant city in the state of Bahia. Notable historic structures in Feira de Santana include the Church of Our Lady of Remedies, St. Ann Cathedral, various bandstands, the March 25th Philharmonic Society Building, and the charming Chapel of Saint Joseph of Itapororocas. In the realm of culture, Bahia boasts significant institutions like the Bahia Academy of Letters, the Bahia Geographical and Historical Institute, and the Bahia Institute of Music. The state has been home to prominent historical figures, including abolitionist and essayist Ruy Barbosa and renowned 20th-century novelist Jorge Amado. Notably, capoeira, a musical martial art with deep African roots, originated and thrived within Bahia's slave communities before spreading worldwide as a formal art form.

name: Nora
description: Founded by the Phoenecians on an even older indigenous settlement around the 8th century BC, Nora is said to be the first city in Sardinia. Under Punic, and later, Roman rule, it was a thriving trade town, being both the start of all roads on the island and the first stop on the sea route to Carthage. However, following the Muslim conquest of Carthage in 698, it lost its importance and was abandoned within a century. Today, the archaeological site is one of the most important in Sardinia, and it won't pull you too far from the beach. In fact, the ancient Punic cemetery is right on the shore, partially submerged. You'll also find the remains of four Roman thermal bathhouses, aqueducts, private houses, an amphitheater, and theatre, with a healthy smattering of mosaics. And with a large part of the city now underwater, you can even arrange for a snorkel tour!

name: Arles
description: Founded in the 7th century BC, Arles grew into a major Gallo-Roman city. As such, it was bestowed with the empire's integral structures, such as an arena and theatre. Today, these sites are integrated into the town's architecture, rather than sitting apart as they do in most places. The 1st century arena is still used for events today, as is the the amphitheatre, and the Musee Departemental Arles Antique allows visitors to examine ancient artefacts excavated in the area. The town's main square, the Place de la République, offers a snapshot of the city's history, with 19th-century fountain topped by a Roman obelisk, surrounded by the 17th century town hall, Sainte-Anne d'Arles Church, and 12th century Saint-Trophime d'Arles Cathedral and peaceful cloister. Van Gogh stayed here for 14 months, and producing 200 paintings in that time, the subjects of which many fans seek out during their visit.

name: Nin
description: The picture-perfect town of Nin was established 3,000 years ago. First an important trade center, the town developed to become the seat of Croatia's first bishopric and the seat of the Princes of Dalmatia. In the 9th century, Gregory of Nin began holding services in Croatian, in opposition to the Pope's required Latin, which was a major milestone for Croatian language and culture. The bishop is memorialized by statues in Nin and Split. On both, his big toe is polished gold because, it's said, if you rub it and make a wish, your wish will come true! Be sure to visit the remains of the Roman temple, St. Cross Church (the smallest cathedral in the world), St. Jakov Church, and St. Anselmo Cathedral. Additionally, Nin is well-known for its therapeutic mud which has been used for health purposes for many years.

name: Pensacola, FL
description: Located at the westernmost portion of Florida, just at the frontier with Alabama, Pensacola is the largest city between New Orleans and Tampa. Predating St. Augustine by over half a decade, Pensacola was the first Spanish settlement in the contiguous US. But it had to be abandoned for over a century, so doesn't get the title of America's longest-inhabited city. Over the course of history, it's changed hands between the Spanish, French, British, Confederates, and finally, the United States, with each era bearing a cultural influence. Visit the Saenger Theatre for a taste of Baroque Spanish-inspired architecture as well as a taste of culture! Plaza Ferdinand VII is also a testament to the Hispanic history of the city. Their French heritage is on especially proud parade during Pensacola's Mardi Gras. The Naval Aviation Museum makes Pensacola a destination for military buffs, with over 150 restored aircraft and great educational opportunities! And, of course, there's Pensacola's famous beach where you can have some!

name: Berat
description: First inhabited by Greek tribes in the 6th century BC, Berat is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities. Today, the city is an architectural melting pot, with Byzantine churches and Ottoman mosques existing in harmony. Berat Castle, which was destroyed by the Romans in the 2nd century BC, has recovered over the centuries, and visitors can tour the ancient inner castle, or wander the thriving Kala neighbourhood within the castle's walls. The Muslim 'Mangalem Quarter' is home to the 16th century Sultan' Mosque - one of the oldest in Albania. Across the river, the city's iconic white houses, which earned it the nickname of 'The City of 1000 Windows', is the old Ottoman Christian quarter.

name: Cochabamba
description: Sprawled across a fertile valley, Cochabamba was founded by the Spanish as an agricultural center in the 16th century, and to this day, is known as "the granary of Bolivia". Every visit should include a cable car up to Cochabamba's proudest landmark - the giant Cristo statue (which locals will proudly tell you is 44cm taller than Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer). As with most other cities in South America, the heart of Cochabamba is the airy plaza. Admire the elegant cathedral before heading to the Convento de Santa Teresa for a tour, which includes a great view from its roof. There are also some worthwhile museums, like the Museo Archeologico, and the lavish Palacio Portales, the grandiose former home of a tin baron. For something more down to earth, join one of the two-hour street art bicycle tours. And, of course, being the country's major food producer, Cochabamba is a great place to eat - head to the market on Calle 25 de Mayo and gorge on local fare alongside hordes of hungry locals.

name: Stirling Castle
description: First recorded in the 12th century, Stirling Castle was a favorite residence for the Stewart dynasty. Nearly everything seen today was built between 1490 and 1600 by kings James IV, James V, and James VI in an eclectic mix of English, French and German influences. During its heyday, the castle hosted some of the Stewart's grandest celebrations, including the coronation of Mary, Queen of Scots, while the extensive 18th century Outer Defences allude to its important military role. Today, the castle's rich history is brought to life by costumed characters, and knowledgeable guides. After getting a taste of castle life in the royal bedchambers and great kitchens, you can also visit the Regimental Museum to learn about the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders or the Tapestry Studio to learn about the 13 year project to create a new set of Unicorn tapestries. For more information, please visit stirlingcastle.scot

name: Volubilis
description: Founded around the 3rd century BC, Volubilis flourished as a Roman outpost from the 1st to 3rd centuries. After being reclaimed by local tribes it remained inhabited for another 700 years, even serving as the seat of the Idrisid dynasty before they relocated to Fez. Amazingly, Volubilis remained in good condition until the mid-18th century, when it was devastated by an earthquake and subsequently quarried for to build Meknes. Even so, Volubilis is recognized by UNESCO for being being so well preserved. Though only half the site has been excavated, visitors can still find the remains of a 3rd century basilica and a triumphal arch, and plenty of other building foundations. However, the highlights are the beautiful mosaics that have been preserved in-situ. While some have been moved to archaeological museums, the 'Labors of Hercules', and remaining mosaics at the House of Venus or stunning.

name: Gjovik
description: With Lake Mjøsa sparkling along its countryside, Gjøvik is known for its idyllic setting, rich cultural heritage and vibrant atmosphere. The town owes much of its early growth to local glassworks, with the Gjøvik Glassverk offering fascinating insight to the region's history of the craft inside a glassworks factory turned museum. Nature lovers will be in their element in Gjøvik, with Lake Mjøsa being a popular location for fishing and leisure boat trips. Visit the Gjøvik Olympic Hall, built for the 1994 Lillehammer Olympics as a spectator hall inside of a mountain. See the distinctive red brick exterior and intricate interior design of the iconic Gjøvik Church before heading to the Gjøvik Olympic Cavern Hall for a unique underground concert venue where you might catch a performance or two. Sample traditional Norwegian dishes at one of the many restaurants and cafes while enjoying the warm and welcoming atmosphere of Gjøvik.

name: Saint Pierre
description: Saint Pierre, nestled on the southwestern coast of Réunion Island, is a vibrant coastal town that offers visitors a delightful blend of Creole culture, stunning beaches, and exciting outdoor activities. One of the main attractions of Saint Pierre is its picturesque waterfront promenade, where visitors can stroll along the palm-fringed esplanade and soak in the breathtaking views of the Indian Ocean. The town's lively harbor is also a hub of activity, with fishing boats bobbing in the water and local vendors selling fresh seafood. For those looking to explore the town's rich history and culture, Saint Pierre offers several intriguing landmarks and attractions. The Musée Régional de Saint Pierre, housed in a beautifully restored colonial building, showcases exhibits on the island's history, art, and heritage. Visitors can also explore the charming Creole houses and historic monuments that dot the town's streets, offering glimpses into Réunion's past. Outdoor enthusiasts will find plenty to love about Saint Pierre, with its pristine beaches, clear turquoise waters, and abundance of water sports opportunities. Whether it's swimming, snorkeling, diving, or simply soaking up the sun on the sandy shores, there's no shortage of ways to enjoy the island's natural beauty.

name: Brewers Bay
description: Relax on a crescent of serenity at Brewers Bay, a captivating haven on Tortola's north shore in the British Virgin Islands. Immerse yourself in the vibrant marine life with snorkeling adventures in the nearby coral reefs, or simply unwind on the shore and soak up the warmth of the Caribbean sun. For those seeking a bit of excitement, kayaking and paddleboarding opportunities abound, allowing you to explore the bay's pristine waters at your own pace. As the sun sets, casting a golden glow across the horizon, Brewers Bay transforms into a magical paradise, inviting visitors to gather around bonfires or enjoy romantic beachside picnics under the starlit sky.

name: Rio Claro Valley
address.addr1: Reserva Natural Cañon Del Río Claro
description: The Rio Claro Valley is a small private nature reserve just a few hours from the hustle and bustle of Medellín. Here, the cool waters of the Rio Claro flow through a marble canyon that over millions of years has transformed from sea bed to dense rainforest. Labelled as one of Colombia's endemic hotspots, the park is home to hundreds of different species, ranging from the brilliant blue Morpho butterflies to howler monkeys and otters. Bird watchers flock here for the 350 avian species that call the park home, several of which are endangered. The park and its eco-lodge are popular among nature-loving Colombians and foreigners alike who come to enjoy the scenery and the many outdoor activities offered here, from rafting down the river through exploring the Cueva de los Guacharos. Activities must be booked in advance, so you'll want to contact the park before your visit at http://www.rioclaroreservanatural.com/index.html

name: Malia
description: The seaside resort town of Malia is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Crete, famous for its beautiful beach and wild nightlife. But look past the wild reputation, and you'll find a town of surprising charm. In the old village of Malia, the narrow streets are still lined with traditional houses and dotted with historic churches like Agios Nektarios with its vibrantly painted interior and the Church of St. George at Loutres, which was built to protect the locals from the elves. The 14th century church of Panagia Galatiani is another standout, particularly because it used milk instead of water for the mud in its construction. And then there's the Palace of Malia just outside of town. The third-largest Minoan palace in Crete, it's said to have been built by the legendary King Sarpedon, the son of Zeus and goddess Europa, and brother of King Minos. While there's limited signage, it's still fascinating to see architectural elements that are nearly 5000 years old (we'd recommend having this website on hand when visiting http://www.minoancrete.com/malia.htm).

name: Franz Josef
description: Franz Josef Glacier, named by German explorer Julius von Haast in honour of the Austrian Emperor, is the most popular glacier in New Zealand. While being steeper than its neighbour, Fox Glacier, the steeper drop creates more dramatic scenery and ice formations. Although you can no longer climb the ice directly from the valley floor, if you're feeling up for the challenge you can take a heli hike from the township for an unforgettable experience (allow 4 hours for this). Alternatively a 90 minute round trip from the car park will take you to the foot of the glacier for some amazing photo opportunities. From the township itself you can opt for a guided walk through the lush rainforest (which until recently touched the glacier itself, one of only three places in the world to do so), again to the glacier foot, which will take you around 3 hours.

name: Ex Convent of Guerrero Cuilapam
description: The Ex Convent of Guerrero Cuilapam was founded in the 1550s by four Dominican monks. Even after a century of construction, their grand vision was left partially incomplete when work on the site was halted in 1650. Built from quarried green stone and river rocks, from a distance the convent looks more like a castle, complete with cylindrical towers. Upon closer inspection, detailed murals and frescoes reveal a masterful blending of indigenous and Christian symbology, some of which are still visible even in the roofless basilica. The beautiful cloisters (the only part of the convent with an entrance fee) not only showcase multiple archaeological styles and historic frescoes, but a statue of the revolutionary leader of Mexican independence and ex President of Mexico, General Vicente Guerrero, who was executed by firing squad here on Valentine's Day in 1831.

name: Skocjan Caves
description: This natural phenomenon is a system of limestone cave passages (6.2km long) that have been carved out by the Reka River. Candlelit steps (500 of them) and pathways guide you to this enormous underground space. Revel in diverse stalactite forms including limestone pools and larger stalactites. Skocjan caves also houses gorgeous natural bridges, lakes, waterfalls, and gorges, as well as a surprising amount of natural flora. The temperature in the caves is a constant 12 degrees celsius, so a jacket or sweater is recommended.

name: San Marino
description: The dimensions in size are the only thing small about San Marino. This independent state boasts one of the highest GDP per capita, no national debt, and a budget surplus. But more than two million visitors a year don't flock to San Marino to enjoy its low unemployment rate; they come to view the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Monte Titano. Monte Titano stands 2,425 ft above sea level and has the most terrific fortress at one out of its three peaks. On another peak lies Guaita, with its castle and tower. The astonishing views from any of its peaks are sure to be crossed off your bucket list.

name: Serravalle Designer Outlet
description: Serravalle Designer Outlet is a sprawling shopping village inspired by classic Italian architecture. The first designer outlet in Italy, Serravalle is a shopper's paradise, offering top designers like Prada, Burberry, Bulgari, and Dolce & Gabbana, to favorites like Nike and Desigual. Discounts range from 35-70%, and the outlet will sometimes even stock current season collections! While you shop, you can also enjoy free wifi, and even borrow a portable charge if your phone needs some juice. If you're feeling drained yourself, there's a selection of restaurants to choose from. To complete your new look, you can even stop by the Go Coppola hairdresser. For more information, please visit mcarthurglen.com/en/outlets/it/designer-outlet-serravalle

name: Punta del Este
description: This resort city has many well-deserved comparisons - Saint Tropez of South America, Monaco of the South, and Pearl of the Atlantic. Warm but not oppressive, the climate is a haven for those who enjoy the seaside. It's two beaches each have something to offer - La Brava's rough waves for windsurfing, and La Mansa's sheltered waters for bathing. It's not only about sea and sand. The streets have a fascinating contrast of colonial and modern buildings, la Gorelo is a glamorous avenue day and night, and high-class restaurants are plentiful. It is a city of art too. Chilean artist Mario Irarrázabal's "The Hand" sculpture rising out of the sands of Brava beach has become a symbol of the resort, and the Pablo Atchugarry Foundation, one of the leading artistic institutions of Uruguay, which hosts art exhibitions, ballets, and concerts during the summer, and is surrounded by a 30-hectare sculpture park.

name: Johor Bahru
description: Johor Bahru, or JB for short, was in 1855, and less than a decade later, was made the capital of the Sultanate of Johor. As the last Malaysian city before Singapore, JB has long been known as fiercely proud, but hectic border town. However, recent renovations and the Iskandar development project are radically changing Malaysia's second largest city. Tradition is still a major part of the city's identity, and visitors can explore Jalan Tan Hoik Nee, one of JB's oldest neighborhoods, to enjoy a spectacular mix of Chinese and Colonial architecture. Then there are the centuries-old temples and churches, the Sultan's former palace, and even the 80-year-old Salahuddin Bakery where you can experience the city's proud history. Food and shopping are two of JB's other main draws, and even Singaporean's flock here for the malls and premium outlets, but if you're in town after dark, the Pasar Karat flea/night market is the place to be.

name: Luxembourg City
description: Starting as a Roman fortified tower built to watch of the crossing of two Roman roads, For much of its history, Luxembourg's capital was best known as a fortress, which was passed between the European powers, each of whom reinforced and expanded its fortifications. By the 19th century, Luxembourg City was perhaps the mightiest fortress in the world, and was so desirable it almost caused a war between the Netherlands and Prussia. Today, visitors can walk through the picturesque Old Town, where, along with historic buildings like the beautiful Ducal Palace, you'll find a surfeit of strange spaces, such as the Alzette gorge's labyrinth of military tunnels, which now offer stupendous views over the town center.

name: Cerro Tres Kandu
description: Cerro Tres Kandu, also known as Cerro Pero, is the highest peak in Paraguay, and was a historically important holding to the Armed Forces of Paraguay because of its strategic location. It was used for radio communication facilitated by the national electric company. Today, the radio installations are no longer in operation and the trails are accessible to visitors for a small fee. To reach the top, expect to spend around 1.5 hours of navigating the moderately difficult and, at times, steep terrain. Take a break at one of the viewpoints on the way to the peak to take in the stunning panoramic views of the coloful scenery below.

Here, brands like Brooks Brothers, Calvin Klein, Furla, and Molton Brown are offered at discounts of up to 60% off their RRP. If you get tired of shopping, you can relax and recharge, you can enjoy the authentic Italian cuisine served at L'Officina Restaurant, or fresh, seasonal fare at the elegant Le Pain Quotidien boulangerie. For more information, please visit www.kildarevillage.com

name: Tivoli
address.addr1: Tivoli, Metropolitan City of Rome, Italy
description: Perched on the falls of the Aniene river, Tivoli offers a wide view over the Roman campagna. Dating back as early as the 13th century BC, this town is filled with a long list of must-see ruins, temples, and villas. Stroll through the narrow streets and take in the striking beauty of this quiet hillside town. While visiting Tivoli, you will have the chance to see - among many things – Villa Adriana, a large archaeological complex once used as a retreat for Roman Emperors; Villa Gregoriana, a park located at the feet of the town's ancient acropolis, commissioned by Pope Gregory XVI in 1835; Rocco Pia, a 15th century fortress; and the ruins of the Temple of Vesta, a 1st century BC Roman temple. Tivoli offers the perfect blend of natural and man-made beauty, and is a must-see when visiting the area.

name: Manzanillo
description: With 350 days of sunshine, visitors can enjoy Manzanillo's expansive beaches and warm Pacific waters anytime of year. Known as the "Sailfish Capital of the World," fishermen from all over the world flock to the sea and surrounding area to claim the title for biggest catch. The town is made up of two crescent-shaped bays that create excellent snorkeling and scuba diving conditions - take a dive and discover a colorful reefs and an abundance of flashy fish! Miramar Playa offers surfers a chance to hang loose or just hang out. On dry land, grab a bucket of cold beers at a local Botanero (open-air bar) and mingle with locals while enjoying some typical Mexican music. Check out the ecological park Natura Camp to hike the trails, zipline or simply enjoy the sounds of nature. Make sure to purchase tickets in advance to Natura Camp and spend a total of at least two hours in Manzanillo to get the most out of the the park stop. Fun times await in Manzanillo.

name: Aveiro
description: Established during Roman times, Aveiro served as a major port until a storm raised a sandbar along its coast in the 16th century. The sandbar not only blocked the port, but the resulting stagnant water brought disease and the population was reduced by half within two decades. Today, Aveiro upholds an ancient fishing tradition as well as boasting thriving salt and seaweed industries. Visitors may wander along the canals, making their way to the fish market to enjoy a view of colorful tiled cottages facing each other across the canal. The gonda-like boats to be found there, known as "barcos moliceiros", are traditional flat-bottomed boats used for fishing and collecting seaweed from the lagoons. It is also worth stepping into the Convento de Jesus to admire its renaissance cloisters and 17th century gilded carvings. Though not exactly Venice, this Portuguese fishing town certainly has a unique charm of its own.

name: Fox Glacier
description: The Fox Glacier (also known as Te Moeka o Tuawe) is located in Westland Tai Poutini National Park on the South Island of New Zealand. This impressive mass of ice is 36 square kilometers, which is larger than the city of Christchurch, and 13 kilometers long. During the last ice age, this glacier reached even further than the coastline of today. Glaciers obviously move quite slowly, but this one moves 10 times faster than most around the world, causing its terminal face appearance to change year by year. This is a great hike which has delicate beauty through a valley carved by the travelling ice. Perfect for both experienced and inexperienced hikers, you shouldn't pass up an opportunity to experience this amazing natural wonder.

name: Rainbow Mountain Pitumarca
description: Located 5,200 meters above sea-level, Rainbow Mountain, or Vinicunca, is an unusual geological phenomenon where different types of stone have formed in layers, creating different color stripes. While not as colorful as brochures and Instagram will have you believe, the mountain's unique mineralogical composition is still one of Peru's natural wonders, and makes for some breathtaking photos - especially with some enhancement or a filter. You'll have to put in some effort to reach it though, as it's relatively isolated - which explains why it was only discovered by tourism in the mid-2010s (the rise of Instagram might also have had something to do with it…). Be ready for about a 2-hour uphill hike on an at-times unkept trail at high altitude - you'll need appropriate footwear, and warm, waterproof clothing. It's demanding, but if you remember that this is an amazing geological site and not a rainbow-turned-to-stone, it's well worth it.

name: La Orotava
description: La Orotava sits like a gem at the northern crown of Tenerife, bordering mountainous inland terrain and bursting with lavish aesthetics. Its old town was declared a National Artistic Historic Site in 1976 and is the most preserved in all of the Canary Islands. The meticulous design of architects Maffiotte and Manuel de Oráa is open for admiration in the Town Hall Square of La Orotava, which fills with religious iconography made of flowers and volcanic sand during the festivities of Corpus Christi in June. The historic landmark Casa de los Balcones features famous Canarian balconies jutting from its three-story facade, built in 1632. Survey the wooden exterior from the courtyard for free or buy admission to view the works of artist Eladia Machado inside. Take a walk through Hijuela del Botánico, a public garden filled with trees and flowers from all over the world. Take in views of the sea and old town from Victoria Garden, a spectacular hillside park complete with fountains, an 1800's mausoleum and gorgeous tiered terraces.

name: Anthony Quinn Bay
description: Anthony Quinn Bay, situated on the captivating island of Rhodes in the Greek Islands, is a hidden gem awaiting discovery by travelers seeking paradise on Earth. Enclosed by rugged cliffs adorned with lush vegetation, Anthony Quinn Bay boasts crystalline waters that shimmer under the Mediterranean sun, beckoning visitors to indulge in its refreshing embrace. The bay's secluded cove provides an intimate setting for sunbathing on its pebbled shores or snorkeling amidst vibrant marine life that thrives in its underwater realm. For the adventurous souls, Anthony Quinn Bay offers opportunities for exploration both above and below the water's surface. Kayaking along its tranquil waters allows for a closer encounter with the bay's natural splendor, while diving enthusiasts can delve into its depths to discover ancient rock formations and hidden sea caves teeming with marine biodiversity. Those seeking respite from the sun can retreat to the shade of the bay's surrounding cliffs, where clusters of pine trees offer a cool refuge and panoramic views of the Aegean Sea.

name: Nakuru
description: Nakuru, Kenya's fourth largest city, is quickly transforming from provincial to pleasant, with gentrification already bestowing it with the better aspects of Nairobi. While the city has its fair share of cafes (Moca Loca is worth seeking out), galleries, and museums, the real attractions lay outside of town. At Hyrax Hill, you'll find a prehistoric site, and museum exhibiting artefacts from civilizations that are up to 3000 years old. The Menengai Crater and Mau Mau Cave are perfect places to visit if you're looking for a natural excursion (be sure to get a local guide). The crater was formed over 1 million years ago, and it has not erupted in over 350 years. The city is also a great base for visiting Lake Nakuru National Park, one of the finest in the country, which is famed for its flocks of flamingos, black and white rhinos, lions, leopards, hippos, and endangered Rothschild's giraffes.

name: Batu Caves
description: Though the Batu Caves were officially discovered by American naturalist William Hornaday in 1878, they were known to locals and guano-collecting Chinese settlers for centuries. Shortly after, Indian trader K. Thamboosamy Pillai promoted the caves as a place of worship because of their shape, and had a giant statue of Lord Murugan consecrated in 1890. A popular attraction year-round, the caves attract hundreds of thousands of pilgrims during the three-day Thaipusam festival, in which a procession of devotees walk from Kuala Lampur's Chinatown. Along with the giant statue, the cave exterior is home to legions of bold monkeys, while inside the caverns, visitors will find bats, insects, and perhaps one of the world's rarest spiders. Please note: the caves are accessed by over 200 steps, and entry is subject to availability. For more information, please visit http://www.tourism.gov.my/en/my/places/states-of-malaysia/selangor/batu-caves

name: Vaxholm
description: Vaxholm and its cobbled sloping streets unravel across islets connected by bridges, offering a unique and charming Swedish experience hard to find elsewhere. It was established in 1558 when King Gustav Vasa bought some farmland, and later became a popular spa town in the 1880s. One of the main attractions in Vaxholm is the Vaxholm Fortress, a historic military fortress that was built in the 16th century to protect Stockholm from naval attacks. The fortress has been well-preserved and now offers guided tours and exhibitions on Swedish military history. Vaxholm's oldest buildings stand just north of the town hall, including a typical 19th century fisherman's house which has become a charming cafe. You can make a visit to the nearby Bogesund Island, with beautiful nature trails surrounding a 17th century castle, and stop for a swim at Tenöbadet beach.

name: Nova Gorica
description: Nova Gorica offers a rich selection of annual events including concerts, festivals, and exhibitions. It also hosts one of the three national theaters in Slovenia. Many wellness and entertainment centers (casinos) can be found in this vibrant city. Despite being established in 1952 after WWII, the town exudes soul and a pleasant, lively atmosphere.
