name: Zamora
description: History shows that Zamora was first settled in the 1500s after a period of several migrations into and out of the region. Luckily for the dominating Spaniards, the fertile swampland was well-suited to agriculture and ultimately allowed the region to flourish through times of peace. Today, a number of beautiful historic buildings in the city center draw in visitors while the people and food keep them there. Grab a seat and people watch in the main plaza while vendors offer up fresh fruits and other sweet treats then stretch your legs and wander around to admire the well-preserved Spanish Colonial buildings. At the stop of the plaza, the striking neo-gothic Cathedral of Our Lady Guadalupe juts 105 meters into the sky and is a must-see, or rather, a can't miss!

name: Pamukkale
description: Pamukkale and Hierapolis are a double-threat, showcasing both a stunning natural landscape and historic ruins. Pamukkale (Cotton Palace) is a series of white travertine basins formed over millennia by mineral-rich hotspring waters. Visitors are free to walk through the basins (barefoot only), and bath in the vibrant blue waters before heading to the 2nd century BC spa town of Hierapolis. Built by the Attalid kings, this Grecco-Roman retreat became an important Christian site after St. Philip was martyred here in 80 AD. Several ruins still survive, including the city's monumental arch, necropolis, and nymphaeum. However the most impressive are the theatre, with its intricate backdrop, and 'Cleopatra's pool', where you can bathe among fallen columns.

name: Cali
description: Founded by Sebastián de Belalcázar in 1536, Cali remained a relatively quiet agricultural city for much of its history. However, as the only major Colombian city with access to the Pacific, Cali now has one of the country's fastest-growing economies. Cali's historic center, known as the Barrio San Antonio, has become the hippest place in town, with trendy cafes, bars, and restaurants taking up residence in its charming colonial buildings. While walking the streets, you're bound to notice the beating heart of the city - the irresistible rhythm of salsa. Known around the world as the salsa capital, Cali is filled with dance clubs, dance schools, dance shows, and impromptu street dances. There's even a salsa circus (that you'll want to reserve tickets in advance for). Of course, if the rhythm doesn't move you, there's a few more downtempo places to visit, like the cat-sculpture-filled Cat Park, or the 26-meter-tall El Cristo Rey.

name: Jerico
description: Founded in 1850, Jerico is best known as the birthplace of Madre Laura, Colombia's first patron saint. So it should be no surprise that religion plays a major role in the city, with a giant Jesus statue watching over the town, and the 16 churches chiming every 15 minutes. From the main square and elegant cathedral, you can dive into a maze of cobbled streets, like the famed Street of 100 Steps, or the vibrant artist community in Bomarzo, to see the colorful colonial architecture that earned it a spot as one of Colombia's 17 Heritage Towns. Regardless of where your feet take you, keep your stomach ready - Jerico is said to have the best street-food in the country, be it cookies and wine from the convent, to honey and guava Luisas, which are only baked here. If you're looking for a functional souvenir, the many-pocketed Carriel bag, a national symbol, is only made here.

name: Coventry
description: Founded by Earl Leofric and his wife Lady Godiva as a Benedictine monastery, Coventry quickly grew into one of England's largest and most important medieval cities. By the 18th century, it was a center for manufacturing, starting with watches, then shifting gears to bicycles, cars, and planes. Today, Coventry's rich heritage is preserved through a variety of museums and monuments. The remains of the city's 14th century Cathedral with its 90 meter spire stand next to its modern replacement, which is considered one of the finest 20th century structures in the country. Next door, the 14th century St. Mary's Guildhall was where Mary Queen of Scots was imprisoned. At the Coventry Transport Museum you can see its automotive legacy first hand. Music fans won't want to miss the Coventry Music Museum, which celebrates the city's music scene in all its forms - from the Specials to John Lennon and Yoko Ono acorn-planting visit.

name: Corinium Museum
description: The Corinium Museum, can trace its origins to the discovery of two Roman mosaics in 1849. After this, interest in archaeology in Cirencester ballooned, and the first museum opened a few years later. Today, the Corinium museum houses over 60,000 historic artefacts from around the region, dating back to the Neolithic age. The principal collection still consists of finds from the Roman town of Corinium, including the famed Four Seasons and Dog mosaics. In fact, the Corinium Museum houses the UK's richest collection of Roman relics outside of London. Along with these Roman finds, visitors can discover Prehistoric tools, Anglo Saxon burial treasures, Medieval sculptures, Civil War hoards, and elegant Victorian costumes. For more information, please visit coriniummuseum.org

name: Piran
description: Part of the Venetian empire from the 13th century to the late 18th century, Piran is the best-preserved town on the Adriatic. Its medieval Venetian Gothic architecture and narrow old town streets attract visitors from all over the world. Piran is home to the well-known violinist and composer Giuseppe Tartini, whom the main square has been named after. A statue erected in his honor can also be found in the square. Enjoy the rich cultural heritage of this small seaside "dream" town.

name: Banos
description: Banos de Agua Santa is named for the apparent healing properties of the city's many hot springs due to the many minerals they contain. A city of natural beauty, it sits at the base of the Tungurahua volcano which has been slowly bubbling away since it erupted in 1999. Banos is a religious centre for Roman Catholics with many reported sightings of the Virgin Mary, most notably at local waterfalls. She can be thanked for her miracles at the Basílica de la Virgen del Rosario de Agua Santa in the city's central plaza. Banos is Ecuador's capital of adventure and the El Pailon del Diablo - the Devil's Cauldron - waterfall is a popular spot for hikers. The most famous hot spring is Termas de la Virgen, so-called as the Virgin Mary is said to have bathed there herself. They have cold pools and hot ones, heated by the neighbouring volcanoes. Whichever you choose, you'll be sure to leave with a spring in your step!

name: Moustiers Sainte-Marie
description: Built high up a cliff, Moustiers-Sainte-Marie owes its founding to a group of monks in the 5th century. With a magnificent mountainous backdrop and waterfall in the heart of town, it's no wonder Moustiers has been named one of France's most beautiful villages. The town's historic streets and quiet squares are dominated by the Romanesque bell tower of the 12th century Church of Notre-Dame de l'Assomption. While exploring the charming streets, and admiring the endless bounty of beautiful natural views, visitors will also find a slew of pottery workshops making the town's famous fayence. For a truly breathtaking view of the town and countryside, a set of stairs leads even higher up the cliff to the 12th century Chapel Notre-Dame-de-Beauvoir.

name: Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden
address.addr1: Warner Drive, Hertfordshire, Abbots Langley, Leavesden WD25 7LP, UK
description: The Warner Bros. Studios in Leavesden was originally a World War II airplane factory - the world's largest factory by volume, though the site was eventually abandoned as England's manufacturing industry declined. In 1994, when the huge space was gutted and transformed into a film studio for the James Bond film GoldEye. A succession of major films followed, but it was Harry Potter that would become the studios' golden ticket. Over the next 10 years, every Potter film was shot here, and the production crews had the foresight to save many of the sets and props in case they were ever needed. The result was an astounding collection of artefacts that were made into a permanent exhibition for fans of the series. Visitors can join a guided tour and step into the Hogwarts Great Hall, the Forbidden Forest, Diagon Alley, and of course, Platform 9 ¾, as well as see costumes, as well as props, and even magical creatures like Buckbeak and Aragog. Please note: tickets must be booked in advance at https://www.wbstudiotour.co.uk/

name: Trujillo
description: Settled since prehistoric times, the town fell during the Muslim invasion in the 8th century and remained in their control for centuries. A walk around the castle perimeter, and it's easy to see why Christian forces considered it a miracle they retook the town in 1232. The town's heyday came in the 16th century, when many of the town's young men set off to the New World in search of wealth. Perhaps most famous was Francisco Pizarro, who launched the capture of the Inca Empire and founded the city of Lima. When the conquistadors returned home, they reinvested in the city, building up the Plaza Mayor, with its tiered town hall, stately San Martin church, 12th-century Casa de los Cardenas, Palacio de la Conquista, and an imposing statue of Pizarro.

name: Finca Sala Vive
description: The Finca Sala Vivé winery in Querétaro is owned by Freixenet, the world's leading producer of sparkling wine. In the 19th and early 20th centuries, when European vineyards were being ravaged by the phylloxera plague, Freixenet shifted their focus to the production of cava, a sparkling wine made following the traditional method of French Champagne. In 1914, they produced their first bottles of sparkling wine, and since then have expanded to a global empire with 18 wineries in 7 countries. Finca Sala Vivé is their award-winning Mexican winery that adheres to Old World values. On a guided tour you'll learn about the process behind making the still and sparking wines, and get to enjoy a glass for yourself, or you can join a guided wine tasting. For hard-core wine lovers, they even offer a 5-hour workshop by a sommelier! Throughout the year they also host special events, such as an international paella festival! Reservations are not required, but can be made in advance at reservations not neccessary but can be done here: https://www.freixenetmexico.com.mx/visita-clasica/venta-en-linea-visita-clasica/

name: Guimaraes
description: Founded in the 4th century, the city became Portugal's first capital when the nation declared its independence in the mid-12th. The medieval settlement has been preserved in the town center, and shows the development of Portuguese architecture from the 15th to the 19th centuries. The medieval style of a stone ground floor and half-timbered structure above preserved here was disseminated to Portuguese colonies in Africa and the New World. The city's medieval architecture is best represented by its the castle and monastic complex. During the nation's boom period in the Renaissance, many noble houses and scenic city squares were constructed.

name: Varna
description: Settled by the Thracians, Varna flourished thanks to diverse trade relationships, even working with the infamously war-like Scythians. The city's ancient history has been preserved in its archaeological museum, where among the many ancient artefacts, visitors will find the world's oldest gold treasure, which was discovered in a 6500-year-old tomb. For a slice of more recent history, the Retro Museum pulls back the curtain on life during the socialist era. Here visitors will find everything from Bulgarian cigarettes to vacuum cleaners and cosmetics and wax figures of the most prominent public figures alongside Eastern European cars. In the Maritime Park visitors can enjoy 22 acres greenery and gorgeous views of the Black Sea, and probably Varna's best-known building - the Varna Aquarium, where visitors will find fauna and flora from the Black Sea as well as more exotic species from around the world.

name: Mineral de Pozos
description: In a region with so many mines, mostly extracting silver, it's no surprise that a city of 50,000 once stood here. But the lower levels of the mines flooded and the city was abandoned to the elements. By 1950 only 200 people remained. More recently the relatives of former miners have been returning to breathe new life into Mineral de Pozos. The 3,500 residents are repairing old houses and installing art around the town. But away from the central areas Mineral de Pozos remains a ghost town with many abandoned ruins to explore. The best sites are a little away from the town proper. The smaller mine works to the east, Santa Brígida, contains the old silver smelting kilns and a remarkably intact villa. West is the larger complex, El Triángulo, a ruined village in itself and is best appreciated with a guide from the centre of town.

name: Heraklion
description: On the surface, Heraklion (also called Iraklio), Crete's sprawling capital, isn't the prettiest city. But dig a little and you'll find a wealth of history and culture. Just outside the city is the Palace of Knossos, the former seat of the Minoan Empire, which was a major player in ancient Greek mythology. At the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, you'll find Minoan artifacts excavated from the palace and other ancient sites around Crete. The Historical Museum of Crete covers everything after the Minoans, from Byzantine sculptures to WWII battles, and the only two paintings by Crete-born Renaissance master El Greco left on the island. You can also see this rich history around the city - from historic churches and fountains to Venetian walls, and the old harbor guarded by the indomitable Koules Fortress, which held off the Ottomans in the second longest siege in history. All of this is interspersed in a city with a thriving cafe and restaurant scene, which will keep you fueled for you explorations.

name: Tanah Lot Temple
description: According to legend, Tanah Lot was founded during the 15th century when the Hindu high priest Niratha came to Bali to spread the religion. Local lore disagrees on whether the locals welcomed him or resisted the conversion, but both versions of the story agree that the priest turned his sash into a giant serpent. Over the centuries, exposure to the powers of the sea significantly eroded the island and the temple to the point that both had to be reconstructed in the 1980s. For Balinese, Tanah Lot is part of the sacred string of sea temples founded by the priest Niratha, and in fact, only Balinese are allowed to actually enter the temple. Visitors, on the other hand, can admire the distinctive island from afar, or during low tide, walk to the rocky base where you can see the legendary sea snakes or be blessed by holy water from the island's fountain.

name: Rock of Cashel
description: The Rock of Cashel dates back to the 4th century, when it served as the seat of the Kings of Munster. It's said that St. Patrick converted them to Christianity here in the 5th century. In 1101, the rock was donated to the church and transformed into an ecclesiastical center. Entry is granted through the 15th century castle and the Hall of the Vicars, which houses a museum exhibiting the original Cross of St. Patrick. At the top of the grassy hill, you'll find the partly ruined 13th century Gothic cathedral and 12th century round tower. The highlight of the complex, however, is the 12th-century Cormac's Chapel, widely considered as one of the finest examples of Romanesque architecture in the country. While entry is only via guided tour, it's well worth it to see the beautifully carved doorways and some of the oldest wall paintings in Ireland. Please note: as one of the most popular destinations in Ireland, the castle can get quite crowded. For more information, please visit www.cashel.ie

name: Shiraoi
description: Shiraoi takes pride in being a gateway to the unique heritage of the Ainu, the indigenous people of Japan and Russia. Despite the challenges faced by the Ainu, the museum serves as a poignant testament to their rich culture and traditions, gaining official recognition as indigenous people of Japan in 2019. Venture beyond the museum to engage intimately with Ainu culture. The locals, passionate about Ainu-related tourism, invite you to explore traditional dance, craft making, and even indulge in an Ainu-style lunch. Experience a nature walk with a knowledgeable guide through areas of historical significance, fostering mutual communication and respect. For a taste of local flavors, Yakiniku Jingisukan Hitsuji no Ajito offers a unique dining experience with a "Pirate" theme, presenting high-quality grilled meat, including the delectable Ainu green onion sausage. Immerse yourself in Shiraoi's vibrant calendar of events, from the Dosanko Winter Festival to the Cheipu Festival, and explore natural wonders like Lake Kuttara, Inkura Falls, Mount Horohoro, Ayoro Beach, and the historic Sendai Domain Shiraoi Founding Encampment.

name: Matsumoto
description: Located in Nagano Prefecture, Matsumoto stands as a stunning historic city in the Chubu region. Set against a backdrop of majestic mountains, the city attracts both local and international tourists primarily for Matsumotojo — one of Japan's oldest original castles, nicknamed Crow Castle for its black exterior. Constructed in the 16th century, this castle is a registered National Treasure and one of Japan's 12 remaining original castles, ranking among the Top Three Premier Castles in Japan. Visitors can explore both the castle and its park, delve into exhibits that narrate its history, and marvel at the breathtaking views from the castle's top. Matsumoto serves as an ideal base for hiking in the Japanese Alps, boasting surrounding natural beauty. Other attractions include the famed Jigokudani Monkey Park and Nawate Street—a pedestrian-only lane of preserved wooden buildings. Often referred to as the 'frog street' (Kaeru machi) due to its frog-themed decor, it complements the nearby picturesque Nakamachi Shopping Street.

name: Quang Tri
description: Quang Tri is a small provincial town that gained notoriety during the Vietnam War. Strategically important thanks to its 19th century, Vauban-esque citadel, the town was the only major South Vietnamese city to be taken by the North. A counteroffensive saw the US carpet bomb the town and fortress, which, coupled with heavy shelling and fierce doo-to-door fighting caused the deaths of around 10,000. It's still possible to see the moat, ramparts, and gate, the crumbling brick remains of other parts of the fortress, and visit the on-site museum to learn more about the intense battle, and why the site is such a source of pride for the Vietnamese.

name: Caldicot Castle
description: Founded in the 12th century as a simple fort, Caldicot Castle was rebuilt in at the end of the 12th century as the stone keep seen today. After being neglected for centuries, the estate was purchased by Joseph Cobb, who restored the structure into an elegant Victorian home. Today, visitors can explore the castle's nooks and crannies, delve into the dungeons, scale the medieval towers for breathtaking views of the surrounding 55 acre parklands, or sit beside the 12 pound muzzle-loading cannon from Vice Admiral Nelson's first flagship, the HMS Foudroyant. Throughout the year, the castle also hosts special events. For more information, please visit visitmonmouthshire.com/caldicot-castle/

name: Knock Shrine
description: Knock Shrine stands on the spot, where, in 1879, villagers saw apparitions of Our Lady, Saint Joseph, and Saint John the Evangelist, and an altar bearing a cross and a lamb surrounded by adoring angels. In the 20th century, three different popes bestowed blessings on the shrine, and two visited in person. Mother Teresa of Calcutta visited in 1993, and the tens of thousands of pilgrims make their way to the site every year. Today, the shrine consists of the apparition chapel, parish church, and basilica, and is surrounded by a hundred acres of landscaped gardens. At the shrine museum, visitors are brought back to the 19th century to learn about the apparition, the tumultuous times surrounding it, and hear the stories of the pilgrims who were cured here. For more information, please visit www.knockshrine.ie

A popular escape for the English aristocracy at the end of the 19th century, the waterfront is lined with an array of cafes offering fresh seafood, perfect for people watching.

name: Garni
description: Located 28 kilometers east of Yerevan, Garni Temple represents the only standing Greco-Roman colonnaded building in not just Armenia, but the entire former Soviet Union. Built in the first century AD by King Tiridates I, this pagan temple dedicated to the sun god Mihr features classical Hellenic architecture with 24 Ionic columns. The structure was largely destroyed in a 1679 earthquake but meticulously reconstructed between 1969 and 1975 using original stones. The temple sits within a larger fortress complex dating to the 3rd century BC, positioned strategically on a promontory overlooking the Azat River gorge. Near the temple lies a Roman bathhouse featuring an intricate mosaic floor depicting sea gods and mythological scenes. The site's continued importance through Armenia's early Christian period indicates its cultural significance beyond religious functions. The village of Garni provides local food options featuring traditional Armenian cuisine.

name: Cospicua
description: Cospicua has witnessed the rise and fall of civilisations, and exudes a resilient spirit through its fortified walls and bastions. Built by the Knights as a defensive stronghold, the town is double-fortified. Religious devotion exudes from the town, with the impressive Parish Church, a 17th-century structure, renowned for miraculously withstanding the bombings of World War II. Cospicua is famous for its Good Friday procession, featuring intricate statues and artistic displays depicting the Last Supper. On any given day, explore the local streets to discover the charm of traditional and romantic Maltese houses. The waterfront offers breathtaking views, with mirror-like water and a small green park to relax in at the heart of the city. For those seeking greenery, the Cottonera Gardens offer a serene oasis within the city walls of the Cottonera lines.

name: Potsdam
description: Although the Prussian and German aristocrats have long gone, Potsdam's rich history is still proudly displayed throughout the green city. The heart of the city is still its Old Market Square, dominated by the 19th century St. Nicholas' Church at one end, and 18th century City Hall at the other. The nearby Dutch Quarter is unique in Central Europe, with about 150 red-brick houses built the traditional Dutch style. The city's crown jewel is the extensive Sanssouci Park and Palace, built by Frederick the Great. Often referred to as "Dreamland", this Rococo masterpiece was styled after Versailles, complete with a sculpture garden, fountains, and a beautiful terraced vineyard. The park itself has lots to discover and explore — beautiful gazebos, temples, churches, a large windmill, and even some "Roman ruins" can be explored.

name: Seven Sisters Country Park
address.addr1: Seven Sisters Country Park, E Dean Rd, East Sussex, Seaford BN25 4AB, UK
description: A series of seven chalk hills being eroded by the sea, the Seven Sisters Country Park provides a stupendously beautiful walk along the English channel. Unlike at Dover, where the large cliffs are marred by the large port, and are being covered in vegetation, the Seven Sisters are undeveloped, and left to erode naturally, at about 1 meter per year.

name: Harlech Castle
description: Harlech Castle was built in the 13th century by order of King Edward I to solidify his rule of Wales following a massive military campaign. This daunting defensive structure proved an effective stronghold for several centuries after, and was last used during the English Civil War in the 17th century. After being taken, Parliament ordered Harlech Castle be destroyed to prevent it from ever being used as a stronghold by its opposition, though instead the castle was made unusable rather than outright demolished. Today, Harlech is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as an exceptional representation of medieval military architecture. Visitors can roam the imposing castle's ramparts, explore the remains of its halls, or climb its towers for stupendous views of the Welsh countryside.

name: Bergamo
description: Bergamo's Venetian walls are both classic and opulent, with the power to captivate the sternest of men. The wall has two armories, two platforms, 14 bastions, and the chance to walk inside the walls to visit the vaulted chambers of San Michele and San Giovanni. The wall also divides the city into two - the Upper Town, (La Citta Alta) which sits on top of the hill packed with narrow wandering streets, and the Lower Town (La Citta Bassa), which extends towards the plains and the major international airport. This split distinction is Bergamo's most seductive feature. The city boasts its proximity to the Alps, close distance to its airport, and its passion art. Bergamo's historic boroughs, Piazza Veechia, and a visit to any of the city's finest dining establishments are a definite must-do's for tourists.

name: Dazaifu
description: Featuring revered temples and shrines, including the renowned Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine, as well as relics like the Government Office Ruins, Dazaifu is a beautiful city adjacent to Fukuoka. A blossoming spectacle engulfs the city's most famous shrine each March, with over 6,000 plum trees adorning its grounds, a tribute to Sugawara's cherished theme in his poems. Adjacent to the shrine is the Kyushu National Museum, providing insights into Kyushu's history and its ties to Asia. Additional historical gems include Kanzeonji Temple with its revered ancient statues, Kamado Shrine offering an atmospheric escape, and a captivating hike up sacred Mt. Homan, rewarding trekkers with panoramic vistas and a mountaintop sanctuary. Dazaifu preserves its rich history within a serene setting, offering visitors a captivating journey into its legacy as Kyushu's ancient political, diplomatic, and cultural nucleus.

name: Los Osuna Tequila Factory
description: Los Osuna Tequila Factory, located in La Noria, boasts vast fields of mesmerizing blue agave, the key ingredient in their spirits. The distillery has been recognised with the double gold award at the prestigious San Francisco World Spirits Competition, among other global awards. The distillery takes pride in showcasing the entire production process, allowing you to witness the craftsmanship that goes into creating their award-winning products for an entry fee of MXN 50. Included in your entrance fee are two complimentary tequila tastings. Whether you're a tequila enthusiast or simply curious about the art of spirit production, a visit to Los Osuna Tequila Factory is an immersive and educational experience. It is recommended to call or email in advance to arrange a tour with an English-speaking guide and secure your spot - please contact 6692162839, ventas@lososuna.com.mx, or andres@lososuna.com.mx.

name: Lodz
description: The first written records of Lodz date back to around 1332, however, it remained a relatively small settlement until the 19th century when it rapidly expanded following an influx of German and Jewish immigrants. By the 20th century, Łódź had grown to be one of Poland's largest cities, and one of Europe's multicultural and industrial centers, which is reflected by the city's architecture, where luxurious mansions coexist with redbrick factories and old tenement houses. Łódź' most trying time came during the Nazi occupation, when its Jewish population was interned in Europe's second largest ghetto. Today, a memorial for the victims stands at the Radegast railway station, and the Park of Survivors, where the handful of survivors planted trees to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the annihilation of the Jewish community.

name: St. Gallen
description: Founded as a humble hermitage by the Irish missionary monk Gallus in 612, in just 100 years it had evolved into a Benedictine abbey, which required contemplative study and a library. Today, the entire Abbey complex has been awarded a spot on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and the interior of both the cathedral and library are some of the most stunning (and important) examples of rococo design in the country. A walk through the charming, cobblestone streets and squares of St. Gallen's traffic-free old town is a visual treat, bring visitors past half-timbered houses embellished with turrets and colourfully-painted oriel windows dating from the 16th to 18th century.

name: Tena
description: Just steps away from the Amazon Rainforest, Tena is a city most famous for its adventure sports, attracting visitors from all over the world since the area played host to the 2005 World Rafting Championships. Adrenaline junkies should look no further than Tena for an expedition through the remote jungle and rainforest as they crash through the white-water rapids in kayaks or rafts. There are options for complete beginners and courses suited to experienced daredevils, as well as alternatives suitable for families. For a calmer visit, the Parque Amazónico is a small botanical garden with several species of birds and mammals that are in danger of extinction. There is no shortage of jungle tours available in the town and the impressive landscape could fool you into thinking you've stepped onto an action movie set. Remember: it's a rainforest, so plan for rain year-round!

name: Brooklands Museum
description: The Brooklands Museum holds a special place in British auto and aviation history. In 1907, Hugh F. Locke King constructed the world's first purpose-built racing circuit here, and shortly after, Brooklands became the site of one of Britain's first aerodromes, which attracted manufacturers including Hawker, Sopwith, and Vickers. In 1991, Brooklands opened as an open air museum showcasing a wide range of motoring and aviation exhibits amongst the landmark buildings. Here, visitors can admire the sleek curves of early race cars, see a Sopwith camel roar to life, look into one of two surviving Vickers Wellingtons, or even step aboard the Concorde. Visitors can also experience the thrill of thrill of Le Mans, or or flying with the Red Arrows in the exhilarating 4D theatre. For more information, please visit brooklandsmuseum.com

name: Leeds Castle
description: Originating as a wooden fort in the 9th century, Leeds Castle has been everything from a Norman stronghold to a royal palace and country estate. Today, majestic estate lets visitors experience a taste of noble life. In the castle's fully furnished rooms, visitors can marvel at the noble trappings of nearly every style of decor, from Medieval to Tudor to Rococo and Baroque. In the gatehouse, visitors can learn about the castle's 900 year history through artefacts and audiovisual installations, or head to the unique dog collar museum to see the world's largest collection of its kind. The 130 pieces on display date back to the 14th century, and showcase the evolution of the dog collar - from providing protection against wolves to fashion accessory. In the castle park, visitors can lose themselves in the hedge maze, or witness special exhibitions such as jousting or an unrivalled falconry display. For more information, please visit https://www.leeds-castle.com/

name: Arandas
description: Although Arandas exports the most tequila in the region, it always welcomes visitors looking to warm up with a shot of local Cazadores Tequila. Those in search of something more substantial can sink their teeth into some smoked agave or grab a bite at one of the many taquerias in the town. The main plaza, Plaza Hidalgo, is a gathering point where locals basque in the sun while filling up on ice cream and other sweet treats. You can't miss La Campana at one end of the Plaza Hidalgo! This 15,000kg bell is the largest in Mexico. Sitting alongside the colossal clapper is the Church of San Jose Obrero - the first stone was laid in 1879 and construction still continues today. See what Arandas has to offer all year round.

name: Tihany Abbey
address.addr1: Tihany, Balaton Uplands National Park, I. András tér 1, 8237 Hungary
description: Tihany Abbey was originally founded by King Andrew I of Hungary in 1055, with the church seen today being built atop the original site in 1754. Amazingly, the medieval crypt where King Andrew was buried was left completely undisturbed, and now his tomb is the only extant grave of a medieval King of Hungary. The church interior is an exercise in Baroque excellence, with intricately carved altars, pulpits, and screens made by an Austrian lay brother named Sebastian Stuhlhof. Stuhlhof is also responsible for the magnificent choir rail and the cherub-covered organ. The abbey also has a small museum where you can learn about its historical importance, like how the charter is the oldest example of writing in the Hungarian language. As an added bonus, the abbey's hilltop position offers some of the best views of Lake Balaton.

name: Filadelfia
description: In the 1930s, German and Russian Mennonites fled the Soviet Union and found refuge in Filadelfia, an almost deserted town in Chaco, Paraguay. They have dominated the economic scene, by farming, producing goods, and maintaining tourism. You are able to learn all about how these Mennonites created such a flourishing community in the many museums offered by the Fernheim Cooperative. The Jakob Unger Museum provides Mennonite history as well as natural history of the area. Next, learn about how people lived in colonial times at the Museo Knelson-Haus. Then, learn about the growing agricultural industry at the Museo Industrial. Continuing on to the Museo Hospitalario, which is on the original hospital grounds, where the indigenous natives were treated. Finishing at the Museo Escolar, which depicts how life was when the first school in Chaco was opened. This inside look into the life in Filadelfia will certainly answer all of your questions about the wild town!

name: San Martin de los Andes
description: Nestled in the Andes, San Martin de los Andes transforms into a winter wonderland, inviting skiers to conquer the slopes of Cerro Chapelco. As the snow melts, a tapestry of beaches, hiking trails, and National Park adventures unfolds, showcasing the town's diverse natural beauty. The town, with its artisan market in Plaza San Martín, becomes a treasure trove of crafts, jewelry, and wooden wonders—a perfect place to find unique souvenirs. Amidst charming wooden and stone houses, the downtown area invites strolls, offering a blend of shops, restaurants, and chocolatiers. The parish of San José, adorned with wood interiors, adds a touch of history. At the edge of town lies the inviting San Martin Beach on Lake Lacár, a picturesque spot for a relaxing day by the water. Despite the chilly lake, the scenic beauty and proximity to restaurants make it a delightful retreat. The summer landscape is adorned with vibrant lupins, creating a mesmerizing drive through the mountains. The iconic Seven Lakes Route begins here, a 100 km journey through Patagonian wonders. Bandurrias and Arrayanes viewpoints offer breathtaking panoramas, showcasing Lake Lácar and the city.

name: Dornbirn
description: The Rolls-Royce Museum, the most extensive of its kind in the world, houses more than a thousand exhibits, including a few dozen classic examples of this world-renowned company's automotive art. The museum also organizes special rides in selected vehicles. In contrast, the Flatz Museum (nothing to do with flat tyres), is a small two-room space dedicated to provocative Dornbirn-born performance artist Wolfgang Flatz; while the Kunstraum Dornbirn specializes in art-installations created by artists-in-residence. Nature's own dramatic handiwork can be enjoyed for free just a short walking-distance outside of town in the Rappenlochschluct, one of the largest canyons in Central Europe. Actually a complex of three linked gorges, served by an exemplary system of safe paths, steps and bridges, Rappenlochschluct, formed in the late ice age, is nature at her most spectacular and awe-inspiring. Not the least of the gorge's attractions is a huge waterfall halfway through the gorge complex, a mammoth tree and weird geological formations.

name: Modica
description: Settled since around 1300 BC, Modica became an important regional capital in the 13th century. A massive earthquake in 1693 destroyed the town, and it was rebuilt in the elegant Baroque style, gradually spilling from the upper Old Town, to form the 'Lower Modica'. Today, Modica spans three hilltops, and is labelled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its many beautiful Baroque buildings. However, unlike many of the other UNESCO-listed towns in Val di Noto, Modica's monuments aren't packed into one neighborhood. Upper Modica combines the rustic, Old-World atmosphere of a timeless village with renovated and maintained monuments. Most notably, the exquisite Duomo di San Giorgio, a Baroque beauty accessed via garden-lined staircases. The cathedral's interior is filled with ruch gilding, baby blue stucco, and rich religious ornamentation. While exploring the city, visitors should be sure to stop to try some of Modica's famous chocolate, which is based on an Aztec recipe brought back by the Conquistadors.

name: El Fuerte
description: Located in the northwestern Mexican state of Sinaloa, El Fuerte is a captivating city where—as legend will have it—the fictional Zorro was born. Statues of the iconic character are scattered around what was a thriving commercial and agricultural hub for centuries in northwestern Mexico. Today, its cultural heritage is showcased through noble landmarks such as the Plaza de Armas, adorned with towering palm trees and a picturesque wrought-iron kiosk. Other emblematic buildings such as the Municipal Palace and the Temple of the Sacred Heart of Jesus surround the Plaza. Learn about the pervasive indigenous and mestizo history of El Fuerto at The Museo Mirador del Fuerte Sinaloa, which displays indigenous handicrafts, historical photographs and other artifacts. After strolling through the enchanting town, treat yourself to local delicacies such as Zarandeado fish or chicharrones.

name: San Juan
description: This temperate, fertile oasis enveloped by rocky mountains is the perfect balance of rural and urban. Its colonial history can be traced back to 1562, but due to a devastating earthquake, most of that aspect of its heritage has been erased. Nowadays, the town has a modern layout, with wide streets irrigated by canals and widespread vegetation. Tourism is centered around wine production and degustation, with the region of San Juan being ranked as the second most important wine producing region in Argentina. Take a stroll through the flora at 25 de Mayo Square and take in the picturesque surroundings and monuments- including one of the former president who called this city home, Domingo Sarmiento. This prominent politician's birthplace, the Sarmiento House, is located a short way away. You can wander through the house where Sarmiento was born and raised, and travel back in time through reading newspapers and manuscripts from different stages of his life. We would advise you to check the opening timetables by phone (+54 264-4224603).

name: Montemaggiore
description: Dwarfed by the dramatic Monte Grasso mountain, Montemaggiore may at first appear a peripheral village of Corsica - but entering its center, you will soon be endeared. Old houses with uniquely sculpted doors maintain the quirky charm of centuries passed, squashed together haphazardly amongst original stone sculptures. The "Casa Colonna d'Anfiani" house was the fictional birthplace of the mother of Don Juan and still stands proudly in the village. For a historical monument entrenched in reality, visit the 18th century Church of Saint-Augustin on the edge of the village and admire the largest dome of any church in Corsica. Locals of Montemaggiore love their traditions and celebration, with high spirits spilling onto the streets at all times of the year. Make a trip in July for "A Fiera di l'Alivu", a tribute to the olive oil production integral to the village's economy. Or, stop by in Winter for the "pulenda figatellu" celebration when the village square is brilliantly set alight with the flames of a bonfire.

name: Reynisfjara Beach
description: On the southern shores of Iceland, Reynisfjara Beach is a black ribbon before the open sea. The towering black basalt columns, black sand, and tumultuous seas made this desolate-seeming stretch of coast the perfect location for filming Eastwatch by the Sea - perhaps one of the most remote locations in Game of Thrones. You also might recognize it as planet Eadu from Star Wars: Rogue One. The beach has long been catalyst for fantasy: it's said the basalt sea stacks just off the coast are two trolls and a 3-masted ship that turned to stone. While the beach is undeniably beautiful, be sure to follow safety instructions regarding the waves. Because there is no land between here and Antarctica, waves have thousands of kilometers to form, and rogue 'sneaker waves' have been known to catch visitors by surprise.

name: Cetinje
description: Being an independent state on the borders of the Ottoman Empire put Montenegro in a politically strategic position, and as such, every major European power had an embassy in Cetinje. Because of this, the old town has a continental style a thousand miles away from any reference point. The town was taken by the Ottoman Empire several times, but the locals would always rebuild, as the Monastery of St. Peter can attest. Housed inside are relics of Saint Petar of Cetinje, one the illustrious patrons of Montenegrin history. In a country that's 70% Russian Orthodox, this monastery represents the nation's spiritual seat. When the communists moved the capital to Podgorica in 1946, the Cetinje was left with just 9,000 residents. Today, feels like a time capsule. The population has grown slightly, but the buildings and the streets don't look too different.

name: Rishtan
description: Unveiling the secrets of ceramic artistry, Rishtan, Uzbekistan, beckons with the allure of ancient traditions and vibrant bazaars. Wander through workshops filled with the rhythmic clatter of potters' wheels and the earthy aroma of wet clay. Witness skilled artisans transform lumps of clay into exquisite ceramic creations, their hands guided by techniques honed for centuries. Explore galleries overflowing with hand-painted plates, intricate vases, and decorative tiles, each piece a testament to Rishtan's artistic legacy. Rishtan isn't just a shopper's paradise; it's a cultural tapestry waiting to be unraveled. Delve into the Chorsu Bazaar, a kaleidoscope of colors and scents. Haggle for unique souvenirs alongside friendly locals, and perhaps discover a hidden gem crafted by a local artisan. Savor steaming bowls of Uzbek plov (national rice dish) enjoyed at family-run restaurants, the air filled with the warmth of hospitality.

name: Trang An
description: Formed over millions of years, Trang An is an amazing region of karst cones and towers, interconnected by a network of depressions and subterranean waterways, which uniquely have been invaded by the sea in geological-times past. Though it's possible to walk or bike through much of this amazing landscape, the best to experience it is on a boat tour. Lasting about two hours, a ride on a traditional flat-bottomed boat brings you through the waterways that run between these mountains, and into the caves and tunnels that connect them for a truly unforgettable experience.

name: Carlos Keen
description: Carlos Keen is a tiny tourist town in the Buenos Aires province that comes alive on weekends or holidays. The locals call it "polo gastronómico" or a gastronomic hub, because of a large number of restaurants that offer typical Argentinian food, including the famous carne asada. Once you have a nice big meal, get rid of your food coma by walking around the town and visiting the city's main square and the Chapel of the San Carlos Borromeo Parrish. The local market offers artisanal goods, chocolate, and fresh eggs and dairy. Children will enjoy riding a horse under supervision of a gaucho. We recommend visiting the town on a Saturday, to avoid traffic on Sunday and to not come to a ghost town on a weekday.

name: Dinant
description: Born as a hilltop castle in the 11th century, the town of Dinant grew and flourished through the Middle Ages, though its unique position also frequently put it in harm's way. Over its long history, Dinant was damaged or destroyed multiple times, most recently in 1914, when German troops attacked the town and executed 675 of its inhabitants. Today visitors can enjoy a scenic walk along the Meuse before heading up to the citadel for some stupendous views of the surroundings before heading into the exploring the dungeons, kitchens, and weapon museum. The home of Adolphe Sax, inventor of the saxophone, is now a museum dedicated to the man and his invention. Perhaps the most distinctive building in Dinant is the 15th century Collegiate Church of Our Lady with its signature onion-domed tower and onion dome and multi-staged lantern.

name: Rio Camuy Caves
address.addr1: Cavernas del Río Camuy, puerto rico
description: Carved out by the Rio Camuy, the third largest underground river in the world, the Rio Camuy Caves are undoubtedly one of Puerto Rico's finest natural spectacles. To date, over 10 miles of caverns, 220 caves and 17 entrances have been mapped, and many experts believe there are still another 800 caves in the system waiting to be found. On a guided tour, you'll be led through an unforgettable fraction of the complex. Passing through tunnels up to 170 feet high and 200 feet wide, you'll find cave ornaments that have developed over the course of millions of years, including the largest stalagmite in Puerto Rico, all while surrounded by the flutter of bats and rush of the river below. Perhaps the highlight though is the Sumidero de Empalme (Empalme Sinkhole), where the sun shines through an opening in the cave 450 feet above. Please note: the cave is currently only accessible on foot (about a 1 hour hike) and closed-toe shoes are required. Tickets for the tour are not included in the stop price and cost $20 per person.

name: Durbuy
description: Durbuy was an important medieval trade center, and was elevated to the rank of city by King John I Count of Luxemburg, and King of Bohemia, in 1331. At the time, the honor made it (supposedly) the smallest city in the world, with only a few hundred residents. Today, Durbuy still celebrates this status, and even though it can no longer officially claim the title. Regardless of how you classify it, the cobbled streets and stone buildings are undeniably an all-too-charming place to lose yourself, take in views of the 18th century castle from every angle, and pop into a cafe. If you get stone-sick, Durbuy has another claim to fame: the world's largest topiary park. Covering an entire hectare, you'll find green hedges shaped into over 250 different designs including humans and animals.

name: Logrono
description: The origins of the city have been associated with those of the Roman Vareia from the 1st century B.C. As such, Logroño is a steeped in history and traditions, much of which has been preserved since the Middle Ages and is still visible in the city today. The city features a number of impressive religious buildings, including the 13th-century Church of San Bartolomé, and the Cathedral of Santa Maria de la Redonda, built on a primitive temple from the 12th century. Visitors can also enjoy an array of beautiful squares and parks, and a number of museums while strolling through the narrow medieval streets of this picturesque city. Logroño has been named the Commercial City of Spain (1996), the Spanish Gastronomic Capital (2012), and the European Sports City (2014).

name: Lancaster Castle
description: Built in the 11th century on the site of a Roman fort, Lancaster Castle has been a Royal possession since 1164. In 1196, the castle was first used as a prison, a role that grew increasingly important during the English Civil War, and would not be relinquished until 2011, making it the longest operating prison in Europe. Today, the castle is still an active courthouse offering visitors a fascinating look into its 1000 year history. On a guided tour, you'll learn about its many infamous trials, like the Lancashire Witches sentenced to death in 1612, the Lancashire Martyrs between 1584 and 1646, and the imprisonment of George Fox, the founder of the Quaker movement. Along the way you'll see everything from Gillow furniture to a branding iron, and even experience being locked inside an 18th century cell. Throughout the year, the castle also offers a range of special events including dark history tours and murder mysteries. For more information, please visit lancastercastle.com

name: Sudeley Castle
address.addr1: Sudeley Castle, Sudeley Castle & Gardens, Winchcombe GL54 5JD, UK
description: Built in the 15th century, this stunning castle has close ties to British royalty, with King Richard III, Elizabeth I, and Lady Jane Grey all inhabiting its regal rooms at some point. Katherine Parr, the last of Henry VIII's six wives, lived and died in the castle, and is interred in the castle's exquisite 15th century church, making Sudeley the only private castle in England to have a queen entombed on its grounds. Visitors can learn more about the life of this remarkable queen through her personal effects, including books she authored, which are displayed alongside other royal artefacts such as lacework made by Anne Boleyn, and bedside beer holders made for Marie Antoinette and Charles I. The centrepiece of Sudeley's world-renowned gardens is the Queens Garden, where Anne Boleyn, Katherine Parr, Lady Jane Grey, and Elizabeth I all spent their days admiring the hundreds of rose varieties. For more information, please visit sudeleycastle.co.uk

name: Malmo
description: Founded in the late 13th century, Malmö has since grown into Sweden's 3rd largest city. The cobbled streets and historic buildings of the charming Old Town (Gamla Staden) look much as they did centuries ago, except now, the buildings house funky galleries, trendy boutiques, and hip cafés, especially in the Lilla Torg neighborhood, which lies just south of the city's oldest square and the 14th century Saint Peter's Church, which has some of the finest late-medieval paintings in Scandinavia. Nearby, hidden in an old tenement building, is the Form/Design Center, which celebrates modern art, design, and architecture. Equally unique is the 16th century Malmöhus Castle, which isn't just the oldest preserved Renaissance castle in Scandinavia - it houses multiple museums and an aquarium! North of this is the trendy Western Harbour neighborhood, which is run entirely off sustainable energy and is watched over by the towering "Turning Torso".

name: Norheimsund
description: Situated on the shore of the Hardangerfjord, Norheimsund is an enticing destination for tourists looking to experience the natural beauty of the fjords and surrounding mountains. With a gorgeous harbor and delightful esplanade, it's not only a wonderful town in and of itself, but boasts the Steinsdalsfossen waterfall just a few kilometers from the center. This impressive waterfall is unique in that visitors can walk behind the cascading water and experience the power of the falls up close. The surrounding area offers numerous hiking trails, from easy strolls to more challenging mountain hikes. Norheimsund is also known for the Hardanger Folk Museum, which showcases the rich history and culture of the Hardanger region through exhibits on traditional crafts, music, and clothing. The Maritime Museum is also a highlight, located in a former sardine factory and exhibiting the region's seafaring history. The Norheimsund Market is held every August, replete with local crafts, food and music, while the nearby ski resort of Kvamskogen hosts a range of winter sports activities.

name: Hatta
description: Situated in the rocky Hajar Mountains, sports enthusiasts come to Hatta to hike and bike in the rocky landscape and enjoy the fresh mountain air. The historic town, however, is an attraction in its own right, standing as one of the oldest heritage sites in the UAE, and offering visitors a glimpse at a traditional Emerati village. The loam houses, 18th century military towers, and Juma mosque from 1780 have all been restored. In the local ruler's house, you'll find artefacts like instruments, weapons, furnishings, and tools for a more detailed look at local culture. The nearby Al Sharia palm farm, with its traditional falaj irrigation system offers a pleasant retreat from the heat.

name: Apricale
description: This mountain gem will make you forget all about the Mediterranean, just 30 minutes away. Rustic houses nestle together along narrow streets, working their way up to the Castle of the Lucertola, embedded in a rocky spur. Strolling the picturesque cobbled paths, visitors are rewarded with lovely churches, the old town hall, and shops with locally produced regional specialties. True to Italian tradition, work here stops for lunch and doesn't resume for a few hours.

name: Lahich
description: Lahich is one of the most ancient human settlements in Azerbaijan, located within the Ismayilli District. The small local population primarily speak the Tat language, also known as Tati Persian, and are skilled storytellers who will be eager to share tales of their families and ancestral traditions to you as you wander through the markets. Stepping into Ismayilli Rayon, the rhythmic sounds of metal being hammered and clanging together fill the air as shop owners arrange their merchandise. The village's cobblestone alleys lead to an array of shops offering exquisitely crafted copperware that has gained recognition not only in Azerbaijan but also in the South Caucasus region. Delve deeper into the village's history at the Lahich History Museum, housed in a former mosque next to the tourist office, and be treated to breathtaking landscapes adorned with lush forests and picturesque rivers at an altitude of 1505 meters above sea level.

name: Tiwanaku
description: Considered the most important archaeological site in the country, Tiwanaku is also one of the largest, covering an area of four square kilometers. While the site's exact age is argued, one thing for certain is - it was the political and spiritual capital of the Tiwanaku Empire. Its significance is in no small part due to the cultur's impressive technology, which revolutionised the agricultural industry, perfected the carving of stone for architectural purposes, and allowed the people of Tiwanaku to thrive in pottery, ceramics, and textiles. The Pumapunku temple contains the largest stone block in all of Tiwanaku, weighing more than 130 metric tons. It houses the Gateway of the Sun, a megalithic archway, a supposed agricultural calendar. The site contains two museums showing collections of ancient pottery and ceramics and other artifacts, monoliths engraved with intricate artwork and even a mummy!

name: Pollensa
description: Primarily inhabited by locals, Pollença provides a cultural retreat away from bustling resorts. Café life thrives, especially on Sundays when Plaça Major bursts with market stalls, locals congregating post-church for leisurely moments. Boutique hotels dot the town, while luxurious retreats and villas grace the lush countryside. Pollença's historic allure spans ancient Roman bridges, an 18th-century church with a famed rose window, and the mesmerizing Convent de Sant Domingo. The town's artistic spirit thrives, evident in the Dionis Bennassar Museum and local markets showcasing traditional crafts. The scenic journey to Port de Pollença unveils glorious beaches and coastal delights. Strolling Pollença's pristine streets, exploring historic landmarks like Pont Romà and the Calvari church's 365 steps, transports visitors through time.

name: Obidos
description: The maze of cobblestoned streets that make up Óbidos' striking historic centre are lined with whitewashed houses, accented with splashes of vivid yellow and blue paint, and garnished with flowers, all ensconced within the walls of its medieval castle. Since Queen Urraca was given the title of the village by King Afonso II in 1210, the several royal consorts enriched the village with donations, making it into one of the most scenic in the country. The hilltop castle has been converted into one of Portugal's most luxurious hotels, and now offers stunning views of the city as well as incomparable accommodations. For history buffs with a sweet-tooth, the tile-bedecked main gate, Porta da Vila, leads directly into the main street, Rua Direita, which is lined with chocolate and cherry-liqueur shops. The best way to enjoy the town's signature ginja liquor is in a small edible chocolate cup.

name: Springfield, MA
description: Springfield, MA, the first of its name in the US has a lot more firsts under its belt. It was home to the first American dictionary (Merriam-Webster), the first successful motorcycle company (Indian), the first mass-produced vulcanized rubber (Charles Goodyear), and maybe most famously, it was the birthplace of basketball! Hoop-heads won't want to miss the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, which has memorabilia as well as hands-on mini games and shows. If you're traveling with kids, or just want to relive your childhood, pay a visit to the free Dr. Seuss National Museum Sculpture Garden, and the (not free) Amazing World of Dr. Seuss Museum. For something more refined, the Michele and Donald D'Amour Museum of Fine Arts next door has a great collection, particularly when it comes to Impressionists. Or, visit the RMS Titanic Museum for the boasting the largest collection of original artifacts in the world, donated by the survivors themselves!

name: Amsterdam
description: One of just two world capitals set below sea level, Amsterdam is a hive of history, art, and culture, nestled within a labyrinth of marvelous canals. With intricate waterways and eye-catching architecture, this major world port of the Dutch Golden Age is often called 'the Venice of the North'. Amsterdam is such an intriguing destination; not just for the canals, but rather the diversity of the sights on land. Great landmarks like the Rijksmuseum and the Royal Palace atop Dam Square, show the prominence this city has. A short walk away, you'll discover The Jordaan, a quaint neighborhood, brimming with specialty shops and designer boutiques. Fill up on the arts at the Van Gogh Museum or the House of Rembrandt. For most newcomers to the city, another house - one of true historical importance - no doubt tops the list. The story of Anne Frank is known by all and portrays the most important perspective of the Second World War. Her house, surely, is unmissable. Those with an interest in the obscure, are sure to find it down in Amsterdam Dungeon or the BodyWorlds exhibition, and even more so in De Wallen, an area famous for its Red Light District. You can easily get around town using boats, bikes, and trams; just don't forget to stop for a plate of the country's favorite bar snack, Bitterballen, and a pint of locally brewed Heineken!

name: Innsbruck
description: Nestled in an alpine valley, Innsbruck offers panoramic views of the towering Alps. If those soaring peaks don't take your breath away, the opulent architecture surely will. Settled since the early Stone Age, Innsbruck has been a coveted commercial center since Roman times. Over the next 1000 years, Innsbruck grew in stature, becoming a seat of European politics and culture as Emperor Maximilian I took up residence in the 1490s. Today, the city's rich heritage is proudly on display, from the lavish Golden Roof, a balcony with 2,657 fire-gilded copper tiles erected to mark Emperor Maximilian I's marriage to Bianca Maria Sforza, to the Tyrolean Folk Art Museum, where centuries of alpine culture are on display.

name: Shrine of Our Lady of Remedies
address.addr1: Shrine of Our Lady of Remedies
address.city: Shrine of Our Lady of Remedies
description: Resting on the Tlachihualtepetl pyramid overlooking Cholula, this stunning church is truly a view in itself, while also providing a breathtaking view of Cholula. This church was erected in the 16th century in a neoclassical style with tiled domes and painted a warm, burnt yellow. One of the reasons people travel to this church is to see the image of Our Lady of Remedies, she is carved and gilded and put on display in the church as it is her namesake. She was brought to Mexico by Captain Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte, in hopes it would protect him during his travels. Twenty years after the Spanish defeated the Aztecs, she was discovered by indigenous people under an aloe plant, which is why she is known as the Lady of Remedies. Whether you are pious, or chasing the best views and architecture, this church has enough beauty and history for everyone.

name: Skjolden
description: Situated at the head of the Sognefjord, the longest and deepest fjord in Norway, the village of Skjolden is surrounded by steep mountains and breathtaking natural scenery. It is the meeting place of the two valleys of Mørkridsdal and Fortunsdal and boasts spectacular waterfalls and national parks including the Jotunheimen, Breheimen and Jostedalen National Park in the vicinity. It was home to renowned philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein who lived here over several periods after 1913 and wrote some of his most important works in a small wooden house on a remote rock over the Eidsvatnet Lake. The village regularly holds sports events such as Skjolden Extreme, while Adventure Tours offers biking, hiking, fishing, stand up paddling and more. Easily reach the UNESCO Urnes Stave Church while visiting, or head to the brewery in the Skjolden Hotel basement, which offers unforgettable gourmet dinners.

name: Halle
description: Founded around the 9th century, Halle was an important trade city for centuries. In the 18th century, the city became a center for Pietism, which saw the city filled with orphanages, and the first 'modern' education system. One of the city's iconic 'Five Towers' comes courtesy of the Red Tower, home to the world's third largest carillon. The other 4 towers rise above the Church of St. Mary, where Handel used to play organ - an instrument christened under the keen ear of Johann Sebastian Bach. Nearby, the Renaissance building where Handel was born now serves as a museum dedicated to the great composer. In the Museum of Prehistory, home to one of Germany's most important archaeological collections, visitors will find artefacts from the Stone Age through early Iron Age, including the famous Nebra Sky Disk, a UNESCO-protected artefact labelled as one of the most important finds of the 20th century.

name: Nimes
description: Founded by the Romans, Nimes quickly became a regional capital, with a population of 60,000 by the time of Augustus. In 736-737, much of the city before heading back north. Despite being a shadow of its former self, the city is still home to France's best collection of Roman remains. Before even entering the city, the massive aqueduct, a UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of the finest remaining anywhere. The city is also home to one of the three large arenas in the South of France, and still used for events to this day. It's other Roman jewel is the Maison Carrée - the best preserved Roman temple in the world. At the edge of town, the Jardins de la Fontaine are one of the oldest city parks in France, offering a delightful mix of of greenery, fountains and shade, with a Roman Temple of Diana thrown in for good measure.

name: Karlovac
description: Karlovac is located in the heart of Croatia, at the junction of four rivers. Founded by the Austrians in 1579, the historic town center was built in the shape of a 6-pointed star. The reason for the structure was to strengthen the defenses against the invading Ottoman Empire. After threat faded, the city walls were torn down. Today, only a small section of the original defensive walls remains. Another important sight is the 13th century Dubovac Castle. The castle sits on an ancient hill overlooking the city (providing a spectacular city view) and is open for visitors to revel in what was once home to many Noble families and army generals. There is also a city museum and many park and green areas to explore. Karlovac is also home to one of Croatia's two most popular breweries, Karlovacko. This gives the city its infamous nickname of the 'city of beer'.

name: Vilnius
description: Centered around a 13th century castle, Vilnius was named the capital of the region less than a century after its founding. The city flourished until the 17th century, first thanks to trade, and then thanks to its university. Wars, plagues, and brutal leadership rocked the city until the 1990s. Today, the historic city center is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site thanks to its beautiful architecture, which organically combines Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and Classical styles. Walking the picturesque streets, visitors can see the original 16th century Gate of Dawn, before heading to the opulent 17th century Church of St. Peter and St. Paul, filled with about 2,000 stucco figures. Vilnius' struggles are also well documented in the historic Jewish quarter, and the Museum of Genocide Victims, which remembers the Jews by the Nazis, as well as the brutal treatment by the Soviets during their occupation.

name: Cenote Maya Park
description: At nearly 20 meters tall and 60 meters in diameter, the Cenote Maya is the largest dome in the entire Yucatan Peninsula. From an opening in the dome, a staircase leads down to the swimming platform and the cenote's cool refreshing waters. But this isn't the only way to descend to the watery depths - you can also free rappel into the cave. The Cenote Maya is so large that it has its own underground zipline, "Tarzan" ropes, and there's enough room to kayak around the cavern! Once you're done with the watery adventures, a Shaman will lead you through an authentic Mayan blessing ceremony, and a buffet lunch will let you try some traditional Mayan dishes.

name: Perfume Pagoda
description: The first temple at the Perfume Pagoda was built in the 15th century, and over the years, the limestone hills and caves came to be filled with more shrines and temples. Reaching the Perfume Pagoda is half the fun - you first travel by road, then by river, then on foot or by cable car (for an additional fee). Once you reach the complex, you can see some of the area's most revered temples, like the Pagoda Leading to Heaven, the Purgatorial Pagoda, and the Pagoda of the Perfumed Vestige. The heart of the complex is the Inner Temple, housed within a cave shaped like a dragon's mouth, which is filled with a variety of statues, and numerous stalactites and stalagmites. The variety of temples in such a stunning setting has made the Perfume Pagoda immensely popular among the Vietnamese in February to April, so be prepared for crowds if you're visiting during this time.

name: Petropolis
description: Petropolis sprang up almost overnight in the 19th century after Emperor Dom Pedro II ordered the construction of a summer palace and a settlement formed by German immigrants on land his father purchased. Keeping up with the emperor, other aristocrats had summer manors built here, and soon Petropolis became Brazil's de facto summer capital. Even today, the "Imperial City'' is filled with reminders of its rich pedigree. Take a tour of the lavish palace of Dom Pedro II, to see the period furnishings and a 1.7-kg diamond-and-pearl-studded crown. Another highlight is the intricate Palácio de Cristal, a greenhouse Princesa Isabela brought from France 1884. Then there's the Rio Negro Palace, used by the president of Brazil as a country retreat, and "The Enchanted" - the summer residence turned fascinating museum of Brazilian aviation pioneer Alberto Santos Dumont. Petropolis' German heritage is also proudly on display, with the Bauernfest being held every July, and the Cervejaria Bohemia pumping out Bohemian brew year-round.

name: Heidelberg
description: At the top of every visitor's list is the symbolic heart of the city — the red-sandstone Heidelberg Castle, which is consistently voted by foreign visitors as the top tourist attraction in Germany. Visitors can wander the grounds and from the castle walls, marvel at the views of the Old Town that never fail to thrill. The Old Town itself is a must see in order to sample the charms of the elegant churches, picture book lanes, and alleyways set against the backdrop of the beautiful Neckar River. This area of the city also contains the longest pedestrianized shopping strip in Germany. Slightly out from the center, but no less impressive is Philosophers' Way, the name given to the path just above the city that allegedly inspired the philosophers of old. The path offers fabulous views and is often described as 'peaceful, romantic and beautiful, a place to commune with nature'.

name: Urbino
address.addr1: 61029 Urbino, Province of Pesaro and Urbino, Italy
description: During the 6th century Gothic Wars, this tiny Roman town became an important stronghold. By the end of the 13th century, it was an important regional centre, and positively flourished during the Renaissance. In the mid-15th century, Federico da Montefeltro became Duke of Urbino, and began to reorganizate the state, restructuring the city according to a modern conception - comfortable, efficient and beautiful. The resulting ducal palace was more "a city with the form of a palace", and today houses one of the most important collections of Renaissance paintings in the world. For those who truly worship Renaissance art, the master Raphael was born here, and his home is now a museum. Another hidden gem is the Oratorio di San Giovanni Battista, which is covered in vibrant 15th century frescoes. Wandering within this walled town is a treat with its abundance of remarkably well preserved medieval and renaissance sights.

name: Rabat
description: Rabat was founded in the 12th century as a port for launching attacks on Iberia, and the city briefly served as Morocco's medieval capital. After nearly being abandoned, Rabat became a stronghold for Barbary pirates in the 16th century, and they continued to use the port until the mid 19th century. In 1929, the French made Rabat Morocco's capital and revitalized the city. Unlike Morocco's other major cities, Rabat is relatively quiet, meaning you can peacefully explore the medieval alleys of its UNESCO-listed medina, and blue-painted walls of the kasbah. Don't miss the Hassan Tower - the minaret and ruins of what would have been the world's largest mosque when it was commissioned in 1195 by Caliphate Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur.

name: Targoviste
description: First settled at the end of the 12th century, Targoviste quickly grew to become the capital of Wallachia by the end of the 14th century. During this time, it was ruled by Vlad Tepes III (Dracula), who is credited with both sprucing up the princely court with the iconic Chindia Tower, and also having the city's elite killed and its youth sent to build his Poenari Castle for their role in assassinating his brother. The Princely Court is one of the only surviving Medieval ensembles in Southern Romania, with the tower now serving as a museum dedicated to Vlad the Impaler, and the frescoes within the Great Princely Church a gem of Romanian art. After the capital was moved to Bucharest in 1688, Targoviste lost its importance, though was notably where Nicolae Ceauşescu and his wife, Elena, were executed on Christmas Day, 1989 - the house where the despot was held, tried, and executed has been preserved as the Museum of Communism.

name: Mariana
description: After gold was discovered along the Ribeirão Nossa Senhora do Carmo river in 1696, the Portuguese founded their first city in the Minas Gerais region - Mariana. As the first mining center, capital, and bishopric in the state, the mineral wealth coming from the nearby mountains funded a bounty of beautiful buildings. The Catedral de Nossa Senhora da Assunção is Mariana's largest and most important church, with contributions from artists including Aleijadinho, and his father, Manuel da Costa Ataíde. Right behind the Cathedral, a colonial mansion now houses the Museu de Arte Sacra - Brazil's best sacred art museum. There are a number of other beautiful Baroque churches to be found, including two on Minas Gerais Square. While exploring the historic downtown, be sure to take a stroll down Rua Direita. The second-oldest street in the city, it's lined with the oldest and best-preserved houses, including the former state governor's house, and the home of poet Alphonsus de Guimarães.

name: Maldonado
description: Founded in the 1500s, Maldonado was built on a mix of Spanish and native Guarani influence. This can be seen throughout the city, such as San Fernando de Maldonado's Cathedral, or the Spanish style barracks that create an attractive backdrop for sight-seeing. The gems of Maldonaldo are the Didactic Artigas Museum, which is a small museum in the Spanish barracks. This museum has a wonderful collection of paintings and sculptures that show Uruguayan art and its many changes throughout history. The other delightful destination of Maldonado is the Francisco Mazzoni Regional Museum, located in a former high-society mansion, this charming museum that displays colonial life with a collection of tools and instruments from both the high society and indigenous people of the time. If the museums haven't tired you out, make sure to check out Calle Royal (Royal Street), as it is known for the fast food restaurants, where you can sample Uruguayan cuisine!

name: Carmelo
description: With Carmelo's inhabitants descendant from Italy, it is no wonder why Caremlo is the second biggest wine region in Uruguay. In this town there are a handful of boutique wineries, each with a personal story that add an element of hominess. These wines can stand with some of the finest in South America, and visiting one is not to be missed! On the Arroyo de las Vacas, there is a swinging bridge that was imported from Germany in 1912, used for when boats and yachts need to pass, the center of the bridge rotates 360 degrees to create room for the large vessels. Or, if you prefer art, check out the Jose Castro Wood Sculpture Planet. Literally at the back of a hardware store, you'll find a surprising amount of wood carvings that depict different displays of humanity. Don't underestimate Carmelo, it will impress you every chance it gets!

name: Lleida
description: The capital of an ancient Iberian tribe who warred against other Iberians as well as the Romans, the city's history is a long list of military engagements. After finally being conquered by the Romans, it was the site of a battle led by Caesar himself during the Roman Civil War. Ever after, the city faced new adversaries - most infamously, when the Condor Legion bombed a school. Today, the city's spirit is represented by the massive cathedral-cum-fortress. Built in the 13th century, the cathedral's robust Romanesque construction played prominent part in the city's defense during the French invasion. Here visitors are treated to Gothic details, one of the largest cloisters in Europe, and spectacular views of the city. The city is also littered with Catalan Modernist buildings, scenic parks and a multitude of museums.

name: Merida
description: Founded in 25BC, this "mini Rome" was designated by the Emperor for Roman legionnaires and their families. Eventually it evolved into the capital of Lusitania, which was arguably the most important province in the western empire. Over the centuries, the region passed between Christian, Moorish and Portuguese control, influencing the city's culture and architecture. For a taste of Rome, visitors can see the amphitheatre, theatre, Circus Maximus, bridge, aqueducts, and National Museum of Roman Art. The city is also home to the 6th century Visigothic Basilica of Santa Eulalia, and 9th century Moorish castle.

name: Boulogne-sur-Mer
description: Built upon the Romans' primary northern port, Boulogne-sur-Mer is today the largest fishing port in the country. With such a long history, it's no wonder that the sea is the backbone of the city's culture. Dominating the city is the 100 meter tower of the 18th century Basilica of Notre-Dame, which is one of the largest in Europe. Inside, the church's much older crypt is one of the largest in France with elements dating back to the early Middle Ages, and houses the many riches of the treasury. Visitors can also enjoy a walk along the medieval battlements, or step into the 13th century castle, which now houses the city museum, exhibiting everything from Egyptian artefacts to ethnographic objects. In the lower city, visitors can indulge in fresh seafood and local specialties, or see sea creatures from around the world in Nausicaà, the National Sea Centre.

name: Delphi
description: This magnificent sanctuary on the slopes of Mount Parnassus is estimated to have been built in 8th century BC. For centuries, Delphi was considered to be the center of the world by Greeks, and as such, was showered with attention. The site is home to truly spectacular Temple of Apollo, a theatre, treasuries, and many other monuments. Delphi occupies a special place in the Greek mythology as the site used to be a home to Pythia, the high priestess also known as the Oracle of Delphi. Pythia could channel prophecies from the God of Sun, Apollo. Today, visitors can admire this amazing site and learn in-depth about its history and importance, while taking in the stunning views the location offers.
