name: Takamatsu
description: Takamatsu, situated on Shikoku Island, is a captivating port city that offers a blend of natural beauty, historical sites, and gateway access to the enchanting Seto Inland Sea islands. Ritsurin Koen Park stands as one of Japan's most exquisite gardens, a serene haven adorned with seasonal wonders. Its allure peaks during cherry blossom and autumn foliage seasons. Traditional boat rides and tea ceremonies in the park's tea room enhance the experience. Takamatsu Castle boasts a unique seawater moat, and its restored old keep welcomes public exploration. The Yashima plateau, crowned by Yashima-ji Temple, grants panoramic Seto Inland Sea views. Shikoku Mura, an open-air museum at the mountain's base, showcases regional history and culture. A brief stroll from the train station leads to the ferry port, connecting to Naoshima's contemporary art scene, Shodoshima's Mediterranean-like ambiance, and Megijima's cherry blossom haven.

name: Takayama
description: Takayama is nicknamed "Little Kyoto" because of its old-world charm and stunning traditional architecture. However, without the immense crowds of Kyoto, this city offers a much more pleasant exploration experience. Located in Gifu Prefecture, Takayama boasts narrow alleyways lined with wooden houses, with ancient temples and bridges arching over canals adding to the city's allure. Visitors should include the Nakabashi Bridge in their itinerary; the city's symbol, it is beautifully surrounded by cherry blossoms in spring. Takayama's historic district is called the Sanmachi Suji district, known for its traditional wooden structures and streetside canals. Rising amid trees is the Sakurayama Hachimangu Shrine, believed to have origins dating back to the 4th century. For those keen to try local delicacies, such as Hida beef (a type of wagyu) or Mitarashi Dango (rice dumplings coated in a sweet soy glaze), the Miyagawa Morning Market is a must-visit. Sake enthusiasts should consider a visit to the Harada Sake Brewery.

name: Edirne
description: Dating back to antiquity, the ancient city of Edirne was an important regional center, eventually becoming the capital of the Ottoman empire when it was conquered by sultan Murad I in 1369. While the seat of the empire was moved to Constantinople in 1453, the city has retained a regal air. The city is filled impressive Ottoman architecture, ranging from stone bridges to grand mosques. The 16th century Selimiye Mosque is the most impressive - a UNESCO World Heritage Site that's a self-contained community, with covered market, schools, and a library. Considered the greatest achievement of Sinan, the greatest architect of his day, the complex is both beautiful and pragmatic. Edirne also boasts the Great Synagogue, the largest Jewish house of worship in the Balkans, which was recently restored after 30 years of abandonment.

name: Edfu
description: While modern Edfu is a friendly provincial center known for its sugar and pottery, thousands of years ago it was a major religious center. It was here that the largest Temple of Horus was built by Cleopatra, and earlier pharaohs had even erected pyramids nearby. Thanks to the temple's hilltop position, it was untouched by the Nile river's devastating floods, making it the best-preserved temple in Egypt. Amazingly, even the temple's roof has survived, adding a sense of mystery as you explore the dim corridors. Among the temples many carvings, it is the back of the inner hypostyle hall that's the most interesting. Here, in what was once the temple laboratory, the recipes for perfumes and incenses were inscribed on the walls.

name: Warwick Castle
description: Built by William the Conqueror in the 11th century on the site of a fortified town, Warwick Castle grew to become one of the grandest in the country, having survived attacks, sieges, and fire. Today, the castle gives visitors an exciting look at over 1000 years of history, and a glimpse of the staggering wealth of one of Britain's wealthiest families. In the elegant 17th Century Great Hall and State Rooms, visitors will find historic treasures, including a museum of arms and armor. Visitors can also scale the towers and ramparts for fantastic views of the countryside. The castle also works to bring history to life through special events like a summer jousting tournament, falconry show, and a demonstration of the world's largest trebuchet. For more information, please visit warwick-castle.com

name: Ston
description: Built in the 15th century, the Walls of Ston were once 7 kilometers long, featuring 3 fortresses and over 40 towers. So remarkable in fact, Ston's walls are the longest fortress system in Europe and only second in the world after China, hence the moniker, The European Wall of China. Only an hour's drive from Dubrovnik, Ston was unique and completely advanced for its time. With a modern infrastructure, profitable land, and a well fortified system, Ston was a hidden gem. Besides taking a stroll along the walls, one may suggest visiting its most profitable business even today: the salt works. But everyone must eat! If you get to stop at local restaurant be sure to check off your list tasting some of the locally farmed oysters. It's a must eat in Croatia!

name: Tepatitlan de Morelos
description: Tepatitlan is your go-to stop for a sample of Mexican culture. From its rich collection of local restaurants to its catalog of attractions and monuments, you'll not be at a loss for entertainment. If you crave a taste of colonial or Baroque architecture, you'll find the stunning San Francisco Parish (dedicated to Saint Francis of Assisi) or the charming two-story colonial city hall suited your needs. You can relax in the main square (Plaza de Armas) or make your way to the Centennial Market, where vendors can be found selling a variety of wares from local crafts and leather goods to season fruits and vegetables. The historically-oriented can visit the city museum, or the more whimsical can step into the Cactus Museum, complete with Chinese pagoda. Just don't forget your camera!

name: Luang Prabang
description: The ancient city of Luang Prabang served as the royal capital of the Lan Xang Kingdom until the 16th century, and was reinstated as the country's royal residence by the French. This prestigious pedigree made the city the country's cultural center (both Lao and colonial), and this fusion has been preserved to this day in the UNESCO-listed historic center. Walking through Luang Prabang, visitors are treated to elegant French architecture, alongside glittering gilded Wats. You can also visit the former Royal Palace, which as been preserved just as the last King left it, allowing visitors to experience the distinctive Franco-Lao fusion, and see the 14th century Buddha that gave Luang Prabang it's name. One of Luang Prabang's highlights comes after dark, when the kilometer-long night market comes alive, offering everything from street food to souvenirs and handicrafts.

name: Posadas
description: Posadas was originally a Paraguayan river port and trading post known as Trinchera de los Paraguayos, but changed its name in 1879 to honor the national hero Gervasio Antonio Posadas. Today, most travellers just see the city as a stopping point, but it's laid-back atmosphere and pleasant riverside setting warrant a bit of exploration. The city has a surprising wealth of street art, and along with colorful murals, you'll stumble across decorated stairways and giant metal statues. The 15-meter-tall cubist monument to Andres Guazurari is the city's most impressive work of art, made even better by its riverside location. The statue stands on a long boardwalk where locals exercise, or relax with a mate - there's even a small beach where you can take a dip if terere isn't enough to beat the heat.

name: Ubud
description: According to tradition, Ubud's origins date back to the 8th century with the founding of the Gunung Lebah Temple, which still remains a pilgrimage destination. Ubud began attracting tourists after Walter Spies entertained celebrities like Charlie Chaplin and H.G. Wells, and brought in some of Bali's greatest artists. Today, the town is still Bali's artistic epicenter, hosting countless shops selling antiques, artwork, and jewellery, and some of the country's best art museums. One such is the Blanco Renaissance Museum, where visitors can tour of the late artist's home to see his provocative artwork, often depicting favourite subject: nude Balinese women. Another cultural landmark is 19th century Ubud Royal Palace, where you'll be able to admire exquisite Balinese art and architecture, charming gardens, and in the evenings, dramatic dance performances. At the Sacred Monkey Forest, you'll not only find playful macaques, but a series of serene temples, in a lush environment.

name: Gisborne
description: Located on the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, Gisborne has a reputation for excellent wine, great food and a lush coastline. Bask in the sunshine outside one of many cafes or restaurants lining the coast, or on one of the towns numerous beaches (where you can also catch some surf!). The Cook Landing Site National Historic Reserve commemorates the landing site of Captain James Cook, famous British navigator who first set foot on New Zealand soil in Gisborne in 1769. The Tairāwhiti Museum is home to the Captain Cook statue, memorialising the explorer, whose arrival is cause for controversy due to the bloody encounters resulting in the death of several indigenous Māori people. The museum has Māori history exhibitions, extensive artwork collections and photographic displays. The maritime gallery showcases Māori waka,a vintage surfboard collection and there are an assortment of Māori textiles, stoneworks and carvings on show

name: Piribebuy
description: Because many of the official documents containing written history of Piribebuy were destroyed during the Paraguayan War, some details of the town at the time of colonization are lost to history. The Pedro Pablo Caballero Historical Museum offers a unique look into the tragedy of war and heroic efforts by citizens of the country. Presently, the unique landscape of Piribebuy is rich with resources that contribute to its economic success in the region. Piribebuy is the main producer of caña, a traditional drink made from sugar cane. It is regarded as the best city to sample this sweet liquor. Don't miss the Church of Dulce Nombre de Jesus which houses a small museum containing memorabilia from the Paraguayan and Chaco Wars. Its hand-carved altarpiece is one example of beautiful Franciscan works in the country.

name: Chiang Rai
description: Founded by King Mangrai in 1262, Chiang Rai was actually under Burmese rule for several hundred years, and wasn't annexed by Thailand until 1899. Chiang Rai's central landmark is an elaborately decorated golden clock tower, designed by the artist behind the famous White Temple, that serves as a traffic roundabout. Nearby is the beautiful Wat Klang Wieng, which has a vivid red façade, and is covered with ornate grillwork, and gilded decorations. While you're downtown, take some time to try Northern Thailand's signature khao soi dish. Those with a taste for the macabre shouldn't miss the Baan Dam Museum, otherwise known as the Black House, a complex of 40 buildings filled with intricately carved woodwork and the skulls, bones, and skins of countless animals. If you're planning on heading into the mountains to visit the hill-tribes, be sure to stop by the Hill-Tribes Museum and Education Centre to learn about their culture.

name: Porvoo
description: First mentioned in the early 14th century, Porvoo holds the title of Finland's second-oldest city. Its Old Town is a maze of cobbled streets lined with colorful wooden houses and dominated by the 15th-century Porvoo Cathedral, which will transport you to a bygone era. Running through the center of the Old Town, the Porvoo River is a highlight in itself, with red-ochre warehouses and charming cafes lining the riverbank, offering a perfect spot to stop for a snack or snap some enchanting pics for the 'gram. If you have a sweet tooth, Porvoo is a delight, with the Runeberg torte being a must-try delicacy. And if you're a chocolate or ice cream lover, you're in luck too! Stop by the Brunberg Chocolate Factory for some sweets (and their famous salty liquorice) or the Old Porvoo Ice Cream Factory.

name: Santiago
description: Situated in the Sierra Madre Oriental mountain range, Santiago is a "Pueblo Magico" and charms its visitors with its quaint town and magnificent views. It dates back to the 16th century and is home to several colonial buildings and landmarks, including the Santiago Apostol Church and the Casa de Cultura. In the heart-warming Plaza Central, walk past locals sitting on benches under lights dangled from trees, and hear the laughter of children as they run around fountains playing tag. Purchase locally-made pottery and embroidery from local markets before heading to a popular lookout for panoramic views of La Boca, a large lake with majestic mountains. Indulge in fresh seafood from the restaurants that line the lake. For free entry, visit the Santiago Museum of History to browse replicas of prehistoric animals and even old rifles from the 1910 Mexican civil war.

name: Kurukshetra
description: Kurukshetra, a city steeped in mythological significance, is a captivating destination that unfolds the epic tales of the ancient Indian scriptures, especially the Mahabharata. Renowned as the battlefield of the Kurukshetra War, where the Pandavas and Kauravas clashed in a colossal conflict, the city is a living testament to the events recounted in the Mahabharata. The Brahma Sarovar, a sacred tank believed to have been created by Lord Brahma, is a prominent site that draws pilgrims who come to take a dip in its holy waters during solar eclipses. The Sannihit Sarovar, another significant water tank, is believed to be the meeting point of seven sacred Saraswatis. Devotees often perform rituals and offer prayers on its banks. Adjacent to these sarovars lies the ancient Sthaneshwar Mahadev Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, adding a spiritual dimension to the city. Kurukshetra's landscapes are adorned with numerous ghats, temples, and monuments that narrate the tales of the Mahabharata. The city's rich heritage is reflected in the architecture of its temples, each resonating with the cultural and religious tapestry of the region.

name: Huancayo
description: Sitting in the Andean plateau around 10,650 feet above sea-level, Huancayo is the region's capital and commercial center. The heart of Huancayo is the Plaza de La Independencia and its beautiful church, which serves as a great starting point to sample the city's cuisine - some of the finest in the country. Highland culture is also alive and well, which is amplified to an unmissable event during the Sunday Fair when hundreds of vendors from around the countryside come to show their crafts. At the whimsical Parque de la Identidad Huanca you'll find stone statues of Huancaino crafts and famous Andean folkloric artists, or you can head to Torre Torre outside the city to admire the unusual geology of the highlands.

name: Bruges
description: The former capital of Flanders, Bruges was one of the most culturally and economically advanced cities in Medieval Europe. This port city was home to the world's first stock exchange, and in the 15th century, nobles, exiled kings, and some of the world's best painters and weavers. Miraculously, Bruges survived World War I and II essentially unscathed, meaning that it looks today much as it did centuries ago. While the swan-filled canals, cobbled streets and medieval stone buildings are reason enough to visit, the UNESCO-listed town center also has some unmissable landmarks. Most famous is the 13th century belfry, which provides the best view of the town. At the 15th century Jerusalem's Church, you'll find an unusual skull-themed altarpiece, while the Church of Our Lady is famed for its 'Madonna with child' sculpture by Michelangelo. Art-lovers won't want to miss the Groeningemuseum, where you'll find works by everyone from Jan Van Eyck to René Magritte.

name: Les Baux-de-Provence
description: Easily defensible, Les Baux-de-Provence's rocky hilltop has been inhabited since around 6000 BC. Even today, one of the Most Beautiful Villages of France is crowned by the ruins of a medieval citadel. In the village, visitors can simply enjoy walking through the narrow cobblestone streets, between grey-stone buildings and Medieval monuments. At the rocky pinnacle, the Chateau-Fortress offers stupendous panoramic views, reaching to Aix-en-Provence in one direction, and Arles in the other. Among the castle ruins, visitors can see how stone was cut directly from the living rock, while the explanations of life and medieval battle are embodied by recreations of medieval siege engines.

name: Dunedin
description: Initially founded by the Free Church of Scotland, Dunedin (named after the Gaelic name for Edinburgh) grew in size and stature due to the Otago Gold Rush of the 1860's. The city was envisioned to encompass the architectural romantic style of the old Scottish cities, leading to something of a mixture of quirky streets and grande buildings. Some such examples of stunning buildings can be seen in the form of the Dunedin Railway Station, the First Church of Otago, and the University of Otago, New Zealand's oldest such establishment and reputedly the most beautiful in the world. Culture is a biggie in Dunedin, with attractions ranging from the excellent Speights Brewery tour, to the Toitu Otago Settlers Museum with it's engaging displays of the region's history. There is a 90 minute street art trail to follow too, with vibrant and whimsical works dotted around the centre.

name: Congonhas
description: The capital of Brazil's Minas Gerais region, the vast amounts of gold passing through Congonhas in the 17th and 18th centuries blessed the city with a wealth of Baroque architecture. Chief among its elegant monuments is the Sanctuary of Bom Jesus do Congonhas, which includes a church, several small chapels, and manicured gardens. The crown jewel of this UNESCO World Heritage Site is the churchyard, which is lined with soapstone statues of the 12 Old Testament Prophets carved by Aleijadinho, one of the finest Baroque artists in the world. If you have time, take a stroll through the historic city center, particularly Rua Bom Jesus Street. The Church of Our Lady of the Pilar is an opulent reminder of Brazil's "Golden Age", with sculptures painted in pure gold. If you're curious where all this wealth came from, pay a visit to the Museum of the School of Mines to see artifacts from the colonial mining camps.

name: Caen
description: Founded by William the Conqueror in the 11th century, the Norman King's castle that still stands to this day. However, Caen is perhaps best known for the bombing that destroyed 80% of the city during World War II. While it doesn't have the same historic charm as other Norman towns, Caen does offer visitors some fascinating landmarks. The curtain wall and dried moat of William the Conqueror's castle, one of the largest medieval fortresses in Europe, now houses the Museum of Fine Arts and the Museum of Normandy. During his reign, William ordered two abbeys to be built -the 'Men's Abbey' is now the final resting place of his thigh bone - all that remains of the legendary king. Visitors can also head to the Memorial of Caen, built in an old bunker, which is widely considered to be the best World War II museum in France.

name: Waddesdon Manor
address.addr1: Waddesdon Manor, Waddesdon, Aylesbury HP18 0JH, UK
description: Waddesdon Manor was built at the end of the 19th century in the style of a French Renaissance château for Baron Ferdinand de Rothschild. This breathtaking manor was a weekend residence for parties and showcasing the Baron's art collection. Today visitors can tour the lavishly furnished rooms where the Baron would entertain his friends. As one of the greatest art collectors of the 19th century, Waddesdon's collection showcases some stupendous pieces, such as two of the largest Guardi paintings in the world, and three of the ten remaining Sèvres ship-vases. The manor gardens are equally stupendous, filled with carpet bedding and hidden fountains, and crowned by the only surviving Rothschild aviary. Registered as a zoo, the aviary is an important breeding center for endangered species like the Rothschild's Mynah bird, which had a wild population of 6 in 2001. For more information, please visit waddesdon.org.uk

name: Ureki
description: Ureki, is small seaside resort nestled along Georgia's picturesque Black Sea coast. Located in the Guria region, Ureki offers an idyllic retreat with its subtropical climate, characterized by mild, snowless winters and hot summers. Unlike many coastal areas, Ureki has sandy beaches that allow visitors to indulge in their soft embrace, in contrast to the typical pebble-covered shores found elsewhere. Notably, the sand in Ureki is renowned for its unique composition, featuring magnetic properties and a distinctive black hue. Believed to possess healing qualities for the cardiovascular, endocrine, and respiratory systems, this magnetic sand also proves beneficial for promoting bone strength and facilitating optimal blood circulation. Furthermore, Ureki's shallow sea depth extends over long distances, making it a particularly family-friendly destination for relaxing getaways with children.

name: Port Louis
description: Port Louis, the bustling capital city of Mauritius, is a vibrant tapestry of culture, history, and modernity, offering visitors an immersive experience in the heart of the island nation. Stepping into Port Louis is like embarking on a journey through time. The city's historic landmarks, such as the majestic Citadel Fort Adelaide and the graceful Champ de Mars Racecourse, bear witness to its colonial past, while its bustling markets and vibrant streets pulse with the energy of modern Mauritius. Wander through the colorful stalls of the Central Market, where the tantalizing aromas of exotic spices and fresh produce fill the air, or lose yourself in the narrow lanes of Chinatown, where traditional Chinese architecture and culinary delights await around every corner. For a deeper understanding of the island's rich heritage, visitors can explore the diverse array of museums and cultural institutions scattered throughout the city. From the Blue Penny Museum, home to the world-renowned Blue Penny and Red Penny stamps, to the bustling streets of the Port Louis Waterfront, where historic warehouses have been transformed into trendy boutiques and waterfront cafes, there is no shortage of fascinating attractions to discover.

name: Grutas de Calcehtok
description: With over 4 kilometers of explored passageways, the Grutas de Calcehtok are said to be the Yucatan's longest dry-cave system. The caverns are filled with impressive formations like stalactites and stalagmites, curtains, pearls, and columns, and with some chambers reaching over 100 meters in diameter, there's an undeniable majesty to them. Along with their natural significance, archaeologists have uncovered ceramic arrowheads, quartz hammers, and Mayan fortifications within the caves, giving them historical importance as well. There are three "difficulty levels" to the cave tour, ranging from 1 to 4 hours, all of which have you getting your hands (and knees, and back) dirty. For the truly adventurous, the 4 hour adventure tour includes rope descents, belly crawling, and possibly squeezing through the 20cm tall "Pass of Death". Add time to your stop for this option.

name: Bellavista
description: Established in 1841, the Bellavista Factory showcases European-inspired architecture that seamlessly blends with the natural beauty of central Nayarit. Named "Bellavista" after a similar factory in Ghent, Belgium, the textile factory was meticulously designed as a replica of its European counterpart, even utilizing imported brick stones. Over time, it became a symbol of labor activism in Mexico. In 1905, the factory witnessed the country's first recorded strike led by the Elias brothers and supported by the Quintero sisters. This historical event played a pivotal role in shaping trade unionism in mexico. Take a journey back in time and witness the factory's renovated facade with its nostalgic bell-topped clock, and take a factory tour organized by the local community that guides you through the charming streets of the town and culminates in a visit to the factory. Become captivated by the enchanting fusion of European-inspired architecture and the lush landscapes of central Nayarit. Photo by Ray PVR, CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Moquegua
description: Settled by pre-Incan tribes, the first official mention of Moquegua as a Spanish settlement came in 1626 when it was known as 'Villa de Santa Catalina del Guadalcazar'. Considered one of the most successful Peruvian cities thanks to its high GDP and quality of education, it processes much of the local agriculture such as olives, grapes, and pisco (grape brandy). Though commercially important, the residents of Moquegua still like to take things easy - just head to the Plaza del Armas, with its beautiful fountain designed by Gustav Eiffel, to enjoy the fresh are and relax with the locals. If you're looking to delve deeper into the city's colonial past, head to the 18th century Casa del Regidor Perpetuo de la Ciudad, which has been opened to the public as an antique-filled a house museum.

name: Banja Luka
description: Banja Luka is surrounded by rolling hills and the beautiful Vrbas River flowing through the city. The growing city has over 1,000 cafes and bars and a rich nightlife. One of its most notable features is the fortress Kastel, which sits in the city center. The fortress was built by ancient Romans and was fortified by Ottomans. There are many churches, manicured parks, and cultural and historical buildings dating back to the Middle Ages. The city is untouched by crowds, making it a delightful and unforgettable destination spot.

name: Hamamatsu
description: Recognized as a hub of craftsmanship, Hamamatsu is synonymous with Japanese vehicles, musical instruments, and more. Considered a thriving town of all things music, The Hamamatsu Museum of Musical Instruments is a haven for music enthusiasts, boasting around 1,500 instruments from across the globe. The renowned Hamamatsu Castle, constructed by Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1570, adds to its historical allure, gracing the city's legacy with the shogun's legacy, who spent a significant number of years there. The castle grounds, adorned with cherry trees and a Japanese garden, invite leisurely strolls. Hamamatsu's culinary specialty is freshwater eel (unagi). Don't miss the opportunity to savor this delicacy and even unique eel-infused cookies known as "eel pies." The city's allure extends to Hamamatsu Flower Park and Hamamatsu Fruit Park, where diverse blooms and fruits enchant visitors.

name: Vallarta Botanical Gardens
description: The Vallarta Botanical Gardens offer visitors a cool retreat from the hustle and bustle of Vallarta. The gardens were opened in 2005 with the goal of educating the public through environmental conservation tours and classes. Visitors can roam the lush grounds, hike the manicured trails or take a dip in the Rio Horcones river if they feel up to a challenge. Should you find yourself in the area and fancy a visit, insect repellent is recommended. Grab lunch at the restaurant after working up an appetite. You can view all of the etiquette tips on the Vallarta Botanical Garden's website here: https://www.vbgardens.org/ Make sure to double-check the opening hours as these change by the season. They are closed on Mondays from April to November. The price is 200 MEX per person or around 9 EUR (children under 4 are free).

name: Long Bay Beach
address.addr1: Long Bay Beach, British Virgin Islands
description: Long Bay Beach invites travelers to indulge in a world of relaxation and adventure, where every moment is infused with the magic of the tropics. Whether you're seeking solitude amidst swaying palm trees or craving excitement beneath the sun-drenched skies, this idyllic haven promises an unforgettable experience. Sink your toes into the soft sands and feel the warmth of the Caribbean sun caress your skin as you unwind in paradise. Take a leisurely stroll along the shore, letting the gentle rhythm of the waves soothe your soul, or embark on a snorkeling adventure to discover the vibrant marine life that thrives beneath the surface. For those craving a taste of adventure, Long Bay Beach offers a myriad of water sports and activities, from kayaking and paddleboarding to windsurfing and sailing.

name: Hohenzollern Castle
description: This ancestral seat of a Prussian family dynasty makes for both a lively and historic stop by and its phenomenal location once prompted Emperor William II to exclaim "The panorama from the Hohenzollern Castle is truly worth a journey". The family still uses the castle today, and their presence is signaled by the flying of the flag with the family crest. Visitors can tour the plentiful showrooms that reflect the castle's history, see the actual Prussian Crown and roam around the castle cellars, the casements, the two churches and the tower. What sets this castle apart is its interaction with its visitors who get to see, hear and touch a lot more than is usually on display in many similar properties. Not only are there excellent views for photo opportunities, but there's a good chance you might snap a selfie with a real life prince and princess whenever they are at home!

name: Acre
description: Settled since 2000 BC, Acre was the capital and chief port of the Crusader's Kingdom of Jerusalem. After being conquered by the Muslims, the original defenses were further enhanced, owing their current state to the Ottomans. The Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its well-preserved Ottoman architecture and remains of the medieval Crusader settlement. The bustling main market and charming Turkish Bazaar let visitors experience life as it's been in the city for hundreds of years - not to mention offer an opportunity to do some shopping and enjoy the city's exceptional food. The 18th century Al-Jazzar Mosque is a stunning example of reminder of the city's still-thriving Muslim community, and is the largest in the country outside of Jerusalem. Perhaps the most unique experience is the "Kingdom Of The Knights". The medieval Crusader settlement was buried by sand, so now you explore its streets and buildings underground, eventually following a secret tunnel to the port.

name: Shreveport, LA
description: Shreveport, Louisiana, situated in the heart of the Ark-La-Tex region, beckons visitors with its unique blend of Southern charm, vibrant culture, and rich history. Delve into the city's rich past by exploring its numerous museums, such as the Louisiana State Exhibit Museum and the R.W. Norton Art Gallery, showcasing a diverse range of exhibits from local art to historical artifacts. Stroll through the historic downtown area, where charming brick streets are lined with boutiques, art galleries, and cozy cafes. For those seeking entertainment, Shreveport boasts a lively music scene with venues hosting everything from jazz and blues to country and rock. Be sure to catch a live performance at one of the city's renowned music venues, such as the Shreveport Municipal Auditorium or the Strand Theatre. Nature enthusiasts will find plenty to explore in Shreveport's outdoor spaces, including scenic parks, nature trails, and the picturesque Red River. Take a leisurely stroll along the riverfront promenade or enjoy a relaxing riverboat cruise to admire the city's skyline from the water.

name: Puebla
description: According to legend, Puebla was settled after a bishop dreamt of a magnificent city along a clear stream in a valley of woods. Angels descended from heaven to trace the city out before the bishop's eyes which led him to discover the land where modern-day Puebla rests. The city remains as divine as ever with its beautiful main cathedral and array of elegant churches. These perfectly preserved structures rest amongst stunning Renaissance and Mexican Baroque buildings. Puebla was named a World Heritage City for its rich history and cultural heritage. Today, contemporary eateries, galleries and more lie within the city's old buildings while a thriving nightlife adds to the allure. See everything that the bishop could never have dreamt of.

name: Espel
description: Espel was built on land reclaimed from what was once the Zuiderzee sea. Founded in 1956 as one of Flevoland's carefully planned "green villages," it bears the name of Espelbergh, a settlement north of Urk that was tragically washed away during the devastating All Saints' Flood of 1570. Today's Espel thrives at the intersection of modern land-reclamation technology and the traditional agricultural lifestyle. The surrounding countryside transforms each spring into a spectacular array of tulips and other bulbous flowers, celebrated with seasonal walking and cycling routes. To the west, along the IJsselmeer dyke, the Windpark Noordoostpolder—the Netherlands' largest hybrid on-shore and off-shore wind farm—represents modern sustainability.

name: Taupo
description: Not only is Taupo blessed with magnificent views across a lake to the Tongariro mountains, but it also has some of the most varied activities on the North Island. For the thrill seekers you can bungee jump over the Waikato river, take a jet boat ride up the same river, or enjoy an alternative view of the beautiful scenery as part of a skydive. For those who like their feet on terra firma a trip to the powerful and impressive Hukka Falls is a must, and for geothermal lovers both the Craters of the Moon and Spa Park Hot Pools offer inexpensive thermal activities. For hikers who want an amazing vista the nearby, and relatively easy, Mount Tauhara is well worth the effort. And of course the lake itself offers many opportunities for cruising and watersports of all kinds, and a chance to explore the many hidden bays.

name: Batalha
description: In 1385, King João I vowed that if his outnumbered army defeated the Castilians at the important Battle of Aljubarrota, he would build a magnificent monastery dedicated to the Virgin Mary. The king was victorious, resulting in the independence of Portugal from Spain and the great Batalha ("Battle") Monastery, as well as the founding of the town of Batalha itself. João's monument is a masterpiece of Portuguese Gothic architecture, combining Gothic and Manueline styles from its 200 year construction period. Its most dramatic feature is right in the centre of the chapel: the enormous tomb of Dom João I and his wife, Queen Philippa of Lancaster. On the site of the battle itself stands the humble Capela de Sao Jorge. With its Romanesque architecture and austere decoration, it is the yin to the Batalha Monastery's yang.

name: Holambra
description: A portmanteau of Holland, American, and Brazil, Holambra was founded by a group of 500 Dutch Catholic refugees following the devastation of their homeland during World War II. Originally the immigrants planned to produce milk and dairy products, but after their cattle were wiped out by tropical diseases, they fell back on another quintessential Dutch industry: growing flowers. Today, this vibrant community, still mostly descended from the original Dutch immigrants, is a horticultural hub. Pay a visit in September for ExpoFlora, South America's largest flower festival. Or if you're visiting any other time of year, head to the Garden Center to see the largest variety of flowers in the country - you can even take a 1.5-hour tour of the fields on weekends and holidays (extend your stop time if you plan to take the tour). There are also plenty of Dutch heritage on display. Grab a traditional meal at the Old Dutch, before checking out the colorful houses downtown, or the largest windmill in South America.

name: Chillon Castle
description: The rocky outcrop on the banks of Lake Geneva has provided shelter to its inhabitants since the Bronze Age. The Romans were the first to utilize the rock as a fortified position, with the castle of today having its origins in the 11th century. From the 12th to 16th centuries, it was a summer residence of the Counts of Savoy, who also used it as a profitable toll station. Today, much of the castle's history has been preserved, and visitors can view wall paintings from the 14th century, the subterranean vaults, parade halls, and the noble bedroom. François Bonivard was confined in the castle's cavernous prison for years and was the inspiration for Lord Byron's 'The Prisoner of Chillon'. The gothic arched ceiling and tall windows drew Mark Twain's envy. To best experience the complex's 25 buildings and three courtyards, protected by two circular walls, we recommend booking a guided tour in advance at https://www.chillon.ch/en/Z5066/guided-tours

name: Estepona
description: Lying on the coast of the Mediterranean, Estepona is a popular spot for many travelers. The city is renowned for its marvelous beaches and equally attractive promenades. However, it would be a shame to stick to the sand as there is much more the town has to offer. The historical center featuring distinct architecture of little white houses is there to satisfy those, who decided to give up sunbathing and swimming for a moment. The remains of San Luis Castle from the 15th century should not escape your attention either. However, wherever you'll find yourself, a great espresso and local fish will be always a few steps away.

name: Edinburgh
description: Though the area has been settled since around 8500 BC, Edinburgh as it stands today didn't begin to develop until the early Middle Ages. Despite nearly constant warring with the English, Edinburgh grew exponentially over the years, and by the 18th century, was one of the most densely populated cities in Europe. This led to the development of the neo-Classical 'New Town', and the city's new nickname - 'Athens of the North'. Today, visitors can explore the compact Old Town, highlighted by the 12th century Palace of Holyroodhouse (open to visitors when the Queen isn't home), and the imposing Edinburgh Castle, where visitors will find the Scottish Crown Jewels and the 'Witches Well', where women were burned for witchcraft during the 16th and 17th centuries. In the New Town, amongst the many neo-Classical monuments, visitors can how the upper class lived in the 18th century 'Georgian House', or relax in front of the 200 foot neo-Gothic spire dedicated to Sir Walter Scott.

name: Jardin Botanico Dr. Alfredo Barrera Marin
address.addr1: Jardin Botanico Dr. Alfredo Barrera Marin
address.city: Jardin Botanico Dr. Alfredo Barrera Marin
description: Founded in 1982, the Jardin Botanico Dr. Alfredo Barrera Marin covers 65 hectares of lush forest just outside Cancun's bustling resorts. Two kilometers of hiking trails wind their way through a jungle filled with the region's flora, including the Maya's sacred Ceiba trees, tall palms, bromeliads, ferns, orchids, and plants used in traditional Mayan medicine. A variety of native animals call the garden home, ranging from delicate butterflies to colorful birds, and the last troop of spider monkeys on the Yucatan coast. Along with preserving a bit of the Yucatan's wild side, the reserve also has a small archaeological site, a reconstructed Maya home, and a chiclero camp.

name: Museo de las Animas
description: Housed in a historic church, the Museo de las Animas tells the tale of the region's history through a collection of over 20 mummies. As their clothing suggests, many of the bodies date from the late 18th century and early 19th centuries, and attest to the dangers faced by locals. One woman was likely killed by rat poison, while a man was murdered by bandits after unearthing some gold nuggets. Still others come from the 1920s, when the region was ravaged by a bloody Cristero rebellion, like the guerrilla leader who was executed by firing squad. Along with the mummies, the museum also exhibits everything from religious artefacts to photographs and paintings. Please note: the museum is closed on Mondays.

name: San Miguel de Allende
description: Spearheaded by a culture shift by its foreign residents, San Miguel de Allende has become a prime location for tourists looking for mild-climate, diversity and laid-back atmosphere. The historical core has been adopted by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site. Walking through its characteristic cobblestone pathways, you will find yourself to be in a time capsule, as the city works tirelessly to maintain its trademark colonial aesthetic. La Parroquia de San Miguel Arcángel, built in 1880, is one of the most photographed churches in Mexico, and its colourful spires can be seen from all parts of San Miguel de Allende. The Juarez Park further defines San Miguel de Allende by its mix of French and Neoclassical architecture. Casa de Allende was the home of Ignacio Allende, an inspirational figure of the Mexican War of Independence. Converted into a museum, Casa de Allende characterizes the proud nature of the city's history.

name: Mostar
description: The small town of Mostar (meaning 'bridge-keepers') is located in southern Bosnia and Herzegovina and straddles the Neretva River. Known as one of the most fascinating cities in the world, Mostar combines influences from Christian Europe and Muslim Middle East. The star of the city is the Old Bridge, built in the 16th century. Most of the city's historic old town (including the Old Bridge) was destroyed in the 1990's conflict. The town has since been rebuilt and restored. The Ottoman-style Old Bridge was rebuilt in 2004 and connects the two sides of the city. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site standing as a symbol of reconciliation and harmony between diverse communities. There are also many mosques and Turkish influences throughout the city. The architectural and natural beauty of the city make it a worthwhile visit.

name: Babahoyo
description: Where the riches of plains and river converge, there rises the capital of Los Rios. Babahoyo is not the traditional tourist city, it is a place where authentic life coexists with gorgeous scenery. From the houses rising on stilts from the river to the imposing cathedral with its elaborate murals, there is much to admire and see in this out of the way city. Serving as the convergent point between the coastal and mountain regions, Babahoyo has long been a center of trade and wealth. The Vinces District has even earned the moniker: Little Paris as grand mansions line it's broad streets, a testament to the city's power and prosperity. Perhaps the biggest draw are the cathedral's murals which beautifully detail the Virgin Mary and other religious iconography. Further out from the city lie beautiful waterfalls, old plantations and plenty of greenery. Truly Babahoyo is a city of contrasts.

name: Jipijapa
description: Founded in 1565, Jipijapa remained a small agricultural community until the mid-19th century when coffee was introduced to the region. After this, the town quickly grew, and is nicknamed "La Sultana del Café" for its coffee production. While coffee is a key part of Jipijapa's economy, the town is better known for producing Panama hats, which are known in Ecuador as jipijapas. In fact, the hats are so important that the town built a monument to them, which is recognized as the largest hat in the world, while the traditional weaving of the hats has been added to the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List. Around the central park with the giant hat, you'll find heritage houses, and the picturesque San Lorenzo Church.

name: Belfort
description: The gap between the Vosges and the Jura mountain ranges has been settled since Gallo-Roman times - a strategic position that shaped the development of the city. Situated near the Swiss and German borders, Vauban was tasked with re-fortifying the city in the 17th century. Today, visitors can explore the citadel's network of passageways, enjoy stunning panoramic views from its lookout points, or visit its barracks to delve into local history. Carved into the cliff below the citadel, stands the proud Lion of Belfort - a 22 metre long relief with a lookalike statue on Place Denfert-Rochereau in Paris. In the picturesque city center, visitors take a break at one of the city's many cafe-lined squares, admire the pink-sandstone facade of the Cathedral of St. Christopher, or head to the Museum of Fine Arts, housed in an old fortified tower.

name: Kecskemet
description: In the heart of Hungary's Great Plain, Kecskemét is ringed with vineyards and orchards that meld into the countryside. With its convenient location, the city raked in agricultural wealth, and used it wisely. Starting in the main square, the city gives visitors a crash course in the regional Art Nouveau style. The sandy pink City Hall is bedecked with ceramic tiles and combines Art Nouveau and Romantic styles. Every hour, it chimes out music from local composers Zoltán Kodály, or classical composers like Beethoven and Mozart. The Baroque church next-door is the largest in the region, and displays large tablets honouring the many citizens who died defending Kecskemét. A walk across the square brings visitors to one of city's most representative Secessionist structures: the Cifra Palota, or Ornamental Palace. Built in 1902, the Kecskemét Gallery is housed within its wavy walls and colourful roof tiles.

name: Arusha
description: Arusha is mostly known for being a safari capital, but there is so much more to explore with the cultural vastness of this city! Go on a hike or enjoy a safari near the Arusha National Park. With volcanoes, mountain views, and safari tours available, there is much to do and explore. Enjoy the markets with exotic coffee, spices, fruit, and more! For art lovers, there is the Cultural Heritage craft mall that has a large selection of African artefacts and sculptures.

description: Mixing the old with the new, you'll love exploring all of the historical aspects that are around Oamaru. Begin on Harbour Street where Victorian era buildings line the historic street, filled with shops and restaurants, you'll be discovering pieces of Oamaru's history all around this area of the city. In the same district you will also be able to find many galleries that are sure to question and excite. One of the more unique galleries is the "Lost Souls Gallery," here you will be transported to a weird and wonderful world of sculpture and art. Then stop in Steampunk HQ, a museum/gallery, this indoor interactive playground is one of a kind and fun for the whole family! If you're looking for a neat nature experience, go down to the water just before sunset and watch the little blue penguins return home after being at sea, it is cuteness overload!

name: Lille
description: Founded in the middle ages, Lille was part of the County of Flanders, which was one of the richest and most prosperous regions of Europe. The city flourished under Flemish rule until 1667, when Louis XIV besieged and captured the city. This transition is particularly apparent in the city's historic quarter, where the Baroque facades of the 17th and 18th century houses make the older buildings look downright somber. When it comes to museums, Lille's Palais des Beaux Arts, housed in a breathtaking 19th century Belle Époque summer palace, is second only to the Louvre for size. Inside, works by Monet, Raphael, Gustave Courbet, Rubens, van Gogh, Donatello, and Picasso are accompanied by high-detail 17th and 18th-century scale models of cities. Lille's old stock exchange, consisting of 24 Flemish renaissance houses around a central arcaded courtyard, is considered the city's most splendid building.

name: Bintulu
description: Bintulu is known for its role in producing the majority of Malaysia's Liquified Natural Gas supply, but offers a vast array of serene nature and a plethora of attractions. The district is a haven for eco-tourism, boasting picturesque beaches, coastal regions, and national parks that provide glimpses into Malaysia's diverse wildlife. A leisurely walk along the stunning beaches of Similajau National Park, such as Turtle Beach and Golden Beach, allows for relaxation amidst casuarina plantations, sunbathing, and breathtaking sunsets. Tumbina Bintulu, a two-in-one zoological and botanical garden perched atop a hill, captivates nature enthusiasts with its magnificent orchids and native Bornean animals like hornbills, ostriches, and crocodiles. Food lovers can indulge in a culinary adventure in Bintulu, from savory satay and crispy pisang goreng (banana fritters) to refreshing Es Campur (mixed ice) and flavorful noodles. To experience the vibrant local life and shop for unique goods, Pasar Tamu and Pasar Utama are must-visit markets. Here, one can find a wide array of products, including Pua Kumbu textiles and woven palm bags, alongside an adventurous option to sample sago worms, a local delicacy exclusive to Sarawak.

name: Phitsanulok
description: Phitsanulok was founded in the 11th century as a small Khmer outpost, but became a major city in Thai history, briefly serving as the capital of the Ayutthaya kingdom, and was the birthplace of King Naresuan, who freed the country from Burmese domination in the late 16th century. Today, this friendly city has a slew of attractions that are making it an increasingly popular place to visit. Chief among these is the Wat Phra Si Ratana Mahathat, a 14th century temple with some amazing ornamentation, including mother-of-pearl inlay doors, and one of the country's most revered Buddha images. You'll also be able to examine a sizeable collection of Sukhothai period art at the Buddha Chinnarat National Museum. To learn about local culture, the Sergeant Major Thawee Folk Museum has exhibits everything from tools to textiles, to native fish in five traditional Thai buildings.

name: Ubon Ratchathani
description: Founded by Lao immigrants in the 1700s, Ubon Ratchathani prospered as a US airbase during the Vietnam War. Today, Ubon Ratchathani is still a village at heart, and its residents are famously hospitable to visitors. With two universities the city has a lively hum to it, and hip coffee shops punctuate the historic temples. While not as grand and imposing as those in Bangkok, Uban's temple's have an undeniable charm - just see the 200 year old Wat Thung Si Muang - its scripture hall, an elegant wooden structure that combines Thai and Burmese styles, standing on stilts, rising above a lotus pond, is simply enchanting. At the Ubon Ratchathani National Museum you'll find everything from a 2500-year-old bronze drum to Ubon textiles. While you're exploring, be sure to stop for food - the shops will excitedly try cater to visitors and tone down the heat, but you can still expect blazingly hot Isaan food.

name: Ibarra
description: Ibarra is popular with tourists all year round due to it's favourable Mediterranean climate, kept warm due to it's close proximity to the equator but kept cool due to it's high elevation. Nicknamed the "White City" in relation to it's white-washed colonial-era houses, and blessed with a number of old cobbled streets, this city particularly comes alive on Saturdays when the market comes to town. Ibarra is also famous for its home-made ice creams called "Helados de paila" which was first made during Incan times and is still enjoyed today. The locals take great pride in the many beautiful religious buildings in the old town, each with unique art and architecture, such as historical wood carvings. For a great viewpoint of the surrounding area and the Yahuarcocha Lake it is worth visiting the Archangel Michael monument, from which you can also see the nearby towns of San Antonio and Cotacachi.

name: Nancy
description: Founded around the 11th century as a fortified town, Nancy gradually grew in importance, becoming the capital of the duchy of Lorraine. However, its heydey came in the 18th century when exiled Polish king Stanislaus Leszczyński, father-in-law to Louis XV, was then given the duchy, and oversaw the proliferation of Baroque culture and architecture. To connect the medieval old town to the newer part of the city, Stanislaus had his eponymous square constructed. Today, this, along with the Place de la Carrière, and Place d'Alliance, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites all lined with beautiful baroque building and gilded gates. In the old town, visitors will find narrow cobbled streets lined with medieval and renaissance building,and the Lorraine Museum, the final resting place of the Dukes of Lorraine, and home to one of the finest sculpture collections in France. The city is also proud of its cuisine, so be sure to sample some of the local specialties!

name: Mascota
description: Walking through the town of Mascota feels like a drunkard's nightmare - the houses built every which way, as the people had pleased, before urbanization. Such is the nature of this calm town in the Western Sierra Madre, comfortable despite the chaos. You'll find the climate more moderate, the locals happy and proud, and the Baroque architecture captivating. Enjoy a coffee in the city, or head to the Corrinchis Dam to walk along the water. Looking for a bit of history? Don't miss the Archaeological Museum, where you can view artifacts and petroglyphs collected from archaeological sites in the surrounding region.

name: Flensburg
description: Founded around the 13th century, Flensburg quickly rose to prominence thanks to its sheltered port and excellent fisheries, and prospered greatly in the 18th century by importing sugar cane from the West Indies to produce rum - even today, the city is still home to a rum distillery. Today, visitors can enjoy a walk along the harbour boardwalk, admiring the quaint houses and bobbing sailboats while snacking on a traditional fish roll. Next to the harbour, the Museumswerft Flensburg preserves traditional ship-building techniques, even hosting workshops for visitors to try their hand at it. At the Museumsberg Flensburg, visitors are treated to two museums in a single historic building, exhibiting regional art and culture from the 17th to 20th centuries in historically furnished room. The 14th century Gothic Nikolaikirche has a beautiful 18th century altarpiece, and an exceptionally ornate double organ.

name: Dorset Heavy Horse Farm Park
description: The Dorset Heavy Horse Farm Park is both a family attraction and a Conservation Centre for Rare Breed Heavy Horses. Here, visitors can learn about how Heavy Horses have helped man for thousands of years, from bearing knights in armour, to delivering beer, coal, and milk, and ploughing fields. Daily presentations and displays with over 20 rare breeds of Heavy Horses, including some of the most endangered breeds really drive home their strength, beauty, and impact on human history. There are also plenty of hands-on experiences to be had, from a horse-drawn carriage ride to driving a tractor and typical farm activities like collecting eggs. For more information, please visit dorset-heavy-horse-centre.co.uk

name: Benevento
description: One of the chief cities of Samnium, Benevento's origins likely go back even early, but it first appears in history as a Samnite city the resisted the Romans through two wars. The Romans left their mark on the city, with their Leproso bridge still offering safe-crossing of the Sabato River. Trajan's Arch, built to celebrate the extension of the Via Appia from Benevento to Brindisi, is well preserved, with beautiful bas-reliefs on both façades. The Roman Theatre, commissioned by Emperor Hadrian, is still used for theatrical performances today. The Longobards ruled the city for about five centuries, leaving behind the 8th century Santa Sofia Church. A UNESCO World Heritage Site, as part of a group of seven buildings that represent the Longobards' influence in Italy, it still has fragments of its 8th- to early 9th-century frescoes.

name: Asolo
description: Originally known as Acelum to the ancient Romans, their influence on the city can still be seen today by the remains of an amphitheatre and aqueduct. The unassuming medieval cathedral in the heart of town, built on the site of the original Roman baths, is renowned for its important works of art, such as the 16th century 'Assumption' by Lorenzo Lotto, a 19th century copy of the Assumption by Titian, and a 15th century painting of Saint Francis of Assisi. Visitors with an eye for the decadent can't miss the many villas. The frescoed Palazzo della Ragione now houses the regional museum, and Villa Scotti Pasini which was home to acclaimed English poet Robert Browning in the late 19th century. The crowning jewel of The Pearl of Treviso is the Rocca Di Asolo, a 13th century castle that offers stupendous views.

name: Ex-Convento de Santo Domingo de Yanhuitlan
address.addr1: Ex-Convento de Santo Domingo de Yanhuitlán
address.city: Ex-Convento de Santo Domingo de Yanhuitlan
description: The Ex-Convento de Santo Domingo de Yanhuitlan was constructed in the 16th century. Constructed by Dominican settlers who arrived after the Spanish, the architecture was built in a Gothic and Plateresque style as well as decorated with Dominican motifs, which included dogs and fleur de lis. As a newly opened museum, the goal is to display the 17th century economy and culture. Some of the exhibits include artifacts from that time such as an exact copy of the Yanhuitlán Codex, elements of architecture from the Mixtec, and land parcels from the 17th century. Shining a light on the Mixtec's perspective of history, this ex-convent will be just as interesting as it is historical.

name: Villa de Merlo
description: Founded at the very end of the 18th century, Villa de Merlo is little known to foreign travelers, but is a popular holiday destination for Argentinians. The main draw is the unique microclimate, which experiences 300 days of sun at the foot of the Comechingones Mountain Range. While the climate and beautiful surroundings make Villa de Merlo a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, the historic center is a hidden gem of colonial architecture. From the main square, which is centered around a statue honoring the town's founding, head to the charming little Our Lady of the Rosary Chapel. From there, you can meander to the pleasant home of poet Antonio Agüero to learn about the author and his love for Merlo. Nature lovers and dendrophiles will want to add at least 30 minutes to include a drive to the "El Algarrobo Abuelo" - a thousand-year-old carob tree the poet wrote about.

name: Ibague
description: Dating back to the 16th century, Ibague is a thriving mountain city in the heart of Colombia's coffee country. To Colombians, it's known as the "City of Music" thanks to the prestigious Conservatory of Tolima. A quiet mountain city, one of the preferred past times here is sitting in the Plaza de Bolívar and people watching. Filled with fountains and gardens, and watched over by the elegant Catedral Inmaculada Concepción, it's a great place to unwind with some street food. The tamales in Ibague are said to be the best in Colombia, so grab one (or five), to see for yourself. Nature lover might want to pay a visit to the Fundación Orquidea to see rare flowers like the endangered Cattleya trianae, learn about orchids, and hike up to the mirador for some great views.

name: Santa Maria de Montserrat
description: Tradition states that St. Luke carved the statue of the Black Virgin of Montserrat around 50 AD, which was brought to Spain and hidden from the Moors in a mountain cave. It was rediscovered in 880 AD, and shortly after, four chapels had sprung up on the site, of which one still remains. The Monastery, located near the top of a 4,000-foot mountain, is home to about 80 monks who welcome visitors to join Mass and the Liturgy of the Hours. Next to the monastery, the neo-Gothic Basilica houses the Black Virgin, and is also home to one of the oldest and most renowned boys' choirs in Europe, who sing every day at 1:00PM. To see the Holy Grotto where the Black Virgin was discovered, a funicular brings visitors halfway and the rest of the trip must be made on foot.

name: Reims
description: In 816 Pope Stephen IV crowned Louis the Debonnaire here, establishing a tradition that would last until 1825. The UNESCO-listed Notre-Dame cathedral is a masterpiece of Gothic art, and provided a magnificent backdrop for the royal coronation ceremonies held within. Nicknamed 'The Cathedral of Angels' because of its magnificent statues of angels with opened wings, the interior is illuminated by stupendous stained glass windows. Next door, the Tau palace, a former archbishop's palace where the coronation banquets were once held. Today this UNESCO World Heritage Site is home to the Works of Notre-Dame museum where tapestries, sculptures, the cathedral treasury, and coronation-related objects are exhibited. The third UNESCO site is the striking Romano-Gothic Saint-Remi basilica, which dates back to the 11th century. In the former Saint-Remi abbey, also UNESCO-listed, visitors can find a museum that exhibits art and artefacts from Prehistory to the Middle Ages.

name: Lake Kournas
description: Snuggled in a valley and surrounded by the hills of the White Mountains, you'll find Lake Kournas, Crete's only freshwater. The lake attracts visitors because of its scenery, of course, and its wildlife inhabitants who can be observed from a rented pedal boat or canoe. It's possible to swim in the lake, that is if you don't mind bumping into fish, eels or a turtles. Thanks to the crystal clear water that also changes color throughout the day, you won't miss your new friends! Birds and ducks in particular also inhabit the lake, so there's a good chance you'll be able to say hi to them too. On the hills and along the bank stand tavernas offering apaki (smoked pork) and giftshops with pottery, produce and clothing. Depending on the water levels, the lake even has sandy beaches, which sounds good enough to pay this place a visit.

name: Marigot Bay
description: Indulge in the allure of Marigot Bay, a Caribbean paradise that has charmed Hollywood and visitors alike. Located just south of Castries along the central western coast of Saint Lucia, Marigot Bay is a cinematic masterpiece featuring swaying palm trees, anchored boats, and pristine white sand beaches. Described as a romantic haven, Marigot Bay offers a blissfully quiet escape, contrasting the lively atmosphere of nearby Reduit. Recent visitors, captivated by its beauty, recommend viewing the bay from the surrounding hills or the charming Marigot Village for a panoramic perspective. While some travelers yearn for more beach space and activities, Marigot Bay's enchantment is best experienced from both land and water. Kayaking through the mangroves or opting for a water taxi excursion allows you to immerse yourself in the scenic landscape.

name: Mazamitla
description: The town of Mazamitla is tucked into lush hills not far from the shores of Lake Chapala. The surrounding forest dampens noise to blanket the town in a cool embrace. If you're passing through, cobbled streets and simple wooden houses further offer calm and tranquility to anyone needing a change of pace. Endless gardens and parks dot the small town while restaurants and shops pop up between small churches and homes. Breeze through and leave feeling relaxed and refreshed.

name: Phraya Nakhon Cave
description: The Phraya Nakhon Cave consists of two main chambers. The first contains a dry waterfall, stalactites and stalagmites, and an information board to familiarize visitors with the cave's layout. The second, and main reason for going, is a huge dome with an opening in the center that lets in sunlight. Beneath this opening, atop a small hill and surrounded by trees, stands the beautiful Kuha Karuhas pavilion, which was built in preparation for a visit by King Rama V in the 19th century. To reach the cave, visitors must first get to Laem Sala beach, which is accessible by a short boat ride, or about 30 minute walk through the forest. From here, you must take a rather steep staircase for 430 meters to reach the cave entrance, so appropriate footwear is strongly recommended! Please note: while the cave is free, there is a 200 baht fee to enter the National Park.

name: Santiago de los Caballeros
description: Settled in 1495 by 30 aristocrats who followed Columbus to the Dominican Republic, Santiago de los Caballeros was the country's first capital before it was leveled by an earthquake in 1562. It's since recovered, and today, the "Ciudad Corazón", is the second largest in the country. The historic center is lined with Victorian houses and crowned by the Neo-Classical Cathedral of Santiago.To the southeast, the 18th century Fortaleza San Luis serves as a museum displaying everything from cannons and tanks to statues of important historical figures and Taino artifacts and cultural items. But Santiago's chief landmark is the Monumento a Los Héroes de la Restauración, a white marble tower, surrounded by gardens, which has four floors of displays documenting the Restoration War. On the fifth floor, a wraparound balcony offers panoramic views of the city with the Cordillera Central mountain range in the distance.

name: Mexican Turtle Center
description: The Mexican Turtle Center opened in the little beach town of Mazunte in 1991 as a way to make amends for the former turtle slaughterhouse that devastated the local sea turtle population, while still supporting the local economy. Every species of marine turtle found in Mexico, as well as 6 species of river turtle, and 2 types of native land turtles are housed in large outdoor tanks, aquariums, and terrariums here. A guide will educate you about each species as well as the center's conservation work to repopulate the critically endangered sea turtles. If you visit between March and November, you might be lucky enough to see the baby turtles released into the wild! The Mexican Turtle Center is open to the public Tuesdays through Saturdays, 10 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., and Sundays from 10 to 2:30 p.m. Please note: the entrance fee of 38MXN is not included.

name: Vilcabamba
description: Vilcabamba has been made famous at least twice in it's history. Firstly Incan nobility used to come to this peaceful valley for the fresh mountain air, water and mineral-rich food. The mountain that overlooks the village is known as the Sleeping Inca and is said to protect the valley from earthquakes. In the 1970's the village became famous for having an unusually long-lived population, with reports of residents living up until 135. Tourist and visitors flocked to the area to experience this miracle, but several years later the myth was debunked and it was proved that the oldest person in the village was actually 96! The legend still brings in tourists today, but much of the draw is to do with the spectacular scenery and natural surroundings, much like the Incas 500 years ago. The local cuisine is particularly fine, and vegans especially will be surprised by the selection.

name: Telavi
description: Telavi is a city rich in Georgian heritage, with historical monuments and a thriving winemaking scene. Visit the magnificent King Erekle II Palace, adorned with a statue of the king himself, built as a testament to the city's royal past. Nearby, the "Old Tree" is a majestic plane tree that has stood for nine centuries and serves as a symbol of Telavi, encouraging visitors to gather around and marvel at its grandeur. Take a trip to the awe-inspiring Alaverdi Cathedral, one of the tallest churches in the region, and be accompanied by the winding and pristine Alazani River on your journey to it. Immerse yourself in the city's vibrant cultural scene by visiting the Telavi cultural center, where concerts, theatrical performances, and other artistic events take place. Stroll through the city's medieval-like streets with their charming cobblestone sidewalks, and find tranquility in Telavi's park before sampling some authentic Qvevri Georgian wines at the esteemed Schuchmann Winery. See history, culture, and the art of winemaking intertwine in this unforgettable city.

name: Puerto Vallarta
description: Known for its calming shores and captivating nightlife, this oceanside wonder will have even the most laidback of beachgoers, immersing themselves in the hubbub of Puerto Vallarta. The adventure starts at sunrise on the sands of Playa de las Olas Altas or 'High Wave Beach'. Surfing and fishing are popular pastimes here. From the beach, enter the town and cross swinging bridges onto Isla Cuale. This small island is steeped in authenticity, with monuments, museums, and a two-storey market to explore! Standing tall on the horizon, is the Cathedral of Our Lady Guadalupe, an homage to the patron saint of Mexico. Return to the shore and take a boat tour into the Bay of Banderas and the protected Los Arcos Marine Park, where you can dive beneath huge, naturally formed, granite arches. The surrounding reefs are bursting with color and marine life, and the calm waters make snorkeling accessible for even the newest of swimmers. Back on dry land, as the sun sets on the Pacific, make your way to the bustling boardwalk. Stretching from Zona Romantica and Los Muertos Beach Pier to La Rotonda del Mar and Playa Rosita; here the fiesta is in full flow.

name: Tataouine
description: For nerds around the world, Tataouine is one of the most famous cities that you never knew existed. Relatively modern, the city itself wasn't featured in Star Wars, but George Lucas did use its name in recognition of the many filming locations in southern Tunisia. The main draw here are the nearby fortified granaries where the movies were actually filmed. Built in the 15th century by the local Berbers, Ksar Ouled Soltane is a multi-level building designed to protect grain and people from raiders and the scorching desert sun. The sun-baked adobe buildings with their narrow exterior stairways stood in for Mos Espa and the slave quarters where young Anakin Skywalker and his mother Shmi lived in Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace. The nearby Ksar Hadada also served as part of the Mos Espa slave quarters.

name: El Tatio
description: Geysers alone are an impressive sight: hissing steams and scalding water erupting from the earth create a captivating natural display. El Tatio Geysers in the Atacama Desert of Northern Chile not only promise this spectacle but also stand as the highest geyser site in the world. If that isn't enough, El Tatio ranks as the third-largest geyser field globally and the largest in the Southern Hemisphere. The site boasts at least 80 geysers, all set against the surreal backdrop of the Atacama Desert, which is often likened to Martian landscapes. Visitors might spot wildlife like vicunas, Andean foxes, and flamingos. Please note: the site's high altitude can cause altitude sickness. It's advisable to wear layers due to potentially harsh weather, always apply sunscreen, and bring a swimsuit if you fancy a dip in a thermal pool.

name: Steyr
description: Steyr sits at the confluence of two rivers in the town center, the Enns and the Steyr, and to witness these two fast flowing rivers coming together is a sight to be seen. Although Steyr has been a center of wealth and industry throughout history and is currently the Austrian headquarters of BMW, it is the town square that grabs the attention with its beautiful collection of historic old buildings. The square fills many visitors with a sense of wonderment at being surrounded by a festival of decorative architecture and it is not long before you realize that Steyr has everything imaginable in a medieval fantasy — a drawbridge, a castle (dating back to 980), tiny alleyways that wind up in crumbling courtyards, and rococo church towers that soar into the sky. This is a town that pleasantly surprises and never disappoints its visitors, many of whom leave impatient to return.

name: Niort
description: An important French financial center, Niort also knows the value of history, and is filled with Medieval and Renaissance monuments. Dominating the town is the 12th century Donjon. Built by Henry II and Richard the Lionheart, it is one of the largest castles remaining from this period, and now houses a Museum of Ethnology and Archaeology. The Pilori is a 14th century Renaissance building with some 15th century Gothic embellishments that once served as the city's town hall. The Gothic Church of Notre-Dame is the tallest building in the region thanks to its spire. The 19th century market hall, built from glass and steel, still hosts markets on every day but Monday.

name: Quatre Bornes
description: Quatre Bornes, nestled in the heart of Mauritius, offers visitors a delightful blend of bustling markets, cultural richness, and natural beauty. At the heart of Quatre Bornes lies its colorful and bustling market, where the sights, sounds, and aromas create an intoxicating sensory experience. Here, visitors can wander through stalls brimming with exotic fruits, spices, textiles, and handicrafts, engaging in the lively banter of vendors and locals. Beyond its markets, Quatre Bornes is home to a diverse array of cultural attractions and landmarks. The town's rich heritage is evident in its charming colonial architecture, with historic buildings offering glimpses into Mauritius' past. Visitors can explore the Eureka House, a beautifully preserved Creole mansion, or take a leisurely stroll through the Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanical Garden, where lush greenery and vibrant blooms provide a tranquil escape. For those seeking outdoor adventures, Quatre Bornes is surrounded by natural wonders waiting to be discovered. Nearby, the Tamarind Falls beckon with their cascading waters and lush surroundings, offering hiking trails and breathtaking viewpoints for intrepid explorers.

name: Kuantan
description: Officially founded in the 1850s, Kuantan is the largest city on Malaysia's east coast but is still under the radar for most travellers. Since it doesn't target tourists, Kuantan is a perfect place to immerse yourself in an authentic Malaysian metropolis. Enjoy the city's mini zoo, situated on a promontory in the South China Sea, or feel the sand between your toes on one of the city's beaches. You can even hop aboard a boat for a river tour. In the city center, visitors can admire Kuantan's big, blue, state mosque (and even go inside outside of prayer times), which is surrounded by Colonial-era buildings. The Pehang Museum is housed in a fine colonial-era house, and showcases the state's history and art through a collection ranging from contemporary ceramics to an exhibition on Orang Asli, Malaysia's aboriginal people. And of course, as a major city, there's plenty of great places to eat!

name: Arenal Volcano National Park
description: Famous for its perfect cone shape, Arenal is Costa Rica's most active volcano. Its lava has been flowing consistently since its last eruption in 1968. While the eruption was a tragedy, it also transformed the region into one of the most unique in the country. Surrounding the volcano is a vast rainforest that's especially popular with birders - nearly all of Costa Rica's 850 identified bird species can be found here. Within the park you can hike to see the moonscape of the still-smoking caldera, walk over hanging bridges in the rainforest, relax in naturally-heated hot springs or take to the water in a raft, boat or canoe.

name: Mitla
description: Inhabited as early as 900 BC, Mitla became the ceremonial center of the Zapotec beginning around 850 AD. From this point, it continued to grow right up until it was destroyed by the Spanish in 1553. Upon their arrival, the Spanish recorded that Mitla was home to the high priest, whom they likened to the Mixtec pope. Located in a valley, the buildings were intended to be functional rather than flashy, but the bright red walls and incomparable mortarless mosaics are more than impressive. As the religious center, Mitla was also a noble burial site. Within the burial tunnels of the aptly named "Column Group", one (now fenced off) column was said to tell you how long you have to live. Abutting this is the Church of San Pablo in Mitla, which was built using stones from the ancient city. The rest of the charming modern town is worth a wander as well, especially to sample their famous mezcal.

name: Volos
description: Today, Volos is bustling Greek city and one of the country's most prominent ports. During the time of the ancient Greeks, the region around Volos was the birthplace of the mythical Centaurs. Half human, half horse, the legend of these creatures has endured to this day. Apart from mythical tales, Volos is considered one of the most beautiful cities in Greece thanks in no small part to its gorgeous seafront lined with small cafés and restaurants. Volos castle also should not be missed together with Volos' gorgeous Orthodox churches.

name: San Rafael
description: Surrounded by mountains, lakes, rivers, and valleys, San Rafael is an ideal stop for nature lovers exploring Argentina's famed Mendoza province. It is a place of departure to enjoy almost any outdoor activity from hiking to paragliding, learn about the region's past in the historic Villa 25 de Mayo, and pay a visit to vineyards, fruit and olive oil plantations. Like any respectable city in the province, San Rafael is home to excellent vineries where guests can sip on local wine and even champagne. Other attractions include Fort San Rafael del Diamante (constructed in 1805), the Borgian labyrinth (a maze-like garden), and spas. Overall, the region's mild climate, beautiful nature, and friendly people make San Rafael worth a visit.

name: Khao Laem National Park
description: Covering 1500 square kilometers, Khao Laem National Park is centered around a man-made reservoir and surrounded by limestone mountains. For visitors looking for a quick natural excursion, the 5-meter tall Kroeng Krawia Waterfall is the most easy to access site (and it's free). If you'd like to explore the forest, you first need to stop at the nearby visitor center to inform the park rangers. Birdwatchers would enjoy the 5km trek to Krawia Swamp, while those looking for some more impressive falls can opt for the 4km hike up to Kra Teng Cheng Waterfall. Of course, if you'd rather just soak in some stunning lake views, you can head up to Pom Pee, which is particularly beautiful at sunset.
