name: Labin
description: Situated on a 320 meters high hill and only three kilometers from the seaside, Labin was inhabited already two thousand years B.C. Titus Livius said that Labin inhabitants were pirates. After the conflicts between the local inhabitants and Romans, which had started in the 3rd century B.C., Istra came under the Romans in 177 B.C. Labin and its surroundings thus became an integral part of Illyrian. Walk around the quiet streets and squares packed with art galleries and studios; discover numerous noble palaces and the highest Labin bell tower of St. Justus. There are more than thirty professional artists in Labin. The town is also known for its longstanding cultural event Labin Art Republic. End your day with a stroll through Dubrova Sculpture Park, an open-air gallery of the greatest Croatian and international artists' works.

name: Hanmer Springs
description: The basis of this spa town is, and always will be, the amazing natural hot springs that has drawn in so many visitors down the years. The therapeutic pools at the spa complex have provided a relaxing experience for over a century and the range of hot pools on offer means there is something to suit everyone, from cold plunge pools to scorching baths, as well as sauna and steam rooms. More recently a fresh water pool and a water slide have been constructed, which is great for the kids. Away from the pools is the outstanding array of outdoor activities. Take your pick from forest walks, mountain biking, whitewater rafting, bungee jumping, and jet boat rides. Maps and information are available at the local tourist information centre. Don't forget to refuel at one of the cafes and enjoy the view of the impressive Mt Isobel.

name: Chinchero
description: Overlooking the Sacred Valley of the Incas, Chincheros is known for being the home of Peruvian weaving, which is displayed at the Sunday Market. This market is smaller than the one in neighboring Pisac, but just as colorful, and is said to replicate the colors of the rainbow. Make sure you pass by the town's center and see an ancient Incan ruin, a stone wall with trapezoidal markings. Mixed in with ruins and rainbows is a colonial church, from when the Spanish were in Peru. The church was built upon Incan ruins and is adorned with beautiful religious designs. Chincheros is definitely a little-known gem for those looking to experience the real Peru!

name: Puerto Penasco
description: Puerto Peñasco beckons travelers with its golden beaches, cobalt waters, and the promise of a truly unforgettable vacation. Envision vast stretches of pristine sand perfect for sunbathing and water sports, along with unforgettable sunsets painting the horizon. The beaches, like Playa Arenosa with its excellent snorkeling and scuba diving, or Playa Bonita, perfect for a relaxed day by the sea, offer endless possibilities for relaxation and adventure. For those craving a taste of the extraordinary, venture beyond the beaches to the surreal lunar-like landscapes of the Pinacate Reserve and Gran Desierto de Altar Reserve. Explore vast shifting dunes and ancient volcanic craters. Puerto Peñasco's Malecon, a lively beachfront promenade, invites you to embrace local culture. Enjoy shopping for handicrafts, dining at diverse restaurants, and savoring breathtaking Pacific Coast sunsets. Marvel at public art, from vibrant street murals to international creations in galleries like Galeria Del Mar Bermejo.

name: Ayutthaya
description: Founded in 1350, Ayutthaya was the second capital of the Siamese Kingdom, which flourished until it was destroyed by the Burmese in the 18th century. Before its fall, Ayutthaya was one of the world's largest and most cosmopolitan cities. Today, it's a 289 hectare archaeological site recognized by UNESCO. At the 15th century Wat Ratburana, you'll find a Khmer-style prang, and stairs leading down to a secret crypt with unrestored images of Buddha on the walls. At Wat Mahathat, the next temple over, you'll find the iconic Buddha head stuck in the roots of a Banyan Tree - one of the most famous Thai images. The largest temple at Ayutthaya is Wat Phra Si Sanphet, otherwise known as 'the Grand Palace', which is best known for its three large chedis. Wat Lokaya Satha is another favourite for its 42-meter-long reclining Buddha Statue. Wat Chai Wattenaran, on the other hand, goes for quantity, with 120 Buddha statues throughout the grounds.

name: Murten
description: Derived from the Celtic word for "lakeside fortress", Murten was founded in the 12th century next to an older fortification. A 15th century fire destroyed most of the town and it was rebuilt in stone, and it underwent a second wave of reconstruction in the 17th century thanks to an influx of wealth. Today, the Murton still looks much as it does in centuries past. It's still encircled by its defensive wall, the only one in Switzerland that you can fully walk around, which offer fantastic views of the lake and the town below. After wandering the charming cobbled streets of the old town, and seeing what the arcaded shops have on offer, you can head to the town museum to learn about the region's 6000 year history, or enjoy the sun down on the waterfront promenade.

name: Vaux-le-Vicomte
description: Commissioned by Nicolas Fouquet, Louis XIV's superintendent of finances, the chateau was a collaboration between the renowned architect, landscape architect, and painter-decorator who would go on to create the Château de Versailles. When it was completed, Fouquet threw a lavish banquet to impress the King with his good taste. Instead, Jean-Baptiste Colbert, an ambitious advisor, convinced the Louis that Fouquet was trying to outshine him, so Louis had Fouquet arrested and imprisoned for life. Today, the chateau has been restored to look as if Fouquet and his relatives still lived there. The innovative layout is fully furnished with lavish furniture, opulent fixtures, and magnificent artwork, all accented with fine stucco and woodwork. In the stables, the carriage museum exhibits an impressive collection of beautiful antique carriages and their equipment catered for use in the city, the country, and the hunt. Visitors can also explore the groundbreaking gardens that would set the bar for all future estates. Before scheduling your visit, please check the chateau's hours at http://www.vaux-le-vicomte.com/en/prepare-your-visit/date-and-time/

name: Calenzana
description: Immerse yourself in the agrarian charm of Calenzana, best known as the starting point of one of the most beautiful walks in Europe - the GR20 long-distance footpath across Corsica. Thousands of people flock to this unassuming town every year to attempt the trail and fall in love with its old-world beauty. Nestled amongst fairytale foliage, Calenzana boasts a fascinating history and traditional Corsican culture.The austere Chapel of Sainte Restitude in the main square contains the sarcophagus and crypt of Saint Restitude and her five companions who were martyred in the year 304. Ancient olive trees gently encircle the chapel, some having stood for up to 800 years. Bars, restaurants and shops are just a stroll away in the square, where Corsican music can be heard drifting through the narrow streets. Don't visit Calenzana without sampling its divine wine and cheese products, especially the famous, spicy "calinzana" cheese or the sweet "cuggiulelle" biscuits.

name: Henry Moore Studios and Gardens
address.addr1: Dane Tree House, Perry Green, Much Hadham SG10 6EE, United Kingdom
description: In 1940, British sculptor Henry Moore and his wife Irina moved out of London to escape the Blitz, setting up shop in half of the Hoglands farmhouse. The Henry Moore Studios and Gardens were a team effort between the two - he created the sculptures, while she tended the gardens. After purchasing the home from the Moores' daughter, the Henry Moore Institute opened the studios and gardens to the public. Today, visitors can step into the artists former home and studios for a look into his private life, and learn about how the sculptures were created. Surrounding the house is a 70 acre sculpture garden, filled with the renowned artist's work. Please note the house and grounds are closed Mondays and Tuesdays. For more information, please visit www.henry-moore.org Photo by Jim Osley (https://www.geograph.org.uk/profile/11136) under CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Armagh
description: Armagh was established by the ancient pagans, and was cited as the royal capital of Ulster in Irish Mythology. After the spread of Christianity, it was converted into an important church and monastery by St. Patrick in 457, and eventually developed into the country's ecclesiastical capital. Today, the heart of the town is still the church founded by St.Patrick, which has been heavily restored, but retains plenty of medieval elements, including many carving housed inside, and the crypt. Armagh's Neo-Gothic Catholic cathedral is also dedicated to St. Patrick, and is ornately adorned with stained glass windows, mosaics, and gilded sculptures. The Navan Centre on the outskirts of town bring the Iron Age to life through reenactments and an informative exhibition. The elegantly decorated Milford House Collection is an interesting visit, as it was the most technologically advanced house in 19th century Ireland.

name: Alberobello
address.addr1: 70011 Alberobello, Metropolitan City of Bari, Italy
description: Trulli are a traditional style of house found only in Puglia. Made from local limestone, with thick walls and conical roofs, their design allows residents to control the interior temperature - an ingenious solution from the days before air conditioning. Founded in the 16th century, visitors can wander around the town, admiring the unique architectural style that dates back to pre-history. Several have been converted into museums or shops to further educate visitors about the tradition. The history behind Alberobello's settlement, and their choice of using Trulli is particularly humorous - the houses could be dismantled at a moment's notice to fool the authorities into thinking Alberobello was not an inhabited settlement so locals could evade taxes.

name: Vrsac
description: While the area has been inhabited since paleolithic times, historians believe the town of Vršac was founded by Serbs in the 15th century. In the 16th century, the Ottomans destroyed the town in their conquest, but quickly rebuilt it under their administration. Having had a good relationship with Germany, and even merged with a nearby settlement, during the early 1900s the town's primary language was German. Today, visitors can enjoy the city's wealth of historic architecture. The city's old marketplace, Save Kovačevića Square, is now a pleasant pedestrian area. The interior of the 18th century Orthodox cathedral is brightly painted by prominent Serbian artists, but Vršac's most imposing building is the Roman Catholic Church. Completed in 1863, the neo-Gothic edifice is one of the largest in the area, and is painted from floor to ceiling. In the Vršac National Museum, artefacts and artwork are used to tell the area's history.

name: Kalopanagiotis
description: The picturesque village of Kalopanayiotis was founded in the 11th century when the good Christian Panayiotis built his home next to the St. John Lambadhistis Monastery. In fact, the village's name is a derivation of Kalos Panayiotis - literally "Good Panayiotis". Over the years, more faithful followed suit, and they ended up making one of the prettiest towns in the Troodos Mountains. Wandering the winding streets, you'll have 6 charming chapels to enjoy. These historic churches have earned Kalopanayiotis the title of "Byzantine destination of Cyprus". Chief among them is the Ayios Ioannis (St. John) Lambadhistis Monastery. Established in the 10th century, this Byzantine beauty bundles 3 churches around a central courtyard. Inside, you'll find some amazing frescoes and icons dating back to the 13th century, and a silver reliquary holding the skull of St. John Lambadhistis. Just outside the monastery is an icon museum, housing a treasure trove of Byzantine icons and religious objects.

name: Khamis Mushait
description: Nestled amidst mountainous terrain with fertile soil, Khamis Mushait has evolved from its traditional role as a bustling commercial center. Its name, "Khamis," signifies the Thursday market of the Mushayt clan. In addition to its military importance, agriculture remains a vital pillar of Khamis Mushait's economy. The region cultivates essential crops like wheat, rice, coffee, and henna. Visitors to Khamis Mushait are welcomed by the enchanting Khamis Mushait Boulevard, situated on Prince Sultan Bin Abdul Aziz Road. The boulevard features lively fountains, modern amenities, and open spaces where visitors can savor the city's delightful weather. A hub of activity, the boulevard offers an array of shops, restaurants, and cafes accompanied by live music. For culinary enthusiasts, Khamis Mushait offers an assortment of dining experiences. From traditional morning dishes at Gulf Council restaurant to shrimp delights at Shrimpianu Restaurant, the culinary journey is diverse. Adding to the allure, Boulevard stores provide an opulent shopping experience, ranging from perfumes and clothing to watches and sunglasses. Photo by Aiman titi, CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Eureka, CA
description: The bustling coastal city of Eureka is nestled on Humboldt Bay, 100 miles south of the Oregon border. A tale of two halves, Eureka is equal parts cool college city, hosting students, artists and writers from far and wide, and olde-worlde Victorian town boasting a quaint, historic charm. Eureka started as a Gold Rush transport center and received its name from a Greek word meaning "I have found it!" Not just the name of this Humboldt Bay city but also the California state motto, Eureka thrived as a successful gold mining town in the mid-1800's. Today, visit the beautifully restored Victorian-era Old Town, which is still a working seaport. The waterfront hosts plenty of food and drink options and lots of opportunities to get out on the water. The Maritime Museum educates visitors on the region's rich seagoing heritage. The city is host to plenty of events and festivals throughout the year, so check the calendar before your visit!

name: Riffa
description: Explore the vibrant East and West sides of Riffa, home to the former royal rulers of Bahrain and endless tourist attractions. Take a glimpse into the city's past at the Sheikh Salman bin Ahmed Fort, built in 1812 as a residence for the sheikh. Appreciate its architectural beauty while enjoying the views of the Hunainiyah Valley from the terrace. For shopping enthusiasts, Riffa boasts several shopping malls and bustling markets, with Rifa Market and Bukuwara Street Market popular spots for a local experience. In East Riffa, the Enma Mall and Lulu Hypermarket Mall are the modern shopping alternative. History buffs will enjoy a trip to the Bahrain Military Museum, showcasing a collection of weapons, uniforms and documents from various eras of the country's armed forces history. Conveniently located near Riffa Fort, you can easily explore both attractions in a few hours.

name: Sankt Goar
description: On the hill overlooking the picturesque town of Sankt Goar are the ruins of Rheinfels Castle, the largest fortress to ever overlook the Rhine. Once five times its current size, the massive ruins still form an imposing sight. Built in the thirteenth century, it is not difficult to imagine life back in medieval times as you wander the castle remains, the museum and the underground tunnels. The fact that the original castle was built to house up to 4,000 people during sieges gives an idea of just how large it was in its medieval heyday. Visitors can explore the 600 feet long underground tunnels, for which a flashlight is needed (although candles are provided free of charge), and experience the castle dungeon. All in all, Rheinfels Castle is the best hands-on visitor experience of castle ruins along the Rhine and comes with the added bonus of providing excellent photo opportunities of the region.

name: Speyer
description: Speyer Cathedral, officially known as the Cathedral of St.Mary and St. Stephen, is the world's largest surviving Romanesque church. Its huge triple-naved vaulted basilica is the central element in a design that greatly influenced Romanesque architecture in the 11th and 12th centuries. Its fully-preserved crypt is also the largest Romanesque columned hall in Europe. Size really does matter in Speyer Cathedral. Apart from the largest body-count of Holy Roman Emperors and kings under the high altar, it boasts the monster Cathedral Bowl outside the main door. With a capacity of 1,560 litres, every new bishop has had to fill it with wine as a gift to the people. So it should come as no surprise that the Speyer Technic Museum has the biggest Space Exhibition in Europe, with original and replica copies of Russian and American spacecraft, and a new Moon-themed area. Elsewhere in the museum you can inspect an original jumbo jet, a submarine and have hands-on technological experiences.

name: Pont du Gard
address.addr1: Pont du Gard, 400 Route du Pont du Gard, 30210 Vers-Pont-du-Gard, France
description: In the 1st century AD, the burgeoning city of Nemausus (modern day Nîmes) was facing a growing water shortage, so the Romans had to build an aqueduct from Fontaine d'Eure 20 km away. The result was a winding, 50km long structure that descended 2.5 cm in 456 m, with variations in the slope because a constant gradient would have required the Pont du Gard be higher than they could feasibly build it. It served as an aqueduct until the 6th century before becoming a tollgate in the Middle Ages, and was used as a bridge from the 18th to 20th century. A massive project in started in 2000 cleared any construction from the surrounding area, putting the Pont du Gard back in its original setting. Along with seeing the monument, visitors also have access to a museum covering the aqueduct's construction, and several other exhibitions relating to the area's history. Before booking your visit, please check the site's hours at http://www.pontdugard.fr/en/practical-information

name: Khoni
description: Legend whispers of Roman general Pompey paving his path in where the town of Khoni now stands in 65 BCE, with remnants of his drawbridge—the Bumbua Bridge—still standing today. Traces of settlements have been found around Khoni from the late Bronze Age, but the current one sprung from the pivotal 8th-century Khoni Church. As a former trade post, Khoni boasts a vibrant cultural life with theatrical and musical traditions dating back to 1865. But there's more than history here. Surrounded by lush forests and vibrant rivers, Khoni offers a serene retreat or a thrilling hike. The nearby landmarks include the sprawling Askhi Alpine Plateau, the stunning Okatse Canyon, and the scenic Tskhenistskali River Valley, interspersed with waterfalls and lakes.

name: British Motor Museum
description: Opened in 1993, the British Motor Museum combines cars from the British Motor Industry Heritage Trust and the Jaguar Heritage Trust to create the World's largest collection of historic British cars. There are over 300 Classic cars on display, from the very first Land Rover to the very last Aston Martin DB7. These are joined by a range of culturally important autos including vehicles used by the Royal Family and 'Star Cars' that have been featured in films. The museum also hosts a variety of temporary exhibitions, car shows, and events, so visitors can experience different facets of the automobile world. For more information, please visit britishmotormuseum.co.uk

name: Primosten
description: Primosten has narrow streets and condensed houses, giving it a medieval 'fishing town' feel. The small town is adorned with pebble beaches and a promenade that surrounds the old town walls. Primosten's most famous beach, Raduca beach, is the perfect spot to sunbathe and enjoy the crystal-clear water. Stroll the quaint, old streets and visit some of the town's churches. The parish church St. Juraj, built in 1485, is situated on a hill and offers breathtaking coastal views. Another notable church worth visiting is St. Roko church. St. Roko church was built in 1680 and is considered a cultural monument. There are also many sport and recreational activities in Primosten such as tennis, mini golf, beach volleyball, and watersports. If you're looking for some fun in the sun with an amazing view, Primosten is the place to be!

name: Rum Point
description: Escape to Rum Point, a captivating sliver of paradise on Grand Cayman's north side. Palm trees sway gently in the warm Caribbean breeze, offering a touch of shade as you soak up the idyllic scenery. Rum Point isn't just a beach paradise; it's a haven for water enthusiasts. Explore the crystal-clear underwater world teeming with colorful fish and vibrant coral reefs. Rent a kayak or paddleboard and glide across the tranquil surface, marveling at the beauty of the coastline. For the more adventurous, try your hand at windsurfing or kitesurfing, harnessing the power of the Caribbean winds. Beyond the water activities, Rum Point offers a taste of Caymanian culture. Browse the collection of souvenirs at local shops, finding unique keepsakes that capture the essence of your island getaway. Savor delicious, fresh seafood dishes at a beachfront restaurant, the flavors infused with local spices and the breathtaking ocean views adding to the ambiance.

name: Santa Ana Zegache Church
description: At first glance, this modest town in Oaxaca may not catch your eye, but hidden within its quiet streets is the colorful Santa Ana Zegache Church - a part of Zegache Talleres Comunitarios, an organization which restores artifacts all around the southwestern region of Mexico. This organization was founded by Rodolfo Morales, who in the last part of his years was dedicated to restoring the natural beauty of his homeland. Now, what is this gem? A creatively restored church that would give a rainbow a run for its money. Once a plain stone church, it has now been repainted in bright beautiful colors that showcase the elegance of the structure. Even the interior has had a facelift and is just as beautiful, with lovely artifacts native to the region, truly a unique spiritual place.

name: Krakow
description: Krakow's Old Town is a 13th-century merchants' town, planned in 1257 following the city's destruction during the Tatar invasions of 1241. The green park around the Old Town marks the city's original fortifications that were demolished in the 19th century. In the middle of one stretch is the Gothic-style barbican, built around 1498, which once connected the fortified walls. It is one of only three such fortified outposts still surviving in Europe, and the best preserved. As a center of the most religious countries in Europe, Krakow offers and almost endless list of churches to visit. Right in the middle of the town square it the Church of St. Wojciech, one of the oldest stone churches in Poland. Of course, no medieval city would be complete without a castle, and the Wawel delivers with sweeping views and multiple museums. Be sure to plan your visit at http://www.wawel.krakow.pl/en/index.php?op=40

name: Takoradi
description: Famed for its bustling ports and lively atmosphere, Takoradi is a melting pot of cultures, where traditional Ghanaian heritage meets modern-day dynamism. Colorful fishing boats bob gently in the turquoise waters, their presence a testament to the city's deep-rooted maritime traditions. Delve into the city's fascinating past at the Takoradi Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the fort's ramparts and dungeons, remnants of the colonial era that stand as silent witnesses to Ghana's journey towards independence. Immerse yourself in the vibrant culture at the Takoradi Market, a sensory overload of sights, sounds, and smells. Haggle for unique souvenirs handcrafted by local artisans, and lose yourself in the kaleidoscope of colorful fabrics, intricate beadwork, and fresh, local produce.

name: Newport, RI
description: A haven for America's wealthiest residents in the late 19th century, Newport, Rhode Island is most famous for the grand mansions the country's elite built as summer homes. These enormous homes have 50+ rooms, lavish interiors and spectacular gardens! Today, many of the extravagant homes are open to the public, most famously The Breakers, which is widely regarded as the grandest of them all. With 70 rooms, five floors and unparalleled views of the Atlantic Ocean, this Vanderbilt Mansion is the epitome of opulence. Take a self-guided tour through the decadent rooms for a glimpse into the lives of America's richest family. For the best views of the Newport Mansions, head to the Cliff Walk. From this public walkway along the rugged, you'll see why Newport was the destination of choice for the city's famous mansions. There's plenty of beaches, and the main commercial drag, Thames Street, is packed with wonderful bars and restaurants serving up delicious meals, most notably the locally caught shellfish!

name: Lloret de Mar
description: Originally an Iberian settlement set inland, the town eventually expanded towards the sea, transforming it into one of Catalonia's premier resort destinations. Fortunately, behind its huge swaths of sandy beaches, the city worked to harmonize its historic core with the times. The church of Sant Romà was originally built in 1522 as a refuge from Turkish and Algerian pirates. The original Catalan Gothic style served as the base for a major 20th century overhaul when bright tiles were added to the towers and facade in the style of Gaudi. The church also references traditional Mudejar, combining horseshoe arches and contrasting stripes with Catalan Modernist tiling. Even the dead benefited from the tourism boom, with the even the cemetery receiving a unique modernist pantheon. For something even more secluded and peaceful, the cliff-top Santa Clotilde Gardens are adorned with marble sculptures and edged by cypress trees in the Italian renaissance style.

name: La Cumbrecita
description: La Cumbrecita boasts the distinction of being the highest urban settlement in the province, offering a serene and recreational escape for families and couples alike. Founded in 1934 amidst the serene solitude of mountains, rivers, and crystalline streams, La Cumbrecita has preserved its unique character as the first pedestrian town in Argentina. Venturing through picturesque villages like Athos Pampa, Intiyaco, and Villa Berna, visitors are treated to a landscape adorned with pircas (dry-stone walls) built by the Comechingones, the region's first natives. The journey culminates in the heart of La Cumbrecita, where the absence of gas stations adds to the town's authentic charm. Wandering through the alpine-style village, guests encounter artisanal shops, eateries, and cultural sites. Plaza de los Pioneros and the firemen's oak wooden fountain stand as testament to the town's history. Explorers can embark on trails leading to natural wonders like the Almach stream's pool, Mount Wank, and an enchanting 18-meter-high waterfall. Culminating the experience, the Ecumenical chapel and Chess Plaza add to the town's unique allure.

name: Baden-Baden
description: Baden-Baden's curative waters have attracted many visitors over the years, including President Obama, Queen Victoria and Victoria Beckham! As well as being used to treat a wide range of medical conditions, the thermal spas can do wonders for your health and well-being even if you are already fighting fit. Settled back in Roman times, Baden-Baden underwent a reinvention in the 18th century due to an influx of French refugees fleeing the French Revolution. Thanks to its proximity to the French boarder, the spirit of France still prevails in Baden-Baden and can be seen in the town's chic boutiques, charming cafes and picturesque gardens along the Oos River. The town is also home to Germany's oldest Casino and the Frieder Burda Museum which houses one of the best collections of modern art in the world. An attractive and ambient town, Baden-Baden is designed to be enjoyed by everyone.

name: Skikda
description: Skikda is a popular resort destination, renowned for its pleasant climate and white sandy beaches, including Plage Remila, Plage de Oued Lekbir, and Plage d'el marsa. The Port of Skikda is a good place for snorkeling, try the local cuisine, and enjoy the views of the open sea. The area's amenities include restaurants and organized scuba diving outfits, providing rentals and organized tours to popular diving spots. Supporting Algeria's third largest port, the downtown is abuzz with things to do, with plenty of cafes and restaurants where you can grab a bite to eat. Architecture fanatics will want to make a bee-line for Skikda's City Hall, unique neo-Moorish project designed by Le Corbusier. The architectural pioneer also designed the nearby railway station, incorporating local design elements into his modernist vision. There are also a few museums to keep you busy on a rainy day, including the small but interesting Skikda Museum across from the City Hall, and the lavish Palais Meriem Azza house museum.

name: Baddesley Clinton
description: First built in the 13th century, Baddesley Clinton passed to the Ferrer family at the beginning of the 16th century, and remained their home until it 1940. Over the centuries, the Ferrers made their own additions and renovations to the house - from secret rooms to hide Catholic priests to stained glass windows bearing the family's coat of arms. Today, the combination of bridge, moat, and crenelated gatehouse make Baddesley's facade one of the most beautiful in England. Inside, visitors can explore the various rooms, which are feature centuries-spanning furnishings. Step into the 16th century Great Hall, the drawing room, chapel, library, and Henry Ferrers' bedroom, and feel free to ask the friendly volunteers about the history of Baddesley Clinton. Outside, visitors can enjoy a walk through the gardens to admire the manor's charming facade, and soak in the colors of the dahlia-bordered formal garden, or take a quiet stroll around the lake. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/baddesley-clinton

name: Almeria
description: Situated in the southeast of Spain on the Mediterranean Sea, Almería first grew wealthy on trade and the textile industry in the 10th and 11th centuries. The city suffered many sieges and fell under Christian domination in 1489 until it was devastated by an earthquake in 1522, the effects of which were still felt well into the 19th century. Visitors to the area can see, among many important monuments, the Alcazaba, a medieval fortress constructed in the 10th century; the Almería air raid shelters, now the longest in Europe and open for tourists; the Renaissance church of Santiago, built in 1533; and Chanca, a group of houses carved into rocks. There is a palpable history present in every corner of this dynamic city, which deserves to be explored during your travels through Southern Spain.

name: Sant Joan de Labritja
description: Immerse yourself in the whitewashed architecture and charming cobbled streets of Sant Joan de Labritja - a picturesque village that feels worlds away from San Antonio or Ibiza Town. Tourists come in search of peace and quiet to stroll through the alleyways, adorned with colorful bougainvillea, peppered with small bars serving cheap caña or espresso, and overlooked by a small Christian church. The village is neighbored by a tributary of the Riu de Santa Eularia, which in winter months is Ibiza's only constant-flowing river, and during tourist season becomes a dry river bed bursting with green vegetation. If you're in Sant Joan de Labritja on a Sunday, swing by the local artisan market packed with organic produce and handcrafted goods. Head to the Cala San Vicente beach for a gorgeous dip in the Balearic sea and discover a breathtaking coastline with hidden coves.

name: Vrsar
description: Set on a small hill, and surrounded by islets, Vrsar offers visitors beautiful views and stunning sunsets. If you look within the ancient, circular walls, you can see the remnants of thousands of years of occupation. Since very few buildings ventured outside the fortified walls until the 19th century, a walk through the old town is like walking through Vrsar's past. The town's gate, dating to the 13th century, is still in use, and the various churches showcase Christianity's architectural development. The remains of a 4th century basilica are in the walled-in backyard of the 12th century Romanesque basilica of St. Mary. The architecture isn't the only history Vrsar has saved – they also have an annual celebration to commemorate Casanova's visits to the town. Art fans shouldn't miss Dušan Džamonja's Park of Sculptures, which covers a hill with the world-renowned artist's work.

name: Brixen
address.addr1: 39042 Brixen, Province of Bolzano - South Tyrol, Italy
description: Brixen/Bressanone is the third largest city and the oldest in Tyrol. It's located in a broad valley beneath the Dolomites and offers 300 sunny days per year. Due to its close proximity to the mountains, Bressanone has become a popular winter sports resort. Bressanone's romantic old town is based around the Piazza Duomo. An ancient marble pillar erected to commemorate the city's first thousand years dominates the square. The Church of St. Michael, also located in old town, is a Baroque cathedral containing one of the largest Alpine frescoes from the 14th-16th centuries. The Cathedral of Brixen is also an important town monument worth visiting. This Baroque cathedral has two towers and is considered a masterpiece of priceless artistic value. Located near Bressanone is the Augustinian Abbey of Neustift, one of the most important monasteries in Tyrol. Make a stop at the famous Abbey after marveling at the range of historical buildings that Bressanone offers.

name: Moalboal
description: Moalboal itself is a quiet town about 6 kilometers from the coast that's often just used a stopover point, though the ruins of its 19th century Spanish colonial church are worth checking out. The Moalboal that tourists from around the world flock to see is the beach resort area. With restaurants and bars jutting out into the sea, it's a great place to relax and appreciate the view of the hills of Negros across the Tañon Strait. But with a coral wall not far off shore, you'd be remiss not to take some extra time to experience some of the best snorkelling in Cebu. A short swim from Panagsama Beach will bring you to Moalboal's world famous sardine run, where millions of the tiny fish congregate year round.

name: Sirince Koyu
description: Sirince Koyu was first settled in the 15th century after Ephesus was abandoned. According to one story, it was a group of freed Greek slaves who founded the village, naming it Çirkince (Turkish for "ugly") in order to deter others from following them. Up until the 1923 population exchange between Greece and Turkey, it remained a Greek settlement, and in 1926, the village's name was changed to Şirince ("Pleasant" in Turkish). In the 1990s, linguist Sevan Nişanyan and his wife settled in Şirince, and worked to restore the charming village and get it protected as a national monument. Today, this sleepy village is home to only 600 residents, but its 19th century atmosphere is so pleasant that tourists flock here to lose themselves in its cobbled alleys, and enjoy the finest wine and olives in Turkey.

name: Rionegro
description: Beginning as a single farmstead in 1581, Rionegro would grow to be one of the most important cities in Colombia's War for Independence, and very nearly, the capital of Antioquia. Today, the small hillside city is a refreshing escape from bustling Medellin. Bisected by the shady Rio Negro, the city offers visitors a slew of charming churches, like the beautiful Baroque cathedral. The Parque Comfama Rionegro is a popular retreat for families, offering green spaces, a small museum, playgrounds, and even a small waterpark. The main draw in Rionegro is the suburb of San Antonio de Pereira, which is famous across Colombia for its sweets.

name: Almunecar
address.addr1: Castillo de San Miguel, 18690 Almuñécar, Granada, Spain
description: Dating back to 800 BC when it was founded by the Phoenicians, the city's long history has left this resort town strewn with historic monuments. Even today, the ancient necropolis and salting works still stand, inviting visitors to step into the distant past. And left behind from the Roman rule are an aqueduct and baths on the outskirts of the city. Within the Cueva de Siete Palacios, which predates even the Phoenicians, the Almuñécar Archaeological Museum has collected artefacts from surrounding site. The city's strategic location made it appealing to the Muslims, who erected the San Miguel castle, which was later refortified under Christian rule. The area around the castle has retained its historic air, with cobbled streets and whitewashed houses, and courtyards full of flowers. The Renaissance Church of La Encarnación was designed by Juan de Herrera, and is the first church in the region to begin incorporating Baroque elements.

name: Cascada de Roberto Barrios
description: The Cascada de Roberto Barrios are a not-so-secret hidden gem. Locals love swimming in the refreshing water, but they're not frequented by tourists. This means you'll be able to enjoy the stunning scenery without the hordes of tourists that plague better-known locations. You can walk along the limestone-crusted riverbed and bathe in the pools of cool water while surrounded by lush jungle.

name: Izola
description: Izola, a fishing village at heart, is an old Mediterranean town established in the 7th century. It's located the southwest shore of the Gulf of Trieste, between Koper and Piran. Although often overlooked by tourists, Izola is worth a second glance. The narrow medieval streets, stone houses, and ancient churches give the town a romantic character. There are also many museums and galleries to gain a sense of traditional Istrian arts and crafts. Izola is a great place to visit year round due to its beaches and mild climate. Savor the view of the swaying boats and the aroma of fresh seafood as you explore this charming port town.

name: Chioggia
address.addr1: 30015 Chioggia, Metropolitan City of Venice, Italy
description: While not prominent in antiquity, the city of Chioggia is undeniably ancient, being first mentioned by Pliny in the 1st century. Destroyed by the King Pippin of Italy in the 9th century, it was rebuilt around a new industry based on salt pans, which played a key role in its political alliances for centuries. While its scenic canals lined with brightly coloured buildings. It's rebirth has been well preserved by the Church of St. Andrew's 11th century bell tower, the oldest in the world. To learn the distinction between Chioggia and their northern lagoon neighbours, a visit to the Museum of the South Lagoon, housed in a former monastery, has artefacts and pictures relating to the south lagoon including models of boats, agricultural equipment, and paintings. Of course, as a fishing village, visitors should take some time to enjoy some fresh seafood.

name: Tepotzotlan
description: When the Spanish arrived to the area in 1520, they leveled the indigenous settlement at Tepotzotlan and used it as a base for spreading Christianity to the area. The Jesuits established 3 schools here in the late 16th century, and today, the complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A living survey of colonial architecture, the complex showcases everything from elegant Renaissance to opulent Baroque architecture, and the entire building is now a Museum of the Viceroyalty of New Spain. Inside, you'll not only find a small exhibition of indigenous artefacts, but some of the country's most precious folk and religious art (loaned from Mexico City's Cathedral). Make sure to save a large chunk of time for the Templo de San Francisco Javier - one of Mexico's most opulent examples of Churrigueresque architecture, where the almost overwhelmingly ornate altars are completely covered in gold gilt.

name: Cotopaxi National Park
description: Being only 37 miles from the capital Quito, Cotopaxi National Park is where many Ecuadorians come to touch snow for the first time. At 5,900 metres Cotopaxi is one of the world's highest active volcanoes. The entrance to the park starts at Laguna de Limpiopungo, a shallow lake that can be circumambulated in about 90 minutes. It is the perfect way to experience this park without breaking much of a sweat, being a hiking trail without any undulations. With a little luck you will get a breathtaking view of the volcano and a magnificent photo of the mountain reflected on the mirror-like lagoon. There are also horseback riding possibilities (please booking this in advance) if you want to go easy on your legs. Or maybe a bike tour - e-bikes are available if you want to ascend the slopes a little easier! Please don't forget to bring warm and waterproof clothing. Your driver will take you to the entrance to the national park and can help you hire a certified local guide if you haven't done so in advance.

name: Queen's View
description: It's said the Queen's View was so named following Queen Victoria's Visit in 1866, though some have suggested that it was named after Queen Isabella of Scotland over 500 years prior. The stunning views of Loch Tummel and the Tay Forest Park, aren't the only attraction - visitors can also enjoy some wonderful woodland walks, learn more about the highlands at the visitor center, and take a break at the café.

name: Sandham Memorial Chapel
description: Sandham Memorial Chapel is a unique and poignant tribute to the sacrifices of World War I. Designed by the renowned architect Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1930, the chapel is celebrated for its stunning murals painted by the artist Stanley Spencer. These striking artworks vividly depict the experiences of soldiers and their families, blending themes of war and everyday life with a deeply personal touch. The chapel is constructed from red brick and features a distinctive bell tower, making it a notable landmark in the English countryside. Managed by the National Trust, the chapel is open to the public, providing guided tours and informative exhibitions that enrich the visitor experience. A visit to Sandham Memorial Chapel is a meaningful journey into the past, commemorating the bravery and resilience of those who served.

name: Harrogate
description: Harrogate was first mentioned in the 1330s though the town of today didn't begin to develop until the 16th century when mineral springs were discovered. High and Low Harrogate attracted wealthy visitors from around England and Continental Europe through World War I, merging into a single town in the process. Today, the heart of the town is still the mineral baths. The Turkish Baths, which have been restored to their 19th century Moorish glory, and allow visitors to experience the pools and steam rooms that attracted people to Harrogate centuries ago. At the Victorian Royal Pump Room, you can visit Europe's strongest sulphur wells in Europe, which were visited by the Tsarina of Russia in 1911. In the museum, you can learn about the town's spa-history, and marvel at its collection of Egyptian artefacts.

name: Cork
description: Founded as a monastic settlement in the 6th century, Cork prides itself as the "real capital" for its opposition to the Anglo-Irish treaty in the Irish Civil War. Their pride is well placed as Cork has everything you'd want from a capital, from hip coffee shops to centuries-old monuments. The Neo-Gothic St Fin Barre's Cathedral isn't just notable for its beautiful stained glass, prodigious pipe organ, and well-preserved medieval carvings - it also marks the site of the monastery that spawned the city. The clocks of the beloved St Anne's Church each tell a different time, and unlike almost any other church, visitors can ring the bells in the belfry! Even more than their monuments, what Corkonians really love is food, as is apparent from their Michelin star restaurants, English Market (hailed as the "best in the UK and Ireland"), and Butter Museum honoring its role as the historic center of Europe's butter trade.

name: Guatape
description: Guatape was founded as a small agricultural community in the 19th century, but after a hydroelectric dam flooded the area, much of the farmland was submerged. Fortunately for the people of Guatape, they had a tradition attractive to tourists: they painted their buildings in bright colors, with ceramics on the lower walls. Often times these are related to the products sold within, or the residents. This makes the town a great place to simply walk around, and livens up sipping on a coffee at the main square. The other big attraction here is the giant rock behind the town. Known as La Piedra del Peñol, 720 stairs lead to the top of the 200-meter-tall granite boulder, where you're treated to some great views of the manmade lake.

name: Matsalu National Park
description: Matsalu National Park is home to the breathtaking Matsalu Bay and its coastline, the Kasari River delta, and nearly 50 islands and islets. It is one of the most important wetland bird areas in Europe, with the land being officially established as a park in 1957 to protect the birds and their nesting. Every spring, over two million waterfowl pass through the 4,000 hectares of Kasari meadow - the largest preserved flat meadow on the continent. Vibrantly coloured Orchidaceae grow among oak and hazel trees in the wooded meadows, making for a spectacular scene for plant-lovers to lose themselves in. Matsalu National Park is also known for its cultural heritage, with several historic farmsteads and fishing villages dotting the area. Get a glimpse into traditional Estonian rural life by exploring these villages on foot or by bicycle, and head to the Visitor Center for a permanent exhibition. The Center is open 15 April to 30 September, Mon to Fri from 9.00 to 17.00 and Sat to Sun 10.00–18.00, then 1 October to 14 April, Mon to Fri, from 9.00 to 17.00, except on public holidays.

name: Shkoder
description: Settled since the Bronze age, Shkodër was a local tribal capital from 200BC until almost 200AD, when it was conquered by the Romans and became an important trade and military root. In the centuries that followed, empires fought for control of its strategic location, all the way to the early 1900s. The city's long history is embodied by Rozafa Castle, a former Illyrian stronghold, renovated under Venetian rule in the 15th century, and has withstood sieges in both the 15th and 20th centuries. The city suffered greatly under communism, with thousands of political prisoners being taken. Today, the Site of Witness and Memory commemorates the victims and educates visitors. One of the city's most unique attractions is St Stephen's Catholic Cathedral, a colorful, 19th century church that was a sports facility under communist rule.

name: Camaguey
description: Founded in 1514 by Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar, Camaguey was one of Spain's seven original settlements in Cuba. This first town was abandoned in 1528, and the colonists relocated further inland for safety. Even this didn't save it from being burned to the ground by Henry Morgan, after which the city was rebuilt as a maze to confuse any future attackers. While Cuba's third largest city isn't a typical tourist stop, the warren of narrow streets, colorful colonial buildings, and rich culture make it second only to Havana in sophistication, and earned it a spot on the UNESCO World Heritage list. The best thing to do here is simply wander the historic center's maze of streets. There are dozens of nooks and crannies to explore, as well as wide open squares lined with charming houses and baroque churches. Camaguey is also a cultural hub, and there are a huge number of art galleries and studios to discover. While walking, keep an eye out for the many clay pots - they're the symbol of the city, and used by locals to catch water in the arid climate.

name: Castell Coch
description: While foundations of Castell Coch were first laid by the Normans at the end of the 11th century, but structure standing today was erected in the 18th century. John Patrick Crichton-Stuart, the 3rd marquess of Bute, gave architect William Burges free reign to create a neo-Gothic castle that would be the envy of Victorian society and compliment his main residence of Cardiff Castle. The castle's interior was outfitted with stupendous ceilings, lavish furnishings, and regal furniture to create a opulent rural retreat. Today, Castell Coch remains true to Burges' vision, with multimedia exhibits bringing the building's story to life. For more information, please visit http://cadw.gov.wales/daysout/castell-coch

name: Balzan
description: Balzan is a quintessential Maltese village full of historical buildings that once housed influential figures. Notable structures include the former residence of Vincenzo Bosio, an officer of the Knights of St. John, and Casa Borg on Pope Pius Alexander Street. Take a leisurely stroll along Main Street and encounter traditional townhouses adorned with charming balconies and colorful doors, home to local hotspot Old Smugglers Bar. Balzan boasts a traditional Maltese square, locally known as the "pjazza", inviting visitors to relax on comfortable benches and take in the cobblestoned streets. The centerpiece of the town is the parish church, the Annunciation of Our Lady, built in the mid-17th century. This Tuscan-style church takes the form of a Latin cross and features an elegant dome and single belfry that can be admired throughout the village. It hosts renowned artworks by Emvin Cremona and Giuseppe Calleja, and every second week of July, the village celebrates the parish's lively feast. Balzan captivates with its historical architecture, serene atmosphere, and welcoming community, providing a delightful glimpse into traditional Maltese village life.

name: Waterfall Quetzalapan
description: 365 steps into the jungles of Puebla, and you will find yourself in the midst of the most majestic falls in the region: Quetzalapan. At nearly 100 meters tall, they're one of the highest cascades in the region, and the perfect place to spend a day with the waters flowing down like silk and the sounds filling the ambience with natural grandeur. Watch as birds sing and zoom overhead through the mists of the falls and admire the hundred foot wall of water overlooking the jungle. If you would like to seek adventure, try for the zip line or the hanging bridge that overlooks the area.

name: Woolsthorpe Manor
description: Built in the 17th century, Woolsthorpe Manor was the birthplace of Sir Isaac Newton, and where he conducted many of his most famous experiments after Cambridge closed because of a Bubonic plague outbreak in 1665. It was here that Newton used a prism to split white light into its component colors, and most famously, where he was first inspired to develop a theory of gravitation after seeing an apple fall from a tree. This same tree still stands in the manor's orchard, still bears fruit, and has offspring in Universities around the world - not to mention 'space saplings', that were brought to the ISS as pips. Within the manor, you can learn about Newton's childhood, replicate some of his most famous experiments, and see what 17th century English life was like thanks to the period furnishings, including some shelves built by Newton himself. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/woolsthorpe-manor

name: Catania
description: Established in the shadow of Mt. Etna in the 8th century BC, Catania's history is closely tied to the volcano, having been destroyed by earthquakes and eruptions on several occasions, most significantly in 1693 when it was wiped out and then rebuilt in the Baroque style. Today, this well-preserved historic core is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, perhaps best characterized in the Piazza Duomo, Catania's main square, which is surrounded by beautiful Baroque buildings all designed by Giovanni Battista Vaccarini. The striking dark grey cathedral is a particular stand-out because it incorporates elements ancient Roman structures. Of the city's many monuments, the Palazzo Biscari is the most lavish, with a sculpture-covered facade and opulent Rococo interiors (which require advance booking to visit). Visitors can also see the city's ancient origins in the Roman Theatre, smaller Odeon, or huge amphitheatre. And of course, be sure to try the city's signature pasta alla Norma!

name: Las Grutas
description: A mere 15 kilometers from San Antonio Oeste, Las Grutas, named after the coastal cliffs adorning its beaches, beckons those seeking an escape from the summer heat without the crowds of popular northern beaches. Enjoy swimmable waters late into fall, relishing the tranquility and affordability. It boasts the warmest and bluest waters along the Gulf of San Matias, reaching almost 27°C. Witness the fascinating tidal cycles that draw the waters far out to sea, revealing a kilometer of exposed coral and sand at low tide. From moonlight horse rides to kite-surfing classes, recreational diving, and shore-fishing for a variety of fish species, there's an activity for every preference. Explore surrounding sand dunes or embark on expeditions like the Fuerte Argentino plateau or a jeep safari through Los Alamos. Throughout the year, Las Grutas hosts events like the Las Grutas Bikini Open and beauty pageants, adding a touch of entertainment to the coastal charm.

name: Tiradentes
description: The little town of Tiradentes enjoyed a period of prosperity during the gold rush of the 17th and 18th centuries. But after the boom, this sleepy mountain town was all but forgotten - that is until the 1970s when locals partnered with investors from Rio to restore the charming colonial buildings. Tiradentes might be small, but it's undoubtedly one of the best preserved and most charming colonial towns in Minas Gerais. You don't need much of an itinerary here, just explore the twists and turns of the cobbled streets as they bring you past 300-year-old buildings. The one thing you can't miss is the Church of Saint Anthony, which has the most richly gilded interior in all of Brazil. As a bonus, Tiradentes is an excellent place to stop for lunch - it's well known for its food, and if you're visiting in August, you can gorge yourself during their Food Festival!

name: Hradec Kralove
description: Thanks to its popularity as a dowry item for medieval Czech queens, Hradec Kralove prospered as the region's military, political, religious, and cultural centre. This is apparent from a stroll around its compact historic centre with its captivating Renaissance, Gothic, and Baroque buildings. The red-brick, late-Gothic Holy Ghost Cathedral, destroyed and rebuilt a number of times is a symbol of the city's survival instinct. But it's the White Tower which is the city's proud emblem. Made of white stone and, at 72 meters tall arguably the tallest building in eastern Bohemia. It dates from the 1570s and is home to a famous occupant, the Augustine Bell, the second largest in Bohemia, weighing in at 10 tons. The climb to the top of the tower's 233 steps is rewarded with a thrilling panorama of the city and even the Giant and Orlicke Mountains to the north.

name: Brodsworth Hall and Gardens
description: Brodsworth Hall & Gardens were built in the 1860s in the Italianate style, taking inspiration from Queen Victoria's Osborne House. Over the years, the family's fortunes dwindled, with its final resident living in a limited number of rooms, patching and mending and upkeeping the manor as well as she could. After being given to English Heritage in 1990, it was decided to leave the interiors in situ, rather than replacing or restoring them. Yes, you'll see dazzling chandeliers and magnificent marble on a tour of the house, but you'll also see peeling wallpaper, mended textiles, and well-used furniture - all part of a unique demonstration of how an opulent Victorian manor can wear into a comfortable home through generations of use. The manor's gardens have been painstakingly restored to their original Victorian splendour, with the three-tiered Italian marble 'Dolphin Fountain', statue walks, fern dell, and rose dell giving an exquisite taste of the Victorian country life. For more information, please visit english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/brodsworth-hall-and-gardens

name: Dunnottar Castle
description: Likely fortified since the early Middle Ages, what remains of Dunnottar Castle mostly dates from the 15th and 16th centuries. Jutting out into the North Sea and surrounded by steep cliffs, the castle's strategic position gave it a prominent role in Scottish history. While it's been visited by William Wallace, Mary Queen of Scots, the Marquis of Montrose and the future King Charles II, Dunnottar is best known for its role in guarding the Honours of Scotland, the Crown Jewels. During Oliver Cromwell's campaign, the Honours were hidden at Dunnottar, and its small garrison weathered an 8 month siege to secret them past the English army. Today, though the castle is mostly in ruins, its dramatic position still makes it one of the most memorable sites in Scotland. Visitors can reach the castle via a steep, 800-metre footpath from the car park, though some might want to experience the 3-kilometre cliff-top path from Stonehaven. For more information, please visit dunnottarcastle.co.uk

name: Meteora
description: The Meteora rock formations are a jaw-dropping natural jewel on their own. The addition of 6 beautiful Orthodox monasteries in the 14th through 16th centuries makes for a truly unique sight. Each of the structures has its own distinct history, as the Nazi-shelled Monastery of St. Stephen will attest. All six monasteries are open to visitors, where you can learn about learn about their heritage and admire the Meteora landscape. Please note that it might be more physically challenging (high and steep staircases) to visit some of the structures.

name: Seven Miles Beach
description: Seven Mile Beach caters to every vacation wish. Luxurious resorts line the shore, offering world-class amenities and impeccable service. Indulge in pampering spa treatments, savor gourmet cuisine at oceanfront restaurants, or simply unwind by your private pool overlooking the mesmerizing turquoise expanse. Explore the crystal-clear underwater world teeming with colorful fish and vibrant coral reefs. Rent snorkeling gear and embark on an underwater adventure, or try stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking, or parasailing for a thrilling experience. Explore a variety of shops selling everything from designer swimwear to handcrafted Caymanian souvenirs.

name: Sveti Stefan
description: Formerly an island reserved as a playground for the rich and famous, Aman Resorts acquired Sveti Stefan and built a narrow attachment to the rest of the township of Sveti Stefan. While it is an exclusive resort, visitors come just for the sight of the island's timeless stone villas backed by dramatic mountains. While you can view the island while relaxing on the public beach or walking through the nearby park, many opt to relish the breathtaking views of the Budva Riviera while dining at one of the seaside restaurants like the Olive Restaurant, where you can tuck into some tomato-based fish chowder with a clear view of the islet. For those desperate to set foot on the isle, it is possible to do so by booking a reservation at the restaurant, or taking a guided tour at 11:00 or 14:00. For more information, or to make your reservation, please visit aman.com/resorts/aman-sveti-stefan

name: Batangas City
description: Batangas City was founded by the Spanish in the 16th century, though it had been a center for indigenous people for centuries before their arrival. Since its inception, the city's lifeblood has been its port, which had seen trade with locales as far-flung as India and Japan, and today, Batangas' port is one of the largest in the Philippines. The downtown area developed rapidly in the 20th century, but this is where you'll find one of the city's oldest landmarks: the late 16th century Basilica of the Immaculate Conception. To learn more about the city's heritage and history, you can head to the Museo Puntong Batangan, which a range of cultural artefacts and installations from different periods.

name: Niagara Falls, NY
description: Spanning the border between the US and Canada, Niagara Falls is the most powerful and iconic waterfall in North America. And part of the oldest state park in the US. There's a lot to see, so the trick to visiting is deciding how wet you want to get. For a completely dry experience, head to the Observation Tower near Prospect Point for the only panoramic view of all three Falls. From there, take an elevator to the dock where you can board the "Maid of the Mist" - the iconic boats that have been taking visitors into the splash zone since the late 1800s. Or walk to the base of the Bridal Veil falls at the Cave of the Winds after learning a bit about their history (and getting a poncho and sandals) at the World Changed Here Pavilion. For the wettest and wildest experience, head up to the Hurricane Deck is a must where the falls' self-made weather system will blow you away.

name: Bordeaux
description: While Bordeaux's history predates the Romans, its golden age came in the 1700s. Described by Victor Hugo as Versailles mixed with Antwerp, Bordeaux's 18th century beauty was used as the model for rebuilding the still quasi-medieval Paris. Today, the city's 18th century architecture still symbolizes the city, particularly the Place de la Bourse. Built in the 1720s by Louis XV's favourite architect, Jacques Gabriel, its beauty was amplified when the huge Water Mirror reflection pool was installed in front of it. The city's gorgeous Gothic cathedral and two basilicas are on the the way of Saint Jacques de Compostelle. Along with the older historic monuments, the city's sparking new 'City of Wine' Museum has 10 hours of audiovisual material celebrating the history of wine around the world. Of course, the other most important stops to make in the city are for wine, and the delectable Canelés pastries.

name: Corte
description: Located in the very heart of Corsica, Corte is a simply unmissable inland location with swathes of greenery and historical delights that will leave you swooning. Its citadel, built in 1419, teeters improbably atop a rock promontory at the very center of town. The military buildings were used as barracks and a prison during the Second World War, and one barrack now holds the Musée de la Corse, where you'll find 3000 traditional objects from Corsican history. Head to the Belvedere for the best views over the city, overlooking the Restonica and Tavignano valleys. For a tasty treat, visit the oldest grocery store in Europe - in business since 1769 - or pick up some Corsican pastries, brocciu donuts, ice creams or amaretti from one of the many shops lining the streets. Travel past semi-wild pigs and goats dotted along the roads on one of Corsica's most famous trails to the Gorges de la Restonica valley, and take a dip in Lake Melo or Lake Capitello.

name: Dole
description: Dole was the capital of Franche-Comté until Louis XIV conquered the region and moved the parliament from Dole to Besancon in 1422. Nevertheless, remnants of the town's importance still remain visible to this day. Found in the centre of the town and dominating its skyline is the Collegiale Notre-Dame de Dole, an impressive medieval cathedral constructed between 1509 and 1586. Clustered around the cathedral are the narrow streets of Dole's old town, which welcome visitors with numerous shops and cafes, making Dole a pleasant setting for an afternoon stroll. After exploring the streets of the old town, visitors are encouraged to head to the equally pleasant area of the town along the canal, known by locals and tourists alike as "Little Venice". Be sure to keep an eye out for the 3-story house with green shutters near the canal, known to be the birthplace of famous biologist and creator of the world's first vaccines, Louis Pasteur.

name: Bacalar
description: Bacalar was originally a Maya city which was conquered by Spanish conquistadors in 1543, and replaced by a Spanish settlement two years later. Located on the shores of a freshwater lagoon, Bacalar was frequently raided by pirates in the 17th century, and it wasn't until the construction of San Felipe's Fort in 1733 that the town was able to defend itself. Today, the imposing fort still stands watch over the lagoon, offering spectacular views, and a small museum dedicated to the days of piracy. After appreciating it from afar, you'll likely want to get your feet wet in the seven-colored lagoon. Along with simply swimming, it's a great place for snorkeling, diving, and kayaking. Those "lumpy rocks" in the water are rare fossilized formations formed by single cell organisms over the course of millions of years, and make up perhaps the largest freshwater organism on the planet!

name: Xochicalco
description: Set atop terraced hills, The Archaeological Zone of Xochicalco can be seen from afar and could be mistaken for nothing more than a pile of rocks. Up close, it's an exceptional display of ancient architecture with views for miles, containing pyramids, a palace, and ball courts where opponents would literally play for their lives, the losers being sacrificed to the Gods during ritualistic ceremonies. The pre-Hispanic fortified city filled a vacuum after the collapse of several large empires and became a political, religious and commercial centre, and now one of Mexico's most important and well-preserved archaeological sites. The main spectacle is the Pyramid of the Feathered Serpent, a huge pyramid structure covered in murals and carvings. Within the pyramid is an observatory where astronomers would congregate to confirm the calendar for reasons of agriculture and religion. The on-site museum is also well worth a visit shouldn't be missed (not only because you need to purchase your entry tickets there!).

name: Salem, MA
description: After being settled by Europeans in 1626, Salem quickly became one of early America's most important seaports. But its isolation from the established European towns and cities in the early years made it a hotbed for hysteria. This culminated in infamous witch trials that saw hundreds accused, and 20 executed. Fortunately, things have settled down since then, though the witch remains the town mascot. Today, you can visit the memorial to the victims of the Witch Trials, as well as the Witch House, the only structure in Salem with direct ties to the trials. The rest of the town is decidedly quaint, with some excellent historical offerings. Visit the Pickman House, built in 1664 that also has the Burying Point Cemetery, the second oldest cemetery in America. And the Salem Maritime National Historic Site along the waterfront consists of 12 buildings and a replica tall-ship that interpret American maritime history from colonization through independence.

name: Lamego
description: Settled since pre-Roman times, this hilltop town named itself 'the town with a permanent festival'. While they might not party every day, there's a lot to celebrate. The historic town centre is crisscrossed with narrow lanes and tree-lined boulevards, with spotlit medieval landmarks at every turn. Condensing the town's rich history into a single building, the Lamego Museum, housed in an 18th century bishop's palace has an astounding collection of ancient art and artefacts, including a fully reconstructed chapel dripping with gold. The iconic Santuario Nossa Senhora dos Remedios is accessed via hundreds of zigzagging stairs decorated with painted tiles, climbing out of a tailored garden. After the hike, be sure to enjoy some raposeira, the town's famously fragrant sparkling wine.

address.addr1: Pragser Wildsee, 39030 Prags, Province of Bolzano - South Tyrol, Italy
description: Lake Braies is a small Alpine lake that was formed during a landslide which blocked the river Braies. The natural lake is encompassed by the Dolomite peaks and many acres of surrounding forest. Its natural scenery paired with exquisite turquoise-blue waters make this virtually unknown gem a sight worth seeing. Trail along the lake circle or rent a rowboat and picnic along the river. Lake Braies' many hiking trails also make it the ideal spot for hikers, bikers, and climbers alike. This scenic fairytale lake is one of the deepest in the Alpine region, reaching depths of 38 meters. Enjoy the clean, fresh air and unspoiled beauty of one of Italy's best hidden gems as you explore the majestic Lake Braies.

name: San Carlos Nuevo Guaymas
description: As you step into the coastal paradise of San Carlos Nuevo Guaymas, you'll find yourself wishing you had discovered it sooner. Start your journey with a visit to Mirador San Carlos, a world-class viewpoint renowned by National Geographic for its breathtaking vistas of the Sea of Cortez and the majestic Mount Tetakawi. Of course, no visit to San Carlos is complete without experiencing its pristine beaches. Explore the white sands of Playa Algodones, ideal for snorkeling, or head to Playa Piedras Pintas, known for its mesmerizing tide pools and diving spots. For a unique souvenir, head to the nearby Pearl Farm in Guaymas, where you can purchase dazzling natural pearls directly. As your visit winds down, take a leisurely stroll along the enchanting boardwalk. Enjoy the finest seafood in the state as a perfect end to your San Carlos adventure. Such is the beauty of San Carlos Nuevo Guaymas that it has been featured in hit Hollywood films "Catch-22" and "The Mask of Zorro".

name: Las Vegas, NV
description: Las Vegas, often called "Sin City," started in 1905 as a small railroad town. The transformation of Las Vegas as we know it today began in 1931, when the state of Nevada legalized gambling, created loose divorce laws relative to the rest of the US, and construction on the Hoover Dam commenced. These activities brought an influx of workers and tourists looking to have fun and commit a little sin. The 1940s saw the rise of iconic casinos and entertainment venues funded partly by organized crime. The 1950s and 60s ushered in a golden era, with lavish resorts and performances by legends like Elvis Presley and Frank Sinatra. Over the decades, corporate investment replaced mob influence, leading to the development of mega-resorts like The Mirage and Bellagio in the 1990s. Today, the dazzling lights of Las Vegas attract hopeful gamblers from all over the world.

name: Nono
description: Derived from the Quechua language, Nono, originally ñuñu, translates to "breasts," inspired by the two hills, Los Nonos, overlooking the Los Sauces river. The main square, adorned with old grand houses, showcases the passage of time, with some buildings maintaining their original charm. The square itself transforms into an open-air art gallery, featuring metallic sculptures crafted from various materials, a testament to the town's artistic spirit. Sarmiento Street, the main thoroughfare, and Vicente Castro Street, the only paved ones, reveal the village's dusty ambiance, providing a glimpse into the local lifestyle. Amidst the historical tapestry stands Saint John Baptist's chapel church, a testament to the town's spiritual heritage. The journey through Nono unfolds like a tapestry of natural wonders. From the picturesque Ford on the Chico River to the mesmerizing beaches of Los Remansos and Paso de las Tropas, visitors are treated to pools, cascades, and serene beaches. A highlight of Nono is the Rocsen Museum, a testament to one man's passion for collecting artifacts from every facet of human life. With over 23,000 pieces, this museum, founded by Juan Santiago Bouchon, presents an eclectic mix of archeological wonders, antiques, art, and more, making it a must-visit destination for those seeking a unique cultural experience.

name: Vive Mar Turtle Camp
description: Vive Mar Turtle Camp was founded in 2011 with a simple goal - to conserve the ecosystems along the Oaxaca Coast. Vive Mar protects over 27 km of coastline, providing a safe habitat for 4 of the world's 7 species of sea turtles. The Vive Mar team keeps the beaches clean, and even patrols them at night to keep away poachers who come in search of valuable turtle eggs. On your visit, the friendly volunteers will proudly tell you about Vive Mar's work, and the dangers facing sea turtles. Of course, the highlight of your visit, and possibly your entire holiday, is releasing a baby turtle into the sea (this of course depends on if there are any hatchlings when you visit)! For more information, please visit https://vivemar.com.mx/en/home/

name: Guanajuato
description: With the colors of houses cascading down the hills in a chaotic rainbow towards the city center, Guanajuato is a no-brainer dream destination for those travelers who are looking for diversity, tradition, and authenticity. Rich in history as the site of the first battle of the Mexican War of Independence, it is nowadays a UNESCO World Heritage site as a tribute to its place in Mexican culture. If you are the type to plan your itinerary, you can certainly add the stunning yellow Guanajuato Cathedral to your list, along with its accompanying Plaza de la Paz for a bit of lounging relaxation. Those with a morbid curiosity can also visit the famous museum Mummies of Guanajuato, which were taken from the adjoining cemetery. However, this is a city of narrow cobblestone streets and transfixing colors - take advantage of the opportunity to wander, and find a precious spot for yourself!

name: Jokulsarlon
description: Jokulsarlon is a glacial lake that formed during the 20th century as the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier began a rapid retreat due to rising temperatures. The melting glacier also left chunks of itself behind as it made its retreat, filling the waters with a fleet of icebergs. Each of these giant blocks of ice is uniquely shaped and colored, with streaks of blue and black, making for a breathtakingly beautiful parade as they slowly head out to sea, melting along the way. One of Iceland's most beautiful natural sights, it's also a chilling reminder of the effects of climate change.l A short walk away, you'll find the "Diamond Beach" - a stretch of black sand where crystal-clear remnants of these icebergs wash ashore.

name: Culiacan
description: Culiacán is a must-see for nature and museum enthusiasts, with rich culture and heritage crawling into all areas of the city. Immerse yourself in nature at the Jardin Botanico Culiacán, showcasing a diverse collection of over 900 plant species. Take a leisurely tour of the beautiful gardens and unleash your creativity in a botanical workshop on site. The city is also home to the Parque de las Riberas, a sprawling 120-hectare natural park that seamlessly blends urban amenities with natural surroundings. Here, outdoor enthusiasts can bird-watch, mountain bike, and even zip-line for an exhilarating experience. Downtown Culiacán is where art enthusiasts will thrive, where the large art museum and numerous smaller galleries offer a glimpse into the region's artistic heritage. For a pleasant stroll downtown, check out the iconic Culiacán Cathedral near the picturesque Tamazula River. This scenic spot is adorned with the giant Culiacán letters and a central plaza around which the city's charm revolves.

name: Toro Verde Adventure Park
address.addr1: Toro Verde Adventure Park, puerto rico
description: High in the mountains of central Puerto Rico, the Toro Verde Adventure Park offers some of the best views on the island - if you're up for some adrenaline-inducing adventure. You can choose from a number of tour options, combining zip lines and suspension bridges, depending on how daring you are. The park's most famous attraction is "The Monster", the world's second-longest zip line, which will turn you into superman as you soar above the trees for 2.5 kilometers, reaching speeds over 150 kmh. If that's a bit too much, "The Beast" is its baby brother, which still offers the same amazing views, but at a more modest 100kmh over its 1.4km length. Then there are highflying obstacle courses, thrilling rope courses, and even a flying bicycle ride! Please note: adjust your stop time to fit your tour option. Tickets must be booked in advance at https://www.toroverdepr.com/

name: Pigeon Forge, TN
description: Pigeon Forge, TN was a sleepy mountain hamlet until FDR established the Great Smoky Mountains National Park in 1940. From there, a few campgrounds emerged, and then a themed railroad ride, and in the 1980s, it reinvented itself as a resort destination. In 1985, Dolly Parton partnered with one of the theme parks to launch Dollywood. With over 40 rides, not to mention daily shows and festivals throughout the year, Dollywood offers nearly endless entertainment for all ages. It's worth the pilgrimage just for a loaf of their famous cinnamon bread! And there's plenty to do outside Dollywood. Take in the amazing view from the 200-foot-tall Great Smoky Mountain Wheel, or watch a choreographed fountain display at The Island. For a great educational experience, head to the interactive Titanic Museum, which has everything from real artifacts to recreations of different rooms. The entry ticket is even a boarding pass with the name of an actual passenger or crew member!
