name: Cave of Zeus
description: The Diktaeaen Cave (also known as the Cave of Psychro) is one of the most significant sites in Greece – it is allegedly the birthplace of Zeus himself! According to the myth, it was the place where the king of the gods was hidden from his cruel father, Cronos. The area surrounding the cave is quite windy since it is located over three thousand feet above sea level, so enjoy the stunning views and serpentine roads before you get in. Once you arrive, still need to follow a steep path up to the cave entrance, although it's also possible to rent a donkey to make the journey a bit easier. Inside the cave, each chamber has impressive stalactites and stalagmites (but be aware that bats and rock doves call this place home). Numerous archeological excavations confirm that the cave was used as a place for worship since the early Minoan times. Objects found include an altar, bronze, iron, stone, clay and bone artifacts, semi-precious stones, and even human figurines – a rare discovery indeed. Some of the items are now on display at world-renowned institutions such as the Heraklion Museum, the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, the Louvre, and the British Museum. After the visit, indulge in local delicacies such as kvass and yogurt ice cream at the nearby restaurant. For information about ticket costs and opening hours, visit the Cave of Zeus website at http://odysseus.culture.gr/h/2/eh255.jsp?obj_id=1628.

name: Qumran National Park
description: Qumran was founded under the reign of John Hyrcanus towards the end of the 2nd century BC, and destroyed a few short centuries later. Details about the site's nature are still debated, with explanations ranging from it being home to a Hebrew sect or a production center for pottery. Within the ruins, you'll find the remains of houses, a groundwater aqueduct, a ritual bath, and potter's kiln, with plenty of informative signage. However, the site's most significant find was a series of caves containing nearly 1000 manuscripts from around 400 BC to 300 AD, including the second-oldest known works that would be included in the Hebrew Bible canon. Along with being able to see the caves in which these significant texts were discovered, Qumran's informative visitor center goes into more details about the settlement, and the manuscripts.

name: The Lost Gardens of Heligan
address.addr1: The Lost Gardens of Heligan, Pentewan, Saint Austell PL26 6EN, UK
description: The Lost Gardens of Heligan were created between the 18th and 20th centuries by the Cornish Tremayne family from the mid-18th century to the beginning of the 20th century. In 1920, the estate owner moved to Italy, and rented out the house, leaving the gardens neglected to the point that they were reclaimed by nature and forgotten. In the 1990s, the gardens were rediscovered, and a massive restoration project undertaken to restore them to their former glory. Today, visitors can admire ancient rhododendrons and colossal camellias, a series of lakes fed by a century-old ram pump, and 'The Jungle' - a subtropical filled with tree ferns. The gardens also have Europe's last pineapple pit, which is kept warm by rotting manure. Amongst the lush surroundings, visitors will also find a Burmese rope bridge, and the garden's two famous figures - the Mud Maid and the Giant's Head. For more information, please visit www.heligan.com

name: Trikala
description: It was around 49 000 BC that the first permanent settlement was established where the modern city of Trikala lies, while the ancient city of Trikke, which was mentioned in Homer's Iliad, was founded in 3rd millennium BCE. This rich heritage is easy to see even today, thanks to various ruins in the city. In the 17th century Varoussi neighborhood, visitors will find picturesque narrow alleys and multi-colored houses, as well as several churches, while the Koursoum Mosque from the 16th century is a reminder of the Ottoman rule.

name: Taxco
description: Founded by the Spanish in 1529 not far from an important Aztec settlement, Taxco grew rich during the colonial era for the abundance of silver in the surrounding hills. While much of the city's economy has since shifted from mining, it is still famous for its skilled silversmiths. Walking up the sloping cobblestone streets, you'll pass colorful colonial buildings that are still in use as family homes, shops, or restaurants. But no matter where you are, you'll be in sight of the Templo de Santa Prisca Guerrero standing proudly on the central hilltop. A masterful example of Baroque architecture, the church's opulent decor stands as a reminder of the town's former wealth. The nearby Museum of Religious Art is also worth checking out for both its ornate architecture and interesting collection.

name: Portimao
description: A fishing center since pre-Roman times, the city's old fishing docks have been transformed into a scenic promenade, leading to the quaint and tree-lined plazas of the old town. The waterfront's series of squares are filled with outdoor cafés facing gushing fountains. Heading up the river, the many open-air restaurants serve up the city's staple: sardines. The narrow streets just back from the bridge are Portimão's oldest, with more than a hint of their fishing-quarter past. While an earthquake in 1755 destroyed most of the city's buildings, the Igreja da Nossa Senhora da Conceição managed to retain its fourteenth-century Manueline door.

name: Parma
description: One of Italy's most prosperous cities, Parma was founded by the Romans in 183 BC. The distinguished city has many important art galleries, museums, old churches and buildings to explore in this compact city. Three delectable foods are associated with the city of Parma: parmesan cheese, prosciutto, and handmade pasta. This, of course, means that there's also a wide range of restaurants serving local delicious cuisine to choose from. In the heart of Parma lies its cathedral square, Piazza Duomo, with its attractive cobblestone. Located within the piazza is the renowned city cathedral. This 13th century cathedral is a prominent example of Romanesque style of the Po Valley. Another notable attraction located in the heart of town is the baptistery, or Battistero. This striking octagon-shaped building dates back to the 12th century and features pink Verona marble decorated with medieval carvings. Inside, many colorful frescoes are waiting to be discovered. Sample some parmesan cheese and prosciutto as you make your way through this colorful city.

name: Kericho
description: Kericho town, capital of Kericho County, is in the heart of Kenya's countryside in the highlands west of the Rift Valley. It is famous nationally as being home to the best tea Kenya has to offer, with its many tea plantations and locals consuming typically 3 to 4 cups every day. Kerichos picturesque scenery makes the town a peaceful place to visit and a tranquil destination for those looking to get away from the hustle and bustle of daily life. Visit the tea plantations for an insight into the local agricultural industry (some even let you see the factories!) and enjoy some of the finest tea you'll taste. Surrounded by plantations is the Chagaik Botanic Gardens, a serene tropical jungle containing lots of lush vegetation and even the possibility of spotting monkeys and many forest birds. If you're looking to wind down, Kericho is the place for you!

name: Zabljak
description: Durmitor is a massive National Park in Montenegro that as 2005 has been honored in joining the UNESCO World Heritage List. It is full of breathtaking views, inspiring valleys, and majestic mountains. It's natural beauty attracts people from all over, but especially those who aspire to see Europe's deepest canyon, the Tara River Canyon and the Tara River. Previously, only the Tara River was protected by the UNESCO list. Today this river flows through Bosnia Herzegovina and Montenegro, sometimes acting as their natural border. Hike through these moderate trails and get a chance to view some waterfalls for yourself.

name: Calakmul
description: Between 500 BC and 900 AD, Calakmul was a superpower, helping shape Mayan culture in the region through its influence over an estimated 1.5 million people. When it collapsed in the 10th century, so too did the entire culture, and in the centuries that followed, the area has remained essentially depopulated. Today, the ruins are thought to include more structures than any other Maya settlement in the region, though it's the central plaza that steals the show. Here, a large hilltop pyramid stands next to the 47-meter-tall "Structure 2" - the tallest structure in the country and one of the largest Mayan pyramids. The ruins of Calakmul sit within one of the world's largest biodiversity hotspots, which adds an extra element of adventure to a visit. You'll likely see several of the area's 350 bird species while walking the grounds, and from atop the pyramids, nothing but forest.

name: Vitoria-Gasteiz
description: Originally a defensive outpost founded by Sancho the Wise in 1181, the city grew in size and prominence over the years. In the 19th century, the city played a pivotal role in Spanish history when General the Marquess of Wellington broke the French army, assuring the eventual end of their control, and giving Beethoven inspiration for Opus 91. In Vitoria's historic center, many of the buildings date back to the 16th century or earlier, and are partly surrounded by an 11th century wall. Several palaces are sequestered within, such as the Renaissance Bendaña Palace, which houses a card museum. The 13th-century Cathedral of Santa María offers visitors a singular experience. In 1994 it was closed for restoration, but now offers a guided tour of the restoration process. Visitors are led over scaffolded walkways and stone staircases for an intimate look into the very heart of the church.

name: La Roque-Gageac
description: A quiet medieval fishing and trade village, La Roque-Gageac rose in prominence during the Hundred Years War when the Bishops of Sarlat built their residence on the edge of town. Since the 12th century, the cliffs behind the town have been fortified with a cave keep, which was expanded through the 17th century thanks to the village's strategic position. Today, La Roque-Gageac is recognized as one of the most beautiful villages in France with its gorgeous, golden stone houses nestled between steep cliffs and a lazy river. Essentially unchanged for centuries, the village is a jumble of charming cottages and grand manors, interspersed with tropical greenery - the cliffs protecting the village from harsh weather. The fort that defended from invaders, however, is visible but inaccessible - it was closed following a collapse.

name: Sassandra
description: Unveiling the soul of Côte d'Ivoire's southwest coast, Sassandra isn't just a town; it's a captivating melody where the rhythm of the ocean meets the vibrant pulse of African culture. Delve into the heart of the bustling market, a sensory feast for the curious explorer. Friendly vendors display an array of treasures, from colorful fabrics perfect for creating unique garments to hand-carved wooden masks whispering tales of local legends. The air thrums with the rhythmic beats of traditional music, a vibrant invitation to immerse yourself in the town's infectious energy. Beyond the market's allure, explore the rich history of Sassandra. Visit the colonial-era port, a captivating reminder of the town's maritime past. Envision grand sailing ships arriving from distant lands, their holds overflowing with exotic goods. Learn about the region's fascinating cultural heritage at the local museum, where ancient artifacts and captivating exhibits bring the stories of the Bété people to life.

name: Huelva
description: Settled over 2,500 years ago by the Tartessans, this riverside city of Huelva has been an important port since antiquity. When the Romans conquered the region, they began to exploit the area's natural resources, - a practice that continued for centuries. Huelva's port helped launch Christopher Columbus' 1492 voyage to the New World. In the 12th century La Rábida monastery, Friar Juan Pérez and Friar Antonio de Marchena promoted Columbus' voyage, and he stayed there until just before his departure. Today, visitors can roam the idyllic grounds, and learn about Columbus' fateful voyage on a model of his ship. The city's historic center has maintained its historic identity, with the 16th century church of San Pedro made in the Gothic-Mudejar style on the remains of an old mosque, while the 18th century Cathedral of La Merced houses the Pantheon of the Counts of Niebla.

name: Tirano
description: While best known as the starting point for the UNESCO protected Bernina Express railway, this alpine city has a lot more to offer visitors than just a trip out of town. On September 29, 1504, the Virgin Mary appeared to the village and ended a pestilence. Within days, wheels were in motion to construct a basilica dedicated to the miracle. Within 6 months, construction had begun, and the church was officiated in 1513. The interior is lined with vibrant frescoes and dominated by a massive pipe organ with gilded wood frame. The 17th century Palazzo Salis has over ten rooms decorated with frescoes and stucco from the 17th and 18th century. Dubbed 'one of the most frescoed' mansions', the trompe l'oeil artwork is a feast for the eyes - as is the manicured Italian garden.

name: Mdina
description: Founded in the 8th century, Mdina was Malta's capital from ancient times to the medieval period and has now become a quiet, historically significant retreat. Located on a hilltop with stunning views of Malta and surrounded by tall bastion fortifications, the city is a well-preserved treasure filled with centuries-old buildings. A ditch surrounding the bastion walls has been transformed into a charming public garden, and the streets inside the city are paved with large stones and cobbles. Hear the clip-clop sound of horse-drawn carriages through the city as you explore the impressive St. Paul's Cathedral and chapels lining the narrow streets. For magnificent views of the eastern part of Malta, head to the bastion at Triq is-Sur, a peaceful spot to enjoy the city's tranquility and scenery. Close to the Main Gate, you'll find the Mdina Dungeons, an intriguing museum showcasing underground passageways, chambers and cells that recreate the dark events that transpired within these walls over the decades.

name: Ciudad Guzman
description: Ciudad Guzman is a picturesque city offering visitors a taste of small-town life with all the amenities of a larger city. Visitors can wander the main plaza and discover restaurants or small shops offering local cuisines and creations. Gorge on tostados (child de uña is a local favorite) before feasting your eyes on the Ciudad Cathedral which boasts gothic vaults and a stone facade and features four stunning altarpieces inside. The vibrant city is home to many families, students and all around friendly individuals and continues to welcome more tourists each year!

name: Daanbantayan
description: Daanbantayan is a sleepy seaside town that's a great destination for travellers who just want to relax on the beach, but it also has a surprisingly varied offering of historic monuments. The Daanbantayan Town Plaza was the site of a battle between local volunteers and a group of bandits, which was settled with a man-to-man duel. Tapilon Point provides great views of the coast, and in the 19th century was the site of a watchtower that was eventually abandoned as pirates shifted their sights elsewhere. The locals called it the "old watch tower" (daang bantayanan), which gave the town its name. The standout monument is the 19th century Sta. Rosa de Lima Parish Church - the only church in Cebu with a three-sided facade and receded belfry. While the exterior is well-preserved, the interior has been entirely renovated, and is a simple affair with raw stone walls, and modest Baroque altar.

name: Linkoping
description: Founded in the 12th century, Linköping was the site of the second diocese in Sweden. Despite its early religious importance, Linköping remained a small town until 1937, when the Saab Aerospace set up their headquarters here and ushered in a period of rapid expansion. While today the city is a tech-industry hub, it's still dominated by its amazing medieval cathedral. The 13th century Linköping Castle is now home to the country sheriff of Östergötland county, but part of the building is used as a museum. At Gamla Linköping (Old Linköping) and Valla fritidsområde you'll find early 19th century buildings that were saved from demolition and moved to this open air museum where citizens in period dress give visitors a taste of life gone by. The city is equally as proud of its modern developments, and is home to the Museum of the Swedish Air force and an interactive IT Museum

name: Eskisehir
description: Archaeological findings date Eskisehir's foundation back 4000 years, though it's the Phrygians who are credited with laying the groundwork for today's city in 1000 BC. Despite its name meaning 'Old City', much of Eskisehir had to be rebuilt following the Turkish War of Independence, which paved the way for the city's new, youthful identity. Thanks to recent developments and a huge student population, Eskisehir feels like a happenin' European city with its pleasant parks, cafes, and even a riverfront beach! However, head to Odunpazarı, Eskişehir's protected old town, and it feels like you've stepped back into the days of the Ottoman Empire. The streets are lined with historic pastel-colored houses, many of which have been converted into museums and cafes, and the 16th century Kurşunlu Külliyesi Complex showcases traditional art and architecture.

name: Valletta
description: Valletta is a veritable treasure trove of architectural wonders and cultural heritage on the main island of Malta, and is Europe's sunniest city. An impressive 320 historical monuments fit into the city, with the buildings dating back to the 16th century and constructed by the Knights Hospitaller. Visit St. John's Co-Cathedral, the most popular location in Valletta, with its unassuming facade concealing a breathtaking interior adorned with marble floors, coat of arms, and frescoes depicting the life of St. John the Baptist. The cathedral also houses famous works by Caravaggio. Explore the Grand Master's Palace and its beautiful courtyards, fountains, State Rooms and Council Chamber, before heading to Merchant Street for a plethora of jewelers showcasing the very best of Maltese craftsmanship. Visit Republic Street for rows of cafes, restaurants and terraces, perfect for a leisurely lunch, and take in panoramic views of the sea from Fort St Elmo.

name: Vigan
description: Vigan was founded by the Spanish in the 16th century, though it had long been used by Chinese traders who came to trade goods from the Asian mainland for gold, beeswax, and other indigenous products. While the city developed as a Spanish Colonial town, it was strongly influenced by the Chinese, Ilocano, and Filipino cultures that lived here strongly influenced its architecture. Today, the city's historic center is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage as the best-preserved Spanish colonial town in Asia. Centered around the pedestrian-only Crisologo St., Vigan's two-storey, steep-roofed buildings made from wood and brick are reminiscent of traditional Chinese architecture. A great starting point for exploring Vigan's historic streets is the turn-of-the-19th-century St. Paul's Cathedral, which sits between the two main plazas – Plaza Salcedo and Plaza Burgos.

name: Rennes
description: Starting as a humble Gallic village over 2000 years ago, Rennes grew into the capital of Brittany, and is now a vibrant university town. Because of a major fire in 1720, Rennes' old town is a web of medieval buildings and vibrantly painted half-timbered houses mixed with 18th century stone structures and fine mansions. The Cathedral of Saint-Pierre has retained its original 16th century facade, though the rest of the cathedral was rebuilt in the 18th-19th centuries. Inside, visitors will find a 16th century grand-altarpiece among the many columns of the neo-Classical interior. Outside the medieval quarter, visitors are treated to the many luxurious buildings from the 17th and 18th centuries. The Musée des Beaux-Arts, like many French museums, exhibits masterpieces seized during the Revolution. The 18th-century historian Christophe-Paul de Robien's collection of exquisite Egyptian, Greek, Etruscan and Roman artefacts are kept in good company with works by Rubens, Rembrandt, da Vinci, and Picasso.

name: Zrenjanin
description: First mentioned in the 14th century, when it was a village of Hungarian farmers, Zrenjanin's long history has helped it grow into a vibrant, multi-cultural hub. Under the Ottoman rule from 1551 to 1717, the city became a part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes after the First World War. Today, the city is filled with monuments from the 18th to 19th centuries. At the heart of the city's languid Liberty Square, a statue of Peter I of Yugoslavia keeps watch over the surrounding architecture. The neo-Baroque city hall was built as a symbol of the city's economic power, and exhibits some beautiful architectural details, stucco, and stained glass windows. The nearby neo-Romanesque Cathedral is filled with frescoes and stained glass, but it's the copy of Da Vinci's "The Last Supper" attracts the most attention.

name: Lahti
description: In the early 20th century, Lahti was dubbed "the Chicago of Finland" because, like its American counterpart, it was a major center for the meat and lumber industries. But Lahti has since turned a new leaf and blossomed into a leader in sustainability. It was even named the European Green Capital in 2021. The city's industrial architecture has been repurposed, and now house restaurants, shops, and cafes, which help feed a vibrant cultural scene. Head to the harbor for cozy cafes, architectural gems, small boutiques, and beautiful views of Lake Vesijärvi. Catch the symphony at the quintessentially Scandinavian Sibelius Hall, or check out one of the city's many museums, which cover everything from art to military medicine. Lahti is also well-known for its quality beer and liquor, so be sure to ask for a Lahden Erikois or Teerenpeli beer, or a Taivaanranta whiskey. If you're looking to experience the Lake District's signature nature landscapes, head to the Päijänne National Park, a UNESCO Global Geopark just outside the city to enjoy the moss forests, sandy beaches, and crystal clear water.

name: Nine Mile
description: Nestled in the heart of the lush, rolling hills of St. Ann Parish, the tiny village of Nine Mile is cemented in history for its cultural significance. It was the birthplace, childhood home, and now final resting place of one of the world's most beloved musical icons: Bob Marley. For fans of reggae music and Marley himself, a visit to Nine Mile is a pilgrimage of sorts, offering a chance to connect with the roots of the genre and pay homage to its most famous son. The Bob Marley Museum, located on the grounds of Marley's former home, is a must-visit and provides a glimpse into Marley's life: from his humble beginnings to his rise as a global superstar. Marley's mausoleum is also located on the property, where he lays together with his half-brother and Mamma Marley. The tours are provided by Rastafarian guides, and visitors can also find a restaurant and gift shops on the property. Complemented by the breathtaking natural beauty of the place, a visit to Nine Nile will complete your trip to Jamaica.

name: Jarabacoa
description: Tucked away 529 meters (1,736 feet) up in the Dominican Alps, the mountain resort town of Jarabacoa is a favorite for adventurous tourists and locals alike. The high altitude offers a respite from the heat, while the sweeping green landscapes are filled with natural attractions. Some come to make the 2-3 day trek to the summit of Pico Duarte, the tallest peak in the Caribbean. Most, however, are drawn to the rivers and waterfalls that stream through the countryside. You can go river rafting, tubing, canyoning and rappelling down Salto Baiguate. Or hike up to the Salto de Jimenoa falls to swim in a natural pool at the foot of one of the Dominican Republic's highest waterfalls. If you're traveling with kids, head to La Confluencia, where you can take a dip in the river or go on a family horseback ride.

name: El Cora Crocodile Sanctuary
description: The good folk at El Cora Crocodile Sanctuary are dedicated to preserving and educating visitors from all over about the world on the beauty and importance of nature. Their mission is to cultivate interest in and respect for wildlife through tours of the sanctuary grounds and by educating their guests on various aspects of the crocodile habitat and life cycle. If you have a passion for ecotourism, small children who love to point at big scary animals, or just a passing interest in wildlife, this is the place for you to expand your interest or learn something new! Tours start every 20 minutes and last 1.5-2 hours. For more information, please visit: https://www.rivieranayarit.com/activities/land/el-cora-crocodile-sanctuary/

name: Kerikeri
description: Kerikeri, situated in Northland, the northernmost region of New Zealand, is home to preserved historic sites that tell the story of how the indigenous Māori people met with Christian missionaries in the early 1800's. The towns' Mission Station is home to New Zealand's oldest standing building, Mission House (now Kemp House), built in the 1820's by missionary carpenters. The neighbouring Stone Store is the country's oldest stone building, constructed in the 1830's, a former storehouse for the missionary's supplies. A visit to the Kemp House and Stone Store is by guided tour only and the museums depict the missionary and Māori interaction and other local history. For a taste of nature visit Rainbow Falls, a stunning 27-metre high waterfall with three viewing platforms and a popular swimming hole beneath the drop. The short walk to the falls is accessible and surrounded by beautiful greenery and native birds and wildlife.

name: Seixal
description: Seixal is a living postcard, with its Madeiran beachfront views, ocean pools and charming village life making for a wondrous retreat on the island. Visit the Porto de Abrigo do Seixal beach, where black sand collides with clear waters, surrounded by verdant green mountains. Bodyboarding, canoeing and other water sports are popular activities at Seixal beach all year round. A natural pool is in walking distance from the beach, where you can bathe in refreshing waters enclosed by rocky alcoves. Go for a walk through the village situated at the bottom of the steep mountains, with a gorgeous seafront promenade offering views of the north coast. Within the valley, beautiful vineyard terraces dot the luscious green surrounds, such as Barbusano Winery at which you can enjoy some wine samples.

name: Hsinchu
description: Hsinchu offers a deep dive into the historical roots of Taiwan. It's a place where Hakka culture thrives, representing the original Taiwanese aboriginal minority from the southern-eastern part of the country. Chenghuang Temple, also known as the 'City God Temple,' is a historic landmark in Hsinchu, boasting a 270-year-old legacy. This two-tiered architectural marvel features towering red pillars, vibrant symbolic paintings, and an ever-present aroma of incense. Remarkably, it stands amidst the bustling urban landscape, surrounded by restaurants and snack vendors. One culinary treasure that Hsinchu offers is its renowned duck noodles. The city's specialty involves cooking fresh duck in a flavorful sauce, smoking it, and then simmering it in a hearty soup alongside thick noodles, resulting in a delectable fusion of flavors.

name: Quito
description: Settled since around 8000 BC, the modern city of Quito was established in 1534 by 204 Spanish settlers after they subdued the indigenous resistance. The city flourished through the colonial era, and was the starting point in Ecuador's war for independence from Spain. Despite having grown into one of the largest cities in the country, Quito's historic Old Town has remained essentially unchanged. The city's own unique brand of Baroque architecture, blending European and indigenous art styles, helped it earn UNESCO recognition. The best place to start exploring the Old Town is the Plaza Grande, which is surrounded by amazing colonial buildings like the Presidential Palace and 16th century Metropolitan Cathedral. A few blocks away is the 17th century La Compañía de Jesus, which is one of the most ornate in the country. The Plaza San Francisco is also worth seeking out to see Quito's oldest church and the stunning Andes views.

name: Saint-Jean-de-Luz
description: Saint-Jean-de-Luz began as a small port known for little more than fishing and pirates. Thanks to its strategic position, in the 17th century it enjoyed its 'Golden Age', being of such stature that Louis XIV wed the Infanta Maria Theresa of Spain here on 9 June, 1660. Towards the end of the 19th century, the town's white-sand beach made it a destination for French and Spanish aristocracy, and it remains a popular beach resort to this day. The Church of St John the Baptist, where the royal wedding was held, is lavishly decorated inside and dominated by a massive gilted Baroque altarpiece. You can also visit the houses where Louis XIV and the Infanta of Spain stayed before taking a stroll along the waterfront promenade. Of course, being a fishing port in Basque country, you'd be remiss to not stop to enjoy the local cuisine.

name: Villafranca del Bierzo
description: Situated along the legendary Way of St. James (Camino de Santiago), Villafranca del Bierzo is the backdrop of centuries of pilgrimage tradition. First mentioned in 791, this charming Spanish town gained prominence in the 9th century as a vital rest stop for pilgrims journeying to Santiago de Compostela. Its unique distinction comes from being the only place where pilgrims can receive the Jubilee blessing without completing the entire pilgrimage. The town's name, meaning "French Town," originated in 1070 when Alfonso VI of León established a Cluniac monastery for winemaking, attracting French pilgrims who settled nearby. Today, visitors can explore its rich architectural heritage, officially recognized as a Cultural Interest Asset, including the impressive Castle, the picturesque Calle del Agua, historic churches of San Francisco and San Nicolás, the vibrant Plaza Mayor, and the stately Collegiate Church.

name: Rotorua
description: Rotorua is New Zealand's most prominent geothermal town. Here you can see boiling mud in the parks, steam coming from the drains, and pungent gasses emanating from cracks on the edge of the lake. But don't let the eggy smells put you off - there is a reason why Rotorua is such a popular destination. In the town itself the Polynesian Spa offers a large range of pools for therapeutic bathing, while just across from the baths is the Rotorua Museum - worth a look for the beautiful Government Gardens and elegant colonial-era mansion. There's also many opportunities for hiking on doorstep, from the great lake views of Mount Ngongotaha to Whakarewarewa Forest, one of the few places in the world where Californian giant redwood trees grow successfully. Moari culture is also strong here, with several showcase villages and meeting halls from which to learn and experience more of the native culture.

name: Korhogo
description: Dive into the vibrant heart of northern Côte d'Ivoire and discover the captivating town of Korhogo. Friendly vendors display their wares, from hand-woven textiles in vibrant colors to intricately carved wooden sculptures depicting local folklore. The rhythmic beats of djembe drums fill the air, creating an infectious energy that pulsates through the streets.Explore the fascinating Sénoufo villages surrounding the town. Here, traditional mudbrick houses adorned with symbolic motifs offer a glimpse into a way of life unchanged for centuries. Witness age-old ceremonies and immerse yourself in the rich cultural heritage of the Sénoufo people. For a taste of serenity, escape to the Grande Mosquée, a magnificent architectural marvel. Admire the towering mudbrick minaret, a testament to the town's Islamic heritage, and find a quiet corner to soak in the tranquility of the central courtyard. name: Winchester City Mill
description: The Winchester City Mill was first recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086. In 1744, James Cook rebuilt the mill, and it's stayed the same ever since. After a 90 year hiatus, the mill was restored to working order in 2004, giving visitors a rare opportunity to see a fully functional urban corn mill. Today, the mill stands as an interactive museum to both the site's industrial heritage, and the area's wildlife. Visitors can immerse themselves in hands-on activities, as well as milling and baking demonstrations, and learn more about milling and the natural ecosystem through audio-visual displays. Along with kingfishers, trout, and the occasional salmon, the River Itchen, which powers the mill, is one of the only urban locations in the UK with otters. Motion-activated cameras record their comings and goings, letting visitors can enjoy clips of their comings-and goings, and view the live feed from cameras along the river. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/winchester-city-mill

name: Monolithos
description: Perched atop a rugged cliff overlooking the azure waters of the Aegean Sea, Monolithos stands as a symbol of ancient grandeur and timeless beauty in the Greek Islands. At the heart of Monolithos lies the imposing Monolithos Castle, a medieval fortress steeped in history and surrounded by breathtaking natural scenery. Built by the Knights of Saint John in the 15th century, the castle served as a strategic stronghold against invaders and offers a glimpse into the island's storied past. As visitors explore the labyrinthine pathways and ancient battlements of the castle, they are transported back in time to an era of knights and crusaders. Beyond its historical significance, Monolithos enchants visitors with its unspoiled natural beauty and tranquil ambiance. Surrounded by lush pine forests and fragrant olive groves, the village exudes an air of serenity and relaxation, making it an ideal destination for nature lovers and outdoor enthusiasts. For those seeking adventure, Monolithos offers a myriad of outdoor activities, from hiking and mountain biking to exploring hidden coves and secluded beaches along the coastline.

name: Trim Castle
description: Trim Castle was built in the 12th century on a hill overlooking a crossing of the River Boyne. The area was an important medieval ecclesiastical and royal site, and during medieval times and served as the seat of the Norman administration for the Lordship of Meath. Covering 30,000 square meters, it's the largest and best preserved Norman castle in Ireland. The towering keep at the heart of the castle is partly ruined, with its wooden floors have long since rotted away. Even so, it's a fascinating example of medieval defensive architecture, with its elevated entrance, the narrow windows for archers, and spiral staircases to give defenders the upper-hand. A guided tour adds even more life to the moss-covered walls, offering insights into the daily lives of the people who once lived here - right down to how they'd dry their clothes over the toilets to kill off bugs. For more information, please visit http://www.heritageireland.ie/en/midlands-eastcoast/trimcastle/

name: Ponte de Lima
description: It's said when the Romans reached the Limia River, they thought it was so beautiful, it could only be the legendary River Lethe, which would erase the memories of anyone who crossed it. The Roman general Decimus Junius Brutus had to cross the river himself and call out each of his men by name before they would cross. Today, Portugal's oldest village is also one of its most scenic. Positioned in the heart of Portugal's wine country, the town has grown to encompass both banks of the river, connected by the original Roman bridge, where statues of Roman legionnaires stand, waiting to be called. Roaming the streets, visitors are treated to ancient architecture, such as the Romanesque Igreja Matriz de Ponte de Lima, as well as scenic azulejo murals.

name: Nha Trang
description: As the 8th century Po Nagar Cham temple complex can attest, the coastal town of Nha Trang has a long and proud history. After admiring the 1000-year-old red brick complex with its detailed carvings, visitors can bask on the white sand beach, walk along the waterfront promenade, or head up to the 45th floor of Havana Hotel, where you can enjoy a rooftop bar and 360° views of the city and coast. Set on a hill overlooking the train station, the neo-Gothic Nha Trang Cathedral, though the 4,000 tombstones mounted on the walls were added in 1988 when the cemetery was leveled to extend the train station. For Buddhist monuments, the Long Son Pagoda and its giant white Buddha is the most notable. If you're looking for an experience you won't find anywhere else, head to Vinpearl Land, Vietnam's "most attractive amusement park", where you can ride the world's longest cable car sea crossing.

address.region: Archipiélago de San Andrés, Providencia y Santa Catalina
description: El Hoyo Soplador is a must-visit for travelers seeking a dash of excitement and a touch of natural wonder, where you can witness sea water burst through a tiny crevice in the rocky terrain. With a high tide and a touch of swell, the water reaches impressive heights of up to 20 meters. El Hoyo Soplador is not just a geological wonder; it's a hub of activity. Here, you'll discover charming small rasta cafes, perfect for sipping on local refreshments, and a spacious restaurant where you can savor delectable island cuisine. Prepare to feel the rush as you stand by the hole, poised to capture the moment when the mighty waves force the sea water through, creating a breathtaking natural geyser. Even if you don't get drenched by the sea spray, the sheer force of the air blowing up will leave you in awe. El Hoyo Soplador offers a thrilling encounter with nature that you won't soon forget, making it a memorable stop during your visit to San Andres.

name: Murter
description: Located in Croatia's Sibenik archipelago, Murter island captivates visitors with its natural splendor and rich historical heritage dating back to the 14th century. This compact island hosts four distinct settlements, each offering well-developed tourist infrastructure alongside unique cultural landmarks. The island's namesake capital, Murter town, features ancient settlement ruins and the accessible 120-meter Raduch Mountain, providing panoramic views of the other islands. Beyond Murter's shores lies the uninhabited Kornati archipelago, a protected national reserve accessible through daily excursions. For travelers seeking authentic Croatian experiences, Murter delivers an ideal combination of hiking opportunities, architectural exploration, and immersion in the traditional life of farmers and fishermen.

name: Cilaos
description: Nestled amidst rugged peaks and lush greenery, Cilaos stands as a captivating mountain retreat in Reunion Island. Cilaos is renowned for its breathtaking landscapes, characterized by dramatic cliffs, cascading waterfalls, and verdant valleys. The village is a paradise for outdoor enthusiasts, offering a plethora of hiking trails that wind through stunning terrain, including the iconic Piton des Neiges, the highest peak in the Indian Ocean region. Adventure seekers can embark on exhilarating treks to explore the island's diverse flora and fauna, while adrenaline junkies can indulge in activities like canyoning and paragliding. Beyond its natural wonders, Cilaos boasts a rich cultural heritage that reflects the island's vibrant Creole identity. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local culture by exploring traditional craft workshops, sampling authentic Creole cuisine, and attending lively music and dance performances. One of the highlights of a visit to Cilaos is indulging in the region's famed thermal baths, known for their therapeutic properties and rejuvenating effects. After a day of exploration, travelers can unwind and soak in the warm mineral waters while gazing out at the surrounding mountain vistas.

description: Nestled amidst rugged cliffs, La Piscinita forms a tranquil haven for tropical fish seeking refuge from predators and strong currents. Whether you bring your snorkeling gear or rent it on-site, the underwater world is yours to explore. Don't miss the opportunity to indulge in delectable seafood and potent cocktails at the nearby restaurant, West View. Adventurous souls can even take a thrilling plunge from the diving board. For those yet to invest in snorkeling equipment, San Andrés' tax-free shops offer excellent options. With a nominal $2 USD entrance fee, ample picnic tables, and the dazzling marine life, you're guaranteed an unforgettable aquatic experience. La Piscinita embodies a natural wonder and a watery paradise that will leave you entranced by its crystal-clear depths. Dive in, explore, and make memories that will last a lifetime. Photo by Joao Carlos Medau from Campinas, Brazil, CC BY 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Laguna Quilotoa
description: The view of the caldera from the rim of this ancient volcano is truly spectacular! Mineral deposits give this lake a turquoise hue that almost glows when the sun is shining. Created when the crater collapsed after an almighty eruption 740 years ago, the resulting depression proceeded to fill with water until it reached a depth of 250 metres. Although better visited for it's amazing scenery, there is the chance to see hummingbirds, doves and falcons here. Mountain wolves may also be viewed in the distance. Being a farming region there is always a chance that you'll run into sheep herds accompanied by a llama or two. Hiking to the lake is moderately strenuous, but the good news is that you can be led on horseback if you're not up to the climb. Kayaks can be rented cheaply at the lake when you get there if watersports is your thing.

name: Jerez de la Frontera
description: Starting as a Phoenician colony called Xera about 3,000 years ago, the city was Ceret under Roman rule, and Sheres or Xeres when it became an Arabic fortress. Under Catholic rule, it prospered greatly by trading its famous wines with England. The Muslims left a deep mark on the town, as the medieval Alcázar and the Mosque attest. Within the walled enclosure of the Mosque, visitors can also find the Arab Baths and the Olive Garden, with its cisterns and fountains. The Baroque palace of Villavicencio, built upon the ruins of an Islamic palace, has the city's tallest tower, which allows visitors to view landmarks through a camera obscura. The 15th century Church of Santiago houses works attributed to La Roldana. Visitors can get a closer look at the local culture at the Royal Andalusian School of Equestrian Art, or lunch with tapas and sherry.

name: Hameenlinna
description: Hämeenlinna is the oldest inland city in Finland, having grown around the13th century Häme Castle. Situated on the picturesque shores of Lake Vanajavesi, the castle and surrounding Linnanpuisto castle park make for a pleasant place to soak up the past and take in the stunning scenery. Afterwards, take a stroll through the charming city center, where you can immerse yourself in the culture and learn more about local history at museums like the Finnish Prison Museum, The Artillery Museum of Finland, or the home of composer Jean Sibelius. If the lake views from Häme Castle weren't enough for you, head to the Aulanko Natural Reserve for hiking and other leisure activities.

name: Samaipata
description: Journey through Bolivia's mysterious past in the town of Samaipata. At its heart stands El Fuerte, a UNESCO World Heritage Site shrouded in mystery and intrigue. This ancient archaeological site, carved into the rock face of a towering cliff, boasts intricate carvings and ruins dating back over a thousand years, offering a glimpse into the region's pre-Columbian past. Explore the labyrinthine passages and marvel at the craftsmanship of its ancient inhabitants, whose legacy still echoes through the ages. Delve deeper into the enigma at the El Fuerte museum. Explore fascinating exhibits that showcase artifacts unearthed at the site, and ponder the theories surrounding the carvings' origins. Hike the scenic trails that wind through the surrounding hills, enjoying breathtaking panoramic views of the lush valleys below.

name: Harburg
description: Built in the 11th or 12th century, Harburg Castle is one of the oldest surviving castles in Germany. In 1295, it became the property of the Count of Oettingen, and has remained in the family ever since. Working around its medieval core, additions were made over the centuries, resulting in a large complex with a mix of architectural styles. Visitors can walk the castle complex, admiring the medieval architecture of the guard towers, defensive wall, and sentry walk, or join a guided tour to see the richly decorated interiors, or delve into the dungeon.

name: Ironbridge Gorge
description: In the early 18th century, Abraham Darby pioneered the smelting of iron using coke, a process that was a catalyst for the Industrial Revolution. His grandson, Abraham Darby III, used the same techniques to cast the ironwork for the world's first iron bridge, which still stands today. This structure singlehandedly paved the way for iron's use in bridges, aqueducts, and buildings. The surrounding settlements also prospered during this time thanks to the bounty of raw resources, and the ability to easily ship materials down river. Today, the entire area is considered a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of the influence it had on technology and architecture. Visitors can see the historic bridge before heading into the town proper where history is brought to life through the traditional buildings, early industrial technology, and museums documenting everything from the lives of the Darbys to the towns industrial heritage.

name: Zona Arqueologica Zaachila
description: This centuries old archeological zone sits behind Zaachila's community church and includes two tombs which you can enter and see artifacts from the 14th and 15th century Zapotec people. The tombs were discovered in the 1940s, but were not completely excavated until 1962, as archaeologists were being run off by Zaachilians. Among some of the artifacts found were animal sculptures, figures of mythical creatures, and ceremonial masks. Then in 1971, two more tombs were discovered and excavated, with not much to be found inside, there was paint still left on the walls of the tomb, solidifying the site's importance.

name: Nakhon Pathom
description: With archaeological finds dating back to the 4th century, Nakhon Pathom might just be the oldest city in Thailand. Its main landmark is the 118 meter tall Phra Pathom Chedi - the world's tallest Buddhist monument, allegedly built on the spot that Buddhism was first introduced to Thailand. Within the complex, you'll also find a giant golden Buddha, clear quartzite Buddha, and many smaller temple halls. At Wat Sisathong, dedicated to Phra Rahu, the god of darkness, worshippers come seeking blessings from the deity with eight black offerings. The beautiful 'Thai-Gothic' Sanam Chan Palace, with its fairytale covered bridge, was the summer residence of King Rama VI, and the many outbuildings in the surrounding park make for a picturesque place to unwind. Nakhon Pathom also has a famously authentic floating market behind Wat Lampaya, where you can ride a boat past vendors selling local products and produce, and traditional food like curry fish patties.

name: Gapyeong
description: Gapyeong is nestled in Gyeonggi Province and is graced by the flowing north branch of the Han River, creating a stunning natural environment that looks straight out of a storybook. Among its captivating attractions, Nami Island stands out as the main draw. Shaped like a half-moon, this picturesque island is adorned with metasequoia-lined walking paths, wild peacocks, and even popular movie filming locations. Explore the island's charm by renting bicycles, taking a treetop adventure, and enjoying paddle boating on the river. The island transforms into a cherry blossom paradise during the spring season. A delightful stop near Nami Island is the Gapyeong Rail Park, offering a fun-filled experience for travelers. Riding the rail bikes along the scenic route is a thrilling way to enjoy the surroundings. Stepping into Petite France, be transported to a colorful village reminiscent of France itself. With a fairytale theme and buildings set up as homes for fairytale characters, this unique spot is a favorite among K-drama fans due to its filming locations.

name: Mikulov
description: Often favoured by visitors with a more active approach to life, Mikulov has much to offer. Surrounded by idyllic countryside, crisscrossed by bicycle paths and marked hiking trails, and the nearby Nové Mlýny lakes, there is something for everyone to enjoy. After all that fresh air, a glass of wine will be more than welcome, and fortunately, Mikulov is the centre for Czech wine making. Due to a high concentration of limestone in the local soil, wine from this region has a unique character and distinct taste. If you like your wine with a side-serving of history, Mikulov Castle dates from the 1730s, and the Dietrichstein Tomb is the final resting place of a Bohemian noble family. Mikulov is also significant for its strong Jewish history. In the early 1800s Mikulov's Jewish Quarter was the largest in Moravia with half the town's inhabitants being of Jewish faith.

Selva Gardena is surrounded by the mountains Sella and Sassolungo and is considered one of the most famous and popular villages in the Alps. The village's beautiful natural landscape is the perfect spot for sport enthusiasts. Whether you fancy skiing, hiking, mountain biking, or similar sports, Selva Gardena is sure to provide. Within the village's famous ski resort is a connection of four valleys interconnected by a network of lifts. The resort's many slopes are ideal for skiers of every level. Selva Gardena's lively center has various shops, bars, and restaurants, as well as world-class hotels and quaint B&Bs. Whether searching for sport or recreation, you're sure to find it in lovely Selva di Val Gardena.

name: Mondsee
description: Mondsee's earliest, prehistoric settlers lived above the lake waters in houses built on stilts. These prehistoric pile dwellings have be preserved and recreated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site that gives visitors insight into the culture of ancient man. The beautiful lake and charming town are loved by the people of Salzburg, who often come here on weekend trips. Of the town's historic monuments, the medieval Abbey is probably the only one that's recognizable to people around the world, though you might not know it by name. It was here, in front of the skeleton-filled altar, that Maria and Captain Georg von Trapp, were married in the Oscar-winning Sound of Music.

name: San Miguel de Tucuman
description: San Miguel de Tucumán is the capital of Tucumán, a small but incredibly diverse province in the Argentine North. The city is the commercial center of this agricultural area, aptly nicknamed the Garden of the Republic because of its fertile lands which produce sugarcane, rice, tobacco, and fruit. A stroll through the city's downtown has plenty to offer, in terms of history, architectural marvels, local art, and sports- and as you explore all that San Miguel de Tucumán has to offer, be sure learn why Tucumán is famous for its deli meats and cheeses and grab a sandwich. For a taste of local history, visit Casa de Tucumán (Independence House), where Argentina's independence was declared. This has a museum with free entry on site, which is open every day except Monday. Delight in some architecture and art and visit the House of Government of Tucumán, built in Art Nouveau style at the end of 19th century, or the Timoteo Navarro Museum of Art. Lastly, you won't want to miss the Cathedral of San Miguel de Tucumán, which still preserves some elements of colonial and Italian architecture. This cathedral, which you can enter for free, is open every day but Sunday. Everyone knows Argentinians are mad football fans, but the ones from Tucumán are some of the most passionate ones; if you are a football fan yourself, you might want to watch a match at the Stadium of San Martín de Tucumán.

name: Tekapo
description: The town of Lake Tekapo sits at the very Southern tip of the lake with the same name, but the lake itself is what visitors are really after. The stunning, solid turquoise color of Lake Tekapo is derived from fine rock-flour, giving it an almost milky quality. Go for a dip, or perhaps rent a kayak to experience the view from the center of it all. For those not keen to dip their toes during their stop, there are bike paths, golf courses, and an observatory to entertain. The Earth and Sky observatory is open during the day as an AstroCafe to refresh tourists passing through, but if you want to visit after dark, be sure to make a booking in advance, and see why this entire area is declared a reserve by the International Dark Sky Association. More information at https://www.darkskyproject.co.nz/

name: St. Augustine, FL
description: Established in the 16th century by Spanish conquistadors, St. Augustine is the oldest continuously inhabited colonial settlement in the contiguous United States. Founded on the feast-day of St. Augustine, this city was destined to be the jewel of the New World. Serving as the capital of Spanish Florida for over two centuries, it was finally conceded to the United States, with a short stint as Florida's state capital. Visit the Castillo de San Marcos, the oldest masonry fort in the United States, built by Spanish engineers. Explore the heyday of the city by strolling through the Colonial Quarter. With countless shops, restaurants, and even a watchtower, you can enjoy contemporary comforts while seeing history come alive.

name: Berchtesgaden
description: Surrounded by soaring peaks, vast parks, and Germany's deepest lake, this alpine village is undeniably beautiful. When the region was annexed by Bavaria in the early 19th century, Berchtesgadener became instantly popular with the royal family. The castle is an architectural timeline, where rather than renovating, multiple extensions were added in the style of the day. Today, Duke Franz of Bavaria uses the castle as summer residence. Hitler had been vacationing in Berchtesgadener since the 1920s, and was so smitten with the area that he purchased a home overlooking the village, and received the nearby Eagle's Nest as a birthday present. Walking the town's narrow, winding streets, lined with pastel houses, is an experience in itself, but in a region famous for its salt deposits since the 12th century, the Salt Mine Tour, with its unique underground slide, should be on every adventurer's to-do-list.

name: Bucharest
description: First mentioned in 1459, Bucharest gained notoriety as the home of Vlad the Impaler. In the following centuries, the city experienced periods of both development and decline, which has left it with a distinctive blends of gorgeous historic buildings and not-so-gorgeous Communist-era constructions. Most notable is the Palace of Parliament, a Communist dictator's megalomanic monument, and the world's second largest administrative building after the Pentagon. With a volume of 2,550,000 cubic metres, and weighing in at 4,098,500,000 kilograms, it's also the world's heaviest building, and the most expensive, using the same amount of power as a small city even though 70% of the building is empty. In the Old Town, you can admire the beautiful Art Nouveau buildings that had earned Bucharest the nickname 'The Paris of the East', 17th- and 18th-century Orthodox churches, and even the remains of Vlad the Impaler's 15th century citadel.

name: Tainan
description: Tainan's illustrious past, bustling sidewalks, and modern transformation has earned it the endearing nickname "the Phoenix City." As the birthplace of Taiwan's cultural roots, Tainan holds a pivotal place in the island's history. In 1661, Cheng Cheng-kung, a Ming loyalist, ousted the Dutch and established his rule in Tainan. This marked the influx of Chinese immigrants to the burgeoning city, shaping its cultural tapestry. Tainan's cultural richness extends to its local street food and traditional cuisine, as well as preserved Taoist rites and living local customs spanning life's milestones, from birth to funerals. Beyond its cultural allure, Tainan's natural beauty shines through. The Taiwan International Orchid Show in Houbi Township showcases early spring's exquisite orchids. The Yanshui Beehive Fireworks Festival, held on the 15th day of the first lunar month, draws visitors worldwide. The West Central district in Tainan bustles with shops, restaurants, and historic sites. It's a city where exploration leads to delightful surprises, with sidewalks transforming into temples or bustling markets.

description: Take a dip, a dive, or a swim at the bottom of the 35 meter-tall Misol-Ha Waterfalls! The single cascade of water streams into a pool where you can relax and bathe in the sun. You can even venture beyond the cascade and discover the small cave behind the waterfall, it's only 20 m in length, but a fun way to explore the rock and tropical vegetation around the falls and pool, away from large crowds!

address.addr1: Basilica of Our Lady of Zapopan
address.city: Basilica of Our Lady of Zapopan
description: Just skirting the West border of Guadalajara lies Zapopan, and within Zapopan, its Basilica - a 17th century stone structure with an impressive following among the local population. It is not the Basilica itself which draws people, however, but its contents. After all, the abbey is home to the "Virgin of Zapopan," a beloved figure of the blessed virgin crafted in the 1500s by indigenous peoples. She is considered the people's patroness against storms, lightening, and epidemics, and numerous miracles are ascribed to her power. From June to October, she lives in the cathedral in nearby Guadalajara, until October, when a parade of up to 1,000,000 locals and visitors shepherd her back to her home in Zapopan. That said, she is a sight to behold any time of year!

name: Porto
description: Dating back as far as 300 BC, this ancient port city is steeped in history and tradition. The city was built along the hills overlooking the Douro river, providing breathtaking vistas over the colourful buildings and narrow cobbled streets. Porto is known worldwide for it eponymous wine, but it's the UNESCO-listed historic center that's truly intoxicating. Start down at the lively riverside Cais da Ribeira for a real taste of the city before setting out to discover the many monuments that dot its picturesque streets. Most put a heavy emphasis on the ornaty, like the lavishly furnished Palácio da Bolsa, and gilt-filled Church of São Francisco. Even Porto's book shops, like Livraria Lello, are jaw-droppingly beautiful. Of course, in the home of port, you'd be remiss to miss sampling the iconic wine.

name: Osaka
description: Renowned for its bustling nightlife, thriving business districts, and mouthwatering street food, Osaka offers an unforgettable experience. Begin your journey in Kita, also known as Umeda, the pulsating epicenter of the city's daytime activities. Explore its myriad of restaurants and shops, absorbing the vibrant atmosphere that characterizes Osaka's dynamic rhythm. Umeda Sky Building awaits, inviting you to take in breathtaking panoramic vistas from its Floating Garden Observatory. Another treasure is the historic Osaka Castle, echoing tales of the past. Its vast grounds, adorned with cherry blossoms in spring, create a mesmerizing scene. Delve into the heart of Osaka's gastronomic culture with the beloved takoyaki, a delectable street snack originating here. These octopus-filled spheres, cooked to perfection in a special pan, are a true culinary delight. As you wander through the city's lively street markets, you'll find these savory treats everywhere, making for an affordable and delicious indulgence. This city captivates with its seamless blend of old and new, crafting an experience that resonates long after your journey concludes.

name: Cusco
description: In the 13th century, Cusco became the capital and center of the Incan Empire, it lasted 3 centuries until the Spanish began conquering South America. The Spanish sought to remove all evidence of the indigenous culture, using the huge slabs of Incan stone to construct many of their buildings, but remnants of the Incan Empire are found in some original structures, such as Korikancha (Sun Temple), and museums like the Inca Museum. Another impressive archaeological site is Sacsayhuaman (pronounced 'sexy woman') where you can see stunning stonework thought to be a precursor to Machu Picchu. For something truly authentic, check out the San Blas district where you will find all of the artisans and unique architecture. The Plaza del Armas, the main town square with a lovely garden, is surrounded by coffee shops, restaurants, and bars - perfect for acclimating to the city's altitude.

name: Sighisoara
description: Founded as a Dacian stronghold in the 1st century AD, the Transylvanian Saxons built a new citadel in the 12th century, which still stands today. The historic center was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site, rivaling the beauty of Prague or Vienna with its cobbled streets lined with pastel houses, ornate churches and perfectly preserved defensive towers. In the 14th and 15th centuries, the town's craft guilds each built, manned and maintained these defensive towers. Perhaps the most striking is the Clock Tower, with its multi-colored roof, which once controlled the town's main gate. Famously, Vlad the Impaler was born here, and today his house is a campy throwback for vampire hunters. For authentic history, the Church on the Hill houses 500-year-old frescoes, while the woodwork in the Church of the Dominican Monastery is particularly stunning. However, for many, the best way to experience the town is to simply explore its picturesque streets.

name: Flagstaff, AZ
description: Famed since its inception in the 19th century, Flagstaff has cemented itself as a premier holiday destination for nature lovers. Surrounded by the Coconino National Forest, Grand Canyon, Oak Creek Canyon, San Francisco Peaks, Sunset Crater and Wupatki National Park, there's no shortage of scenic sights. Along with maintaining a bit of its rugged feel, Flagstaff played a major role in 20th century science. Pluto was actually discovered from Flagstaff in 1930, and the US Naval Observatory was used to plot the Moon landing sites for the Apollo missions. In the city itself, there is no shortage of places to go either! The city's downtown is preserved so nicely and still populated by small family businesses, adding to its charm!

name: Zaragoza
description: First settled by the ancient Iberians, Augustus conquered the area and founded a city for his veterans from the Cantabrian wars. Unlike many other Roman cities, it didn't decline with the empire, and power was peacefully transferred to the Goths in the 5th century. Beginning in the 12th century, the city's unique political, social and cultural status led to the development of the Islamic influenced "Mudejar" art. For the next 500 years, the refined and inventive use of brick and glazed tiles would permeate the city's architecture. The Cathedral of San Salvador, built over a mosque, is one of the finest examples, with its 12th century Romanesque apses decorated with Mudejar tiles. Inside, along with the historic decors is the Museum of Tapestries, which exhibits needlework from as far back as the 15th century. The Aljafería Palace, often called a 'mini-Alhambra', is also UNESCO-protected for its original Mudejar decorations.

name: Hill of Crosses
description: While the exact origins of the Hill of Crosses are unknown, it's believed the tradition began after the 1831 uprising when families couldn't find the bodies of their fallen loved ones. When Latvia was under Soviet control between 1944 and 1990, the hill was bulldozed on 3 occasions to clear away the religious symbols, and even put under guard to try to keep locals away, all to no avail. Today, the hilltop, which is estimated to have 200,000 crosses on it, stands as a monument to Latvia's national spirit, and was even named a place for hope, peace, love, and sacrifice by Pope John Paul II.

name: La Pesca
description: The breathtaking natural environment of Playa la Pesca will indulge you with a variety of recreational activities, such as relaxing in palapas, renting boats, and shopping for fishing gear. Nearby, rustic-style restaurants serve delectable dishes prepared with fresh shellfish. Visit during Holy Week for a range of activities such as sports events, contests, and musical concerts. La Pesca provides a tranquil setting for a "lunada", where friends and family can gather to enjoy delicious snacks in the palapas scattered along the beach. The Laguna Madre stretches approximately 230 kilometers, creating a spectacular backdrop for Playa La Pesca. This coastal oasis is a natural refuge for various aquatic bird species, and it's also fed by the Soto La Marina and Conchos rivers. Sea turtles come to the shores of La Pesca from April through to May and June to lay their eggs. Witness wildlife at its finest on the stunning expanse of Playa la Pesca.

name: Villa El Chocon
description: Villa El Chocón, also known as the "Valley of the Dinosaurs," boasts a rich heritage of fossil remains, tracks, and even a petrified forest. Step into the Ernesto Bachmann Museum, where each room unveils a captivating journey into the lives of dinosaurs through detailed bone replicas and scientific insights. The largest carnivorous dinosaur, Giganotosaurus carolinii, takes center stage, its skeletal majesty sprawled across the sandy floor, sharing the tale of its discovery just kilometers away. Embark on the "Paleontologists for a Day" program, where children become explorers unearthing hidden bones in a sand deposit, learning the essentials of paleontology. The museum's director, Rocío Butin, emphasizes the importance of studying fossil sites in their natural context. Throughout the town itself, the red sandstone ground and the Ezequiel Ramos Mejía dam's banks preserve these treasures, making it an avant-garde information source. Immerse yourself in the energy of Villa El Chocón, where the echoes of the past resound through fossils, a testament to the town's fascinating prehistoric legacy.

name: Nazare
description: For much of its history, Nazaré was a tiny fishing village perched atop a cliff to protect its inhabitants from raids by everyone from the Vikings to Dutch pirates. In the 19th century, it finally expanded to its famed beachfront, which is now a popular weekend and holiday destination. But step back from the bright-colored umbrellas, and you'll find a network of cobbled streets lined with pleasant colored houses, and maybe a traditionally-dressed fisherman roasting his latest catch. A modern funicular brings visitors up to the old town (Sítio) where you'll find historic churches, such as the Shrine to Our Lady of Nazaré, where the town's namesake Byzantine Black Madonna is enshrined. Venture from the picturesque town center to the lighthouse point for stupendous views of the coast. If you're visiting in winter, you may catch Nazaré's infamous 100-foot-high waves, and maybe see the brave surfers trying to tackle them.

name: Hersheypark
description: If you're looking for a sweet experience, look no further than Hersheypark, brought to you by the one and only Hershey's! Started as a leisure park for the chocolate factory staff back in 1903, it was soon opened to the public, hosting festivities such as sporting events and musical performances. Over the decades, rides were added and in 1923 the park's first roller coaster, the Wild Cat, was erected. Today, over 70 rides are on offer, ranging from thrill-seeker favorites like the Candymonium and Fahrenheit, to family-friendly options like the ferris wheel, swinging pirate ship and the tea cups. There's a water park, plenty of shops and dining options, and right next door there's Hershey's Chocolate World. Take a tour, build your own bar, and have a chocolatey good time!

name: Miradores del Canon del Sumidero
description: The Miradores del Canon del Sumidero overlook a deep canyon formed millions over years ago through a combination of erosion and tectonic activity. At 1 to 2 kilometers across, and up to 1000 meters deep, the Canon del Sumidero is Mexico's "other" grand canyon. Overlooking the canyon are viewpoints that showcase its natural beauty from varying altitudes. The first is the La Ceiba viewpoint, from which you can see the city of Chiapa de Corzo and where the walls of the Sumidero Canyon begin to take shape. The El Tepehuaje viewpoint overlooks the picturesque bend in the river Grijalva amidst the dense jungle. The Los Chiapa Viewpoint is at the canyon's highest point, and according to legend, is where locals threw themselves to their deaths rather than be subjected by the Spanish.

name: Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary
description: The Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary is a site not to be missed during your Uganda stay. As home to the only wild white rhinos in the country it offers a unique experience to trek through the bush and see these endangered creatures in their natural habitat. With over 7,000 hectares for the rhinos to roam, the sanctuary proudly offers a secure space protected from predators, where it is hoped the population will expand over time through breeding. As well as rhinos you can expect to see storks, waterbucks and over 300 species of bird, which can be admired on one of the available tours. If you're visiting the Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary, be sure to wear closed shoes and long pants - and mosquito repellent is a must! It is recommended that you pre-book to ensure your visit can be accommodated. Make sure to adjust the duration according to the tour you plan to take! Please find more information here http://www.ziwarhino.com/

name: Palenque Gracias a Dios
description: The Palenque Gracias a Dios started with a small mezcalería in Querétaro, México in 2010. The team met mezcalero Oscar Hernández while on a 2-year search for the best mezcal in Mexico, and were so impressed with his liquor that they made him a partner and opened their own distillery. At Gracias a Dios, the artisanal mezcal is ground and fermented, and distilled in copper. Piñas from Espadín agave and other varieties are crushed the old-fashioned way - by horse-drawn tahona (though the Karwinskii agaves have to be mechanically pre-shredded due to their toughness). On a guided tour of the palenque, you'll learn the ins and outs of mezcal making, and get plenty of tastings to see the differences for yourself. Reservations must be made in advance at https://www.thankgad.com/en/tours-airbnb (be sure to select the tour at Palenque Gracias a Dios).

name: Al-Kharj
description: Only 60 miles away from Riyadh, Al-Kharj is not exactly a tourist hotspot, but more of a window into the lives of ordinary Saudis. The trademark of the city is Ayun AlSeih, meaning Eyes of Al-Seeh – two deep holes in the ground located in close proximity to each other, allegedly formed by meteor showers thousands of years ago. Additionally, the city is home to Al-Kharj Park Zoo, a compact zoo featuring wild animals such as lions, tigers, leopards, bears, and monkeys. The city's Water Tower is another recognizable structure, dramatically lit up at night. Families may also enjoy a visit to Al-Baijan Amusement Park, a spot your children would love to explore. If you're in the mood for shopping, head straight to Jaw Mall or Hodaithi Mall, or take a leisurely stroll in King Salman Walkway.

name: Braganca
description: Bragança stands proudly on a plateau only a few kilometres away from the Spanish border. The walls and castle date from the 12th century and boast a 33 metre keep and various watchtowers. Situated on a hill overlooking the city center, the well-preserved Cidadela was built in the 12th century by Benedictine monks. The city's religious roots and rich history are exemplified in the Church of Santa Maria, a seemingly humble white church, but inside, painted wooden ceiling is as beautiful as any fresco. Unexploited by tourism, this remote, mountainous city offers beautiful scenery, historic architecture, and rich local cuisine. Bragança lies on the edge of the Montesinho Natural Park – one of the wildest forested areas in Europe, with a great diversity of flora and fauna.

name: Hoi An
description: Hoi An was founded as early as the 7th century by the Cham. Situated at the estuary of the Thu Bồn River, Hoi An grew into a nationally important trading center, attracting Chinese, Portuguese, Japanese, Dutch, and Indian merchants from the 15th to 19th centuries. After Vietnam's trade center was moved to Da Nang, Hoi An was forgotten, leaving it with an exceptionally well-preserved Old Town that's been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999. Here you can see Chinese temples alongside the tombs of Japanese traders in this golden-yellow neighborhood. This cultural-blending is embodied in the 17th-century Tan Ky House, which was built by a Vietnamese family, but with Japanese and Chinese influences. The symbol of the city, however, is the 16th century Japanese covered bridge. You can also visit one of the city's museums to learn more about its rich history, stretching back 2000 years to when the area was first settled.

name: Hallstatt
description: Hallstatt's allure is plain to see: a picture-perfect town on an alpine lake surrounded by mountains. Walk the streets past the centuries-old buildings, and simply take in the amazing views. The charming town is so popular that an exact replica was built in Huizo, China as a tourist attraction. Towering over the picturesque town is the oldest salt mine in the world - the Salzberg (Salt Mountain), where you can explore tunnels dug by hand over 3000 years ago. If you've never been to a salt mine, then this is the place to do it. Head to the top of the mountain on foot or by funicular to the spectacular viewing platform that hovers above the rooftops of the town below and offers eye-popping panoramic views of Lake Hallstatt and the mountain scenery. Listen to the gentle lapping of the lake before launching yourself down one of the two 200-foot slides in the mine. Then sit back and relax on the train that takes you out of the mountain at a gentler pace. We recommend adding an extra 2 hours to your visit if you'd like to venture into the mines. For those looking to delve underground again, the Dachstein Ice Caves overlooking the lake are a breathtaking natural phenomenon. Be sure to wear warm clothing and add another 2 hours to your stop.

description: After word got out about the rugged beauty of the Torres del Paine National Park, Puerto Natales transformed from a sleepy fishing village on the shores of Última Esperanza Sound to a mecca for Patagonian adventure. There's craft breweries and even a sushi restaurant alongside local eateries roasting whole lamb over open coals. The main activity for visitors and locals alike is just walking the waterfront, with its views of glacier-capped mountains beyond the bay, to appreciate the region's natural beauty. If you're lucky, you'll see a flock of flamingos wading in the shallows. And if they're not around, you can still get an extra splash of color at the boatyard. If you have any interest in the region's past, be sure to visit the Puerto Natales Historical Museum to learn about Patagonia's indigenous peoples. It's succinct, informative, and only $2!

name: Ingolstadt
description: Located on the banks of the Danube River, the fortified city of Ingolstadt presents visitors with an exciting mix of past and present. Mary Shelley chose Ingolstadt as the setting for her novel Frankenstein and the Frankenstein themed tour of the Old Town is always popular with tourists. In contrast, this innovation guided city is home to the Audi Forum Ingolstadt, which is visited by over 500,000 people each year. The Audi manufacturing plant has factory tours available while the Audi Museum is a must-see for car enthusiasts, where a vast range of modern, classic, and vintage automobiles are on display. Both visitor experiences offer the best of German technology, design and innovation. If that's not your cup of tea, then Ingolstadt provides the perfect opportunity to indulge in some retail therapy with its small, sophisticated privately-owned shops and boutiques set in the bustling and lively Old Town.

name: Beaune
description: Founded as a Roman fort around the 1st century AD and had become a prosperous wine-growing region by the Middle Ages. Today, the village is still surrounded by old ramparts, guarding its beautiful old town. Among the many beautiful Renaissance mansions and half-timbered, the Hôtel-Dieu stands out. With its brightly patterned roof tiles this former charity hospital is now a 15th-century gem of Burgundian architecture. Today, along with a medical museum, visitors can marvel at the magnificent ceremonial courtyard, the Gothic chapel, and stupendous 15th century polyptych of the Last Judgement. Every November they host the world's largest wine auction. Speaking of wine, the 14th century palace that once belonged to the Dukes of Burgundy now houses the Museum of Burgundy Wine, where ethnographic and artistic exhibits tell the history of the vineyard and winemaking.

name: Venlo
description: Venlo has been an important trading center since the Middle Ages, joining the Hanseatic League in 1375. Recently, the city was named the "Greenest city of Europe", and won the prestigious 'Best City Centre of the Netherlands'. For visitors, this means a scenic, monument rich experience awaits. At the heart of the car-free historic center stands the Northern Renaissance-style city hall, overlooking a lively square lined with shops and cafes. The red-brick Gothic St. Martinus church was damaged during World War II, requiring extensive renovations. The building's facade has maintained its historic appearance, while the sleek interior is punctuated by a gorgeous, giant gilded triptych behind the altar. The Limburgs Museum is a wonderful multimedia experience with a delightful collection of paintings and movies. The 'historoscope' is particularly fascinating, condensing 150,000 years of history into 25 minutes.
