name: Toulon
description: With its rocky limestone shore dotted with ancient fortifications, Toulon boasts a unique character. The old town, much of which has seen extensive restoration works throughout the years, is one of the city's most interesting areas with its narrow streets, local shops, and numerous public squares. The city is also home to the 18th century Church of Saint Louis, with a classical style facade, three naves, and double Doric columns; the 11th-century Cathedral of Saint Marie, enlarged in the 17th century; and the vast Military Port of Toulon dating back to the time of Henry IV and inaugurated in 1680. As an important centre for naval construction, fishing, wine making, and the manufacture of a wide range of items from aeronautical equipment to paper and tobacco, Toulon is sure to have something for everyone.

name: Beauvais
description: Beauvais was the capital of the mighty pre-Roman Bellovaci tribe, and remained a prominent city through much of the Middle Ages. Much of the town was destroyed during WWI, and again during WWII, but there are still some striking historical monuments. First and foremost is the Gothic Cathedral of Saint Pierre. Despite a slew of architectural setbacks, including the collapse of the spire that made it the tallest building in the world for 5 years, the building is an impressive example of High Gothic architecture with colorful 16th century stained glass windows and a nifty astronomical clock. There are a slew of other historical buildings nearby, such as the 'maladrerie' complex where monks cared for the sick, and the former Episcopal Palace. A beautiful Renaissance building accessed by a fortified bridge, it's now the departmental museum and worth a visit even if you're not interested in seeing art and artefacts dating back to the 1st century.

name: Capalbio
description: Dating back to at least the 9th century, Capalbio is sometimes called "Little Athens" because of its environment and its Renaissance glory days. Today, visitors can enter the town through the 15th century Sienese Gate, which amazingly still has its original wooden doors, and then scale the town walls for spectacular views of the town, countryside, and Tyrrhenian Sea. In the historic center is dominated by the Aldobrandeschi Fortress, which still looks lived in, with its period furnishings and faded frescoes. The nearby Romanesque Church of San Nicola is filled with striking frescoes from the Middle Ages and Renaissance. In nearby Pescia Fiorentina is the unusual Tarot Garden, which is filled with sculptures, covered with mirrors and mosaics, depicting the 22 tarot figures.

name: Surat Thani
description: While most travellers just use Surat Thani as a gateway to the popular islands of Ko Samui, Ko Pha-Ngan, and Ko Tao, the city was once the seat of the ancient Srivijaya empire, and the last bit of 'real Thailand' in the area. The Ban Don district could be considered the city's Chinatown, with century-old Sino-European architecture and traditional shops and temples that make it worth exploring. In the heart of the city, the large Wat Tham Bucha and Srivijaya-style City Pillar Shrine are visited daily by locals, making them a great place to join to admire some fine architecture and glimpse the city's daily life, while a nearby bridge leads to an island park. The nearby Tapi riverfront is also worth a visit - from here you can take a longtail boat trip into the Tapi's tributaries, through tunnels of towering palms and past old stilted houses.

description: Parque Nacional Manglares de Old Point offers an invigorating journey through the cool shade of lush foliage in Nogales, boasting various types of mangroves. It's a sanctuary for wildlife, with a scenic estuary graced by diverse creatures. Here, you'll also discover tranq uil lagoons and dry forests, creating an environment distinct from the rest of the island. It's an ideal setting for birdwatching, as the park is home to an array of avian species. Watch for graceful butterflies and curious crabs that call this paradise home. The mangrove trees, with their exposed roots submerged in the water, lend an otherworldly atmosphere to your stroll. Parque Nacional Manglares de Old Point is a must-visit destination for nature enthusiasts seeking an escape to a unique and captivating environment.

name: Siem Reap
description: Siem Reap was little more than a village in the 19th century, but as soon as the nearby Angkor temples were reclaimed from the forest, it became a tourist destination. Today, Siem Reap is one of Cambodia's most cosmopolitan cities with mouth-watering options for foodies, and a vibrant cultural scene, including Phare - Cambodia's answer to Cirque du Soleil. However, the main draw is undoubtedly the nearby temples of Angkor. Most famous is Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious complex the UNESCO-listed pinnacle of the ancient Khmer empire. The complex's architecture is so ornately detailed that each of the 3000 heavenly nymphs carved in its walls is unique, and sports one of 37 different hairstyles. Around 2 kilometers away is Angkor Thom, the last and most lasting Khmer capital, which is filled with stupendous temples and intricate carvings of its own. For something a little different, Ta Prohm is still covered with trees, just as when it was discovered in the early 19th century.

description: Nestled amidst captivating rock formations and a vast lagoon, Boca de Tunel Adventure Park offers a thrilling experience with its 13 suspension bridges—the longest spanning an impressive 105 meters at a height of 15 meters. Zip lines, via ferrata, horseback riding, and an 11-kilometer bike trail are just some of the exhilarating activities that await. Glide through the air or challenge yourself with rock climbing on the walls of the Juan Caporal ravine, boasting heights exceeding one hundred meters. The Potrerillos Dam serves as a remarkable backdrop for rappelling enthusiasts. Suspended on secure steel ropes above a picturesque gorge with a tranquil lake below, the aerial course provides a rush of adrenaline while ensuring utmost safety. Equipped with safety harnesses and helmets, you'll be guided by knowledgeable instructors who ensure a supportive environment. Conclude the adventure by descending to the water's edge, where a boat awaits to transport you back to the starting point of the canyon.

description: At the heart of Paultons Park lies Peppa Pig World, a magical land where the beloved characters from the popular children's show come to life. Young fans will be thrilled to explore Peppa's house, ride in Daddy Pig's car, and sail along with Grandpa Pig in his boat. The colorful, interactive attractions ensure smiles and laughter as children immerse themselves in Peppa's world. Beyond Peppa Pig World, Paultons Park boasts over 70 rides and attractions set in beautifully landscaped gardens. Adrenaline seekers can enjoy the exhilarating roller coasters, while little ones can delight in gentle rides and play areas. The Lost Kingdom, a prehistoric-themed zone, invites guests to embark on a dinosaur adventure with animatronic creatures and exciting rides like the Velociraptor and the Flight of the Pterosaur. Nature lovers will appreciate the park's stunning gardens, complete with vibrant flowers and tranquil water features. name: Gibara
description: Gibara was founded in 1817 when the first stones were laid for the San Fernando Fort, the white walls of which gave the town its nickname "La Villa Blanca". Despite being a key historic port, Gibara still hasn't made it onto most tourist's radar. The double devastation from hurricanes Ike and Sandy left the town in tatters, but there's still a rustic charm to this colonial fishing village. Start your visit in the pleasant Parque Calixto García, where you'll find a number of brightly colored colonial buildings. At one end is a charming 19th century church, and nearby the wonderful Museo de Historia Natural, which has a whale skeleton on display. From here, follow the streets uphill to the fort for a fantastic view. While Gibara is mostly unknown to tourists, it is known amongst film fans for hosting Latin America's coolest indie film festival - the Festival Internacional del Cine Pobre (festival of low-budget cinema) every Spring.

name: Terezin
description: Originally built by the Emperor Joseph II and named in honour of his mother Maria Theresa, the Theresienstadt garrison town was commandeered by the Nazis from 1940 as a Gestapo prison and ghetto/camp for Czech Jews. Although it was not an extermination camp 35,000 people died in the camp through malnutrition, overcrowding, and brutality, while 88,000 were deported to Auschwitz. Today Terezin is a huge living monument-complex to those who died in horrific circumstances, providing a detailed insight into their incarceration, and is an invaluable, though highly dignified, educational tool. The cramped dimensions of isolation cells can be experienced inside the 'Small Fortress' along with the similarly minimal 'Common Rooms' for women prisoners. Inside the walls of the 'Large Fortress' one can walk down the streets of the ghetto, and later perhaps pay one's respects to the people who suffered here in the Jewish and Christian cemeteries.

name: Angangueo
description: Angagueo is everything you want from a small Mexican town. Nature, red-tiled roofs, majestic churches and quaint plazas. Once one of the most important mining towns in Mexico, the success is reflected in the layout of the town, which remains unchanged since colonialism, and the two churches; the parish of San Simon and the Inmaculada Concepcion. Revel at the majesty of the churches, because the Inmaculada Concepcion was built by a single family in the style of the Notre Dame in Paris, France. Walk inside and admire the marble altar imported from Italy. Visit Angangueo in February, as you will experience a once-in-a-lifetime experience -- the Monarch Butterfly Festival. There are two butterfly sanctuaries situated just outside of the town, and every year, the monarch butterflies fly in grandiose unison to travel north.

name: Newgrange
description: Built around 3200 BC, Newgrange is a monumental tomb that predates both Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids. At 85 metres wide and 12 meters tall, the tomb blended in with the landscape for centuries, only being discovered in 1699 when a local farmer began quarrying the mound. Originally believed to be an exceptionally large passage tomb, archaeologists now believe it had a religious significance, either for a cult of the dead, or astronomical religion. Scientists have calculated that when the structure was built, the entire inner chamber would be illuminated exactly at sunrise on the Summer Solstice. At the Brú na Bóinne Visitor Centre, you'll find a full-scale replica of the Newgrange Chamber, as well as an audio-visual presentation and interactive exhibits to delve into the history of the site. The tomb itself is only accessible on a guided tour, which should be booked in advance. If you'd like to visit the nearby tombs of Knowth and Dowth, we'd recommend adding an extra hour to your stop. Please book your tickets in advance at https://brunaboinne.admit-one.eu/

name: Bassano Del Grappa
address.addr1: 36061 Bassano del Grappa, Province of Vicenza, Italy
description: Founded in the 2nd century BC, Bassano Del Grappa enjoyed a privileged autonomy despite being ruled by the region's various powers before the unification of Italy. The town's historic buildings, nestled on the banks of a river, with a dramatic mountain backdrop attracted the likes of Napoleon Bonaparte, and writers including Ernest Hemingway and Scott Fitzgerald. Today, the symbol of Bassano Del Grappa is the distinctive Renaissance wooden pontoon bridge. Destroyed countless times over the centuries, its always been rebuilt according to Andrea Palladio's 16tyh century designs, and is revered by Alpine soldiers, who took up a private collection to rebuild the bridge after World War II. On the bridge you can also experience another alpine favorite - grappa from Nardini Distillery. Afterward, explore the pleasant cobbled streets, where you'll be rewarded with pleasant squares lined with Renaissance Palaces and medieval churches.

name: Groningen
description: First mentioned in the 11th century, Groningen's was a major trading center during the Middle Ages, which created an explosion of stately buildings. Unfortunately, a major battle during World War II saw many of these historic landmarks destroyed. Though it's the largest city in the Northern Netherlands, Groningen is surprisingly free of traffic thanks to the city encouraging and investing in cycling since the 1970s. The main square, usually abuzz with students, is the best place to see the gems of Groningen's golden age. From the top of the Gothic Martinitoren bell tower, visitors are treated to panoramic views of the city. The richly decorated 17th century Goudkantoor was originally a collections office, but is now a restaurant allowing visitors to enjoy the square's charm. Of the city's many museums, the Groninger Museum, where modern art meets modern architecture, is the most colorful way to spend the day.

name: Sigtuna
description: It's a small town in Sweden, but Sigtuna is one of the country's oldest and most charming, founded in 980 AD. Located on the shores of Lake Mälaren, the town has a rich history with its roots dating back to the viking age. Its prime attraction is Stora Garan, the main street that's persisted since the Middle Ages. Pastel-painted wooden-framed buildings line the streets, with cafes and shops dotting the area. Over 20 runestones are located at the heart of Sigtuna, some of them being over 1000 years old. Retrieve a map from Sigtuna's Tourism Office to trace the location of the runestone that have been carved into bones, wood, metal and horn. Stop at Sigtuna's Museum to learn of the city's fascinating history and visit the city hall, which holds the record for being the smallest one in all of Sweden. This quaint town with capture your heart and imagination with its medieval touches.

name: Yangmingshan National Park
description: Yangmingshan National Park, part of Taipei's latest volcanic and hot spring complex, boasts year-round flower displays, picturesque meadows, and endless outdoor experiences. Xiaoyoukeng, an otherworldly post-volcanic geological site nestled in the park, offers visitors a glimpse into the earth's fiery past, featuring fumaroles, sulfur crystals, and hot springs all set amidst dramatic 'landslide terrain' shaped by volcanic activity. Hiking enthusiasts can embark on the trail leading to Seven Star Mountain from the Xiaoyoukeng parking lot. The summit, Taipei City's highest peak, offers panoramic views. With over 1,000 species of peach blossoms, 800 varieties of azaleas throughout the park, vibrant cherry blossoms, rhododendrons, and lilies, Yangmingshan National Park is a haven for nature lovers, who will be treated to a refreshing natural environment.

address.addr1: Kronplatz, 39030 Mareo, Province of Bolzano - South Tyrol, Italy
description: Nestled on the slopes of the mighty Kronplatz, Brunico is steeped in alpine culture. In winter, visitors flock to the best and most modern ski resort in the region. But with 800 years of history, there's a lot more to Brunico than skiing and snowboarding. On the Kronplatz summit, you'll also find the Messner Mountain Museum Corones. Designed by the late Zaha Hadid, the museum offers a glimpse into the lives of mountaineers and unparalleled views of the South Tyrolean mountains. Then, just above the town, the medieval Schloss Bruneck castle houses the Messner Mountain Museum RIPA, dedicated to mountain cultures from around the world. In the Old Town below, the streets are lined with historic houses, and punctuated by charming churches. Throughout the year, Brunico hosts numerous markets, including the Stegener Market at the end of October, which is the largest market in Tyrol. If you prefer something more pastoral, pay a visit to the South Tyrolean Folklore Museum to experience a slice of tradtional rural life.

name: Forde Abbey and Gardens
description: Founded in the 12th century, Forde Abbey was one of the finest institutions in England by the time monasteries were dissolved in 1539 and the abbey became a private property. In 1650, the abbey became a private residence, and over the following centuries, was renovated, restored, and modified into the part-Gothic, part-Jacobean estate seen today. Undoubtedly, the highlight of the abbey's interior is the saloon, whis is adorned with the world-famous Mortlake Tapestries. Depicting five of Raphael's seven cartoons, the tapestries have hung in the home for the past 300 years. Outside, the abbey's award-winning gardens have slowly evolved over the past 900 years, from the kitchen garden, to topiaries, an arboretum, bog garden, and the country's highest powered fountain. For more information, please visit fordeabbey.co.uk

name: Arundel Castle and Gardens
description: Established in the 11th century by one of William the Conqueror's most loyal barons, Arundel Castle has been the family home of the Dukes of Norfolk for nearly 1000 years. In the 18th century, the medieval castle was almost entirely rebuilt into a Victorian Gothic mansion, though original elements like the Norman keep. In 1846, Queen Victoria and Prince Albert visited the castle for 3 days, a special occasion for which new furniture and even a portrait of the Queen were commissioned, and now on display in one of the castle's bedrooms. Undoubtedly one of England's grandest country houses, a tour of the castle's lavish interior showcases the historic artefacts, period furnishings, and amazing art collection accrued by one of England's most prominent noble families. The stupendous gardens surrounding the castle showcase a variety of flora, with each section meticulously managed and manicured. Please note: the castle is closed on Mondays. For more information, please visit https://arundelcastle.org/

name: Riva del Garda
address.addr1: Riva del Garda, Province of Trento, Italy
description: Riva del Garda is surrounded by stunning valleys, hills, and lakes. It features a harbor, park, and a long beach. The historic center, Citta Vecchia, is protected by the Rocca, an elegant 12th century fortress. Within the fortress itself lies a civic library and museum to be discovered. Another notable sight is Torre Apponale, a 13th century clock tower. Climb the stairs to the top of the tower for a splendid view of town. Riva del Garda has many restaurants, cafes, bars, and a large shopping area. It's also one of the top spots in Europe for water sports. Whether you're seeking scenery, shopping, or sports, Riva del Garda has something for everyone.

name: Morelia
description: Founded in the 16th century, Morelia flourished thanks in large part to the the construction of its aqueduct, which supplied the growing population with fresh water, and the elegant cathedral, which cemented the city as the province's religious center. Stretching for two city blocks, the baroque structure is widely considered the most beautiful in the country, and is said to be the only cathedral in Mexico not oriented to the east. Stretching out from the cathedral is a checkerboard of streets first laid out in the 16th century that are dotted with beautiful baroque buildings and historic houses. Chief among these are the two former homes of Jose Maria Morelos y Pavon, which have both been transformed into museums honoring the hero of the Mexican War for Independence. The city's rich heritage serves as the perfect backdrop for the many public concerts, art installations, and one of the country's most prestigious film festivals.

description: Encarnacion was founded as a Jesuit mission called Anunciación de Itapua the South bank of the Parana River in 1615. Like almost every town in South America, the heart of the city is its main plaza and church. The Catedral Nuestra Senora is the largest church in town, though still elegantly modest. Encarnacion is unlike most cities in that its Plaza de Armas park has a Japanese garden! But the most popular past-time here is strolling along the costanera, the city's riverside boardwalk, where you can enjoy views of the river and grab some cheap street-food. Right at the center of the costanera, you'll find the San Jose beach, where you can soak up the sun, or take a sunset stroll on the beach.

name: Humahuaca
description: While the Quebrada de Humahuaca valley has been inhabited for over 10,000 years, the town of Humahuaca itself was founded by the Spanish in the late 16th century. At the time, it was one of the most important settlements in the region, serving as a commercial center for precious metals. This rich combination of native and colonial cultures, surrounded by the valley's beautiful landscape, has bestowed upon Humahuaca a treasure trove of charms. Visit the main plaza at noon to see a figure of Saint Francisco Solano pop out of the adorable whitewashed church. Opposite the square, the Heroes of the Independence Monument honors the locals who fought in the National Independence War and offers a fantastic panorama of the valley. To learn more about the region's long history, stop by the Municipal Archaeological Museum to see archaeological artifacts, including two mummies. And if you'd like to bring some culture home with you, you can find a variety of handicrafts at the Humahuaca Craftsmen Centre.

name: Ambato
description: A city with spectacular mountain views, it is a place with many monikers. Known as the "Garden Of Ecuador" due to the large amount of fruit, vegetables, and wine produced in the area. Also known as the "City of the Three Juans" in relation to it's three beloved writers who were born here, and they are still commemorated here with statues and museums. Finally, it's third name "City of Flowers and Fruits" is well earned with it's plentiful parks filled with beautiful flowers and tree-lined streets. The city was almost completely destroyed during the 1949 earthquake and was rebuilt over the course of two years. The white modernist cathedral is striking to look at, and there are a couple of museums worth a visit (Quinta de Juan Leon Mera, and the Museo de Ciencias Naturales Hector Vasquez). The Monday markets are especially an experience not to be missed.

name: Zaruma
description: Located in southern Ecuador, Zaruma is historically a wealthy gold-mining town founded by the Spanish in 1549. Brightly coloured building facades and winding, narrow streets throughout town give it a labyrinth-like, magical feel. Virgen del Carmen Church is a baroque-style church towering above town in the Independence Plaza, and is a must-see for its lit-up grand tower and vibrant interior design. For mining history don't miss La Mina El Sexmo, a 500m-long tunnel 10 minutes out of town, open daily from 8am-5pm. If this is too claustrophobic for your taste the Municipal Museum in the historical centre shows various exhibitions and educates visitors on the towns historical mining activities. Before you leave, tantalise your tastebuds and order the towns' famous dish 'Tigrillo' - mashed green plantain with fried onions fried belly pork. To wash it down try the distinctive flavour of Zaruma's locally produced coffee, with hints of citrus and chocolate making for a unique brew.

name: Cuenca
description: While uninhabited when the Iberian Peninsula was part of the Roman Empire, the Moors quickly realized the value of this strategic location when they captured the area in 714. They built a fortress surrounded by a 1 kilometre-long wall, and Cuenca soon became and agricultural and textile manufacturing city. Visitors can enjoy an impressive list of notable sites, including the 12th-century Cathedral of our Lady of Grace, the first Gothic-style cathedral in Spain; the 13th-century Church of Saint Michael; and the Bridge of Saint Paul, originally built in 1533 and rebuilt after collapse in 1902, giving visitors a stunning view over the river. Perhaps the most famous buildings in Cuenca, however, are the Hanging Houses. Built on the rock above the Huecar River gorge in the 15th century, these well-known structures get their name from their position, seemingly hanging off the edge of the cliffs high above the river below.

name: Carmona
description: A pre-Roman settlement that was gentrified by Phoenician traders, and fortified by Rome, each passing empire supplemented the city's beauty. Today, the Roman road that still runs through the city, and even its fortified gates are still standing strong. There's also a Roman necropolis located on the city outskirts with hundreds of tombs and burial chambers excavated from rock. Within its fortified walls, the old quarter, lined with beautiful religious and civic buildings has maintained its Arab influence. Standing above the city is the 15th century church of Santa María la Mayor, built over a former Arab mosque. A walk through the historic old town reveals a treasure trove of Mudejar houses nestled against Renaissance and baroque buildings. At the city's highest point in the city, the Almohad King Don Pedro Fortress, a former Arab fortress, offers stupendous views in a historic setting.

name: Durres
description: Founded by Greek colonists in 627 BC, it's one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Albania. After the Romans took control in 229 BC, they developed it into a major military and naval base. In the 2nd century, they built the city's massive 20,000 person amphitheatre. The Durres Castle also dates back to the Roman Empire, when Anastasius I made the city into one of the most fortified on the Adriatic. The city thrived for centuries, until it fell under Ottoman control in 1501. For the next 400 years, the city declined, falling into complete anarchy in 1997, when the national economy was devastated by the the collapse of a massive pyramid scheme. Fortunately, the city has recovered since, and offers modern amenities along with its ancient architectural landmarks and the Durres Archaeological Museum is the largest in the country.

Fuji and the five lakes region. Yet, its famed Premium Outlets steal the limelight. With over 210 renowned domestic and international brands, shoppers will be in absolute paradise. Aside from shopping, discover tranquility at Chichibu-no-miya Memorial Park in Gotemba. Once a royal summer retreat, it features a historic 1723 house and charming cherry blossom trees. Visit the exciting safari park at Susono, a short bus ride from Gotemba Station, and witness elephants, giraffes, and lions roaming freely. Take in the jaw-dropping expanse of Mt. Fuji while indulging in recreational pleasures and wildlife sightings in this incredible city.

name: Tomar
description: The Convent of Christ, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a constant reminder of the city's connection to the Knights Templar. Spanning 400 years of Templar rule, the Convent was continuously modified and expanded and now the castle complex exhibits Romanesque, Gothic, Manueline and Renaissance styles. The iconic round church was built towards the end of the 12th century by the Knights Templar. Its structure is modelled on churches in Jerusalem, such as the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. The interior is magnificently decorated with late Gothic and Manueline sculptures and paintings, added during a renovation sponsored by King Manuel I in 1499. The well-organized streets and squares of the city centre were designed by Henry The Navigator, and make it easy to find your way to the many monuments, such as the checkered main square, home to the rich, Renaissance Church of St. John the Baptiste.

description: Locked in between the Olympus Range, home to the ancient Greek gods, and the Aegean Sea, the small town of Litchoro has a truly jaw-dropping setting. The town's history goes back to 14th century. The historical center is built in the typical Macedonian style, with small squares between the houses. The pine-covered park of Katounia offers a pleasant place to stroll and enjoy the town's scenery. At the Olympus National Park Information Center, visitors can learn about the history of the Mount Olympus region, local culture, archeological sites, and the flora and fauna the UNESCO-listed nature park.

name: Novalja
description: Novalja is a town on the Adriatic surrounded by nearly ten beaches. Its most famous beach, Zrce Beach, is one of the biggest party destinations in Europe. The beach has 4 open-air clubs open around the clock and has been awarded a Blue flag, a symbol of quality and purity of the sea. That being said, there is much more to discover in Novalja than just Zrce Beach. The town is also a popular family resort due to its abundance of unspoiled beaches, pristine sea, and sport and recreational activities. The city center is ideal for shopping or grabbing a bite to eat while walking along the shoreline. The Novalja City Museum and archaeological museum houses many interesting archeological facts and contemporary art. Whether you're looking for a fast-paced or a more laidback beach style atmosphere, Novalja is sure to provide!

name: Quiahuiztlan Archeological Zone
address.region: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
description: Quiahuiztlan was founded around the 8th century as a settlement that would be protected from the threat of raiders from the north. Despite their best efforts, the city/fort that served as the Totonac capital still fell to the invading Toltecs at the end of the 9th century, and then to the Aztecs in the early 1400s. When the Spanish arrived, Quiahuiztlan was still a thriving city with 15,000 inhabitants, but was abandoned following their conquest. Today, Quiahuiztlan is one of the most important archaeological sites in the region thanks to its diverse architecture. Here you'll find Totonac tombs, Toltec engravings, and Aztec architecture intermixed. There's even an "I"-shaped ballcourt, and small pyramid with a Mexica-style sacrifice stone! While Quiahuiztlan's monuments are relatively small, the views are grand, with the Cerro de los Metates rock spire in the background and coast where Hernan Cortez landed spread out at your feet.

name: San Jose
description: The first stop on most agendas, this Central American capital has much to offer before you embark on your tropical adventure! With a connection to the Pacific and Caribbean coasts, San Jose presents a full scope of authentic Costa Rica. With pre and post-colonial heritage and a bejeweled natural history, the city guides you through it all. Visit the delightful Jade Museum, the indigenous Galleria Namu, or the subterranean Pre-Columbian Gold Museum. Admire the architecture as you enter the National Theater and take in the grandeur of the National Museum. Locals live by the phrase 'Pura Vida' (pure or good life). To see what they mean, join them at one of the many tranquil parks dotted around the city. You'll find a real sense of community as people dance and play music, while others simply take in the serenity around them. Honoring their natural surroundings is illustrative of Costa Rica; and its delicate beauty is all on show at San Jose's hidden gem, the magical Spirogyra Butterfly Garden.

name: Blarney Stone
description: The legendary Blarney Stone is embedded within a machicolation atop the high walls of Blarney castle. The exact origins of the stone are unknown. According to some, it was brought to Ireland by the prophet Jeremiah, and was used to decide on the Irish Kings. Others say it's part of the Stone of Destiny, given to Cormac McCarthy by Robert the Bruce. Another legend says it's the biblical 'Stone of Ezel', brought back to Ireland from the Crusades. Regardless of its origins, the one legend everyone agrees on is if you hang over the precipice to kiss the stone, you will be bestowed with the gift of elegance and flattery. While now there are handlebars to add an extra layer of safety to the ritual, for centuries one had to be held by the ankles over the drop. This dangerous performance even inspired a Sherlock Holmes case. For more information, please visit www.blarneycastle.ie

name: Senglea
description: Senglea was bestowed the title "Invincible City" after its successful resistance against the Ottoman invasion during the Great Siege of Malta in 1565. Despite its small size, Senglea holds a significant place in Malta's history. On a peninsula jutting into the Grand Harbor, Senglea faces the picturesque walled city of Valletta. From the daringly hanging caper tree along the bastions to the scattered ancient fig trees, the city's landscape reflects the fusion of the island's gentle climate with the city itself. Looking down towards the calm waves of the harbor, the dockyard remains a vital hub of activity, pulsating with life and serving as the city's beating heart. A visit to the tip of the peninsula is a must, offering splendid views of the harbor from the renowned Gardjola, a decorated watchtower that has become an iconic symbol of Malta. Traditional boat races are held twice a year in the Grand Harbour on March 31st and September 8th, the latter date illuminating the town with hundreds of light bulbs, spectacular fireworks, and lavish decorations.

name: Cenotes Kin-Ha
description: Cenotes Kin-Ha is a large underground dome, only accessible from a small "eye" in its ceiling. From above, this innocuous hole in the ground doesn't look like much, but descend the wooden staircase and a water-filled cavern opens up before you. The light, coming in from above and reflecting off the water, illuminates the cave's stalactites in a beautiful natural display, making for an otherworldly swimming experience. At 50 meter wide and 60 meters deep, the cenote is also popular for snorkeling and diving, which allow you to see the mushroom-shaped cave formations below the surface. The cenote lies at the heart of an eco-adventure park where you can zipline into the water or join a wild and muddy ATV adventure.

name: Carapegua
description: Renowned for its fine artisan products such as blankets, sheets, ponchos, and hammocks, Carapegua's nickname of 'Capital del Poyvi' (The Capital of Thread), is well-deserved. Visitors to Carapegua can get a first-hand look into the thriving artist community by learning about the traditional 'poyvi' weaving technique. Check out the Historical Artisan Museum of the Oñondivepá Cultural Center to learn about the history and culture that Carapegua has to share.

name: Mexicali
description: Mexicali is the captivating capital of Baja California, beckoning visitors with an intriguing fusion of contemporary urban life and timeless relics of its storied past. Visitors flock here daily from Calexico, United States, crossing the border by foot or car, enticed by the allure of local taco stands, authentic restaurants, lively dance clubs, and vibrant bars. The streets near the border are adorned with stalls and shops brimming with Mexican curios and souvenirs, making it a perfect spot to indulge in some retail therapy. Explore bath halls, bowling alleys, museums, movie theaters, or enjoy a family day at the zoo. For shopping enthusiasts, the Plaza La Cachanilla, located near the U.S. border, offers an array of stores selling everything from Mexican curios to international imports. You can discover Mexicali's fascinating cultural scene through interactive experiences at the Museo Sol del Niño, art expressions at the State Center for the Arts, and innovative exhibitions at the Alternative Energies Theme Park.

name: Al Qunfudhah
description: Renowned for its vibrant cultural legacy, captivating beaches, and breathtaking natural vistas, Al-Qunfudhah is a thriving hub of commerce and economy within its domain. The city boasts a repertoire of attractions that beckon tourists and locals alike. Among them, the illustrious Qunfudhah Fort, Al-Madrasah Mosque, and Al-Zaytuna Mosque exude historical grandeur. As the Red Sea's waves kiss the coastline, outdoor enthusiasts revel in fishing, swimming, and scuba diving exploits that the city's waterscapes offer. Al-Hebah Historical Mosque stands as a testament to the city's antiquity, an architectural marvel nestled in the western quarters. Al-Qunfudhah Corniche graces the coast, inviting leisurely strolls and tranquil boat rides with panoramic views of the sea. Meanwhile, Al-Darb Historical Village, tracing back to the 17th century, imparts insights into the region's historical tapestry through its ancient edifices. Al-Qunfudhah Governorate showcases its coastal splendors with pristine beaches and captivating islands, paired with verdant parks and amusement havens. The city's allure is augmented by its architectural relics, lofty mountains, verdant meadows, meandering valleys, and perennial waterways.

name: El Bolson
description: Cradled in a fertile valley along the Quemquemtreu river, and embraced by the imposing Mount Piltriquitron, El Bolsón boasts a distinct charm and hospitable locals, inviting you to indulge in delightful traditional products. Embark on a scenic journey from Bariloche, tracing the shores of lakes Gutiérrez, Mascardi, and Guillelmo. Along the way, encounter the quaint town of El Foyel, offering roadside kiosks, cabins, and inns for a tranquil stay. The Guaitecas community showcases Mapuche-descendant crafts, adding a touch of local artistry to your journey. El Bolsón's craft fair at Pagano square is a magnet for artisans, where skilled hands craft metal, pottery, woodwork, knitted products, stained glass, knives, and more. The town is a gateway to two captivating tours—one leading to the Lago Puelo National Park and the other to El Maitén for a ride on La Trochita, an ancient steam train. Embraced by ancient glaciers and mountains, El Bolsón is also a haven for those seeking connection with nature.

name: Herend
description: Though Herend's history goes back to Roman times, the village was essentially emptied when Hungary was under Ottoman control. Between 1764 and 1847 it was gradually repopulated, and the Herend Porcelain Manufactory. Herend's hand painted and gilded porcelain received international attention after being exhibited in Hungary, Vienna, London, New York, and Paris in the mid 19th century, being ordered by the royal courts of Queen Victoria, Francis Joseph I of Austria, Maximillian, the Mexican emperor, as well as by wealthy families like the Rothschilds. Today, visitors can head to the Minimanufactory to learn about the secrets of porcelain-making, and even try their hand at this delicate craft by signing up for a workshop! Meanwhile, at the Porcelain Museum, you can see a permanent exhibition of Herend's exquisite products as well as the Manufactory's history and technology. For more information, please visit http://herend.com

name: Cascadas de Tixhinu
description: Situated near the town of Aculco, North West of Mexico City, the Tixhinu waterfalls are a refreshing must for anyone visiting this region of Mexico. Especially in a town where water defines everything about the culture and landscape (Aculco means "place where the water twists" in Nahuatl language), there is no better spot to find relaxation than in the lush greenery which surrounds the rock formations. The Tixhinu falls stand at 15 meters high, and those who are fond of extreme sports will be able to rappel down the rock face (with a guided tour, that is). Try to plan your visit for a sunny day, when the light beams reflecting off of the flowing water and basalt makes this destination well worth the detour.

name: Kosice
description: Kosice is situated on the river Hornad in the valley. This diverse city is a center for culture, industry, science, and commerce. Nearly all of Kosice's monuments are gathered in the compact city center, Hlavne Namestie Square. The cobblestone streets are pedestrianized, making it easy to get around on foot. The main sight in the square is St. Elisabeth Cathedral, the largest cathedral in Slovakia. The 11th century cathedral is regarded as one of the most dazzling Gothic structures in the world. St. Michael's Chapel (the second oldest building in Kosice) and the State Theater can also be found in the Old Town. Kosice has a vast cafe culture and many restaurants with excellent wine selections. Enjoy a glass of wine while wandering the cobblestone streets and taking in all that Kosice has to offer.

name: Los Angeles, CA
description: Fortunately, the discovery of oil in Los Angeles financed the glorious boom that made this city the global capital it is today. The sprawling metropolis is etched into cinema history and its iconic landmarks are on show for all to see! Start at the epicenter, Hollywood Boulevard. Strut along the star-studded Walk of Fame and pose for the cameras outside the Chinese Theatre. Take to the red carpet at the revered home of the Oscars, the Dolby Theatre, or even step into Madame Tussauds, get up close with waxworks of the city's biggest names! From here, head to supreme Sunset Boulevard. From Downtown L.A. to Sunset Beach, this epic route winds its way through world-famous neighborhoods, Bel Air, Palisades, Beverly Hills, and Chinatown. On your way, get a glimpse of the Hollywood Sign, shop like a millionaire on Rodeo Drive, or step into showbiz history at the Viper Room or Comedy Store. Media giants Disney, Universal, Paramount, and Warner Bros. have all made their mark on the city, at their respective studios and theme parks that visitors of all ages will enjoy! Finally, you can gaze down from the stars and marvel at the sprawling city views from the serene Griffith Park and Observatory.

name: Buchenwald Memorial
description: Ironically lying just a few miles away from Wiemar, the city of German classicism, and set among beautiful countryside, Buchenwald has since become synonymous with German war crimes. The visitor experience is sensitively handled but does not gloss over the horrors that took place at what eventually became the largest concentration camp in Germany. Although the site was partially destroyed in 1950, there still remain the footprints of all the buildings that stood at the camp, one or two actual original buildings including the crematorium and the prison, memorial areas and three museum/exhibition areas. Audio guides are available and there are written explanations in the exhibit areas and in the large three-storey museum. The photographs stun and shock but need little explanation. Even though the majority of people in the world today are aware of the atrocities committed by the Nazis, a visit to Buchenwald takes this awareness to a whole new unforgettable level.

name: Guadalajara
description: Guadalajara was founded by the Romans, who created the early centre of Arriaca, but it wasn't until the 12th century, when Alfonso VII granted a charter to the city, that it truly began to flourish. In the mid 15th century, when Mendoza received the lordship of Guadalajara, he overhauled the city, leaving it splendid for centuries. The main street is lined with many of the city's most important monuments, like the City Hall, and the old palace of the Mendoza's, with its Plateresque courtyard. The real symbol of the city is the magnificent, Renaissance Infantado Palace, which now houses the Museum, Archive, and Municipal Library. This city's many churches are also a cultural gems, such as the 15th century alabaster tomb in the Baroque Jesuit church of San Nicolás el Real, or the 14th century Church of Santiago, which combines Gothic-Mudejar style with a Baroque façade.

name: Chastleton House and Garden
description: Chastleton House and Garden were constructed at the beginning of the 17th century by a wealthy wool merchant as a testament to his of wealth and power. The same family lived in the beautiful country home until 1991, and were involved in everything from the Gunpowder Plot to the invention of croquet. Almost no alterations have been made to the architecture or decor so visitors are treated to timeless look at life gone by. The manor's rooms are full of historic objects like centuries-old tapestries, and stupendous wood panelling, as well as reminders of its owner's continued use - from books on the nightstands to well-worn furniture and centuries of soot on the kitchen ceiling. The garden is equally impressive but informal, with a vegetable plot and Jacobean topiary, and in the Summer, croquet on the very grounds were game's rules were invented. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/chastleton-house

name: Mompox
description: Mompox was founded by the Spanish in 1540 as an important trading post on the Magdalena river - the main artery connecting the Caribbean coast to the centre of the country. The town's strategic location also proved a safe place for the Spanish to stockpile gold. Centuries of prosperity came to an end in the late 19th century when the Magdalena River silted up, and traders began to go elsewhere. Despite being named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995, Mompox was only accessible by ferry until 2015 when the first bridge was built. The town's isolation left it frozen in time, and today is considered one of the best examples of a Spanish colonial settlement left in the Americas. Walking among the historic homes and seven colorful churches, it's easy to see why Gabriel Garcia Marquez used it for the basis of "Macondo" in "One Hundred Years Of Solitude".

name: Corfu City
description: In Corfu, the cobblestone streets of the Old Town whisper tales of civilizations past, inviting exploration of its maze-like alleys adorned with Venetian architecture and neoclassical facades. A focal point of the city's rich history, the Old Fortress Corfu stands as a sentinel overlooking the azure Ionian Sea, its weathered walls bearing witness to centuries of maritime adventures and conquests. Amidst the labyrinthine streets, the Church of Saint Spyridon emerges as a beacon of faith and cultural heritage. Devotees and curious visitors alike are drawn to its ornate bell tower and glittering mosaics, where the legacy of the island's patron saint comes to life in a tapestry of religious reverence and architectural splendor. Beyond its historical treasures, Corfu city exudes a lively ambiance with bustling squares, quaint cafes, and bustling markets offering a taste of local life and gastronomic delights. Visitors can savor traditional Greek cuisine in charming tavernas or sip on refreshing cocktails overlooking the picturesque harbor, where colorful fishing boats bob gently against the backdrop of pastel-hued buildings.

name: Varenna
description: This jewel on the waterfront is in the perfect location to hop on a ferry and enjoy all of the views along Lake Como's coast. Its close proximity to the Alps and Mediterranean-like climate offers plenty of activities and a perfect temperatures all year round. Some of the alleys in Varenna are very steep, but with steep hills come breathtaking views. To catch a glimpse of some Gothic and Renaissance architecture, venture to the center of town and peer at the home of the Church of San Giorgio. Varenna is also home to an old monastery, a museum holding four centuries of history, and a botanical garden. A quick stop in Varenna has much to offer.

name: Karlstejn Castle
description: Czech King and Roman Emperor Charles IV ordered the construction of Karlstejn Cast in 1348 as a place to store royal treasures, holy relics, and the crown jewels. After its completion in the 14th century, the castle received a Renaissance make-over, and its current neo-Gothic look comes courtesy of a renovation in the 18th century. Today, the castle stands as one of the finest and most fascinating in the Czech Republic for both its impressive architecture and captivating history. The centerpiece is the Chapel of the Holy Cross, said to have been designed by Charles IV himself. The gilded walls are inlaid with countless semi-precious stones, with the 129 panel paintings depicting popes, bishops, knights, and mentors of the Czech Republic. Housed within is a replica of the St. Wenceslas Crown - made of pure gold and studded with emeralds, rubies, sapphires, and pearls. To reach the castle, visitors can enjoy a pleasant walk up the hill, or take a romantic carriage ride. The castle offers a variety of different tours in different languages. For more information, please visit www.hrad-karlstejn.cz/en

name: Mount Vesuvius
address.addr1: Mount Vesuvius, 80044 Ottaviano, Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy
description: Perhaps best known for its infamous eruption on August 24, 79 AD, which destroyed Pompeii and Herculaneum, this dormant volcano is now a national park - layering a unique natural environment over a shroud of history. The fateful eruption left a large crater that has fluctuated in size with each subsequent eruption. Since 1995, the volcano has been a national park, requiring visitors to walk 15-20 minutes up to the crater's rim. At the top, visitors can walk around the crater to appreciate the contrasting views of Vesuvius' moon-like landscape, and stunning views of the Bay of Naples. Please note that tickets must be purchased in advance at https://www.vivaticket.com/it/ticket/visita-guidata-al-gran-cono-del-vesuvio/79785

name: Feilding
description: Take a walk along the red brick covered paths of Feilding to guide you towards your next destination. As a small town, Feilding is the perfect break from either the city life or all of the hiking that New Zealand has to offer. While wading through the paths lined with beautiful trees and flower beds, you can decide whether you would like to stop by one of Feilding's many cafes, pubs, art galleries, museums or if you're lucky enough to be there at the right time, the Feilding farmer's market. This charming community has a lot to offer and can be your opportunity to discover why it has been called New Zealand's most beautiful town for many years.

name: Seville
description: Founded around the 8th century BC, Seville grew into a major trade center under the Romans - a status it maintained through much of its long history, especially trade with the New World. The city's old town reflects these centuries of prosperity, perhaps best exemplified by its Gothic cathedral - the largest in the world. This UNESCO World Heritage Site was built over the course of a century on the site of a former mosque, using the most refined and extravagant construction techniques to showcase the city's wealth. The cathedral's massive facade is impossibly ornate, covered with intricate carvings. The iconic bell-tower is topped with the original mosque's minaret. The interior is even more richly decorated, and houses the tomb of Christopher Columbus. Surrounding the cathedral is an enchanting mix of majestic Mudéjar palaces, historic homes and winding medieval lanes. And while in the city, be sure to take part in the locals' favourite past time: tapas!

name: Lake Mburo National Park
description: Lake Mburo was designated a national park in 1983 but despite its protected status it suffered decades of tumult due to the country's power struggle. Regime changes and tribal tensions led to the expulsion of locals, efforts to reclaim the land by those who were expelled and a large amount of dead wildlife. Similarly, projects intended to neutralize the tsetse fly also had adverse effects on the population of animals in the area. The park has since been able to reintroduce a great deal of zebras, giraffes, warthogs, hippos, lions and over 350 species of birds. The work that local tribes have done along with Ugandan governmental agencies have allowed the park to once again flourish. There is much to do and even more to see. From Boat safaris to horseback riding, this little slice of wilderness really allows you to see the diverse wildlife of the African Savannah in a compact and gorgeous location, Make sure to not miss the traditional food served with gorgeous views of the namesake lake. Please note that the park charges an admission fee ($40 for adults and $20 for children), payable upon entry. For more information, please visit https://www.ugandawildlife.org/

name: Aranda de Duero
description: Dating back to the Romans, the capital of Wine Enthusiast Magazine's 2012 'Wine Region of the Year', flourished from the 15th to 16th centuries. The city has its fair share of historic landmarks, such as the Roman bridge next to the Gothic church of San Juan, with its fortified tower. The Church of Santa María la Real was built during the 15th and 16th centuries, and features a unique doorway depicting Biblical scenes, and is topped by the coat of arms of the Catholic Monarchs. However the city's real highlight lies underground. Of the 135 underground wineries, some, such as the 15th century Don Carlos, invite visitors to explore the cave, or enjoy some cave-aged wine underground.

name: Split
description: Split is the largest city in Dalmatia and the second largest city in Croatia. It's located on the Eastern shore of the Adriatic and is home to beautiful beaches and Roman walls, squares, and temples. The city's old town houses Diocletian's Palace, one of the world's most impressive Roman monuments. The palace was built in the 3rd and 4th centuries by Roman emperor Diocletian. Today, dozens of bars, shops, and restaurants lie in the heart of the palace grounds. Wander the vibrant streets of the promenade and explore one of the many pebble and sandy beaches as you make your way through this gorgeous city.

name: Kurashiki
description: Whether you seek historical ambience, artistic riches, or denim delights, Kurashiki has a unique blend of experience that makes it a worthy addition to your Japanese journey. At the heart of Kurashiki lies the Bikan Historical Quarter, often dubbed "the Venice of Japan." This captivating canal area exudes old-world charm, earning comparisons to Kyoto. Stroll its narrow streets, lined with preserved Edo-period buildings and quaint shops, offering a glimpse into the past. The Ohara Museum of Art stands as a treasure trove for art aficionados. Japan's pioneering museum of Western art, it boasts a distinguished collection featuring masterpieces by renowned artists like Monet, Renoir, and Picasso. Kurashiki is more than an artistic enclave; it's a denim paradise. Denim enthusiasts and fashion lovers are drawn to the city's reputation as Japan's denim hub, with hotspots and boutiques sprawled throughout the quaint town.

name: Oxkintoc Archaeological Zone
description: The Oxkintoc Archaeological Zone preserves one of the oldest Maya cities in the Yucatan, having been settled around 350 BC. The site remained inhabited until as kat as 1500 AD when it was abandoned for unknown reasons. Though details of the city's history have eluded archaeologists, its architecture is considered some of the most unique and important in the Yucatan, preserving the early Puuc style with some elements from central Mexico. Oxkintoc is famous for its enigmatic Tza Tun Tzat - a three-level labyrinth within one of the pyramids that terminates in a burial chamber on each. Designed like a cave complex, the only illumination comes from sparse air vents that align with certain sun positions, so bring a flashlight! Oxkintoc's other main attraction is the series of stone columns that have been carved to resemble fat men in elaborate dress, with robes, mesh vests, and body armor. Please note: there are no bathrooms or facilities at the site.

name: Arad
description: Dating back to the 11th century, Arad proved itself an important fortification during the Mongol invasion of 1241. For the next several centuries it primarily played a military purpose, and it was here that Lajos Kossuth issued his famous proclamation, handing over supreme civil and military authority to Artúr Görgey during the Hungarian Revolution. For visitors interested in this important part of the region's history, the city has a museum containing relics of the war for independence. In the 19th century, the town became an important railway hub and producer of railcars. This late boom makes Arad a treasure-trove for fans of neoclassical and Secession style architecture. A walk along the tree-lined central boulevard rewards visitors with views of the many palaces, churches and monuments.

name: Pattaya
description: Pattaya was a tiny fishing village until the 1960s when American GIs visited the town for some R&R and raved about the experience. Today, the city is one of the most popular resort destinations in Thailand, with the go-go bars on Walking Street and 4 kilometer-long beach offering something for bachelors and families alike. Jutting out into the water, the Sanctuary of Truth is a one-of-a-kind temple covered in intricate carvings that walks the line between art and architecture. At Pattaya's floating market you can enjoy everything from traditional food to a foot massage in an amphibious shopping village. Orchid lovers will want to head to the 2.4 sq km Nong Nooch Garden to admire the beautifully landscaped park, catch a cultural show, or enjoy a bite to eat. Pattaya's other unique theme park is Mini Siam and Mini Europe, where landmarks from around Thailand and Europe have been crafted in 1:25 scale.

name: Hammamet
description: Settled since the first century, Hammamet became a Roman colony in the 2nd century, before passing under the control of every empire that ruled the region, including the Spanish and Turks. Reduced to a small fishing village by the 20th century, Hammamet was revitalized when Romanian millionaire George Sebastian and the European jet set began vacationing here. While the beachfront is lined with hotels, early planning constraints dictated that they should not overreach the height of a tree, meaning it's maintained the air of a small-town air. The waterfront is watched over by a 15th century fort, which offers excellent views of the coast, but doesn't have much inside. In the fortified medina, you'll find streets bustling with shops, vendors, and restaurants, charming side alleys, and some interesting museums dedicated to local culture.

name: Kassel
description: Regarded as a major achievement of European Landscape gardening, this eighteenth-century park spreads across 240 hectares and contains over 500 species of trees. Described by one twentieth-century art historian as "possibly the most grandiose combination of landscape and architecture that Baroque dared anywhere", the park contains seemingly endless waterfalls while the spectacular views from above and below offer amazing panoramic views. There are many parts of the park to stroll and relax in, with surprises waiting around almost every corner. The hillside boasts the impressive Wilhelmshohe Palace, packed with historical artifacts and well worth spending a little time in. There is also the botanical atrium, the temple to Mercury, the fountain to Poseidon, a pyramid, an aqueduct, a museum of antiquities, waterfalls, lakes and a three-story bronze statue of Hercules. It is not difficult to see why the rumor that this hillside inspired Wagner's ring cycle may actually have some substance to it.

name: Oviedo
description: It's said Oviedo was founded in 761 by two monks after the Visigoth Pelagius revolted against the Muslims and founded the Kingdom of Asturias. Pelagius' successor Alfonso I, made it the capital of his kingdom, and it remains the capital of the region. The UNESCO-listed Cathedral of San Salvador is an impressive example of 13th century Gothic architecture, and is an important stop on the Santiago de Compostela. On the outskirts of the city, you'll find Ovieda's second UNESCO World Heritage Site - the 9th century Santa María del Naranco, which was originally a palace built by King Ramiro I. The city is especially proud of its long history, with the Archaeological Museum of Asturias, housed in a 16th century monastery, displaying artefacts dating back to prehistory. The Pre-Romanic Interpretation Centre of Asturias details Pre-Romanic history through interactive displays, and shares more information about the area's most important historic monuments. For foodies, the city is worth a stop if just to enjoy a meal at Gloria, Oviedo's two Michelin-starred restaurant.

name: Paradise Wildlife Park
description: Family-owned since the 1980s, the Paradise Wildlife Park was born when the Sampson family purchased the local zoo to provide the animals with larger, more natural enclosures. Over the years, the park expanded to provide a better home to more animals, and now houses over 800 creatures, including Britain's best collection of big cats. In Big Cat Territory you can meet White Tigers, White Lions, Amur Tigers, Snow Leopards, Cheetahs, Jaguars and Ocelots. Other parts of the park offer the opportunity to see Penguins, Monkeys, Zebras, Wallabies, and Reptiles, with the opportunity to touch and feed many of the animals! In the surrounding woodland, visitors can step into the World of Dinosaurs, which is home to 30 life-size, moving and roaring dinosaurs. The park also offers visitors plenty of unique experiences, from shadowing a keeper to feeding the big cats! For more information, please visit pwpark.com

name: Orvieto
description: Starting as a major Etruscan settlement, Orvieto was essentially used as a fortress by whoever ruled Italy up until the 16th century. With its impregnable position atop sheer cliffs it's easy to see why even Popes would flee here in times of strife. The hilltop city has remained essentially unchanged since the 15th century, making it one of the most picturesque in the country. And the heavy papal presence has blessed it with some of the country's finest devotional art and architecture. Overshadowing even the multiple papal palaces is the Cathedral, undeniably one of Italy's greatest Gothic churches. The facade not only has all the usual Gothic embellishments, but is covered in vibrant murals. The interior is just as sensational, with frescoes that rival the Sistine Chapel. Just below the city is a vast network of Etruscan-era tunnels, which can be explored on a guided tour to see a unique part of ancient Italian history.

name: Fredericksburg, VA
description: Also known as "America's Most Historic City", Fredericksburg is home to one of the most colorful histories in the United States. A highly prosperous town in the colonial period, the 19th century saw a surge of development. However, during the Civil War, its location midway between the two opposing capitals made it the site of multiple battles, and near constant bombardment and looting. Today, the 40-block Historic District is lined with charming 18th and 19th century buildings that offer a trip down memory lane. Take a tour of the Mary Washington House, which George Washington bought for his mother, or go peruse the 17th century Hugh Mercer Apothecary (established on Washington's recommendation). You can get even more local history in the 19th century town hall, which now houses the Fredericksburg Area Museum. Or head to the Kenmore Plantation, the home of George Washington's sister! To learn about Fredericksburg's Civil War history, visit the Spotsylvania Military Park, the site of four major Civil War Battles.

name: Guadix
description: This once-Roman colony rose to some importance as a Moorish fortress and trading station in the year 711. Guadix was the site of the Battle of Guadix in January 1362, and was surrendered to the Spaniards under Ferdinand and Isabella in 1489. The city, situated on the left bank of the river Guadix in southern Spain, is now home to several interesting tourist attractions. Included these sites is the 16th-century Guadix Cathedral, built over a Moorish mosque and consisting of a unique blend of architectural styles, built in a Gothic-Renaissance style with a Baroque façade. The city is also home to a Moorish fortress dominating the area, and the Barrio de Santiago, a neighbourhood characterized by 'troglodyte' houses carved into rocks. This intricate maze of homes is not fashioned from natural cavities, but is instead a man-made phenomenon created by the act of burrowing into the soft sandstone rocks.

name: Murcia
description: Founded as a fortified Moorish city in 831, there are still sections of the original walls scattered throughout the historic center, and the Santa Clara Museum offers the opportunity to take a closer look at Moorish artefacts. While the city is filled with baroque architecture, it is perhaps best experienced in the Plaza Cardenal Belluga. Here, visitors can visit the grand, 18th century Episcopal Palace, with a Rococo façade and Churrigueresque courtyard. Next to it is the 14th century Cathedral, with blends a variety of architectural styles, with its richly sculpted Baroque façade, and accented Gothic interior. The city also offers some unique 19th century architecture, such as the neo-lavish Casino, a gambling house that incorporates Moorish elements to the usual Romanticist motifs. For a detailed look at the city' past, the Archaeological Museum exhibits artefacts from the various cultures that have inhabited the area.

name: Polgahawela
description: Enveloped in the lush greenery of Sri Lanka's countryside, Polgahawela and its neighboring towns offer a diverse range of experiences, from spiritual exploration at the monastery to immersing yourself in local culture, enjoying the beautiful scenery, and indulging in delectable Sri Lankan cuisine. At Mahamevnawa Polgahawela, an expansive and vibrant Theravada Buddhist Monastery, English-speaking monks are readily available for guided tours, questions about Buddhism, or insights into meditation technique. Marvel at the majesty of the Dhammachakkha Stupa, a symbol of enlightenment and spiritual awakening, and wander through the Sacred Bodhi Tree Complex. The town is served by a historic railway station, where you can witness the hustle and bustle of local life as you observe passengers boarding and disembarking from the trains. The town is also brimming with local eateries and street food vendors where you can savor mouthwatering Sri Lankan dishes, including rice and curry, hoppers, kottu roti, and various seafood specialties.

name: Bururi
description: Bururi, a provincial capital in southwestern Burundi isn't on most travelers' radars! The city itself has a slew of colonial-era buildings, but that's not why you visit. The star of the show lies on the mountain overlooking the city: Bururi Forest Natural Reserve. Covering 3300 hectares of damp forest, locals considered the reserve a link between heaven and earth, and it's easy to see why. The lush greenery, stunning vistas this is a place that will take your breath away. But the beauty doesn't stop there – the reserve is also home to a diverse array of plant and animal species, including some that are rare or endangered, like chimpanzees and exotic bird species. Plus, it's an important source of water for local communities, and efforts are underway to preserve this natural wonder for future generations. To visit the reserve, visitors must first stop by the INECN office to pay for the entry and get a guide.

name: Malaga
description: Starting with the Phoenicians, every Mediterranean empire for the past 2000 years has sought to control Malaga's strategic port. For the Moors, the city was so integral that they built their largest fortress in the region here. Today, the 8th century Alcazaba is home to the Archaeological Museum, exhibiting Phoenician and Roman artefacts. The 14th century Gibralfaro castle is connected to the Alcazaba by a stretch of wall, which offers stupendous views of the city. At the foot of the castle is the city's historic center, with the Roman theatre, bullring, and 16th century Cathedral. Known as 'the one-armed' thanks to its unfinished tower, this palatial Renaissance building houses a series of artistic chapels. Picasso was born in Malaga, so his eponymous museum is a must visit - housed in a 16th century castle, visitors can enjoy the career-spanning collection, and the glass floor in the basement revealing the remains of Phoenician buildings.

name: Troyes
description: Dating back to the ancient Romans, the city was made the capital of Champagne in the 9th century, and kept the title until the French Revolution. After a massive fire in 1524, most of the city had to be rebuilt. This disaster left the city with a large, coherent, and colorful collection of half-timbered houses unrivalled in France. The 16th century Hôtel de Mauroy is particularly striking, and it houses the world's largest tool museum, exhibiting 11,000 pieces that date back to the 1600s. The town cathedral was built between the 13th and 17th centuries, leaving it with an harmonious mix of architectural styles, as well as historic art collection. The 12th century Église de la Madeleine has a striking Renaissance interior, complete with an unusual choir screen, which separates everyday worshippers from the church's most sacred areas.

name: Prizren
description: Kosovo's historic capital, Prizren, is the country's second largest city and offers a mix of Ottoman-era architecture and lively modern energy. The city's cobblestone center is dominated by the 17th-century Sinan Pasha Mosque, its landmark minaret towering above a maze of shops selling copperware, spices, and traditional textiles. The hilltop Prizren Fortress keeps watch over the city from a spot occupied since the Bronze Age, offering spectacular views. The 14th-century Our Lady of Ljeviš Church is a Serbian Orthodox site and part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Medieval Monuments in Kosovo" since 2006. Thanks to extensive restoration efforts, visitors can admire it's spectacular Byzantine-era frescoes. Compact and walkable, Prizren balances history with youthful energy—a must-visit for travelers exploring Kosovo's heritage.

name: Tarragona
description: Augustus himself wintered in the city formerly known as "Tarraco" after his conquest of Hispania in the Cantabrian wars in the early 1st century BC, and bestowed it with many titles of honor. In fact, the city's ancient Roman archaeological complex has been named a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visitors can take in historical sights such as the Catedral Basilica Metropolitana Primada de Tarragon, reputed to be the finest cathedral in Catalonia due to its grandiose stature and flying buttresses. Just a short walk away, the Tarragona Amphitheatre, built during the 1st century BC, sits on the shore and invites visitors to admire the ancient arena which seated up to fifteen thousand spectators. For those interested in venturing away from the city center, the Pont del Diable is worth a visit. Walking paths scattered around this Roman-age bridge make it easy to exploring the surrounding ruins.

name: Vasto
description: According to legend, the hilltop town of Vasto was founded by the Greek hero Diomedes, though archaeological evidence points to the Frentani tribe settling here around 1300 BC. During the 15th century, much of the city was rebuilt with its Classically-influenced architecture earning it the nickname 'the Athens of the Abruzzi'. Just a century later, the Turks burned down much of the city. Today, visitors can enjoy the same panoramic views of the Adriatic that have been enchanting people for centuries. Its charming historic visitors will find a slew of buildings dating back to the 15th century, such as the Caldoresco Castle. The elegant Renaissance Palazzo d'Avalos houses 4 museums, including the archaeological museum. Of course, visitors could always just explore the cobbled streets to admire the historic architecture before sitting down to enjoy some of the town's signature fresh seafood.

name: Zakopane
description: Situated at the foothills of the Tatra mountains just a few miles from the Slovak border lies the town of Zakopane. The region is widely known for its untouched nature and immaculate landscapes. As the winter capital of Poland, Zakopane offers a multitude of skiing and winter activities and is the ideal base point for hiking and mountain climbing. There are many restaurant and shops situated on Krupowski street, the main pedestrian zone of the city. Zakopane's most popular tourist attraction is its cable car. Ride the cable car up to Mount Kasprowy for spectacular views over the town and the surrounding Tatra mountains. There's also a funicular in the center of town that takes visitors up to Gubalowka hill. Zakopane has nine local museums to explore. The most notable museum being the The Tatra Museum. There are also several art galleries, a theater, and a cinema. Whether searching for unspoiled nature, outdoor adventure, or a slice of culture, Zakopane is the place to be.

name: Sancti Spiritus
description: Sancti Spíritus was founded in 1514 as one of Spain's original seven villas, but moved to its present location on the Río Yayabo in 1522. As a base for the Spanish conquest of the Yucatán and seat of the influential Iznaga family, Sancti Spíritus' prosperous colonial years bestowed the town with a wealth of charming architecture. After the Cuban Revolution, it was left largely forgotten, only getting a makeover in 2014 in celebration of its 500th birthday. Today, the town is still overlooked by tourists, which means you can enjoy its colonial architecture without the crowds and touts. Start at the Plaza Serafin Sánchez, which is surrounded by colorful buildings, and dominated not by a church, but a stunning library. From here, head south down the quiet streets, past the pastel blue Iglesia Parroquial Mayor Parish Church, to Sancti Spíritus' iconic Puente Yayabo, a neo-Romanesque bridge over the Yayabo River.

name: Stonehenge
description: Modern radiocarbon dating has dates Stonehenge's origins to around 3000 BC, effectively dispelling the long-standing theory that it was built by the Druids - they wouldn't arrive for another 1000 years. Most archaeologists agree the site was used for burials and death rituals, and was likely a ritual site for the Romano-Britons as well. During the Middle Ages, in an attempt to explain how the massive stones were moved, legend said that Merlin himself built Stonehenge as a memorial to 3,000 nobles killed by the Saxons. To this day, exactly how Stonehenge was built remains a mystery - the inner ring of stones came from Wales, 240 miles away, and theories to explain how they were moved range from giant baskets to glaciers. But the mysterious origins and purpose are all part of the site's. For those with a passion for ancient history, be sure to extend your stop to explore the area's many prehistoric sites, and visit the exhibition center.

name: Mocorito
description: As you enter Mocorito through its welcoming arches, you'll feel transported to an oasis amidst the semi-desert landscape. Situated between the ocean and nearby mountain ranges, Mocorito offers a unique blend of natural beauty and vibrant festivities, and has been referred to as the "Athens of Sinaloa" due to its deep connection to the fine arts. The town proudly boasts the Dr. Enrique González Martínez Cultural Centre, a vibrant hub that serves as a platform for frequent performances and cultural events. Whether you're drawn to the lively band music of the city or seek outdoor adventures like fishing or experiencing the ancient sport of Ulama, Moorito captures the essence of the northern region. Indulge in the famous chilorio taco, a local delicacy, and try other delectable treats like chorizo cakes, hams and cheeses. Immerse yourself in a town that embraces its artistic soul, showcases its natural treasures and tantalizes your palate.

name: Lagos de Moreno
description: The pride of the people is alive and well in Lagos de Moreno. From its colonial architecture to its colourful streets, you can marvel at the beauty of Lagos de Moreno from the time the sun shines over this city until the night when the moon illuminates the streets. A wealthy colonial centre, Lagos de Moreno embraced the once wildly popular Baroque architecture, and it is reflected in its main bridge with its ornamentations. It is without wonder that this historic centre was declared a UNESCO World Heritage site. In the main square, you can visit the House of Culture, which houses many Baroque pieces, as well as colonial history and Aztec relics. Surrounded by green, you can revel at the beautiful Mesa Redonda, a beautiful shelf mountain mirroring that of Table Rock in Capetown.

name: Al Ain
description: The area around Al Ain has been settled for at least 8,000 years, thanks in large part to its oasis. A verdant gem on the border of the world's largest continuous sand desert, it's said Sheikh Zayed, the father of the UAE, was born under a tree here. Today, the Al Ain Oasis UNESCO World Heritage site where visitors can wander through a 1,200-hectare date-palm forest, which is still fed with the same 3,000-year-old irrigation techniques. The Al Ain Zoo is a great place for animal lovers, and has an added cultural significance because it was founded by Sheikh Zayed to protect endemic wildlife. Culture-lovers will also want to visit the 19th century Al Jahili Fort, which is now a museum with an exceptional exhibition of photographs from the 40s. For truly unique experience, head to the last camel souk in the UAE (near IKEA), to see a timeless tradition live on.

name: Mombasa
description: The culture of Mombasa is nearly impossible to reduce to a single concept. Centuries of influence from Portugal, India, Arabia and Africa have left it in chaos, but in this chaos there is still a sense of order, as any visitor can find something which suits them. In the Old Town, visit Fort Jesus, an old stronghold of the first Portuguese rule in the 1500s (also a UNESCO World Heritage Site). Peruse the city's many bazaars for souvenir shopping, or to discover a treasure trove of local goods. But of course, don't forget that this is a city of beaches - check out Bamburi and Shanzu beaches specifically for clean swimming and scenic beauty.
