name: Santo Domingo de la Calzada
address.addr1: Santo Domingo de la Calzada, La Rioja, Spain
description: Situated on the banks of the Oja River, Santo Domingo de la Calzada marked an important and arduous point for pilgrims along the French Route to Santiago de Compostela. Committed to making it easier for them to cross this difficult terrain, Dominic de la Calzada first built a bridge across the river Oja to facilitate passage, followed by a hospital and a hotel. He also began construction of the town's Cathedral of Santo Domingo de la Calzada, which now serves as his final resting place. After his death, his followers maintained the village which later took his name, and continued his work. Today, a large number of the inhabitants of Santo Domingo de la Calzada still live within the partially walled old quarter. Its narrow network of medieval streets make for the perfect setting for an afternoon stroll as you explore the history of this quaint, but significant, Spanish town.

name: Vizille
description: Dominating the little town of Vizille, this stately chateau dates back to the 17th century, when it was built by the Dukes of Lesdiquieres. In 1780 Claude Perier bought the estate, and invited the disgruntled parliament of Grenoble to meet here - a forum that had been prohibited by the king. Known as the Assembly of Vizille, this progressive meeting is considered the first portion of the French Revolution, and the reason Perier and his estate made it through the turmoil unscathed. Surrounding the chateau is a 100 hectare park, which is so expansive it transitions from a wooded landscape with its own fish farm, to a meticulously maintained garden with footbridges and waterways filled with fish and swans. The chateau's opulent interior, filled with period furnishings tells the story of the French Revolution through its collection of exceptional artwork and artefacts. For more information and to view the museum's hours, please visit http://www.domaine-vizille.fr/

name: Czestochowa
description: As the national shrine of Poland, Jasna Góra Monastery is understandably a sight to behold. Regarded by many as Poland's spiritual capital, Częstochowa welcomes hundreds of pilgrims from all over the world and operates as the centre of Polish Catholicism. The Black Madonna of Częstochowa (also known as Our Lady of Częstochowa) is a beloved icon of the Virgin Mary. Difficult to date due to damage inflicted by Hussite raiders in 1430, legend goes that the icon was painted by Luke the Evangelist on a table built by Jesus. During Nazi occupation, Hitler prohibited pilgrimages to Jasna Góra, but many still secretly made the journey and after Poland was liberated in 1945, half a million pilgrims journeyed to Częstochowa to express their gratitude. Later during the Cold War, Jasna Góra was a center of anti-Communist resistance. A place of both religious and historical significance, Częstochowa is a moving and awe-inspiring visit regardless of one's faith.

name: Bremen
description: Bremen is home to many cultural monuments, many of which line the stunning Marktplatz in its Old Town. Dominating the skyline is 11th century Cathedral, which combines Romanesque, Gothic, and a dash of Gothic Revival. Along with beautiful art and architecture, the Cathedral houses several 400 year old mummies, and a fascinating museum. Next door is the stunning Brick Gothic Town Hall, a UNESCO-listed structure that's one of the finest examples of the style in all of Europe. Home to the Senate of Bremen, the Town Hall also houses the world famous Rastkeller restaurant. Regardless of your dining plans, its worth taking a peek at the restaurant, particularly if you enjoy a glass of wine. Along with a choice of over 600 German wines, the restaurant owns the twelve oldest wines in the world. Walking re rest of Bremen's Old Town, you'll be treated to many well-preserved buildings brought to life by street cafes, street performers, and locals going about their everyday business.

name: Santanyi
description: In the southeast of Mallorca, Santanyi beckons with Balearic charm. Just four kilometers from the town center, its beaches offer a serene escape. laça Major, the heart of the town, is a captivating blend of sandstone facades, swaying palm fronds, and azure skies. Enclosed by remnants of a medieval city wall, Santanyi's old town resonates with history. Porta Murada, a 16th-century tower, stands as a testament to bygone eras. Plaça Major, a central meeting place, boasts three-story stone houses, their ground floors housing charming cafes and restaurants. Art enthusiasts will find galleries at every turn, showcasing a diverse array of creations. For shopping, fashion boutiques line the main road toward Plaça Major. Culinary delights await in Santanyi's restaurants, offering Mallorcan and international cuisine. Saturdays unveil Santanyi's vibrant market scene, a delightful exploration of curiosities. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast, browse galleries, and savor a delicious dinner in one of the town's excellent restaurants.

name: The Living Rainforest
address.addr1: The Living Rainforest, Hampstead Norreys, Thatcham RG18 0TN, UK
description: Housed under 20,000 sq ft of glass, The Living Rainforest is a unique conservation project that brings the wildlife from 2 different rainforest climates to temperate England. Here, over 700 plants and animals, some of which are endangered, immerse visitors in the sights, sounds, and smells of the rainforest. The Keeper Experience offers visitors the rare opportunity to get up-close and personal with the rainforest creatures - from feeding to behind the scenes access, and some incomparable photo opportunities. For more information, please visit livingrainforest.org

name: Borjomi
description: Famed for its globally-renowned mineral water, Borjomi is a premier tourist destination in Georgia. Since the 1830s, Borjomi's mineral baths and springs, nestled near the City Park, have been an invigorating retreat as they are believed to have healing properties. Originally reserved for the elite, these therapeutic waters are now accessible to all visitors at affordable rates. The city's verdant and well-groomed Central Park is where one finds the original mineral water springs, although the springs are scattered all around the city. Offering a refreshing escape, the park leads to the sulfur baths. Beyond the city's boundaries, adventure beckons in the form of Borjomi-Kharagauli National Park, a place of pure Georgian natural beauty.

name: Bunratty Castle
description: Bunratty Castle was built in 1425 on the site of an even older fortification and was made the seat of the powerful O'Brien clan in the early 16th century. In the 19th century, the castle was only used intermittently, and needed four years of restoration work when the 7th Viscount Gort purchased it in 1956. Lord Gort filled Bunratty with his collection of furniture, tapestries, and artwork dating from around 1600 to give visitors a glimpse of Ireland's noble past. Along with the obligatory gardens, the grounds of Bunratty Castle host a Folk Park where over 30 buildings, including a pub and school bring a 19th century village to life. For a real taste of the Middle Ages, Bunratty Castle offers a Medieval Banquet where visitors can enjoy a four-course meal while being entertained by the Bunratty Castle Singers (add extra time for this). For more information, please visit https://www.bunrattycastle.ie/

name: Gjirokaster
description: Originating from the 4th century hilltop castle, this UNESCO World Heritage Site offers visitors unspoiled Balkan beauty. In fact, the second largest fortress in the Balkans maintains a downed American fighter to memorialize their resistance to Western influence. As you work your way through the town's cobblestone streets to the bazaar, with its 16th century mosque, you can stop to visit some of the town's iconic stone buildings. One of the most characteristic is the magnificent 19th century home of the Zekati family, with its twin towers and carved wood ceilings. While there, be sure to try some of the regional specialties like pasha qofte, shapkat, or oshaf with dried figs.

name: Plovdiv
description: Continuously inhabited since 6000 BC, the ancient city of Plovdiv is a living record of Bulgaria's history. Here visitors can see remnants of Roman rule in an archaeological complex containing possibly the best-known antiquity in Bulgaria - the ancient theatre. Other eras are being represented as well through the gorgeous churches, cathedrals, synagogues, and mosques which each tell a tale of the different stages of Plovdiv's history, while the striking architecture of the old town comes from the Bulgarian national revival.

name: Trentham Estate and Gardens
description: First mentioned as a royal manor in the Domesday Book in 1086, Trentham Estate & Gardens are one of the great swan songs of the 20th century. By the 19th century, Trentham was an elegant mansion with cues taken from Buckingham Palace and Westminster, a sprawling landscape park designed by Lancelot Brown, and formal gardens by Charles Barry. However, the estate was abandoned in the early 20th century, and its main hall demolished. After 15 years of restoration, the estate's 725 acre garden are some of the best in the UK. Visitors can wander the floral labyrinth or enjoy a peaceful stroll along the mile-long lake. Afterwards, you can set sail aboard the electrically powered Miss Elizabeth or ride the miniature railway. There's also a variety of more adventurous activities, a shopping village with 64 shops, and even a Monkey Forest with free-roaming macaques.

name: Grantchester Village
description: Grantchester Village was first mentioned in the Domesday Book back in 1086, and has quietly passed through the following centuries. Its idyllic lifestyle made it an attractive escape for academics from nearby Cambridge University - which probably explains why Grantchester is said to have the world's highest concentration of Nobel laureates. In 1897, Cambridge Students convinced the Orchard House to serve tea in the apple orchard, which attracted writers like Rupert Brooke and Virginia Woolf. It was Brooke who was responsible for solidifying the town as a relaxing retreat, particularly because of his poem reminiscing about his time spent living in the vicarage. Today, the town and its charming 12th century church attract an additional set of visitors, who came looking to see the setting of the TV drama 'Grantchester'. This town's all about taking it slow, so enjoy a quiet walk along the river, and then sit down for a cup of tea under the apple trees.

name: Santa Maria Atzompa
description: Santa Maria Atzompa can trace its heritage back to around the 7th century, when it was founded as a satellite city to the nearby Zapotec capital of Monte Alban. Even 1500 years ago, Atzompa was renowned for its ceramics - a tradition that has persevered through today. In fact around 90% of the population are involved in making pottery. Take a stroll through the Mercado de Artesanías to view their handiwork, with items ranging from pots and cups to lampshades and animal figures – those with the dark green glaze are Atzompa's signature "barro verde". Or, if you're more of a history lover, head to the Atzompa Archaeological Site. Formal excavations only began in 2009, and in that time, archaeologists have uncovered three ball courts, two sumptuous residences, several temples and a large kiln that you can enjoy without the crowds of Monte Alban. Plus, the Museo Comunitario de Atzompa 2km down the road exhibits some excellent pottery pieces found at the site, including detailed effigies and huge storage pots.

name: Tequisquiapan
description: Founded in by the Spanish in 1551, the heart of Tequisquiapan has remained largely unchanged for the past 300 years. The cobbled streets are lined with colonial houses in pastel hues, with the pink, Neo-Classical Church of Santa María de la Asunción dominating the main square. There's a large population of indigenous Otomi people, who are easily identifiable by their vibrant dress, who offer handicrafts at the town's market. The many spas and waterparks around the city fill their pools with natural spring water said to have restorative properties, but for more adult homeopathic medication, Tequisquiapan is also part of the Querétaro wine route. While viticulture was only introduced here in the 1960s, its become such an important industry that grapes are featured on the coat of arms and the city hosts the National Cheese and Wine Fair every year!

name: Temuco
description: Temuco began as a humble military encampment built in 1881 during the Occupation of the Araucanía. Within a year, streets were laid, and by the end of the decade, the population had ballooned to over 10,000. Located in a valley halfway between the Pacific and the Andes, Temuco is best known for its location - it's known as the gateway to the lake district to the south and Conguillio National Park to the northeast and the ski resort of Volcán (Volcano) Llaima. But two universities give Temuco a lively air, and it's a great place to make a pitstop to connect with local culture. Head down to Plaza Ánibal Pinto, Temuco's main square, to see the "Monumento a la Araucania'' statue commemorating the area's different groups, including the Mapuche. Then dive deeper into local history at the excellent Museo Regional Auracania, which has thousands of artifacts. From there, grab a bite of local fare (Restaurante Rapa Nui is a local favorite), or savor the city's German heritage with a beer and chorrillana at Beermania.

name: Cheongju
description: Cheongju contains archaeological finds from the Old Stone Age and Paleolithic settlements, making it an important city in the region. Amidst the Cheongju Mountains lies the Sangdang Mountain Fortress (Sangdangsanseong), a majestic structure with 3-to-4-meter-tall walls stretching over 4.2 kilometers in circumference. Nearby, the Cheongju National Museum showcases cultural artifacts from the region, preserving its heritage for generations to come. For those intrigued by the art of printing, the Heungdeoksa Temple Site houses the Early Printing Museum, where the oldest existing book printed with movable metal type, Jikji, was printed. Cheongju embraces modernity as well, as seen in the MMCA Cheongju, a contemporary art haven housed in a restored tobacco factory. Art enthusiasts from all corners of Korea flock to this museum to appreciate diverse exhibitions. A unique experience awaits at Pocheon Herb Island Theme Park, nestled in the picturesque mountainous area. With various themes from traditional Korean villages to whimsical fairy tales, visitors can explore replicas of iconic landmarks and immerse themselves in a world of enchantment.

name: Camiri
description: Stroll through the bustling streets of Camiri and marvel at its colonial-era buildings adorned with intricate facades and vibrant murals. Explore local markets overflowing with fresh produce, handmade crafts, and delicious street food, where the flavors and aromas of Bolivia come to life. Explore the fascinating paleontological museum, overflowing with fossils and life-sized replicas that bring the prehistoric world to life. Learn about the various dinosaur species that inhabited the region millions of years ago, and ignite your imagination with thoughts of these magnificent creatures. For those seeking cultural immersion, Camiri hosts a variety of festivals and events throughout the year, celebrating everything from traditional music and dance to indigenous rituals and customs.

name: Belfast
description: Formerly the world's leading linen manufacturer, Belfast is in reform after decades of division and has been recently recognized as a UNESCO City of Music for its vibrant music scene. Belfast is famous for its shipyards - everyone knows the story of the ill-fated Titanic - down on the docks, you'll find reconstructions, rides, and galleries, detailing its history all under one roof at the Titanic Belfast. Maritime heritage is the theme here at the harbor. For naval exhibitions, climb aboard HMS Caroline and SS Nomadic, or nearby, marvel at Samson & Goliath, two huge cranes, symbolic of this industrial shipyard. Green is the island of Ireland, and surrounding this Northern Irish city, there's plenty to behold! From Belfast Castle courtyard, atop Black Mountain, or through the gardens of Sir Thomas & Lady Dixon Park, you'll be spoilt for choice when searching for natural beauty. The city center offers more beautiful nature to admire at the Botanic Gardens. Here, floral frames and potted paths guide you past The Tropical Ravine, towards the city's treasured Ulster Museum. The strength of Belfast's people is honored throughout the city, at Peace Wall, Falls Road, and the Northern Ireland War Memorial. Join them at St. George's Market or for a pint at one of the lively pubs in the historic Cathedral Quarter.

name: Pula
description: Pula, the largest city in Istria, is situated at the base of the Istrian peninsula and on seven hills. It's a historically rich town with one of the earliest traces of human life. The friendly small-town appeal, mild climate, and beautiful sea attracts many visitors to Pula. The city houses a wealth of Roman architecture. Its most notable is the preserved Roman amphitheater, which dominates the center of the city. The amphitheater was built in the 1st century AD and was once the site of gladiator combat. Today, it's a popular venue for summer concerts and festivals. Another notable feature of Pula is the Temple of Augustus. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Roma and Emperor Augustus and houses a collection of ancient sculptures. Many Venetian and Austro-Hungarian monuments can also be found throughout the city and in the main square. Pula is the perfect destination for culture lovers and for those aim to experience the beauty of nature.

name: Tata
description: Tata is the perfect outdoorsy spot, with an English garden, large lakes, and popular outdoor swimming pools. There is also a spa/sauna in town to relax and unwind. The Renaissance Tata Fortress is one of the jewels of the city. The fortress (including a museum) sits beautifully next to the Old Lake. There's also an open-air geological museum which features the town's local history. Don't forget to check out Tata's many festivals, outdoor concerts, and sporting events in the summertime!

name: Xtampak
description: Xtampak literally translates to "old / ancient walls", and true to its name, the city dates back to around 400 BC. Built on a hilltop, and surrounded by a series of agricultural terraces, at its peak, the city was the capital of the Chene Maya and home to an estimated 10,000 people. Because of its location, Xtampak was a melting pot of Chene and Puuc cultures, which is evident in its hybrid architecture. The excavated city center is a network of interconnected plazas, surrounded by temples and other magnificent monuments. The most impressive structure is undoubtedly the three-story palace, with its 44 rooms and two internal stairways, which is considered one of the finest Mayan buildings of its kind.

name: Rummu Quarry & Prison
description: The Rummu Quarry and Prison is a veritable Atlantis of historic buildings that have dipped below the surface of crystal blue waters. The beach and diving attraction gets its name from the small, nearby town of Rummu and is the site of a former Soviet prison constructed in the 1940's. Around 400 prisoners were forced to pump water out of the pits under harsh conditions and since Estonia's independence in 1991, the abandoned site filled with water, forming a stunning lake. For a fee of €3, visit the secret location and explore the buildings on dry land. If you're experienced, you can go scuba diving through the clear water and see the underwater buildings, or rent a canoe for €25 and paddle along the lake. Ashy dunes surround the site, from the top of which you can admire the impressive view of the prison and lake before heading to the beach cafe for a refreshing drink or ice cream.

name: Sunyani
description: Sunyani, Ghana, beckons with a captivating blend of breathtaking landscapes, rich cultural heritage, and authentic Ghanaian charm. Wander through the city's bustling streets and vibrant markets, where colorful stalls brim with fresh produce, handmade crafts, and traditional wares. Explore Sunyani's rich cultural heritage at landmarks such as the Sacred Heart Cathedral and the Sunyani Traditional Palace. Marvel at the intricate architecture and learn about the city's storied past through informative exhibits and guided tours. Nature enthusiasts will delight in the natural beauty surrounding Sunyani, with its verdant forests, tranquil rivers, and scenic waterfalls waiting to be explored. Take a hike through the lush countryside, go birdwatching in the pristine wilderness, or simply relax and unwind in the serene surroundings. Photo by: Yawsmith, CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Caral
description: Caral was built around 2600 BC, making it one of the world's first urban civilizations alongside those in Egypt, China, India, and Mesopotamia. Along with residences, palaces, and temples, Caral had an amphitheater, and in an interesting parallel to the world's other major civilizations, 6 monumental pyramids built around its central plaza. Archaeological findings showed it a peaceful society and a large collection of carved bone instruments points to a community with time for recreation. Around 1800 BC, the city of 3,000 was simply abandoned and left to the elements. Despite being the model for the subsequent Andean cultures that would rise and fall for the next 4,000 years, Caral sees relatively few visitors, meaning you usually have the site almost to yourself. Along with its building's Caral boasts one of Peru's most significant geoglyphs, resemble a terrified old man, which has been found in other locations in Peru.

name: Knaresborough Castle
description: Knaresborough Castle was first built around 1100 by a Norman baron, quickly rising to fame when it sheltered the assassins of Thomas Becket. Knaresborough grew in importance through the Middle Ages, becoming a royal residence when Philippa of Hainault, wife of Edward III, took possession of the castle in 1331. During the English Civil War, the castle withstood a 6 month siege before finally surrendering to Parliamentary forces. After the Parliamentary victory, the castle was mostly dismantled, its stones being used to build much of the town centre. Today, the visitors can explore the ruins on their own, or join a guided tour to learn more about Knaresborough's royal residents, visit the dungeon, and sneak through the secret underground exit. There's also a Tudor-era Courtroom Museum, hands-on activities in the 'Life in a Castle', and even Civil War costumes to try on. Keep an eye out for the castle's famous ravens, at least one of which can (supposedly) speak.

name: Glendalough
description: In the 6th century, St. Kevin made his way to Glendalough to establish a monastic settlement. This developed into one of the premier ecclesiastical settlements in Ireland - a "Monastic City" that thrived until its monastery was destroyed by the Normans in 1214, and its diocese merged with Dublin. Today, Glendalough is a top destination for people looking to experience both Ireland's natural beauty and its rich history. The monastic settlement is accessed through the fortified gateway, after which you'll discover the remains of several medieval buildings. Even from a distance, it's easy to spot Glendalough's 34-meter tall round tower. Once you get closer, you'll find it watches over a cemetery with one of the largest and most unusual High Crosses in Ireland. A pleasant walk through the wooded valley leads past several other medieval churches, including the Romanesque cathedral. As there's only limited signage, we'd recommend stopping at the Glendalough Visitor Centre to learn more about the site before you set out. For more information, please visit http://www.glendalough.ie/

name: Dalaguete
description: Dalaguete is well known for its many sharply-rising mountains, including Cebu's highest mountain, Osmeña Peak, but the town itself is often overlooked. The town is dotted with historic buildings and colonial houses, the most notable of which is the beautiful Baroque Parish Church of San Guillermo de Aquitania. Built in the early 19th century, the church doubled as a defensive structure to protect the townspeople from Moro attacks. The coral stone facade is ornamented with floral carvings, while the interior covered in colorful murals. And as the "vegetable basket" of Cebu, the local market is also worth taking a look at, if just to see volume and variety of the area's agricultural production.

name: Lake Bohinj
description: Bohinj is the largest glacial lake in Slovenia (approx. 4km in length). It is located in the Julian Alps and is surrounded by nature. This natural pearl rivals Lake Bled for the title of Slovenia's most beautiful lake. Visitors are attracted to Lake Bohinj for its unspoiled nature, crystal clear emerald-green water, and relaxed atmosphere. Not yet overwhelmed by mass tourism, Bohinj is a peaceful and relaxing destination spot. Enjoy the stunning scenery by taking the Vogel Cable Car up the mountains for a fantastic lake view. For the adventure lovers, Bohinj has plenty activities to offer including: swimming, canoeing, cycling, and hiking.

name: Kagera Falls
description: The Kagera Falls, or Chutes de la Karera, is a series of waterfalls located in southeastern Burundi. This beautiful natural site occupies a whopping 142 hectares and encompasses several unique cascades. Nyakai I is a standout, and situated right next to the parking area. If you're feeling daring, hike to Nyakai II. While it's the smallest of the four falls it's a perfect spot for an impromptu dip. But the real showstopper is Karera Falls, the tallest waterfall in the area, which is fed by the merging Nyakai and Mwaro Falls. The cascade is so beautiful and important to locals that it's been added to the UNESCO World Heritage tentative List in the Hybrid (cultural and natural) category. The flow of the waterfalls varies by rainfall, so they are most impressive during the wet season.

name: El Escorial
address.addr1: Av Juan de Borbón y Battemberg, s/n, 28200 San Lorenzo de El Escorial, Madrid, Spain
description: In 1558, following the death of his father, Charles V, Felipe II commissioned the construction of the San Lorenzo de El Escorial Monastery, in the hopes of firmly establishing the House of Austria in Spain, creating an eternal memorial for his relatives, and to atone for the church dedicated to San Lorenzo destroyed in the Battle of San Quintin. Juan Bautista de Toledo oversaw the construction until his death in 1567, when Juan de Herrera took over the project. Among the many attractions, the pantheon where all the Spanish Hapsburg are entombed, the battles gallery, the basilica and the bourbon palace are particular highlights. El Escorial also houses one of the largest reliquaries in the world, and artwork by Titian, Tintoretto, El Greco, Velázquez, and others. The richly frescoed library contains over 40,000 priceless manuscripts, including the collection of the sultan Zidan Abu Maali, who ruled Morocco from 1603 to 1627.

name: Trier
description: You could spend a century or so touring the many fine-wine producing villages of the Moselle, but with time limited an idea is to get through as many wines as you can at the Kesselstatt wine bar in Trier, which is easy to spot thanks to the full-size replica of a Roman wine ship outside. When in Trier go Roman, steep yourself in the city's imperial past by visiting its wealth of Roman sites. The massive Porta Nigra, the best-preserved Roman gate north of the Alps, the hauntingly well-preserved Basilica of the Emperor Constantine, the largest single room structure surviving from Roman times, and, close by the Cathedral, home, allegedly, of Jesus' last suit of clothes. The important early Gothic Church of Our Lady is linked to the Cathedral, the latter three buildings forming one UNESCO site. That Emperor of Communism Karl Marx was born in Trier, and his birth-place in Bruckenstrasse is a museum with interesting personal Marxian items.

name: Levens Hall
description: Levens Hall began as a simple fortified tower in the 14th century, but during the Elizabethan era was extended and filled with splendid panelling and plasterwork, with further additions made in the 17th and 19th centuries. Home to the Bagot family for the past 400 years, the manor interior is filled with fine historic furnishings, including Cordova leather wall coverings, an amazing collection of Jacobean furniture, and an impressive are collection with paintings by Rubens, Lely, and Cuyp, as well as the earliest English patchwork. The world famous gardens date back to 1694, with topiaries, hedges, and colorful flower beds combining into an extraordinary environment. The topiary garden is made up of over 100 specimens sculpted into abstract shapes, pyramids, and even colossal chess men. Some of the shrubs are over 300 years old, making Levens Hall's topiary the oldest in the world. For more information, please visit levenshall.co.uk

name: Mottisfont Abbey
description: Originally a medieval priory, Mottisfont Abbey became a private home in the 16th century when monasteries were dissolved and King Henry VIII gave the property to one of his favourite statesmen. In the 18th century, the Mill family demolished some of the older areas, such as the medieval cloisters, and gave the mansion its current appearance, and adding 'Abbey' to its name. In 1934, Maud and Gilbert Russell purchased Mottisfont, and made it the nucleus for a fashionable artistic and political circle, hosting writers like Ian Fleming, and commissioning unique artworks such as the stupendous trompe-l'œil Gothic illusions in her salon. Today, visitors can catch glimpses of the buildings medieval origins while marvel at this glamorous room and admiring the 20th century art collection. Outside, visitors can enjoy a colorful walk through the walled gardens, which lead to the nature park and a riverside path. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/mottisfont

name: Villarrica
description: Founded in 1552, Villarrica is the sixth oldest city in Chile, but between wars with the indigenous tribes and multiple volcanic eruptions, much of its early colonial past has been erased. Instead, it's the blending of German, Dutch, and indigenous Mapuche cultures, with a sprinkling of modernity that defines the city's atmosphere. Villarrica never quite reached the tourist-destination status of nearby Pucón, but that makes stopping here even more worthwhile. The view of the Villarrica Volcano across the lake can't be beat, and makes for a dramatic backdrop for lounging on the beach. And the rustic Mercado Nehuen is a great place to pick up some artisan crafts like woven blankets and wood carvings without feeling like you're shopping in a tourist knick-knack shop.

name: Haapsalu
description: Haapsalu is situated on the shores of Haapsalu Bay, surrounded by picturesque forests and meadows, and radiates a ghostly aura of age-old legends and apparitions. The town dates back to 1279 and many of its original buildings still stand, including the episcopal castle in which the storied "Lady in White" haunts the once male-dominated fortress after being impaled on the castle walls. While touring the spectral town, stop by one of the three famous salt mud spas, frequented by the royal Russian Romanov family when they first learned of it in 1825. Pick up a famous Haapsalu shawl with delicate craftsmanship made by local women, popularized in the 19th century. The town also has a rich cultural scene, with numerous festivals and events throughout the year. One of the most popular events is the White Lady Festival in summer, celebrating the famous legend, and the August Blues Festival held every August.

name: Lourdes
description: Settled since Roman times, the quiet mountain town existed in relative obscurity for centuries, best known for the fortified chateau rising above the town from a rocky escarpment. All of that changed in 1858, when 14-year-old Bernadette Soubirous was visited by the Virgin Mary 18 times in a rocky grotto. The Vatican acknowledged the visions and beatified Bernadette in 1933. Today, it's the 3rd most visited pilgrimage site in all of Christianity, making the town the second most popular destination in France. A unique experience regardless of faith, the neo-Byzantine cathedral presides over visitors flocking to the grotto and bathing in the site's healing waters. On the other side of town, the château fort de Lourdes has retained elements dating back to the 11th century, and offers visitors great views along with the Pyrenean Museum, which presents the most important collections on the history of the French and Spanish Pyrenees.

name: Ayscoughfee Hall
description: Ayscoughfee Hall was built in the mid-15th century for a wealthy wool merchant. In the 17th century, the house passed to the Johnson family, with Maurice Johnson notably founding the Spalding Gentlemen's Society, an antiquarian society that counted Sir Isaac Newton and Alfred Tennyson as members. Ayscoughfee was purchased on behalf of the people of Spalding in 1896 in memory of Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee, and donated to the town to celebrate the coronation of King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra in 1902. Today the house is a history museum, where you can admire not only the stately furnishings, but get a general education through a variety exhibitions, ranging from the life of a Victorian child, to the etymology of local place names. In the surrounding garden, you can enjoy a pleasant stroll to admire the house's facade, tall yew hedges, an early ice-house, an ornamental lake, and a World War I memorial. For more information please visit sholland.gov.uk/article/5262/Ayscoughfee-Hall Photo by Thorvaldsson under CC BY 3.0 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ayscoughfee_Hall_Museum.JPG)

name: Standen House and Garden
address.addr1: W Hoathly Rd, East Grinstead RH19 4NE, UK
description: The Standen House and Garden were built for the Beale family in the 1890s by renowned architect Philip Webb, the 'Father of the Arts and Crafts Movement'. Complimenting Webb's architecture, the interior is furnished by Morris & Co., with ceramics by William De Morgan, and metalwork by W. A. S. Benson - all the big names of the Arts & Crafts movement under one roof! Today, visitors enter the house as guests of the Beales, and get to see the house as the family would have used it throughout the day. Along with learning about this non-conformist family's lives through letters and diary entries, visitors will learn about the Arts & Crafts movement through the collection of beautiful furniture and embroideries, many completed by Mrs. Beale and her daughters. True to William Morris' view that the garden should be a continuation of the house, Mrs. Beale's Arts & Crafts style garden organically blends the local and exotic in a semi-structured environment. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/standen-house-and-garden

name: Howth
description: Howth dates back to at least the Middle Ages, having been attacked by the Vikings around 819. The Irish and localized Norse forces of the isolated village held out against the invading Normans for 8 years, finally falling in 1177. In the following centuries, it developed into an important trading port, with a large harbour being built in the 19th century, and is now a seaside suburb of Dublin. Today, the charming town is one of the most popular destinations in the country, with many Dubliners coming here for fresh sea air, and even fresher seafood. Down on the harbour wall is the 19th century lighthouse, which provides a historic setting to watch the local fishermen go about their day, and maybe catch the seals play. Many visitors come here specifically to get out of town and explore the walking trails surrounding the town, with the 6-kilometer-long cliff walk offers an easy way to take in the rocky coast.

name: Margilan
description: Journey to the heart of silk production in Margilan, Uzbekistan. Wander through bustling workshops, the rhythmic clatter of looms a constant hum. Witness skilled artisans with nimble fingers transforming silkworm cocoons into threads of shimmering beauty. Explore shops overflowing with vibrantly colored silks, each bolt a testament to Margilan's artistic legacy. Margilan isn't just a shopper's paradise; it's a cultural feast for the senses. Delve into the labyrinthine corridors of the Margilan Bazaar, a kaleidoscope of sights and smells. Haggle for unique souvenirs alongside friendly locals, perhaps a hand-embroidered skullcap or a silk scarf in a dazzling hue. Savor steaming bowls of Uzbek plov (national rice dish) enjoyed at family-run restaurants, the air filled with the warmth of hospitality.

name: Parana
description: The charming city of Parana, the capital of the Entre Rios Province, was founded in 1730 by inhabitants of the nearby city of Santa Fe. In 1853, it was made the capital of the Argentine Confederation, which paved the way for its development into the thriving port city it is today. Start your visit at the magnificent Cathedral of Parana, a beautifully preserved cathedral with two iconic blue steeples. Then head over to the riverside Urquiza Park. A 44-hectare green space overlooking the Parana River, its perfect for a quiet walk amongst lush greenery and opulent fountains while admiring the panoramic views of the river. Continue along the waterfront to unwind at Thompson Beach, where you can try some local cuisine, like freshly caught fish, at the beachfront restaurants, all while admiring the serene shoreline.

name: Bourges
description: An ancient Celtic capital, the Bituriges tribe who founded the city were of such importance that Bourges was the only city not burned by Vercingetorix. Through the middle ages, the city grew in stature, being named Capital of France by Charles VII. The city's UNESCO-listed Gothic cathedral is considered one of the finest in the country. The elaborate facade, with its abundance of decoration and extensive use of flying buttresses often draws comparisons to Notre Dame in Paris. Pay careful attention to the intricately carved depiction of the Last Judgement on the tympanum, and the extraordinary stained glass windows from the 13th century depicting biblical stories. In the 15th century, Jacques-Coeur, the son of a local merchant, become treasurer to the King. With the wealth this position brought him, he constructed this magnificent palace filled with sumptuously sculpted ornamentation, monumental fireplaces, and in a display of medieval extravagance - indoor toilets.

name: St John's
description: St. John's is the palm-fringed Antiguan capital that paints a vivid picture of Caribbean life, emanating a laid-back atmosphere where the aroma of jerk barbecue and the soulful tunes of Bob Marley fills the air. Stroll down Redcliffe Quay, a promenade hugging the waterfront, and soak in the hues of turquoise, red, and yellow historic buildings. Don't miss the vibrant Vegetable Market where bartering is an art. Fridays and Saturdays are prime times to explore the Public Market Complex for a variety of tropical produce, from hot peppers to mangoes. The island's passion for cricket is palpable at Recreation Ground, a cricket field that saw historic moments like the West Indies' triumph over England in 1986. Saint John's Cathedral, a marvel of baroque architecture crowned by twin towers, stands as the spiritual core of the island. Its mahogany-adorned interior evokes the ambiance of a majestic galleon. Nearby, Fort James offers a double delight, featuring both the 18th-century ruins of an English-built fort and a beautiful public beach where swimming and beach volleyball beckon.

name: Man
description: Ascend to a haven nestled amidst west-central Côte d'Ivoire's mountain ranges – Man, a captivating town where nature, culture, and adventure converge. Imagine standing at the foot of La Cascade, a majestic waterfall cascading down moss-covered rocks. The thunderous roar of the water fills the air as mist dances playfully, creating a scene straight out of a fairytale. Hike through lush greenery to hidden coves, or take a refreshing dip in the cool waters beneath the cascading falls. Man isn't just about scenic beauty; it's a cultural kaleidoscope. Delve into the heart of the bustling market, a sensory overload of sights and sounds. Friendly vendors showcase their wares, from intricately woven baskets adorned with colorful beads to hand-carved wooden sculptures depicting local folklore. Engage with the Dan and We people, their warm smiles and rich cultural heritage leaving a lasting impression. Photo by: Gillian Zouzoukov, CC BY-SA 3.0 , via Wikimedia Commons

name: Taroudant
description: One of the oldest cities in Morocco, Taroudant enjoyed a golden age during the Saadi Dynasty in the 16th century when Mohammed ash-Sheikh erected the city walls, as well as the great mosque and its minaret. The Saadians used Taroudant as a base to attack the Portuguese in Agadir. Today, these fortifications still stand, and the 5 gates mark the entrances to the city. The crenelated, red brick walls backed by the soaring, snow capped Anti-Atlas mountains makes for a jaw-dropping first impression. Taroudant's two main markets, the Berber market and the larger Arab souk, are much less aggressive than those in Marrakech. Art lovers shouldn't miss the Palais Claudio Bravo Camus, the former home of Spanish hyperrealist artist Claudio Bravo, where you'll see his work and pieces by friends like Picasso on a guided tour of the interior (and the beautiful garden and grounds are free to visit).

name: Coroico
description: Originally founded by the Spanish as a gold mining town above the river Quri Wayq'u, the colonial settlers relocated Coroico to its more defensible valley location in the early 18th century. The new location proved its worth after a number of native attacks, including during the Bolivian War of Independence, when Coroico's 500 inhabitants fended off an attack from 5000 Aymaras. Coroico is a major trade hub and agricultural center for the region, and a tropical retreat just outside of La Paz. The main attraction here is really just hanging out, especially in the airy main square, doing as the locals do. There's a charming colonial church on one end, and plenty of benches where you can sit and enjoy a fresh jugo and empanada. Things are especially lively on Saturdays and Sundays for the weekend market, and in general, you'll want to avoid visiting on Mondays when almost everything is closed.

name: Xunantunich
description: Founded around the same time as ceramics were invented, Xunantunich remained inconsequential until the end of the 7th century AD when its connection with the Naranjo solidified. This prosperity was short lived as the site was abandoned after a violent event around 750 AD, and wasn't resettled until the 9th century. Again, the city only enjoyed a few years of prosperity, being abandoned for the final time by 1000. Excavations at the site didn't begin until 1890, and almost immediately sightings of the ghost of a woman, dressed entirely in white with red, glowing eyes were reported. She haunts the steps of the 40-meter-tall Castillo, the second largest Mayan structure in Belize, which is ornamented with a monumental plaster frieze. A narrow staircase leads to the top of the pyramid, which gives a stunning view of the other ruins that dot the site - each of which beckon to visitors to discover their secrets.

name: Leicester
description: Founded by the Romans, Leicester is one of the oldest English cities, and one of its industrial capitals - specifically in hosiery. Though developed through the Industrial Revolution, and was severely damaged by bombings during World War II, you can still find many reminders of its Roman and Medieval heritage in its restored old town. Take a look at the ancient Baths, and 14th century Guildhall before heading to the Gothic St. Martin's Cathedral to view the burial place of King Richard III - the remains of the last Plantagenet king were rediscovered in 2012 beneath a nearby parking lot. If the modern age is more your thing, you can pay a visit to the National Space Center. However, Leicester is more a city of atmosphere than attractions - it's one of the most ethnically diverse cities in the United Kingdom, with cosmopolitan comforts like fine restaurants and trendy shops.

name: Ein Bokek
description: Backed by a rocky bluff, the string of resorts along Ein Bokek beach are the most popular place in Israel to enjoy the turquoise blue waters of the Dead Sea. 10 times saltier than the ocean, people have been coming to take advantage of the Dead Sea's skin-friendly properties for thousands of years. Unlike other Dead Sea Beaches, Ein Bokek faces evaporation pools kept full by Dead Sea Works pumps, so its shoreline isn't receding and there are no problems with sinkholes. The beach is a popular destination for locals and tourists alike, so it's likely you'll hear Hebrew, Arabic, and even Russian as you bob in the super-saline waters. And since Ein Bokek is part of a resort area, there are some welcome amenities like sunshades and beach chairs, water fountains, and vitally, showers.

name: Yahualica
description: Capturing the essence of the relaxing atmosphere and laissez-faire attitude of rural Mexico, Yahualica has attracted an interesting mix of visitors. Yahualica has piqued the interests of not only curious tourists, but the culinary connoisseurs with its reputation as having the best peppers in the world. The Chile de Arbol lives up to the culinary arts from the generations-long production practices to the soil and optimal climate of the area. Yahualica be sure to capture your cultural interest as well as your tastebuds. Walk through the Marcado Municipal to sample local and regional flavours. Relax at the Main Square Plaza or visit the Plaza de Toros, a North American example of the bullrings passed down from Spanish colonialism.

name: San Gil
description: San Gil was founded in 1689 after the Spanish conquest eradicated the indigenous people from the region. Nicknamed "the Land of Adventure", this small city is the outdoor-sports capital of Colombia. Adventure-seekers from around the world flock here for adrenaline-inducing activities like paragliding, rappelling, and most famously, whitewater rafting. The friendly city isn't on most "classic" itineraries, but stop by the 300-year-old square, where locals and tourists alike relax, shop, and eat and you'll get a taste of San Gil's character. The park is dominated by the elegant 18th century cathedral, which has some fantastic wooden ceilings. Natural lovers looking for something more laid-back can enjoy a stroll through the riverside Parque El Gallineral, where you can kick back at one of the restaurants or cafes.

name: Daugavpils
description: Starting as a castle built by the Livonian Order in the 13th century, the town of Daugavpils wasn't officially recognized until the 16th century. Surrounded by woods, rivers, and lakes, it's hard to believe this is Latvia's second largest city. Daugavpils was the birthplace of Mark Rothko, and its Daugavpils Mark Rothko Art Centre is the only place in Eastern Europe with his work on display, which is supplemented by interactive installation. This modern art complex is housed in the historic Daugavpils Fortress, the only unaltered 19th century fort in Northern Europe, making for a captivating double-feature. On the aptly named 'Church Hill', visitors will find four churches, each representing a different denomination, making for an amazing architectural ensemble, dominated by Latvia's largest Orthodox cathedral.

description: Perched on a 200 foot high rocky outcrop, 'Dracula's Castle' was actually founded by the Teutonic Knights in 1212, and rebuilt by the Saxons of Kronstadt under the permission of Louis I of Hungary in 1377. Despite its name, Prince Vlad, Stoker's inspiration for Dracula, never lived in the castle. However, it did serve as the royal residence between 1920 and 1957. A gift from the people of Brasov to Queen Marie. Today, the castle is a museum open to the public. Following underground passages and winding stairways through 60 timbered rooms, visitors can admire Queen Marie's collection of art and furniture, see weapons and armor dating from the 14th to the 19th centuries, and even take a closer look at the tools of torture.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: Contrary to popular belief, the Blue Lagoon is not a natural formation, but the excess water from the nearby geothermal plant that opened in 1976. Like elsewhere in Iceland, the plant uses naturally heated seawater to heat fresh water, which is then used to heat people's homes. When this seawater is no longer hot enough, it's pumped out into the lava field to be reabsorbed by the earth. However, the waters at the Svartsengi geothermal power station were so rich in silicates that they coated the porous lava rocks with mud, thus forming the Blue Lagoon. After some brave locals found that the mineral-rich waters were good for their skin, it soon became a popular local retreat, and is now one of the best spas in the world. Aside from the therapeutic properties, the milky blue waters in the middle of a lava field (part of the Reykjanes Peninsula UNESCO Geopark) are just aesthetically pleasing - which is probably why everyone from Bjork to Beyonce has been spotted here. Please note: as Iceland's most popular attraction, advance booking is required well in advance at www.bluelagoon.com

name: Caldas da Rainha
description: When the rheumatic Queen Leonor found the unpleasant smelling spring waters alleviated the pain from her affliction, she ordered the construction of a thermal hospital so that others might benefit. After spa therapy and the royal family fell out of favour, the town became famous for its ceramics. The Queen's hospital was reputed to be the largest ever built in Portugal at the time. If you're 'churched out', the Museu de José Malhoa houses the works of Malhoa and his contemporaries, particularly the famous ceramist Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro. The Museu de Cerâmica the old home of the Visconde de Sacavém displays a large collection of hand painted objects including tiles from the last two centuries.

name: Chirk Castle
description: Chirk Castle was built in 1295 by Roger Mortimer de Chirk to help support King Edward I's chain of fortresses across northern Wales. Over the next 700 years, the castle's inhabitants would transform the stark symbol of power into a lavish noble home while still retaining original historic elements. beautiful and eclectic collection. Visitors can see the medieval dungeons, and eccentric, era-spanning state rooms, including the 17th-century Long Gallery, stupendous 18th-century saloon, and 1920s style 'Bow Room', where the castle's connections to high society are on display. The castle's 5.5 acre gardens are renowned for their manicured lawns, clipped yews, and beautiful rose, shrub and rock gardens, culminating in a terrace overlooking the 18th century ha-ha and the Cheshire and Salop plains. For more information, please visit https://www.nationaltrust.org.uk/chirk-castle

name: Ragusa
description: Settled since the second millenium BC, Ragusa was devastated by an earthquake in 1693. Many of the villagers moved higher up the hill and founded Upper Ragusa, which was built in the lavish Baroque style, while Old Ragusa remained a separate entity until the two towns were fused in 1926. Today, both sections of the city are filled with enough Baroque landmarks Ragusa received UNESCO recognition. In the lower city, visitors can enjoy the views offered by the Hyblean Gardens before heading out to see the Basilica di San Giorgio, and tackle its 200 steps. En route to the upper city, St. Mary of the Stairs, sitting atop 242 steps, still bears some of its original Gothic features amongst the Baroque ornamentation. Dominating the upper city is the Cathedral of San Giovanni Battista, which was actually rebuilt twice after the earthquake as the first version wasn't extravagant enough.

name: Taormina
description: Established by Greek colonists in the 8th century BC, Taormina was their first colony on the island. While it remained an important settlements from ancient times through the Middle Ages, it lost relevance until Johann Wolfgang Goethe described it in his 1816 travelogue, and transformed it into a destination for 19th century creatives and intellectuals like Oscar Wilde, Friedrich Nietzsche, and Richard Wagner. Today, visitors will find reminders of the town's rich history, from the Ancient Theatre and the many artefacts preserved in the Antiquarium, to Lady Florence Trevelyan's hill-top gardens and exoticist buildings. Scattered through the town are charming squares, each crowned by their own monumental landmark, ranging from medieval churches, to the Gothic and Moorish Palazzo Corvaia. And with its splendid panoramic views, be sure to take some time to appreciate Sicily's stunning beauty - preferably while enjoying some of its excellent cuisine.

name: Rome
description: According to Roman mythology, Rome was founded by Romulus in 753 BC after killing his brother Remus over a dispute on which hill their city should be built on. Called the "Eternal City" for its long history, and the "City of Seven Hills", Rome's nicknames give a clue what to expect. Now home to nearly 3 million people, the Eternal City's long history is well-preserved in its many monuments and museums. Head to the UNESCO-listed city center to find most of Rome's most iconic monuments, like the Colosseum, Foro Romano, and Palatino. Along with its many ancient monuments, Rome was a major Renaissance center and the birthplace of the Baroque style and Neoclassicism. The Trevi Fountain, Sistine Chapel with Michaelangelo's famous ceiling, and Saint Peter's Basilica are all masterpieces. Save time for Rome's museums, like the Vatican Museums, the Musei Capitolini, the Borghese Gallery, and the Palazzo Barberini Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica to see the works of Masters up close.

name: Estremoz
description: Rising monolithically from the eastern Alentejo plains, this fortified city was once the seat of Dom Dinis, the monarch responsible for fortifying Portugal's frontiers against Spanish invasion. Its military significance strongly influenced the town's architectural style, right down to the local marble used for much of its construction. This historic upper quarter lies behind impressive 13th century ramparts, which protect the Tower of the Three Crowns keep and 14th century palace built in honour of King Dinis' wife, Dona Isabel, who lived her final moments here. Dona Isabel also lends her name to the 18th century Santa Isabel chapel, which tells her story in tiles. The Igreja da Misericórdia is a 16th century church which now houses the Museu Rural.

name: Trees of Mystery
description: Trees of Mystery is a captivating natural wonder nestled near Klamath, along U.S. Route 101. Its Trail of Tall Tales showcases around 50 awe-inspiring chainsaw sculptures and carvings that vividly depict the legendary logger Paul Bunyan and his intrepid crew. Explore the park's remarkable tree formations, including the Cathedral Tree; a semicircular cluster of nine trees sharing a single root system, the Brotherhood Tree, the Candelabra Tree, and the Elephant Tree, which resembles an elephant's trunk. For visitors seeking a unique perspective, the Skytrail aerial tramway, installed in 2001, provides a breathtaking 1/3-mile journey through the forest, offering a bird's-eye view of the park's captivating features. The tramway concludes at an observation deck that provides a scenic vista of the Pacific Ocean above the forest canopy. Visitors can explore from 9AM to 4PM, with the museum and gift shop open until 5PM and 5:30PM, respectively. Admission is all-inclusive, granting access to trails, the sky canopy, and the gondola, costing $25 for adults and $13 for children.

name: Manchester, VT
description: At the edge of the Green Mountains, Manchester was an affluent resort area during the 19th century. Abraham Lincoln's only surviving son even built his summer home here. While Lincoln himself never set foot in the Hildene Estate, the manor is filled with keepsakes, including his iconic stovepipe hat. And in another part of the mansion, you'll find the 1903 Pullman car used by President Teddy Roosevelt. A testament to the amazing natural surroundings, Orvis was founded here back in 1856. The American Museum of Fly Fishing is located right next door, and along with showcasing the history of American angling has mementos from famous fishing aficionados like Ernest Hemingway and Bing Crosby. The granite streets are lined with quaint houses, mom and pop shops and factory outlets that will keep you busy as you meander the historic downtown. But you're in Vermont, so hiking's on your mind! Make the 4.7 mile out and back hike to the beautiful Lye Brook Falls. Or, trek to the top of Mt. Equinox for great views - and the chance to ride the alpine slide back down.

name: Villa Traful
description: Villa Traful, a haven of untouched nature nestled in the heart of the Andean Patagonian mountain range, beckons travelers to discover its serene beauty. Embark on long walks through the captivating landscapes, where Cerro Negro and Penitentes offer breathtaking scenic overlooks of Lake Traful, the Lanín volcano, and the Villarrica volcano. Delight in the cascades that adorn the region, and explore the submerged forest beneath the lake's surface, revealing the tips of 60 cypress trees. The village thrives as a tourist center, offering cozy cottages, inns, camping sites, and a myriad of services supporting outdoor activities like fishing, trekking, and horseback riding. For fishing enthusiasts, Machónico and Pichi Traful rivers, Traful Lake, and Catarata stream provide an ideal habitat for various trout species. The crystal-clear waters, pollution-free environment, and picturesque beaches make Villa Traful a perfect retreat for aquatic activities and leisure.

name: Ptuj
description: With evidence of a Stone Age settlement, Ptuj was first recorded as a Celtic stronghold that was conquered by the Romans in the 1st century BC. The town has such a rich history, that it's illegal to dig deeper than a meter, less an artefact be destroyed. Today, the city is a is a charming throwback to the past, overlooked by its 18th century castle. Here, visitors will find the largest collection of musical instruments in the country, as well as stupendous views of the town below. Wandering the city streets brings visitors past beautiful landmarks, including a Roman tombstone from the 2nd century, or the Art Nouveau Town Hall.

name: Newcastle
description: Named after the 5th Duke of Newcastle, and not the town in England, Newcastle SAR was founded as 'Post Halt Number 2' - a stopping point on the road from Port Natal-Durban and the Transvaal. During the Anglo-Boer War, it was a depot for the British, and temporary holding of the Boers. War buffs will want to stop just outside of town to visit the battle site, which include Laing's Nek, Schuinshoogte, and Majuba - the latter offering BBQ and picnic. Overlooking the city, Fort Amiel now houses a museum where you can learn about the town's history. There are a slew of other monuments in town worth visiting, like the elegant town hall constructed to commemorate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Victoria, the elegant Kestrels and Quaffers manor house with its Adams fireplaces, original sash windows, and Oregon pine floors, and the Hilldrop House, home to the author Rider Haggard.

name: Bandung City
description: In Surakarta, the streets are alive with camaraderie and energy, with a constant flow of traffic throughout the attraction-filled streets. At the heart of the city lies Alun-Alun, the city's main square. The grassy expanse is overlooked by the Grand Mosque and is a vibrant hub for locals and visitors alike. The city boasts numerous examples of Dutch colonial architecture, particularly the tropical Art Deco style known as the New Indies Style. Hot spring lovers will also find paradise in Surakarta, with resorts offering rejuvenating spa treatments and the chance to relax in natural thermal waters. Indulge in a wide range of culinary delights, explore the city's less expensive fashion shops found in factory outlets and distros, enjoy a game of golf, or spend time at the local zoo for an enriching experience in this Indonesian city.

name: Heroica Veracruz
address.region: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
description: Off the beaten path Heroica Veracruz has been promoting itself more and more as a tourist destination. The tree-shaded Zocalo, where a number of foreign armies once camped, is now filled morning to night with locals selling food and drink, playing board games, playing music, and dancing. Here, the Danzon, a traditional dance brought over by Cubans in the 19th Century, is danced every night. Veracruz houses many dance academies dedicated to keeping the dance alive. The Municipal Palace of Veracruz is the oldest government building in Mexico, with a lookout tower overlooking this prosperous port. Take a stroll down the Malecon, the oldest boardwalk in the country where food, tchotchkes, and seashells are sold. You can visit the Fort San Juan de Ulua just off the coast of Veracruz. This island was once a holy land for the god Tezcatlipoca, but eventually became one of the first landing sites in the Spanish Colonial era. For more of Mexican history, visit the Baluarte de Santiago, a very well-preserved Bastion.

name: Erfurt
description: Once known as 'Thuringia's Rome', Erfut is now a picturesque city with charming cobbled streets and renovated Renaissance buildings. The city is a great place to wander around as it's compact, easy to navigate and mostly pedestrianized. A myriad of architectural designs and colors can be found on every corner, side street, and passageway, as the old sits comfortably alongside the new. The city's original medieval grandeur is still on display in the cathedral and at St Severus Church, the Old Synagogue and the cobblestone street made up of 32 semi-timbered buildings that line the Merchants' Bridge. Then there are the more modern boutiques, department stores, street cafes and riverside cafes to enjoy. The city has excellent craft shops and galleries to browse and if time permits, check out the fortress with its wonderful views of the surroundings. This can all be serenely finished off with a relaxing drink in one of Erfurt's many picturesque cafes.

name: Aguascalientes
description: Aguascalientes is a vibrant city where tradition meets industry. An extensive network of cycling lanes weave in and out of old Baroque-style buildings and shimmering high rises. The city is made up of four traditional neighborhoods all dotted with charming treasures and endless activities. The historic downtown features a range of outstanding museums including the Aguascalientes Museum and the Museum of Contemporary Art that attract art lovers from across the country. Aguascalientes is a hub for arts, recreation and entertainment. Embrace the city's rich architectural heritage and enjoy unlimited contemporary amenities in Aguascalientes.

name: Belton House
description: Belton House was built at the end of the 17th century by Sir John Brownlow in the popular Carolean style. Though Sir John was a lawyer, he was also part of the gentry and received King William III at Belton House in 1695. Belton was one of the first houses to make use of sliding 'sash' windows, and it also employed faux windows to maintain symmetry in its facade. Walking through the interior, you'll be treated to Belton's fine decor, including ornately ornamented ceilings, Chinese wallpaper, and individual treasures like a stunning lapis lazuli cabinet. The friendly staff are happy to share more about the house, like how Prince Charles stayed here while he was a RAF cadet. You can also join an optional guided tour the head below stairs and into the world of Belton's servants to learn about their lives at the manor. For more information, please visit nationaltrust.org.uk/belton-house

name: Sibenik
description: Sibenik's mild winters and humid summers invite visitors to soak in the picturesque views and four fortresses that 'frame' the city. Today, the must sees include the pine forest Falcon Centre and the main symbol of Sibenik's legacy, the 15th century Cathedral of St. Jacob. This Cathedral was built with white stone in a unique Gothic and Renaissance style by a Venetian Dalamatic architect, Juraj Dalmatinac. A stone's throw west of Sibenik is Kornati's National park starring 89 unspoiled islands, islets, and reefs, a 'nautical paradise' to the most adventurous. With no accommodation provided on the uninhabited Kornati archipelagos, a day trip from Sibenik is a clear win for a great time.

name: Nelson
description: One of the oldest cities in New Zealand, Nelson boasts a wide variety of sites and activities. A light walk from the center of town will bring you to a viewing platform that is the Center of New Zealand, from this platform you can see the city, Tasman Bay, and the surrounding mountain ranges. Or, take a look back into Nelson's history at the Founders Heritage Park, with artisan buildings, large windmills, and stunning gardens. Then wander the city center and explore the art scene, boutiques, and various shops. You can stop in to see Jens Hansen, the acclaimed jeweller who made the 'One Ring' for the Lord of the Rings and Hobbit trilogies, or browse the city markets, where you can buy local products and food. The markets are usually adorned with buskers and street artists, who will keep you entertained while you shop. The sunshine capital of New Zealand, this charming town will be your home away from home.

name: Cempoala Archaeological Zone
address.region: Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave
description: Cempoala is Nahuatl for 'Place of Twenty Waters'. Located in the Veracruz State, Cempoala is one of the more important Mesoamerican archaeological sites. During the Mesoamerican era, this city was the centre for tax collection and other government functions. With a population of 30,000 people at its peak, the buildings show an impressive collection of fortresses, architectural structures, pyramids and temples. Admire the murals on the sides of the Templo de la Cruz, or learn about the stone rings that are scattered throughout the vegetation. These stone rings carry an astronomical significance which brings archaeologists and astronomers back to this city again and again.

name: Hacienda Panoaya
description: Hacienda Panoaya was the childhood home of the revered poet Juana Ines de la Cruz. Built in the mid 17th century, this perfectly preserved colonial complex is now a museum and amusement park dedicated to highlighting the achievements of one of Mexico's most famous intellectuals. Juana lived at Hacienda Panoaya with her mother and grandfather, often stealing her grandfather's books to teach herself how to reach which was forbidden for girls of the time. Her underground educational pursuits led her to university where she disguised herself as a male student. Hacienda Panoaya's rooms are well-preserved and set up as they were in the 1600s when Juana roamed the grounds. Visit the museum to see what inspired Juana's most famous works on love, feminism and religion. There is also a restaurant and large gardens on the property with free-roaming animals. The garden area features a full English-style labyrinth and other activities for the whole family. Spend the afternoon revelling in the history and joining in on the fun.

name: Civita di Bagnoregio
description: Founded by the Etruscans around 2500 years ago, this ancient city is slowly shrinking as the rock plateau it was built on erodes away. Thanks to its relative isolation, the town hasn't changed much over the centuries, even with two World Wars. The main threat to the city's history is what makes it so beautiful: the porous volcanic stone it sits atop is quickly eroding. The boyhood home of Saint Bonaventure, who died in 1274, has long since fallen off the edge of the cliff. By the 16th century, Civita was beginning to decline, and an earthquake at the end of the 17th, sent the town's government moved to the suburb of Bagnoregio. Since then, it's been known as 'The Dying Town', with a population that varies from about 12 people in winter to more than 100 in summer.

name: Flam
description: Located in the fjord region, Flåm is a hotspot of spectacular natural attractions for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers. The charming village boasts a gorgeous backdrop, with two of the world's longest and deepest fjords just nearby. The UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord are formed by narrow, 1,400m high crystalline rock walls that rise from the Norwegian sea, and are among some of the most scenically impressive archaeological landscapes in Norway. If you fancy a breathtaking railway ride, the world famous Flåm Railway will take you through spectacular scenery, running through the valley of Flåmsdalen and connecting with Sognefjord. It's the third-most visited tourist attraction in Norway and is an engineering and cultural feat not to be missed on your travels through Norway.

name: Cave of Altamira
address.addr1: Avenida Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola, s/n, 39330, Cantabria, Spain
description: In 1879, Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola's eight-year-old daughter led him into a large cave, exposing the amateur archaeologist to an art gallery that had been sealed off from the outside world for around 13,000 years. The artwork was so well preserved that some initially thought the cave-paintings were forgeries. Modern research suggests the earliest paintings were made 35,000 years ago by neanderthals, while the most recent are only 15,000 years old. After being opened to the public, the paintings began to deteriorate from the carbon dioxide released by the large number of visitors, so the site was closed to the public in 2002. Instead, a replica cave and museum were built nearby, allowing visitors to enjoy a more comfortable view of the famous polychrome paintings of the main hall of the cave, as well other works, and learn about how this masterpiece of cave art was created.

name: Anglesey Abbey
description: Founded as an Augustinian priory in the 12th century, Anglesey Abbey was converted into a country home around 1600. In the following centuries alterations and improvements were made to the house, but it was the 1st Lord Fairhaven, who made the house into the luxurious country home of today. Upon his death in 1966, Lord Fairhaven left the abbey to the National Trust to preserve a dying way of life. Today, visitors can still admire the Lord Fairhaven's extensive collection, which consists of over 10,000 pieces of rare objects d'art, antique furniture, and other fine furnishings. In the estate's 114 acre grounds, you can enjoy vibrant flower beds, quiet walking paths, a lode mill with its origins in the 11th century, and even adventure areas. For more information, please visitnationaltrust.org.uk/anglesey-abbey-gardens-and-lode-mill

name: Saltillo
description: In the desert state of Coahuila, Saltillo will open your eyes to Mexico off the beaten path, packed with provincial charm and history. It's the oldest post-conquest settlement in Northern Mexico after being founded in 1577 by the rambunctious Conquistador Alberto del Canto. It's loaded with historic architecture and museums, including the Museo de la Revolución Mexicana, focusing on the transformative Mexican Revolution. Peer at the beautiful bird species found in Mexico at the Museu de las Aves de México, or learn about the ecology of the desert landscape at Museo del Desierto. Other must-see attractions in Saltillo include the impressive Catedral de Santiago, the sprawling Alameda Zaragoza Park, and the lively Plaza de Armas, where locals and visitors alike gather to enjoy live music, street performances, and delicious food. Pick up a sarape at one of the street markets held every Tuesday, and indulge in the local specialty of pan de pulque - wheat bread made with cinnamon and cactus juice.

name: Ex-monastery of Santiago Apostol
description: Work on the Ex-monastery of Santiago Apostol was begun by four Dominican monks in the 1550s. The order labored to complete their grand vision for a century, but had to give up in 1650 due to construction costs and the loss of local workers. Despite never having actually been completed, the site has been used as a convent, monastery, school, government office, prison, and cultural centerpiece over the centuries. Step into the roofless basilica to see murals that mix Roman Catholic, Mixtec, and Zapotec iconology. Add that with a walk through the well-preserved cloister for examples of Gothic, Moorish, Renaissance and Plateresque architecture. And the Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia have offices throughout the complex, so you can get a peek at active archaeological work from around the Central Valley.

name: Keukenhof
description: Established in 1949 on the grounds of a 17th century manor, Keukenhof is the largest flower garden in the Netherlands and one of the largest in the world. Alongside the world-famous Dutch tulips, hyacinths, daffodils, orchids, roses, carnations, irises, lilies, and many other flowers add to an extravaganza of colors and scents. Please note: the garden is only open for a few weeks in the Spring when the flowers are in bloom. To see the garden's schedule, please visit https://keukenhof.nl/en/

name: Liege
description: Settled since the 6th century, Liège is Belgium's third largest city links Paris, Amsterdam, and Cologne - a crossroads that blends historic architecture, beautiful art, and delicious food. Liège's Old-Town offers new sights at every turn, such as the Flamboyant-Gothic Church of Saint-James, extravagant 16th century Bishop's Palace, and the infamous 374 step "Montagne de Bueren" stairway. The city is also home to several museums, ranging from modern art, to regional life, to a 17th century mansion filled with weapons and Egyptian artefacts. Liège has a distinct culinary identity, best experience in its traditional "boulettes sauce lapin", or beef and pork meatballs paired with Belgian fries, often served with rabbit sauce. For something on the lighter side, stop by one of the many cafes to sample Liège's unique waffle recipe.

name: Altensteig
description: Located in the Northern Black Forest of Germany, Altensteig's skyline is filled with the typical German influence. Burgundy outlined houses with detailed trimmings adorn most of the tall, narrow houses. Along the slopes, the houses are colorful and shine brightly toward the sun. Be amazed as you walk through the town towards the castle or the town church designed in Rococo. Love being near water? This town has a long-standing history of boasting rafting through the Black Forest. Even children are welcome to join tradition and a ride on the Kinderfloß. Relax and enjoy your time in the Black Forest's most beautiful city, Altensteig.

name: Dinkelsbuhl
description: Founded in the 8th century as a royal residence of the Carolingian kings, in the 14th century, Dinkelsbuhl was fortified and made a Free Imperial City. In 1632, the town avoided destruction by surrendering to the Swedish - according to legend it's thanks to one small boy who reminded the Swedish general of his own child. Every July, the town celebrates their surrender, which (along with not being bombed during World War II) has allowed them to keep their medieval heritage. Today, Dinkelsbuhl is one of only 3 German towns with intact city walls, providing visitors a rare opportunity to walk medieval battlements. The Old Town is an explosion of colorful history, with half-timbered houses and vibrantly-painted gabled houses lining the cobbled streets. Towering above them all is the 15th century St. George's church. After admiring its 6 magnificent altars, visitors can scale the tower for fantastic views of the town and countryside.

name: Tetovo
description: One of the oldest cities in Macedonia, the country's oldest artefact - a Bronze Age sword - was found here. But was the arrival of the Ottomans in the 16th century that provided the city's most striking cultural heritage. Under their reign, mosques, fountains, public baths, and even kitchens for the poor were erected. The Decorated Mosque is perhaps the most unique in the country. First built in 1438, it was renovated by Abdurrahman Pasha in 1833 to suit his artistic preference. The typical ceramic tile decorations were replaced by vibrant floral and geometric paintings, which used 30,000 eggs to prepare. Of the many paintings, the depiction of Mecca is a stand-out, likely being the only one of its kind in southeastern Europe.

name: Sillustani
description: Settled by the Culla people long before the Incas conquered the area, Sillustani is a prime example that the Incan Empire did not have the monopoly on impressive stonework. The way the Cuella shaped stone, in much the same style as used in European fortresses, was by cutting rectangular blocks far more intricate than those produced by Incan masons. The towers, some of which are up to 40 feet tall, that dot the peninsula are burial chambers for dead Culla nobles. Built to house the entire noble family, many of the towers are decorated with carvings of sacred animals. The local scenery adds to the magic; peaceful moorland and low hills are to be enjoyed in the immediate vicinity of the lake, as well as a variety of flora and fauna.
