name: Jan Kok
description: Nestled atop a serene hill, the historic Landhuis Jan Kok, dating back to 1704 and rebuilt in 1840, offers more than just a glimpse into Curaçao's past. Renowned Curaçaoan artist Nena Sanchez has turned this space into a vibrant showcase of her colorful creations, adding a new chapter to Jan Kok's rich history. The plantation, primarily dedicated to salt production and spanning 345 hectares, unfolds breathtaking views of the St. Marie Bay salt flats, now adorned with flocks of graceful flamingos. Despite its dark past associated with an infamous slave master, Jan Kok's present is infused with the lively spirit of Nena Sanchez's Caribbean-inspired artwork. As you explore the estate, you'll encounter not only the captivating paintings within the Landhuis but also the enchanting sculpture garden in the open air. The atmosphere reflects the island's vivid hues, translating the essence of Curaçao onto canvas. Free to enter, Landhuis Jan Kok provides a unique blend of historical significance and contemporary artistry.

name: Sleepy Hollow, NY
description: Sleepy Hollow is known for two things: the headless horseman, and the Dutch. Even today, its Dutch heritage can be seen in the city's historic architecture, with the Old Dutch Church being the standout example. Not only is it one of New York's oldest churches, but it was featured in the short story by Washington Irving that made the town famous. If you're a fan of ghost stories, you can also visit the Headless Horseman Bridge from the tale. Irving's home, "Sunnyside", offers a charming glimpse into his life, and the 19th century as you take a guided tour with period-costumed guides. The Sleeping Hollow Cemetery is another great sight, the final resting place of Washington Irving, among other notable Americans, including Elizabeth Arden, the cosmetics giant! For some Gilded Age glamor, pay a visit to the Rockerfeller's Kykuit Estate or the dramatic Gothic Revival Lyndhurst Mansion.

name: Kutna Hora
description: Extensive silver deposits lured a flood of settlers to Kutna Hora in the 13th century, and within a few decades, the town had become the seat of the Czech national mint and financial center of the country. This wealth funded a slew elegant buildings, from burgher homes to beautiful churches and even a palatial college. Stroll along the immaculately-preserved medieval street of Ruthardka, and try to pick out the details of the Plague Column or oversized Stone Fountain. Towering above the cobbled streets, the Cathedral of St. Barbara stands as one of the finest religious buildings in Central Europe. Dedicated to the patron saint of miners, the blend of Gothic and Baroque architecture is a telling testament to its 500-year construction. Right next door, the Jesuit College with its gardens and art gallery is a perfect attraction, rain or shine. But Kutna Hora's most unique monument lies on the outskirts of town. The Bone Church, or Ossuary, showcases a revolutionary interior design: bones and nothing but the bones of the dead, from the 'noughts and crosses' floor to chandeliered ceiling.

name: Scone Palace
description: Scone Palace was founded as an early Christian church, which later developed into an Augustinian abbey, before becoming home to the Earls of Mansfield in 1600. Since at least the 9th century, Scone was the site of the coronation ceremony for Scottish monarchs, who would sit upon the legendary 'Scone Stone'. The stone was captured by Edward I as spoils of war and taken to Westminster Abbey in 1296, where it is still used for royal coronations (though kept in Edinburgh Castle at all other times). The castle of today is an 18th century remodelling, where you can still walk the Long Galley where King Charles II strode to his coronation in 1661, inspect the needlework skills of Mary Queen of Scots in the bedhangings she worked while imprisoned on Loch Leven, and see the desk where Marie Antoinette composed letters, all of which are surrounded by a treasury of fine furniture and objets d'art. For more information, please visit scone-palace.co.uk

name: Tehuacalco
description: First settled around 400CE, Tehuacalco was the ceremonial center of the enigmatic Yopes people, whose culture peaked between 650 and 1100CE. Unlike most other Mesoamerican cultures at the time, the Yopes grew more nomadic over the centuries, yet were still one of the few groups that managed to fend off the Aztec conquest. The Spanish, however, crushed the Yopes resistance and sent the people scattering to other settlements. Tehuacalco was then abandoned until being rediscovered in the early 2000s. After years of excavation and restoration, the site opened to the public in 2008. Unique among archaeological sites, you'll not only see signs of urbanization like pyramids, temples, a large palace, and a Mesoamerican ball court, but also caves and rock etchings left by the Yopes. Be sure to stop by the museum to see artefacts uncovered at the site and learn more about this little-understood people.

name: Nagtabon Beach
description: Nagtabon Beach is a mile long stretch of sand that doesn't put on airs. It's somewhere most tourists have never heard of, meaning it's still a hangout for those who just want to relax in the sun. There's no reef because of the waves and currents, but this also means it's an increasingly popular surf spot, especially in winter. Though the more modest summer swells are perfect if you're still trying to learn. If you need to get out of the sun, you can lounge under the countless palm trees, rent out a wooden hut, or hang at one of the food stands for some cheap local eats. If you're lucky, you might even see turtles hatching!

name: East London
description: East London was founded in the 19th century as South Africa's only river port, and enjoyed a period of prosperity thanks to this. However, as river trade declined, the city shifted its focus to its wealth of sandy beaches, which are considered some of the best in the world. While many visitors come to have some fun in the sun, the city has some charming historic sights to discover. The town hall in particular is a vibrant example of colonial architecture. If you need to get out of the sun (or it's raining), don't miss the East London Museum, which has some excellent exhibits including the only dodo egg left in existence and a coelacanth.

name: New Lanark
address.addr1: New Lanark Rd, Lanark ML11 9DB, UK
description: The cotton mills at New Lanark were founded in 1786, and used some of the era's most advanced industrial technologies. However, workers lived in squalor as the mill owners tried to milk as much profit out of the facility as possible. This all changed in the early 19th century when Robert Owen purchased the mills, and redeveloped them according to his Utopian ideals. This ambitious undertaking saw the construction of decent homes and open spaces, but more importantly, Owen provided fair wages, free healthcare, and a new education system - not to mention the world's first workplace nursery. Today, the town's open spaces and picturesque riverside setting provide a pleasant place to stroll. Visitors can also take a unique guided tour to learn what life was like for workers, step into the mill to learn about the production process, and head into the home of Robert Owen to learn about the man himself.

name: Saltaire
description: Saltaire was founded by Sir Titus Salt along the River Aire, hence Salt+Aire (aha!), in 1851. The pinnacle of the Victorian philanthropic paternalist ideal, Salt's industrial town provided his factory workers luxuries like backyards, bathrooms, and bathhouses in a grid of elegant Victorian townhouses, which would influence the 'garden city' movement. In order to keep his town tidy, Salt even banned washing lines and required all employees take two-baths-a-week. The result of having clean, happy, and cared for workers? Increased factory profits. Today, the elegant architecture and open spaces make the town a delight for visitors to explore, with the old mill standing as the unmissable monument. Once the largest factory in the world, the mill was purchased by Jonathan Silver in 1986, who partnered with renowned artist David Hockney to convert the space into a giant art gallery and shopping emporium. Now, visitors are treated to not just fine shops, but one of the world's largest David Hockney exhibitions.

name: Ruinas de Pomona
description: Deep in the heart of the Tabasco jungle, the Ruinas de Pomona is an important archaeological site with great cultural significance for the Mayan civilization. Meaning 'gateway' in Mayan, Pomona's position was strategically located between two large regions and thus a hub for communication and exchange of goods and merchandise. It was subject to many battles between the cities of Palenque and Piedras Negras, whose people fought for control of Pomona. The unique limestone ruins are split into six archaeological complexes, the northernmost plaza being the only one to have been excavated and ready to explore. The on-site museum showcases permanent displays of ancient Mayan artefacts including furniture, crockery, glassware and even headstones, and is a great insight into the daily life that was lived in the early times of around 600 AD to 900 AD. Because of its location it is common to hear the screeches of howler monkeys residing in the jungle, as well as the songs of local birdlife in the surrounding trees!

name: Concordia
description: Surrounded by lush plantations of coconut, mango, and banana trees, Concordia is a captivating town with origins as a thriving center for gold, silver, and copper mining. The heart of Concordia revolves around its tranquil and shaded town square, where residents and visitors alike gather to enjoy the peaceful ambiance. Immerse yourself in the authentic Sinaloan village atmosphere and explore the various artisan workshops that dot the town, plus the iconic giant chair adorning the plaza that symbolizes Concordia's artisanal scene. Concordia also claims the invention of the renowned raspados, a delightful treat consisting of shaved ice flavored with real fruit syrup. It's a must-try for a refreshing and tasty experience while you wander through the town. The centerpiece of Concordia is the magnificent San Sebastián Church. Built in 1785, this architectural gem showcases a stunning baroque facade adorned with intricate details and elaborately decorated columns highlighted with gilded accents. The town invites you to embrace its rich traditions, savor its local flavors, and bask in the serenity of its charming town square.

name: Santa Fe
description: Situated to the west bank of the Parana River is the captivating yet underrated city of Santa Fe. Founded in 1573 by Juan de Garay, the capital city of the Santa Fe province, the city moved to its current location in1651 due to flooding issues. Sante Fe is known to Argentinians as the place their first constitution was signed, and it hosted multiple Constitutional Conventions in the 20th century. But Santa Fe's most famous landmark is the suspension bridge across the Parana River. Walk across it for beautiful coastal views, especially at night when the bridge is illuminated against the night sky. Stroll alongside the bridge at the redeveloped 'costanera' (waterfront) and try some freshly caught fish at one of the riverside restaurants whilst enjoying the views. Exploring the city center, you will find well-preserved historical and colonial buildings such as Convento San Francisco, a pristine and charming 17th century church that features a museum containing religious and colonial artifacts. Finish with a visit to the Cerveceria Santa Fe where the local beer is crafted for an insight into the brewing process and a refreshing beer tasting experience.

name: Llucmajor
description: In the sun-kissed plains beneath the Randa hills, Llucmajor stands as the largest municipality in Mallorca, boasting 16 charming villages including Cala Blava, Cala Pi, and the renowned tourist haven of S'Arenal. While Llucmajor town is of medium size, its outskirts unfold a mosaic of architectural styles, with ancient landmarks harmonizing with modern residences. A melting pot of Mallorcan life, the town center pulses with vitality year-round, as it's primarily inhabited by locals. Historically, Llucmajor played a pivotal role in Mallorca's past, witnessing the Battle of Llucmajor in 1349, ending the island's brief independence. The town's heritage is reflected in its stone craftsmanship, shoemaking legacy, and historic landmarks, including the Church of Sant Miquel and the town hall. Despite its inland location, Llucmajor has emerged as a charming retreat for travelers seeking authenticity. Former country houses have transformed into idyllic holiday escapes, making it an increasingly popular base for exploring the island. The town's weekly markets showcase local produce, and September bursts with festivities during the main fairs, including the grand 'Es Firo.' While Llucmajor may lack the glossy appeal of bustling resorts, it captivates those yearning for the soulful essence of Mallorca, making it an ideal retreat for an immersive experience in the heart of the island.

name: Eden Project
address.addr1: Eden Project, Bodelva, Par PL24 2SG, UK
description: Opened in 2001, the Eden project brought an abandoned clay mine back to nature by filling it with a beautiful botanical garden and two biomes. These geodesic domes covered with special UV-transparent plastic are entirely self-supporting, meaning the interior is an opens space unmarred by internal supports. Covering nearly 4 acres, the Tropical Biome is filled with the flora found in the rainforest, such as banana plants, coffee, rubber trees, and giant bamboo, and is the largest space of its kind. The 1.6 acre Mediterranean Biome is filled with temperate and arid plants like olives and grapes, as well as various sculptures. More than just gardens, the Eden Project offers an entire learning experience, offering guided tours and a special building dedicated to educational exhibits. Throughout the year, the Eden Project also hosts special events, ranging from activities for grandparents to share with their grandchildren, to a huge summer music festival. For more information, please visit www.edenproject.com

name: Chernivtsi
description: Chernivtsi was a relatively unimportant settlement until it was annexed by the Austro-Hungarian Empire in the 18th century, and Emperor Franz II launched an ambitious redevelopment project. With much of the city rebuilt by Viennese architects, Chernivtsi has some noticeable parallels to the Austrian capital. However, the most stupendous landmark is the former high priests' quarters, a UNESCO-listed compound combining Moresque, Byzantine, and Romanesque styles with local folk elements, and now houses the local university. The Central Square is dominated by the Town Hall, a decidedly eastern take on Late Classicism, but it's the former Bukovinian bank building that gets all the attention - this exceptional Secession-style building now houses an art museum. The breathtaking Theatre Square is crowned by the Olha Kobylyanska Theater, which was designed by the architects of Vienna's and Odesa's opera houses. Ironically, the city's most unusual building is its Orthodox Cathedral, which is known as 'the drunk church' because of its crooked cupolas.

name: Como City
description: Como has long been a place of historical significance. It was the arch-nemesis of Milan, birthplace of Pope Innocent XI and scientist Alessandro Volta, and an early adopter of the printed word. One of the city's oldest structures, the 4th century San Carpoforo, was built on a former temple to Mercury, and houses the remains of Saint Carpophorus and other local martyrs. The famous Gothic cathedral is flanked by statues of the famous, local born comaschi Pliny the Elder and Pliny the Younger, and the neoclassical Villa Olmo, has housed Napoleon, Franz Ferdinand I, Giuseppe Garibaldi, and other eminent figures. To best experience the natural wonders of Lombardy, take some extra time to ride the funicular from Como to nearby Brunate, 715m up a mountain. Como is so renowned that in 1902 William Rockefeller purchased the fountain from the main square and moved it to the Bronx Zoo.

name: Cividale del Friuli
address.addr1: Cividale del Friuli, Province of Udine, Italy
description: Cividale del Friuli is a town part of the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region of northern Italy. It was founded in 53 B.C. by Julius Caesar and belonged to the Lombards during the early Middle Ages. The pedestrian-only streets make the compact town easily walkable in just a few hours. The center square, Piazza Paolo Diacono, is a very picturesque spot, feautring a large fountain and many outdoor cafes and bars. Cividale del Friuli's most dramatic monument is the Ponte del Diavolo, or 'Devil's Bridge'. The bridge arches over the gorge of the Natisone River and offers breathtaking views of the Julian Alps. The jewel of the city, however, is the 8th century A.D. Tempietto Longobardo. The Lombard Temple is the best preserved architectural testimony of Lombard and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Cividale del Friuli has very few tourists, which allows visitors to freely stroll the romantic winding streets while taking in its delicious wines and extensive history.

name: La Paz
description: La Paz was originally founded by the Spanish on a pre-existing Incan settlement before being relocated to its current position. Over its history, the city has been the locus of numerous revolts, be it indigenous uprisings, or sparking the Spanish American Wars of Independence. While it's since grown into an ever-evolving metropolis, La Paz has remained cemented as one of South America's most important cultural centers. Dotted throughout the city are colonial-era landmarks like the San Francisco Church, the Metropolitan Cathedral, the Plaza Murillo, and Jaén Street. And with a predominantly native Aymara population, indigenous culture is still alive and well. The city is renowned for its unique markets, particularly the Witches' Market, and one of La Paz' most popular spectacles is watching cholitas (female wrestlers in traditional dress) do battle. To move between districts, hop on one of the aerial tramways to be whisked away.

name: Bihac
description: Dating back to the 13th century, Bihac is a charming medieval town nestled on the banks of the Una river. Towering above the town is the tower of the 19th century church, the rest of the building was destroyed by Allied bombing during World War II. Nearby, the Captain's Tower is likely the oldest building in town. While there are no records of its construction, it's likely from the turn of the 13th century - before the town itself was even mentioned. Today, the stone structure houses an archaeological museum, showcasing artefacts from the Illyrian and Roman eras. The nearby Fethija Mosque was converted from a medieval church in the 16th century, though still bears elements from the original structure, such as the Gothic rose window. Visitors can take advantage of the river's natural beauty by partaking in one of favourite local past-times - enjoying traditional coffee and Turkish delights at a cafe.

name: Grand Bassam
description: Immerse yourself in a captivating blend of history and charm at Grand Bassam, Côte d'Ivoire's alluring seaside haven. Stroll along palm-lined boulevards, marveling at the elegant French colonial buildings with their wrought-iron balconies and colorful facades. Wander through the historic town center, a captivating time capsule transporting you back to a bygone era. Let your imagination run wild as you envision grand balls and colonial life unfolding within these very walls. Step away from the colonial past and delve into the heart of the N'zima village, a thriving community pulsating with vibrant African culture. Here, colorful stalls overflow with hand-crafted souvenirs and the rhythmic beats of local music fill the air. Engage with friendly locals, learn about their traditions, and perhaps even pick up a unique piece of handcrafted art to treasure as a memento of your journey.

name: Wurzburg
description: 'If I could choose my place of birth, I would consider Wurzburg', wrote the author Hermann Hesse, and it's not difficult to see why. This scenic university city located on the Main River in Bavaria is rich with churches, cathedrals and other historical buildings built in Baroque, Rococo and Gothic style where the huge Residential Palace takes pride of place. Over 85% of the town was damaged or destroyed in World War II and Wurzburg became a symbol of German recovery when, over the next 20 years, the historical buildings were painstakingly and lovingly restored. Today, all traces of destruction have long gone. Downtown Wurzburg is a spectacularly pretty part of the city to spend a little time checking out some of the churches, museums and historical buildings that contain great art. After savoring the wealth of attractions on offer then there are few who would dispute Hesse's perspective of the town.

name: York
description: York was founded by the Romans in 71AD as their provincial capital, and later, served as the seat of the Northumbrian and Jórvík (Viking) kingdoms. In the Middle Ages, the Church of England made York capital of the northern ecclesiastical province - a role it retains to this day. This prestigious position blessed York with its world-famous Minster. The largest Gothic Cathedral North of the Alps, the York Minster is filled with historic treasures from its medieval stained glass to intricately carved screen, and its interactive underground chambers walk visitors through York's 2000-year history. Afterwards, make your way through The Shambles, a street 14th century, timber-framed buildings, and on to the medieval town walls, parts of which date back to the Romans. For culture connoisseurs, there's a variety of great museums to choose from, including the Castle Museum, Train Museum, Art Gallery and Viking Center.

name: London
description: Impossible to pigeonhole, London really does have something for everyone. There are of course the recognizable landmarks like the Big Ben, the Tower of London, Westminster Abbey, and the gleaming Shard, but London's culture runs much deeper. With ⅓ of the population foreign born, representing 270 nationalities, Europe's largest is also one of the world's most diverse. Foodies can revel in sampling every imaginable cuisine, while aesthetes are sure to lose themselves in the cities countless museums and galleries - the Victoria & Albert Museum is the world's largest museum of decorative arts and design, with over 2.27 million objects in its permanent collection. The massive metropolis also offers plenty of opportunities to escape the hustle and bustle, be it Hyde Park downtown, or the UNESCO-listed Kew Gardens farther afield.

name: Vamos
description: The village of Vamos is as traditional as it gets. Its stone roads and houses, olive oil mills, busy tavernas serving fresh seafood and raki, and centuries-old churches tick all the boxes for a quintessential Cretan experience. Having existed since the 8th century, the village has survived the Turks, Venetians, and will surely stand after our time. Vamos is divided into two parts: the old town with historic architecture, and a newer part with tavernas and shops. Taking a leisurely walk through the village or sitting down in one of the tavernas is a good idea. Still, there's plenty of other activities to choose from depending on the season. Whether you're visiting olive oil, oranges, or cheese farms, discovering the local Orthodox churches, sampling traditional alcoholic beverages, or taking a Cretan cooking lesson, the liveliness of Vamos will keep you busy for the entire stay.

name: Toluca
description: If you're a traveler on a foodie mission, then let us tell you that Toluca is so famous for its chorizo, that anyone (in fact, anything) from Toluca is referred to as a "chorizo." But for those seeking other forms of entertainment, don't miss out on the stunning wealth of Baroque and Neoclassical architecture of churches and cultural centers. The Cathedral of Toluca, modeled after old Roman basilicas and sharing design elements with the Cathedral of Mexico City, is a mix of styles based on the different time periods in which it was constructed and redone. However, be sure to include the Cosmovitral on your list - this building is essentially one large stained glass mural. Once a market house, it is now a tourist attraction drawing in visitors with its colorful beauty, and houses a diverse botanical garden covering the floor of the premises.

name: Two Eyes Cenote
description: The Two Eyes Cenote is part of the Two Eyes Cave System, one of the longest underwater cave systems in the world. The two sinkholes are connected by a subterranean passageway, and were where the original diving exploration of the cave system began. The stunning blue water and amazing cave system have made appearances in the IMAX film Journey Into Amazing Caves, and the 2006 BBC/Discovery Channel series Planet Earth. Today, the cenote is widely considered the most beautiful (and most popular) in the region. Stairs and platforms make it easy to get in for a dip, or snorkel. Please note that tickets to the cenote are not included. Prices may change depending on the season, so call ahead for the most up-to-date information.

name: Glorenza
description: It was after the town was destroyed during the Battle of Calva in 1499 that the Emporer Maximilian I ordered the rebuilding of the town and the construction of its protecting walls, which still stand today. Inside the 10-metre-high walls, marked with imposing city gates, sits the idyllic town with historic tree-lined arcades and charming narrow alleyways. In addition to the impressively well-preserved 16th-century walls, visitors to the area can enjoy the peaceful city square; Laubengasse Lane, a former trading centre and market alley, and the St. Pancras Parish Church, located outside the city walls, which was first mentioned in 1227. Glorenza offers an ideal blend of history, tranquillity, and nature, surrounding by majestic mountains and beautiful countryside.

name: Ghent
description: Settled since pre-history, it was the Romans who laid the foundations for the thriving city Ghent would become. The city developed into a major medieval trade center, though began a slow decline after King Charles V was born here in 1500. It wasn't until the 18th century, and an industrial boom that the city would be revived. Today, visitors can enjoy this Flemish gem's rich heritage in the city's many architectural monuments, including several ancient churches, an opulent opera house, the imposing Gravensteen Castle, and UNESCO-listed bell tower. To truly experience the city's charm, find a seat on the Graslei, a picturesque spot in the town center, with views of the many bridges, grand houses, and medieval buildings.

name: Straubing
description: There has been a settlement located at Straubing since Neolithic times and evidence of this long and varied history is apparent throughout the town. Roman artifacts and treasures can be viewed at the town's Gäubodenmuseum while St Peter's Church dates from the 12th century. Romanesque in design, it boasts two distinctive portals exquisitely sculptured. In 1218 part of the city known as 'new town' was constructed and nowadays this acts as the main shopping and dining out area in Straubing. The Town Hall and City Tower are equally stunning models of Gothic architecture, however perhaps the most iconic example is the Basilika St. Jakob. Particularly striking is the 16th century tower, with its sleek design and striking onion dome. The church also well known for its painted glass windows, showcased in four large panels dating from the 14th century.

name: Antequera
description: Inhabited since antiquity, Roman, Moorish, and Spanish influences have left the town with a rich tapestry of architectural gems. The city is home to over 30 churches, all with opulent interiors. A journey up to the 3rd century citadel rewards explorers with spectacular views of the town, and is the best place to see the remains of the Roman baths, while the optional audio-guide brings the fortress's long history to life. For visitors who yearn for natural wonders, the Torcal National Park is un-missable, with its unique rock formations flecked with fossils. Not quite as old as the fossils, the 5000 year old Dolmens just outside of town have been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The 30-meter-long Menga Dolmen is the largest in Europe, and offers visitors the chance to experience one of the most outstanding examples of megalithic architecture in the world.

name: Sorrento
address.addr1: 80067 Sorrento, Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy
description: Settled by the Ancient Greeks, the dramatic clifftop city of Sorrento became a staple holiday destination in the 19th century when Lord Byron brought it to the attention of the vacationing literary geniuses including Dickens, Goethe, and Tolstoy. This stunning city has been attracting discerning travelers ever since, who are treated to stunning views, as well as beautiful historic monuments, such as the Cathedral, the doors of which originated in Constantinople in the 11th century. Along with the scenery and monuments, Sorrento (and the Amalfi Coast) is known for its cuisine, and limoncello. If you want a taste of local culture, take a guided tour at one of the city's many limoncello distilleries!

name: Ascoli Piceno
address.addr1: 63100 Ascoli Piceno, Province of Ascoli Piceno, Italy
description: Ascoli Piceno first became a federated city with nominal independence from Rome in 268 BC, an empire against which it later revolted in 91 BC, before being reconquered and destroyed by Pompeius Strabo in 89 BC. The town sits at the confluence of two rivers, and remains a popular destination for tourists of all types. Among the sites to see in Ascoli Piceno are the Baroque Sant'Emidio alle Grotte church, built in 1717; the Gothic style San Francesco church and the adjacent Convent of San Francesco; Porta Gemina, an ancient Roman gate from the 1st century BC; the ruins of an ancient Roman theater; and Porta Tufilla, a tower-like gate built in 1552, attached to Ponte Tufillo, a medieval bridge built in 1097. Whether you're in the mood for a history lesson, a pleasant stroll, or a unique lunch venue, Ascoli Piceno has something to offer. For those looking to combine all three, you can get tapas to go in the form of a bag of giant, meat-stuffed, deep-fried olives.

name: Changwon
description: Changwon offers a captivating experience for every type of traveler year-round, but is famously known for its district of Jinhae-gu, which turns light pink every spring. The Cherry Blossom Festival celebrates the arrival of the seasonal flower and pays tribute to the legendary naval admiral, Yi Sun-sin. During the ten-day event, visitors can enjoy a vibrant Victory Parade reenacting historic battles from the Imjin War, as well as breathtaking fireworks displays by Sokcheonhang Port. For those seeking cultural enrichment, The House of Changwon is a must-visit attraction. Once the residence of esteemed Korean academic Du-cheol, it now serves as a center for learning about Korean culture. Throughout Changwon, you can immerse yourself in the city's scenic beauty, from its picturesque hills to the enchanting Cherry Blossom Festival. Whether you're strolling along the island-studded bay or exploring cultural landmarks, Changwon promises an unforgettable experience blending tradition and modernity.

name: Skofja Loka
description: Skofja Loka (Slovene for "Bishop's Meadow") is one of the oldest settlements in Slovenia, dating back to the year 973. The city's old town has been protected as a historical monument since 1987. The charming old town square is a hub of social life with many excellent place to eat and drink. In the city, you can also find St. Jacob's church and Skofja Loka Castle & Museum. Climb to the top of the castle for a beautiful view of the Slovenian Alps.

name: Haifa
description: Haifa was founded around 1300 BC as a port city, and has since blossomed into the 3rd largest settlement in Israel. Having been ruled by everyone from the Phoenicians to the Crusaders, Ottomans, and British, these varied influences have left an indelible mark on the city. Overlooking the city are the UNESCO-listed Baha'i Gardens, where 19 flora-filled terraces work their way up the slopes of Mt. Carmel, terminating in a stunning shrine that perfectly embodies the Baha'i egalitarian view on religion through its art and architecture. Before reaching this, you'll first pass through the 19th century Germany colony, where the preserved red-roofed buildings are now home to hip cafes, restaurants, and art galleries. Also at the foot of the mountain is the shrine of Elijah's Cave, where the 9th century BC prophet is believed to have lived and taught.

name: Lecce
description: Likely founded by the ancient Greeks, the city was conquered by the Romans around the 3rd century BC, and remained under the rule of the Eastern Roman Empire until the 11th century. By the 16th century, Lecce had become one of the most important cities of southern Italy, and was enriched with opulent Baroque monuments beginning in 1630. The Piazza Sant'Oronzo depicts nearly the city's entire history, from the ruins of the Amphitheatre, to the 17th century column that was constructed using some of the Roman columns. Representing the Renaissance, the Palazzo del Seggio hosts important art exhibitions, and the nearby Basilica di Santa Croce, with its richly decorated facade, is a masterpiece of masonry, once compared to a lunatic having a nightmare.

name: Bad Hofgastein
description: The waterfall is a real beauty, located in the centre of town and plunging over 340 metres in three tiers down to the valley bottom. Various paths allow this pristine cataract to be viewed from different angles. But if you're feeling particularly adventurous you can take the Flying Waters ride on a zip-line suspended above the waterfall. And if the adventurous mood persists try the suspension foot-bridge on the Stubnerkogel mountain. This strongly constructed walkway requires strong nerves and a head for heights as one can look down through the metre-wide transparent mesh to the valley floor below. But the seemingly air-treading 140-metre walk, from the terrace of the restaurant at the lift station to the transmitter station is a uniquely thrilling experience. Directly across from the suspension bridge the Glocknerblick viewing platform is also designed for thrills. Jutting out from the mountainside it has floor-windows giving views of the mountainous drop below.

name: Iwakuni
description: Iwakuni, a quaint city in southeastern Yamaguchi Prefecture, is famed for its unique Kintai-kyo Bridge, a marvel that entices visitors year-round and truly shines during the cherry blossom season in early April. Once a feudal domain during the Edo Period, Iwakuni boasts a reconstructed mountaintop castle that adds to its allure. Crossing the bridge is a must, with options of a 310 yen round trip or a 970 yen pass including access to the bridge, entry to Iwakuni Castle, and a ropeway round-trip. This pass extends discounts to attractions like the Kikkawa Historical Museum, Iwakuni Art Museum, and White Snake Museum. Amidst its charm, Iwakuni showcases the annual Kintai Bridge Festival on April 29th, featuring samurai-costumed parades and historic reenactments. Iwakuni's cultural richness also extends to its preserved castle town ambience, the serene Ogasawara Tea Garden, and the intriguing White Snake of Iwakuni. Perched atop Mount Shiroyama, Iwakuni Castle, rebuilt in 1962, is a museum displaying armor, weapons, and artworks depicting war. For a taste of local delicacies and ambiance, dining at Hangetsu, a traditional restaurant dating back to 1869, is recommended.

name: Przemysl
description: Dating back to the 8th century, Przemyśl is Poland' second oldest city, after Krakow. The city's strategic location near the border of what is now the Ukraine brought a series of highs and lows over its long history, flourishing during the Renaissance, and suffering greatly during both World Wars. A huge number of fortresses were built around the city in the 19th century, which resulted in a World War I siege which caused an estimated 300,000 casualties. During World War II, nearly 30% of the city's population was Jewish, almost all of whom were rounded up in a ghetto before being sent to extermination camps. Today, the ruins of the fortifications and repurposed synagogues are reminders of the city's most trying days. However, the scenic old town, charming museum of Bells and Pipes, and National Museum, which holds Poland's second largest collection of icons, offer visitors a memorable experience.

name: Fez
description: Fez was founded in the 9th century as the capital of the Idrisid dynasty. By the 12th or 13th century, Fez had already grown to its present size. The Medina of Fez is still one of the largest metropolises in the Islamic world, with 1000 years' worth of religious, civil, and military monuments for visitors to discover in the unpaved urban center. Wander off into the labyrinth of alleys to discover market stalls, local artisans, ornate fountains, and local hammams on your own, or hire a guide. Regardless, by sure to track down Fez' famed Chouara Tanneries (follow your nose), which still make leather using medieval techniques. At the heart of the medina, you'll find the University of Al-Karaouine, the world's oldest university - though non-Muslims can only admire it and its giant mosque from outside. You can, however, visit the historic Medersa Bou Inania college to marvel at the stunning stucco work, intricate wood carvings, and mesmerizing mosaics.

name: Sucre
description: The temperate climate made Sucre the preferred destination for Spanish royalty and wealthy families, who transformed the city into the most beautiful in Bolivia. Its historic center, with its cobbled streets lined with whitewashed houses, ornate churches, and lavish palaces is one of the best-preserved in the New World, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Basilica of Saint Francisco is one of the city's most cherished monuments - it was here that Bolivia signed its independence from Spain, which they rang in until the church bell broke. The 17th century St. Francis Xavier University with its porticoed courtyard is another standout. But for the most unique building in all of Bolivia, don't miss the Glorieta Castle. This sandstone palace was built in the 19th century by mining magnate and banker Don Francisco Argandoña and his wife, who the pope named the first (and only_ Prince and Princess of Bolivia. Their romantic abode incorporates elements from nearly every architectural style, including a copy of the Elizabeth Tower.

name: Gloucester
description: Founded as a Roman fort, Gloucester grew into a significant medieval center, which saw the crowning of ten-year-old King Henry III, briefly hosted Parliament, and was even named its own country with the same rights as London. Gloucester Cathedral is undeniably the city's medieval masterpiece, with its Norman Romanesque core, England's first fan vaulted cloisters, and an intricate Perpendicular Gothic tower - not to mention the tomb of Edward II. In 1827, the 16.5 mile Gloucester-Sharpness canal was opened, which transformed the city into a major inland port, prompting the construction of docks and vast Victorian warehouses. Today, what was once the world's deepest canal now offers a peaceful waterside walk, while the docks and their brick warehouses are now home to a variety of museums and a waterfront shopping center.

name: Merida
description: Merida was founded by the Spanish conquistador Francisco de Montejo y León in 1542 on the site of the Mayan city of T'hó. Stones from the centuries-old Mayan city were quarried to build the Spanish Colonial buildings - the cathedral, for instance, was built using stones from temple of Yajam Cumu. In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Merida flourished thanks to its agave industry, and at one point was said to be home to more millionaires than any other city. This wealth is preserved by the Beaux Arts manors lining the Pasejo Montejo. With the third largest historic center in the Americas, there are innumerable cobbled side-streets where you can wander among charming colonial-era homes in various states of disrepair. With the largest indigenous population of any city in Mexico, it's well worth exploring the sights, sounds, and flavors of the Lucas de Galvez market, or head to the Gran Museo del Mundo Maya to learn more about Mayan culture.

name: Binibeca Vell
description: Binibeca Vell, a picturesque coastal town nestled on the southern coast of Menorca, is a captivating blend of architectural charm and Mediterranean allure. Whitewashed villas and narrow streets define Binibeca, a serene haven designed for tranquility. The village emanates the essence of traditional fishermen's hamlets, echoing simplicity and a bygone era. Initially conceived as an idyllic retreat for intellectuals and artists, Binibeca realized this dream, attracting renowned painter Francesc Poch Romeu. The heart of Binibeca beats in its small commercial center, offering an array of restaurants, bars, and souvenir shops. While the village sways between ghost-town stillness in winter and vibrant life in summer, it maintains its unique charm throughout. Binibeca's allure extends beyond its architectural grace. The nearby Playa de Binibeca, with its Blue Flag Beach status, boasts fine sand and clear, shallow waters—ideal for families and snorkeling enthusiasts. Calas like Binibeca, Pequeña, and Sa Olla beckon with rocky charm, providing intimate escapes from the crowd. Exploring Binibeca Vell early in the morning unveils its authentic beauty, free from bustling crowds. With its distinctive blend of history, artistry, and coastal allure, Binibeca stands as a must-visit destination in Menorca.

name: Ciudad Tula
description: Ciudad Tula was founded in 1617 and boasts a rich cultural heritage that has been meticulously preserved throughout the years. Its well-preserved Historic Downtown showcases charming houses adorned with traditional ironwork balconies and architectural treasures that stand as testaments to the city's cultured and aristocratic past. Renowned for its artisanal crafts, Tula offers exceptional saddlery, pottery, and ixtle products you can peruse and purchase. Indulge in flavors of the region, with delightful dishes such as Enchiladas Tultecas and unique dessert options like Cactunieves—featuring flavors inspired by the semi-desert environment, including garambullo, tepolilla, pitaya, granjeno, una, biznaga, and chocha. Immerse yourself in the site of one of the oldest genetic lineages of America, with archeologists having discovered 30 skeletons estimated to be about 3,000 years old. This city evokes the splendor of the colonial era and the Porfiriato period, with must-see sites such as the Plaza de Armas and the San Antonio de Padua Church.

name: Ludwigslust
description: The elaborate Baroque palace, located in the heart of this small town, was originally built as a hunting lodge, but later became the primary residence of Duke Friedrich of Mecklenburg-Schwerin. In need of more space, the Duke commissioned Johann Joachim Busch to build a new, larger palace. The palace as it stands today, modelled after Busch's noticeably French-inspired designs, was completed in 1776. Visitors may now enjoy a tour of the resulting structure and view rooms such as the Golden Hall-- a huge room containing golden Corinthian columns and crystal chandeliers below an ornately decorated ceiling. Interestingly, many of the wall and ceiling decorations found inside are made of papier mâché, known as "Ludwigslust board". Visitors can also wander into the surrounding English-style gardens to stumble upon fountains, mausoleums, the Swiss House, and the Stone Bridge. Many claim that its surrounding properties are even more impressive than the palace itself!

name: Berlin
description: One of Europe's most infamous cities, for centuries Berlin has been a stronghold for Kingdoms, Republics, and Empires. This major player in the European Union was only reunified in 1990 and has been going from strength to strength ever since. Berlin's history is commemorated and recognized throughout the city in its prominent landmarks that serve as a serious reminder of the events that impacted the world such as the Brandenburg Gate, the Reichstag building, and remnants of the Berlin Wall. All around the city, however, it is clear that it has moved on from what it once was. Just to the south of these monuments is Potsdamer Platz, the heart of the city and cultural hub offering shops, restaurants, and cinemas. To the east is the iconic Berlin Tower and the unique Museum Island, a floating forum of arts and culture. And behind them is Berlin's 'green lung', Tiergarten Park. Although this flowering park is adorned with monuments and memorials, like the Victory Column and the Kaiser-Wilhelm Church; here you will also find the House of World Cultures, Berlin Zoo, bustling cafés, a teahouse, and the beautiful Rhododendron Grove, an enchanting garden full of colorful flowers. Visit at Christmas to be enticed by Berlin's magical Christmas markets, perfect for finding unique souvenirs and trying classic German foods alongside some spiced mulled wine underneath the sparkle of the Christmas lights.

name: Avignon
description: Inhabited since the Neolithic period, this ancient city's name was recorded for the first time in the 6th century BC when a fortified Greek settlement was built on top of the rocky outcrop overlooking the river. In 1309 Pope Clement V selected the city as his residence, and for the next several decades it would be the capital of all of Christendom, receiving a bounty of rich architecture, including the Palace of the Popes - the largest Gothic palace in Europe. Now a UNESCO site, within the castle's 18 foot thick walls, visitors can enjoy exploring staterooms, chapels, cloisters, and frescoed papal apartments. The city's other UNESCO monument is the "Pont d'Avignon", of nursery-rhyme fame, the remains of a 14th century bridge. On top of the UNESCO sites, the city's bounty of opulent churches, majestic palaces, and scenic streets make it hard for many visitors to pull themselves away.

name: Osijek
description: Osijek is Croatia's fourth largest city and the largest city of the Slavonia region. It's a university city with a plethora of parks, pubs, and clubs for visitors to explore. Osijek was heavily damaged during the 1990's conflict. Although remnants from the war are still present, many of the city's buildings have since been restored. The main sight of Osijek is Tvrda, the oldest part of town. It's the best preserved and largest accumulation of Baroque buildings in all of Croatia. Tvrda houses the Museum of Slavonia, a Franciscan Monastery, and the church of St. Anthony (with an impressive spire). Another area worth exploring is the Upper Town, Gornji Grad. This part of town is most known for the Neo-Gothic Church of St. Peter and Paul.

name: Scicli
description: Scicli is likely named after the Sicel tribe who founded the town around 300 BC. While the town flourished as a medieval trade center, its most notable era came in the late Baroque period when the town had to be rebuilt following a massive earthquake. Today, visitors can experience the town's Baroque splendor with a walk through the largely car-free historic center. Of the town's countless Baroque churches and palaces, the most most richly decorated is the Church of San Bartolomeo. But since the Baroque style permeates the entire town, not just the monuments, explorers are rewarded with beautiful details at every turn, particularly on the recently restored Via Mormina Pen, where sumptuous palaces are sidled alongside splendid churches.

name: Sanremo
description: A stone's throw away from Nice, Sanremo has the grit of Paris and the charm of a small town. The Riviera di Ponente is popular amongst tourists for its year-long lovely weather, collection of flowers, and its infamous Sanremo Music Festival. After the gamblers are ready to revel in their winnings from the Monte Carlo casinos, they hop 50km west toward Sanremo to lounge in the exquisite villas and lavish resorts. Sanremo is a perfect stop to dip your feet into the Mediterranean after enjoying some delicious fine dining. Take a moment to explore the priceless gems of the medieval old town section, La Pigna and live large in Sanremo.

name: Daejeon
description: Embrace Daejeon's bountiful natural environment , full of mountains, hot springs, and rivers open for public enjoyment. While Daejeon's SkyRoad often takes center stage in travel recommendations, the Jungang Traditional Market adjacent to the train station offers a genuine experience of Korean culture, tantalizing taste buds with an array of mouthwatering street food delights. For those seeking retail therapy, the Jungangno Underground Shopping Center offers fantastic deals on a variety of local products. For breathtaking city views, a trip to Daedong Sky Park is highly recommended. As part of a neighborhood revitalization project blending art and community development, Daedong stands as the highest village in Daejeon, offering panoramic vistas of the city's skyline. For a soothing retreat, the Yuseong Hot Spring awaits in the North-West section of Daejeon, renowned for its mineral-rich waters containing healing properties, including alkaline minerals like calcium, potassium, sulfur, carbonic acid, silicic acid, and radium. Daejeon's compelling fusion of technology, nature, and entertainment ensures an enriching and unforgettable experience for both locals and visitors alike.

name: Chiapa de Corzo
description: Chiapa de Corzo was the first settlement founded by the Spanish in Chiapas, though the area had been settled since at least 1400 BC. According to local lore, when Diego de Mazariegos invaded the area in 1528, the native Chiapa hurled themselves to their death in the nearby canyon rather than surrender. Today, it's a quiet town where colonial architecture and indigenous culture harmoniously coexist. In the arcade-lined main plaza, where you'll find the 16th century, Moorish-style La Pila fountain, and the nearby Temple and Ex Convent of Santo Domingo is a beautiful blend of Moorish Gothic, Renaissance and Neoclassical styles. The Lacquer Museum inside offers a look at the area's most important craft. You can also get a glimpse of the ancient indigenous capital at the small archaeological site, where the oldest tomb and oldest writing example in Mesoamerica were found. If you're not sure when to visit, shoot for the 4th to 23rd of January when they hold the UNESCO-listed Great January Feast!

description: Nantou, uniquely known as the only landlocked county in Taiwan, will welcome you with the warm hospitality of its locals and rich historical heritage. . Among the notable attractions is the Bamboo Rock Garden, where towering bamboo provides shade and serenity, making it an ideal place for a relaxing break. The garden is also home to a butterfly garden and an adjoining hotel. Nearby, the Tea Research and Extension Station invites visitors to quench their thirst for knowledge and tea. Carp Lake, although situated on the outskirts of the township, offers stunning scenery and a plethora of outdoor activities such as boating, camping, picnicking, and hiking. For those interested in delving into Taiwan's early cultures, the Formosan Aboriginal Cultural Village offers an engaging and informative experience. Visitors can enjoy captivating shows presented by the Yamei, Puwan, and Yen tribes while savoring authentic dishes prepared by tribal master chefs during a delightful dinner.

name: Montecatini Alto
description: Montecatini Alto has been a health spa for many centuries, giving it a reputation of beauty care wellbeing. First appearing on a map in 1016 AD, the town has many ancient buildings (including the remains of a castle), several palazzos, and a few churches. Montecatini Alto's historic funicolare, the oldest in Europe, connects the modern town below with the ancient city above. Built in 1898, the funicolare still uses its original red cable cars. Should you visit before Easter and up until the end of October, make sure to catch a ride on the cable car to catch a glimpse of the gorgeous Tuscan hills. Montecatini Alto's lovely old town has many artisan shops and restaurants boasting delicious wine and traditional Tuscan cuisine. Stroll along old town's large piazza and indulge in delectable food and wine to add to the overall relaxation of your time in this spa town.

name: San Gimignano
address.addr1: San Gimignano, Province of Siena, Italy
description: With strict restoration rules, San Gimignano has maintained its authenticity and history to this day. Considered a gem in the Tuscan region and just a stone's throw from Florence, this town has always had a favorable location. Its beautiful surroundings and elevated position made it the perfect relay point for those on pilgrimage to Rome. A special must-see in San Gimignano are its 14 towers - the survivors of an original 72. Admire the Romanesque and Gothic architecture while discovering one of the many museums holding some of the most coveted Italian artworks of the 14th and 15 centuries. Afterwards, take a walking tour of the inner-city walls. Yes, they are two! San Gimignano is protected by a set of two walls, which are accessible by various entries both from the inside and outside of town.

name: Osan
description: Osan holds dozens of hidden gems, from sprawling markets to historically significant sites. Osan Market has operated continuously since 1792, offering a vibrant and bustling shopping experience. Osan is also the site of the first battle between US and North Korean forces, an event commemorated by a dedicated statue and museum on its outskirts, honoring the bravery of UN forces. The Osan Air Base, a military installation, also provides access to South Korea's rich culture, delectable cuisine, diverse shopping opportunities, and captivating tourist sites. Nature enthusiasts will find delight in the Mulhyanggi Arboretum, a picturesque destination adorned with blooming flowers, lush trees, and charming walking paths. The greenhouses offer an opportunity to explore a variety of plant species, making it an enchanting experience, particularly during spring and fall when nature adorns itself with vibrant colors. Gwollisa Temple stands as a tranquil oasis amidst the city's hustle and bustle. The temple grounds are well-maintained, featuring beautiful structures that exude serenity. Despite being surrounded by urban life, the temple offers a peaceful sanctuary for those seeking quiet reflection.

name: Exeter
description: A prehistoric tribal capital, Exeter was a fortified Roman settlement before becoming a religious centre in the Middle Ages and through the Tudor era. Though large parts of the city were destroyed during World War II, Exeter still has some stupendous historic landmarks, such as the 15th century Cathedral, which has the country's longest uninterrupted vaulted ceiling, spectacular stained glass, the UK's earliest set of misericords, and a 15th century astronomical clock. Heading down to the waterfront, you're sure to pass the imposing Roman wall. For a unique experience, you can even tour the network of medieval tunnels that brought water into the city! To see the city's 2000 year history under one roof, don't miss the Royal Albert Memorial Museum, or if you'd rather learn about the city's rich history while soaking in its sights, you can join an award-winning Red Coat Guided Tour.

name: Florina
description: The regional capital and gateway to the lakes region, Florina enjoyed a Renaissance around 1893 when it was connected to Thessaloniki by rail. This boom is evident throughout the city in the eclectic early 20th century architecture. The best way to enjoy the city's beauty is a walk along the scenic river promenade. Among the buildings on the left bank, visitors will find the Modern Art Museum, and the House of Voyiatzis, where Angelopoulos filmed many scenes for "The Beekeeper". On the opposite side, stands one of the city's most impressive mansions - the "House of Peios". When you're ready for a break, but still want to enjoy the view, stop by a cafe for some coffee or to sample some of the local specialties.

name: Koper
description: A carpet of white stone leads you along the narrow streets to the monumental architecture of Koper's main square. The square is less-inhabited by tourists and gains a heavy influence from the Venetian Era. It also houses the largest cathedral in Slovenia, the Praetorian Palace. The palace served as the official residence of the city's governor during the Venetian Republic. Koper is officially a bilingual town and mixes Italian and Slovenian culture to showcase its colorful roots.

name: Cadbury World
description: Since 1990, Cadbury World has been bringing the story of the beloved chocolate brand to life on the site of its original manufacturing site. Instead of your usual 'factory tour', Cadbury World's 14 zones immerses visitors in the brand through video presentations, multi-sensory cinema, activities, and demonstrations. Discover the origins of the cocoa bean amidst an Aztech jungle, or walk down Advertising Avenue to see how Cadbury has marketed itself over the years. And of course indulge in some sweet, sweet chocolate - from a complimentary pot of delicious melted chocolate to the endless options of the world's largest Cadbury shop. As one of the most popular attractions in Birmingham, we recommend purchasing tickets in advance. For more information, please visit cadburyworld.co.uk

name: Sesimbra
description: When Alfonso I, the first king of Portugal, captured a Moorish castle in 1165, he founded the town of Sesimbra on the hilltop overlooking a sheltered bay. While the castle fell back into Moorish hands in 1191, it was recaptured in the 13th century, and donated to the Order of St. James for defence and settlement. It was restored in the 18th century, and is now an essential place to visit for its marvellous view of the town and the sea. The friendly seas offered a bounty of seafood, persuading the population to settle down the hill, turning this town into one of the region's main fishing ports. A popular getaway for the Portuguese, the excellent local cuisine, specialising in shellfish and fresh fish, can't be missed.

description: This educational center is famous for its colonial architecture, filled with stunning villas, whose murals always make a striking impression. First, stop by Casa del Fundador Gonzalo Suarez Rendon and walk through the patio, adorned with beautiful flowers. Tour the rooms and see some of the intricately painted ceilings that were discovered when a false ceiling collapsed. Next, visit the astonishing Templo de Santo Domingo, plated with red and gold, this church surprises all who enter. Then, tour the 16th century convent Capilla y Museo de Santa Clara La Real, and hear the story of Colombia's version of Mother Teresa, Madre Francisca Josefa, as this was her home in the 17th century. This convent is usually locked, so you will need to knock on the door to get in!

name: Ouarzazate
description: For most of its history, Ouarzazate was a small trade town, seeing villagers from the Atlas, Draa and Dadès Valleys meet at its Taourirt Kasbah. However, in the 1920s, the French used it as a garrison town, administrative center, and customs post, greatly expanding the town. Ouarzazate's traditional architecture has made it a popular film location, being featured in everything from Lawrence of Arabia to The Living Daylights to Game of Thrones. Even American horror movie The Hills Have Eyes was shot nearby, and visitors can still see its abandoned set. After exploring the historic medina, kasbah, or film sets, shoppers will want to head to the central market where you'll find all manner of goods, including the area's signature carpets with geometric designs of red-orange on black background.

address.addr1: 70044 Polignano a Mare, Metropolitan City of Bari, Italy
description: Polignano A Mare has been settled since prehistory, and based on archaeological findings, was known as Neapolis by the Greeks. Believed to be one of the most important settlements in the region, despite there being no written record of it, the town was subsequently settled by everyone from the Romans to the Huns to the Normans. Today, the charming town is a popular weekend escape from Bari, who come to watch the crashing waves from the cliffs, explore the many caves on the coast, or simply enjoy the delicious ice cream and cornettos (Italian croissants). While the Red Bull Cliff Diving competition draws major crowds, perhaps the town's best known export is Domenico Modugno, the man responsible for the international hit 'Volare' (you know the one).

name: Safranbolu
description: Between the 13th and early 20th centuries, Safranbolu flourished as a key caravan station on the East–West trade route, and major saffron producer (its name is literally 'saffron city'). At its height in the 17th century, Safranbolu was influencing architecture and urban development throughout the Ottoman Empire. While trade has since dried up, its reputation as an influential Ottoman settlement hasn't. Visitors flock to immerse themselves in the well-preserved Old Town, which has over 1000 registered historical monuments. Exploring the charming Old Town, you'll find tombs, Turkish baths, a historical clock tower, elegant bridges, and hundreds of traditional mansions and houses. Standout monuments include the Old Mosque, Old Bath, and Süleyman Pasha Medrese, which were all built in 1322. Step into a restaurant or cafe and you'll find costumed staff and traditional dishes keeping Ottoman heritage alive.

name: Great Orme
description: Formed by stark limestone and dolomite cliffs rising nearly 700 feat, Great Orme is Wales' answer to the Cliffs of Dover. After enjoy dramatic views from the Coastal Drive, visitors can hop on Britain's longed cable car or the Victorian-era tramway for a unique ride up to the peninsula's highest peak. After taking in the panoramic views of the coast and countryside, you can learn about the headland's fascinating geology, archaeology, ecology, and history at the visitor center. Hikers can then set out to enjoy the lovely landscape, and perhaps spot rare species like the red-billed chough and silver-studded blue butterfly. History lovers won't want to miss the 3,500-year-old Great Orme copper mine - the largest site of its kind in the world. Called "the Stonehenge of copper mining", over 30,000 animal bones were found in the 5 miles of tunnels, along with Bronze Age artifacts, such as tools and even human fingerprints.

name: Tema
description: Explore the dynamic city of Tema, a modern metropolis on the shores of Ghana's Atlantic coast. As one of Africa's largest seaports, Tema buzzes with activity, serving as a vital hub for trade and commerce in the region. Marvel at the impressive infrastructure and bustling waterfront as cargo ships come and go, connecting Ghana to the global economy. Beyond its industrial prowess, Tema boasts a lively cultural scene and a diverse array of attractions. Explore the vibrant neighborhoods, where colorful street art and lively markets showcase the city's creative spirit. Indulge in delicious Ghanaian cuisine at local eateries, where you can savor traditional dishes bursting with flavor and spices. For those seeking relaxation, Tema offers beautiful beaches where you can soak up the sun, swim in the refreshing waters, or enjoy water sports like surfing and snorkeling. And with its proximity to Accra, Ghana's capital city, Tema serves as an ideal base for exploring the wider region.

name: Matera
description: While 'new', above-ground city was founded in the 3rd century BC by the Romans, the troglodyte city carved into the rocky ravine has been inhabited for the past 7000 years or so. In 1945, the cave dwellings earned international recognition when author Carlo Levi described the children, naked or in rags, ravaged by disease, concluding "I have never seen in all my life such a picture of poverty." The Italian Prime Minister even visited in 1950, calling the living conditions "a national disgrace". The inhabitants were forcibly relocated to the 'new' town, and for many, it was their first time seeing running water. Today, thanks to aid from the Italian government, UNESCO, and Hollywood, the caves have been refurbished, and are now home to thriving pubs, hotels, and airbnb listings. Above ground, the city's home to several medieval monuments, such as the 13th century cathedral, and 16th century castle.

name: Syracuse
description: Founded by Greek colonists in 734 BC, Syracuse was an ancient superpower, warring with Athens, Carthage, and Rome. Over its long history, the city has accrued a rich collection of landmarks and attractions that are sure to satisfy any visitor several times over. At the ancient city, which Cicero called 'the greatest Greek city and the most beautiful of them all', visitors will find one of the world's largest Greek amphitheatres, the "Ear of Dionysius" cave with its legendary acoustics, as well as temples, and a museum filled with more delicate artefacts. Syracuse's island of Ortygia is a delightfully eclectic mixture of architecture, where visitors will find Greek and Roman remains, medieval buildings, and Baroque marvels. This is embodied by the Piazza del Duomo, where the Baroque cathedral incorporates an ancient Temple of Athena. Also on this square is the Baroque Palazzo Beneventano and the church of Santa Lucia - the town's patron saint.

name: Karuizawa
description: Karuizawa is a popular resort town located just a few hours away from Tokyo, at the foot of the active volcano, Mount Asama, in Nagano Prefecture. Despite its small size, which allows for quick exploration, the town offers a dreamy setting amidst beautiful nature. Visitors can explore Harunire Terrace, a shopping strip showcasing notable wooden architecture situated next to a river. Adjacent to the Harunire Terrace are the Kogen Church and Stone Church. Not far from the terrace is the shopping street, Kyukaruizawa Ginza-dori (Old Karuizawa Shopping Street), where one can get souvenirs and local handicrafts. For a serene experience, a stroll around Kumoba Pond is highly recommended, known for its tranquil atmosphere. For relaxation, Hoshino Onsen (an "onsen" is a Japanese hot spring) is a compact yet delightful stop. Many visitors also flock to the town for skiing, as the Karuizawa Prince Ski Resort is one of the most accessible ski destinations from Tokyo.

name: Druskininkai
description: First mentioned in 1636, Druskininkai became a popular destination in the 18th century when it was believed that its mineral-rich waters helped treat asthma and other ailments. In the early 19th century University of Vilnius professor Ignacy Fonberger began promoting Druskininkai to the population of Vilnius as a spa town. Today, Druskininkai is Lithuania's oldest and chicest spa town, attracting both hip Lithuanians, and tourists from abroad. While visitors can of course head to Druskininkai's famed spas, the town is centered around its peaceful park. Walking around a small lake, visitors can't miss the red-brick belltower of St. Mary's Church. A historic villa nearby houses the Druskininkai Museum, which features both historical exhibits about the town, as well as a special exhibition of local artists. M.K. Ciurlionis, one of Lithuania's most famous artists, was from Druskininkai, and his family home is now a museum dedicated to his life and work.

name: Tulum
description: Tulum was founded around the 13th century by the Mayans as a fortified port, and was one of the last cities the empire built before its collapse. Tulum itself managed to survive about 70 years into the Spanish occupation, eventually being abandoned after being ravaged by Old World diseases. Today, a laid back beach town lies just inland, while the sea-front is lined with idyllic beach bungalows. With powdery white sands and cobalt blue waters, the beaches here are some of the best in Mexico and don't (yet) see the crowds that flood Cancun. And there's nowhere else in the world that you can go from exploring a Mayan ruin to swimming with turtles in a matter of minutes. Once you're done with your fun in the sun, you can unwind at one of the many bars and restaurants, sipping a fruity cocktail, and gorging yourself on some of the tastiest, fresh-focused food Mexico has to offer.

name: Vanadzor
description: Tucked away in the northern reaches of Armenia, Vanadzor, the third-largest city, unveils its Bronze Age origins through the archaeological sites dotted across the area. Remnants from the 4th millennium BC peek from the nearby Mashtots hill, while the Lori-Pambak archaeological museum chronicles the region's history. The city's industrial quarters, once bustling with chemical production during the Soviet era, now stand as silent, poignant echoes of its industrial past. Vanadzor, translating to 'Valley of the Church,' is the spiritual heart of the Gougark Diocese section of the Armenian Apostolic Church, with the towering St. Gregory the Illuminator Church as the city's biggest church. The lively Hayk Square with architecture pulses with the city's rhythm. Unique landmarks include Master Mehrab's beautifully decorated house, a testament to the local artist's life, and the eccentric 19th-century Tairov House.

name: San Antonio de Areco
description: Don't let this town's small size fool you - there's plenty of charm packed into this tiny treasure located 70 km northwest of Buenos Aires. Some of San Antonio's most revered art forms include silverwork and saddlery, which testify to its long gaucho and criollo heritage since the town's founding in the 18th century. You can pay the Draghi a museum a visit to find some of these silversmith works on display, and discover local artwork depicting the town's history at the Museo Las Lilas de Areco and Museo de Arte La Recova. Then, grab a bite to eat at the main square, Plaza Ruiz de Arellano, and satisfy your sweet tooth and munch on alfajores at La Olla De Cobre, San Antonio's mini chocolate factory. End the day with a stroll to Puente Viejo, an iconic pedestrian bridge with idyllic sunset views. We recommend planning your visit to account for the siesta hours in the afternoon.

name: Bregenz
description: Nestled on the shores of Lake Constance, Bregenz has been settled since 1500 BC. Over the centuries, the city grew in importance, becoming the regional capital in the 18th century. At the heart of the medieval town center, the Baroque St. Martin's Tower lets visitors admire 14th century frescoes and views across the lake into Germany and Switzerland all in one place. For another all-encompassing cultural experience, the Vorarlberg Museum exhibits regional artefacts dating back to prehistoric times, and art installations. During the summer, the internationally renowned hosts a world famous summer music festival and dance festival. Though no matter the time of year, visitors can always admire the scenery, and the world's largest floating stage, which was featured in the James Bond film 'Quantum of Solace'.

name: Zamosc
description: Zamosc escaped destruction during the Second World War and its buildings present a marvelous sight. Most of the town has been renovated over the years and the elevations and colors on the buildings mean plenty of top-notch photo opportunities. The colorful town hall and the market square are two of the top attractions in the town and the sixteenth-century square is a wide open space comprised of colorful merchant houses. The many bars and restaurants give the square a relaxed and friendly feel while the highlight of the square is the town hall with its fan-shaped double stairway which, unsurprisingly, is a popular spot for couples to have wedding photos taken. It is easy to see why this charming settlement became known as the "Pearl of the Renaissance", with everything in walking distance so visitors can explore, relax and soak up the vibe of this traditional gem of a market town.

name: Leiria
description: According to a popular Portuguese rhyme, Leiria has a river that flows uphill, a tower that does not have a cathedral, a cathedral that does not have a tower, and a High Street that is not straight. Built at the foot of a promontory that's been fortified since Moorish times, the town's dramatically situated castle offers visitors commanding views of the narrow streets and red-tiled roofs of the historic centre, built along the lazy curves of the Rio Lis. The historic city center houses the 12th century church of São Pedro and a Cathedral with 17th century artwork. The Praça Rodrigues Lobo offers visitors great views of the castle, and a scenic place to enjoy some local cuisine. The surrounding pine forest is courtesy of Dom Dinis, the poet king, who planted the trees to control the shifting sand dunes, and to provide quality timber for the building of ships.

name: Lisbon
description: Lisbon comes from humble beginnings. Starting as a mere pre-Celtic settlement, the area became the stuff of Greek legends, Roman Military tactics, and even a Kingdom of Islam. Its story is evident throughout the city; cobblestone paths take you through neighborhoods of Visgoth, Arabic, and Romanesque influence, like charming Alfama, traditional Mouraria, and the lively Bairro Alto. Lisbon is littered with landmarks, like St. Jorge Castle, the Arco do Triunfo, and the Monument to the Discoveries; allowing for panoramic vistas that capture the towering terrain. The city itself is bestowed with, not just one but two UNESCO World Heritage Sites; the iconic Belém Tower and the intricate Jerónimos Monastery. All of which is encompassed by the sprawling River Tagus, spanned by two magnificent bridges, the 25 de Abril and, Europe's longest, the Vasco da Gama. Take it all in from the comfort of an iconic yellow tram, while biting into a sumptuous Pasteis de Nata (custard pie). However, on foot, you will certainly get to appreciate the true beauty of Lisbon; with streets flowered with 'Azulejo' tiles, a quintessentially Portuguese art form.

name: Andong
description: Often referred to as "the capital of Korean spirit", Andong's allure transcends national borders, as evidenced by Queen Elizabeth II's visit in 1999 after being told it was the "most Korean place in Korea". The revered Andong Hahoe Folk Village, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2010, is a sprawling village in Andong that showcases an intriguing coexistence of commoners and nobles from Korea's Goryeo period. Another remarkable landmark is the Bongjeongsa Temple, the largest temple in Andong. Its architectural marvel includes the second oldest wooden building in Korea. One cannot talk about Andong without mentioning its mouthwatering culinary offerings, such as the famed jjimdak, a delectable spicy chicken dish. A journey to Andong is a journey through time, where history and traditions intertwine harmoniously. This city provides an escape from the modern world, inviting visitors to relish rural Korea and immerse themselves in the cultural treasures of the Joseon dynasty.

name: Cacaxtla-Xochitecatl Archeological Site
description: Tombs and artifacts left by the Olmeca-Xicalanca people now reside in the Cacaxtla-Xochitecatl archeological sites. Located just south of the border of Tlaxcala, these sites have an impressive inventory of artifacts from 650-900 CE. Cacaxtla was sprawling a palace during it's time, but now archaeologists have discovered the Gran Basamento, which is covered with ancient paintings, still with vibrant reds, blues, yellows, blacks, and whites. Some of the most famous being the Battle Mural and the murals depicted in the Venus Temple, but there are many more to see! Xochitecatl is a ceremonial complex where figurines revolving around the cycle of women, as well as burial sites for children and other community members. Discover the many rooms and tombs in this incredible archaeological site, fit for Indiana Jones.

name: Turda
description: Originally a Dacian settlement, under Roman control the city eventually earned the status of colony, thanks in no small part to the nearby salt mine. In 1568, Transylvanian legislators met in Turda's Roman Catholic church to sign an edict saying that every priest can interpret the Gospel in whatever way he thought correct, free from punishment or threats - one of the first such rulings of its kind. This long, rich history is preserved in the town history museum, which exhibits everything from Bronze Age artefacts, to a lapidarium, to local artwork. The oddly shaped town square, which is more like a long street, is a scenic walk that brings visitors past pretty 18th-19th century buildings, the courthouse with its squat clock tower, and a bustling marketplace. At the far end is the town hall, and two more churches - the 15th century Calvinist Gothic Church, and the gleaming new Orthodox.

name: Tabor
description: The historic town of Tabor set on a picturesque South Bohemia hilltop is a popular tourist attraction due to its large amount of historical and natural treasures. The compact historic town center can be walked in just over an hour, so makes for an ideal stop-off point. The history of the town is strongly connected to the Hussite movement and its major role in European history and the Hussite Museum provides a fascinating insight into this period. Visitors can choose from a variety of attractions ranging from the town walls through to churches, monuments and a host of historic sites. More intrepid visitors may wish to explore the Tabor Tunnels that form an underground network running underneath the houses in the main square while those with a sweet tooth can while away the time in the Museum of Chocolate and Marzipan, which by all accounts, smells just as good as it looks.

name: Belgodere
description: Belgodère is hidden in the Balagne region in upper Corsica, settled when the Feudal lord Marquis de Massa first climbed the peak of rocks in 1268. Since then, its aging houses, architectural peculiarities and religious relics have brought curious travelers to its winding streets. Admire the baroque style Church of Saint Thomas and the beautiful domes inside, then explore the three chapels and crumbling ruins of a convent. Wander through the fortified area of Belgodère in the Cima du Fondu and Cabanne districts and climb to the top of the tower for an exceptional view. Or, take in the undulating hillsides from a terrace cafe after a stroll through the Sunday morning summer markets.
