name: Elounda
description: Elounda has thousands of years of history, but it's best known as "the Cretan Riviera" for its high-end tourism industry. Both Greek and international VIPs have been flocking here for decades - you might even spot a familiar face, especially if you're hanging out near any of the luxury resorts in the area. Elounda's old town has been influenced by various empires throughout history, including the Minoans and the Ottomans. Akti Virtomartis street and Elounda Square are the places to shop and dine, especially if you crave seafood. The main harbour, also known as the Gult of Korfos, is a perfect place for a coastline walk. If you want to rub elbows while swimming, Elounda Beach (Paralia Schisma) is the place to be, while the Spinalonga Peninsula offers more secluded beaches. To spice up your day with adventure, explore the sunken city of Olous where you can snorkel around the ruins (you'' need to arrange an excursion independently). Please note: that the islands of Kolokitha and Spinalonga are inaccessible by Daytrip drivers, so you'll need to make arrangements in town if you'd like to visit.

name: Latacunga
description: Founded by the Spanish in 1534, Latacunga was destroyed four times by earthquakes and volcanic eruptions between 1698 and 1798. Despite the threat of destruction, the indomitable people of Latacunga rebuilt each time. While most people only pass through Latacunga on their way to the Quilotoa Loop or Parque Nacional Cotopaxi, behind the sprawl by the Panamerican Highway, the city has a surprisingly charming historic center. At the Parque Vicente Léon you'll find the elegant 17th century cathedral, which has an altar made from pumice, and the municipal palace, which is made entirely from the volcanic stone. The splendid Casa de los Marqueses de Miraflores mansion has been turned into a museum house exhibiting artworks and archaeological items discovered in the area. Every September, the city holds its Mama Negra festival to celebrate its indigenous, Spanish, and African heritage, and the Virgin who saved the town during the 1742 eruption.

name: Nafpaktos
description: Considered one of the most beautiful and romantic towns on the Greek mainland, it's no wonder this seaside village has been a favourite escape for thousands of years. Visitors can admire the same beautiful coastal setting that attracted the Romans 2000 years ago, leaving their baths behind as a reminder. Towering above the quiet cobbled streets, naval houses, and well-preserved mansions is the gorgeous Venetian, which offers beautiful views of the bay. To get closer to the water, the promenade is lined with cafés and restaurants serving fresh seafood and superb sea-views.

name: Cavtat
description: Cavat has a healthy mix of ancient and modern architecture due to its origins under Greek rule. After facing total destruction many times, it has been built and restored on the foundation of ruins countless times. Here lies Cavat's charm. Just by wandering the streets one would find traces of the Renaissance, features of the Gothic, and treasures of the old Dubrovnik Republic. Pass by the remnants of the old amphitheater as you make your way to see the Franciscan monastery, the Rector's Palace, and the church dedicated to Our Lady of Cavtat. The hidden passages and small streets will transport you back in time. This heavily wooded peninsula with a great sea view will be a perfect stop near Dubrovnik!

name: Madaba
description: Dating back to the Bronze Age, Madaba is mentioned in the Bible as a Moabite border city. From the 2nd through 7th centuries, it was an important stop on the King's Highway trade route but was destroyed by an earthquake in 746 and abandoned. In 1880 a Christian community from Karak resettled the site, and uncovered numerous mosaics during their excavations of the city. The most famous of which is a 6th century map of the Holy Land on the floor of a Byzantine cathedral, which is now preserved within the confines of the Greek Orthodox Church of St. George. Comprised of millions of pieces of colored stone, it's the earliest record of Byzantine Jerusalem. There hundreds of other mosaics scattered throughout the city, with some exceptional examples being found in the Church of the Virgin and the Apostles, and the several other Byzantine churches in Madaba's extensive Archaeological Park and Museum.

name: Zacatecas
description: The narrow, winding streets lend a medieval charm to Zacatecas, a Mexican city built into a canyon where silver was discovered in the early 1500's. The city was built on the mining industry and became a huge economic centre due to its production of silver, mined by indigenous slaves. Today, mining is still important in Zacatecas and tourists can delve into the depths of the city's industrial history by visiting El Edén, an old mine hand-dug beneath the city. Many galleries sell locally crafted jewelry, but for the chance to experience silversmiths at work, the Centro Platero Zacatecano just out of town is the place to be. There is plenty more to see in Zacatecas as the historical centre is filled with monasteries, churches, cathedrals and museums. The colonial part of the city is a World Heritage Site, declared so due to its impressive displays of baroque architecture, including the iconic pink-stone Zacatecas Cathedral that sits atop the city, dominating the skyline.

name: Setif
description: Once an important trade hub and now a lively student city, Setif is most known for being the center of a century-long controversy over "Algeria's most symbolic fountain". Built by a French architect in 1899, the El Fouara Fountain in the city center depicts a naked woman, and has been the center of debate between Algeria's secularists and Islamists since its erection. The statue was vandalized several times, but it still stands and remains the symbol of the city. Apart from the fountain, Setif is known for its ancient roots, having been part of the Phoenician and Roman empires and the kingdom of Numidia. The city's archeological museum is the prime place to explore this history: small but beautiful, it's often described as one of the best museums in Algeria, particularly for its 4th and 5th century mosaics. About an hour outside of town, the UNESCO-listed Djemila ruins showcase the area's ancient history, and are one of the finest testaments of Roman architecture in North Africa, featuring a forum, temples, basilicas, triumphal arches, and houses. Daytrip offers the ruins as a separate stop.

name: Vannes
description: Founded by the Romans in the 1st century, by the 3rd century, the empire's decline had left the city vulnerable enough to warrant erecting defensive walls. These were expanded an altered up until the 1630s when the Garenne bastion was added. Today, they're one of the only remaining city fortifications in Brittany, made even more beautiful by carefully tended gardens. Much of the historic quarter is from the 16th century, filled with brightly coloured half timbered houses and many of the city's 272 monuments. The 15th-century Château-Gaillard once served as the Breton parliament building, and now houses the history and archaeology museum. Inside, along with historic furnishings, visitors will find prehistoric artefacts, as well as medieval. The town cathedral took 700 years to complete, so it exhibits elements of nearly every architectural style, from its 13th century belltower to its neo-Gothic ornamentation.

name: La Serena
description: Established in the 16th century, La Serena is the second oldest city in Chile and holds a rich cultural tapestry. Take a leisurely stroll from "El Faro" to Plaza Buenos Aires, savoring the artistic sculptures that line the way. Don't forget to indulge in some empanadas from a local bakery during your walk. In the heart of the city, you'll discover La Recova, a central market where you can explore a variety of goods. While it's not exclusively a tourist-centric souvenir market, it's a fascinating place to explore local offerings. Upstairs, you'll find cafes and restaurants to satisfy your culinary cravings. La Serena also boasts a significant number of churches, with 29 houses of worship scattered throughout the city. Among them, Iglesia San Francisco, dating back to the 1600s, stands as the oldest. When hunger strikes, head over to the Boulevard, La Serena's lively food truck corner.

name: Constantine
description: On par with Athens or Rome, Constantine proudly bears the title of one of the world's oldest cities. In fact Constantine is so old that its true origins are lost in time. While it was probably founded by the Phoenicians, it was definitely the ancient Numidian capital before being ruled by the Romans, Ottomans, and French - a true crossroads of civilizations. Proudly sitting on top of a hill and surrounded by water, the city's geographical position required a bounty of bridges, which erected its nickname "City of Bridges". The spans are some of the city's most iconic sights, so don't miss the stunning view from the Suspended Bridge, the ancient El Kantara Bridge, or the remarkable stone-arched Sidi Rached Bridge with a view over the Rhumel River. But Constantine's most impressive landmark is Emir Abdelkader mosque. You don't have to worry about missing it, because the mosque is among the largest ones on the continent, and visible from anywhere in the city! If that's not impressive enough, head to the Palace of Ahmed Dey, one of the finest Ottoman-era buildings in Algeria. Here you'll find lavish, marble-laden interiors and courtyards, and a lush garden with olive and orange trees, one of which was planted by Napoleon.

name: Las Terrazas
description: Las Terrazas (literally "The Terraces") was created in 1968 as part of Fidel Castro's "Green Revolution''. He enlisted architect Osmany Cienfuegos to build 1,360km of terraces, a self-sustaining community, and plant some 7 million trees. In 1985, the area became Cuba's first UNESCO Biosphere, and since the mid-90s, has been one of the island's most beloved natural retreats. Today, you have a wealth of ways to enjoy the natural surroundings. There's a mile-long zipline course that will take you over the village (they won't let you on if you've been drinking), a number of hiking trails, and horseback riding. Or if you prefer something more relaxing, you can sit back by Lago San Juan or the San Juan River. No matter which you choose, keep your eyes open for the many bird species. You can also tour Cafetal Buenavista, Cuba's oldest plantation, the lakeside home of renowned folk singer Polo Montañez, or visit a number of local artists' workshops. Please note: the cost of any activities is not included in the stop price.

name: Uusikaupunki
description: Settled 400 years ago, Uusikaupunki was home base for Finland's second largest fleet in the 19th century.This rich history has been preserved in both the town's historic district, where the streets are lined with signature Empire-style wooden houses, and its slew of maritime museums. Stroll the seaside promenade, where historic salt warehouses now now host cafes, restaurants, and shops before checking out the Sailor's Home Museum or the Naval Pilot Museum. If you're traveling with children, they'll be blown away by the Myllymäki Windmill Park, which has historic windmills, botanical gardens, and a playground. Finally, for a dose of absurdity, head to the Bonk Museum - a showcase of seemingly useless products created by Finnish artist Alvar Gullichsen, all of which are powered by anchovy oil.

name: Capel Manor Gardens
address.addr1: Capel Manor College Gardens, Bullsmoor Ln, Middlesex, Waltham Cross, Enfield EN1 4RQ, UK
description: The Capel Manor estate dates back to the 13th century, though the current Georgian-style house was built around 1750. on the site of a 13th century estate. It's last owner, Colonel Sydney Medcalf left the estate in Trust for future generations to enjoy. In 1968, the Capel Manor College was established - the only college in London focusing on horticulture and husbandry - and for the next 18 years, its visionary principal worked on restoring the manor and grounds. Today, 30 acres of themed gardens await visitors, allowing the opportunity to lose yourself in the Italianate Maze, get a taste of the Orient in the Japanese Garden, or see some of the students' original creations on Sunflower Street. Animal lovers can head to the manor zoo to see everything from alpacas to wallabies, and learn about the animals in special exhibitions. For more information, please visit www.capelmanorgardens.co.uk

name: Amarante
description: Nestled in Portugal's verdant wine country, Amarante has been settled since the 4th century BC. Spanning the river Tâmega is the striking Ponte São Gonçalo bridge. Accredited to the town's patron saint, Gonçalo, it is reputed to have helped local heroes fend off the French in the early 19th century. St. Gonçalo himself is entombed in the São Gonçalo Church. The interior of this charming 17th century Renaissance church glistens with its gilded baroque altar, pulpits, and organ. Just up the hill is the 18th century Igreja de São Domingos, which practically glows inside thanks to its gilded woodcarving. After touring the town, visitors can sit at one of the many riverfront cafes to enjoy Amarante's famous sweets.

name: Niagara Falls, ON
description: After Napoleon's brother brought his new bride to the Canadian side of Niagara Falls, it became the (self-proclaimed) "Honeymoon Capital of the World". North America's most powerful cascade also attracted Nichola Tesla, who helped create the world's first large hydroelectric power station that sent electricity long distances. In the years since, Niagara's popularity transformed the town into a "mini Las Vegas", with casinos and tourist attractions aplenty. At Clifton Hill, the tourist promenade, you can pop into the Ripley's Believe It Or Not Museum, the many haunted houses, as well as multiple wax museums! But who cares about the town? You're here for the amazing view, which you can take in right from the sidewalk (or even your hotel window). You can also ride a helicopter over the falls, take the Journey Behind the Falls, or a boat right up to the cascades!

name: Mauthausen
description: The last camp to be liberated in 1945, Mauthausen was a 'Grade 3' camp, tasked with the extermination through labour of Germany's political and ideological enemies, both real and imagined. Amongst Nazi officials it was referred to by the nickname 'The Bone Grinder' and inmates were forced to perform heavy manual labour in inhumane conditions. Thousands lost their lives. Mauthausen and its surrounding sub-camps now operate as a museum and memorial to the victims of these heinous crimes, ensuring that their ordeal will not be forgotten. Over 100 original objects are displayed in the museum as well as some 30 video and audio eye-witness testimonies from camp survivors and people who lived in the vicinity of the camp. An important and moving tribute to the brutality and persecution of Hitler's regime, Mauthausen deserves to be recognised alongside the more widely visited camps such as Auschwitz, Bergen-Belsen and Belzec.

name: El Jadida
description: This city of El Jadida was founded in the 16th century by Portuguese explorers. Originally known as Mazaga, it was one of their first settlements in Africa on the route to India. Between the 16th and 18th centuries, the city was a melting pot of European and Moroccan cultures, as evidenced by the architecture and town planning. On a short walk you'll be able to see the City Mosque, Chapel of St Sebastian, Church of the Assumption, synagogue, and El Jadida Lighthouse. The Portuguese fort is one of the best preserved coastal bastions in the country, and walking its ramparts, you'll not only get great views, but see the prototype for Renaissance military architecture. For many, the highlight of the visit are the 16th century cisterns. Originally a warehouse that was converted by the Portuguese into a water storage facility, there's often a shallow layer of water on the floor which reflects the vaulted columns in a grand manner.

name: Torreon
description: Torreon is an important economic centre in Mexico with a rich industrial history. The Plaza de Armas at the heart of the city is a great place to watch the world go by! Local museums showcase the history of the cotton industry, and display contemporary and historical art collections. At almost 22 metres high, the Cristo de las Noas statue towers atop Cerro de las Noas hill, arms open to protect the inhabitants of Torreon below. Known as the "Guardian", the statue is the largest of Christ in North America and sits 1,300 metres above sea level alongside a Catholic Church. A challenging climb of 600 steps is rewarded with spectacular panoramic views of the entire city and the opportunity to marvel at the striking concrete figure that was erected over a 27 year period. If you work up an appetite during the climb, treat yourself to a delicious meal in the restaurant at the top of the hill!

name: Lillehammer
description: Lillehammer brings a cozy small-town atmosphere to the grand, breathtaking mountains and scenic landscapes surrounding it, and offers an array of traditional Norwegian experiences. The town center is a charming composition of late 19th century wooden houses overlooking the northern part of lake Mjøsa and the river Lågen. Lillehammer was host to the 1994 Winter Olympics and is also a UNESCO City of Literature, making it a hotspot for cultural events and activities. The Maihaugen is a spectacular open-air museum, with the 13th century Garmo stave church on site. The Hunderfossen Adventure Park is one of the most popular amusement parks in Norway during the summertime and becomes a magical wonderland in winter. Make sure you sample one of the nation's all-time favorite cheeses while visiting Lillehammer, the sweet Gudbrandsdalsost, made right in the nearby Gudbrandsdalen valley from goats and cows' milk.

name: Vasteras
description: Västerås, originating in name from the river mouth of Svartån, is one of the oldest cities in Sweden and Northern Europe and brims with charm. It has been populated since 1000 CE by Nordic Vikings, who left behind a veritable gold mine of ruins and artifacts. Visit the Anundshög Viking Ruins for the best collection of Iron Age ruins in the region, including barrows, graveyards, and a thousand-year-old stone labyrinth. Walk along a pathway lined with rune stones, said to have been the Viking King's highway. Stop to visit the museum at the Västerås Castle, a redbrick building surrounded by gorgeous picnicking fields doused in the area's heritage. A Gothic style cathedral from 1271 offers an impressive array of church artifacts, while a world of adrenaline-inspiring fun awaits at the Kokpunkten water park, housed in an old steam works. Grab an ice cream and wander through the open-air Frösakers Brygga Ship Museum, try some traditional archery practice, and explore the sweet and historic neighborhood of Kyrkbacken.

name: La Falda
description: La Falda, surrounded by the scenic Cerro El Cuadrado and Cerro La Banderita, serves as a hub for tourism in the Punilla Valley. The iconic Avenue Edén beckons exploration, while natural wonders like the 7 Cascades and "El Silenco" castle contribute to the town's allure. Originally inaugurated in 1897 by a German hotelier, the opulent Hotel Edén became a beacon of luxury, hosting dignitaries, actors, and even Albert Einstein. However, its storied past took a darker turn in the prelude to World War II, as it became a haven for Nazi officials, with ties reaching Adolf Hitler himself. Despite its tumultuous history, Hotel Edén stands as a testament to architectural splendor. Declared a Historical Monument in 1988, this once-abandoned gem has been resurrected as a museum, inviting visitors to explore its grand Carrara marble stairs, dining rooms, solarium, and more. The hotel's golden age is vividly portrayed through exhibits featuring gala evenings, families with maids, and trunks filled with summer attire. The former hotel, now a public park and historic museum, welcomes guests for guided tours and private events, with night visits revealing intriguing myths and ghost stories.

name: Pissouri
description: Situated on an idyllic hillside near Cape Astro, Pissouri is divided into the upper village area and lower bay area. At one, you'll be able to enjoy stunning views of the sea and mountains amid a rustic hill-town. The area is renowned for its vineyards, and locals come here to taste a local variety of grapes and Halloumi cheese. Old Pissouri has been carefully preserved to retain its unique architecture and traditional way of living. The village square and amphitheater play host to annual celebrations and each residential building is decorated in a unique way. Nicknamed "The Edge of Heaven" and sometimes referred to as 'Little Italy', Old Pissouri is a haven for culture seekers. But head down to the water, and you'll find a rapidly developing resort town with hotels, shops, tavernas, restaurants, and bars backing the pebbly beach and pristine sea waters.

name: Amberg
description: Come and see what makes Amberg a great place to stop by. Many visitors begin at what is considered to be the symbol of the city — the famous sixteenth-century Stadtbrille gateway where the semi-circular arches cast reflections on the river to form the illusion of a pair of spectacles. Moving into the medieval town, many visitors head for the Marktplatz (the main square) where the Gothic town hall stands alongside colorful buildings. It is not unusual on a warm day to find both residents and tourists sat out in the square enjoying the sun. This small town, rich in culture and tradition has much to offer, with its large number of churches — many of which have been restored — a fascinating sculpture trail, the town walls and gates and of course, the world's smallest hotel where it is said that couples spending their wedding night will live happily ever after and never divorce.

name: Nonza
description: Nonza is a must-see location along Cap Corse, distinguished by a captivating black sand beach below the village and its bright pink 16th century Church of Saint Julie. Stop by the classical style church and admire the light interior with decorated walls and 17th and 18th century paintings. For a dramatic view overlooking the water and village, take an easy walk up to the Paoline Tower and browse through its modern gift shop selling jewelry and scarves. For an unforgettable experience, wine and dine at Michelin star restaurant La Sassa, right within the ruins of an ancient castle with a sea view. Top off the day with a visit to the Fountain of Saint Julie, rumored to have begun flowing at the time of her martyrdom, or find white stones along the beach to draw pictures in the sand that can be viewed above. La Sassa requires a reservation via their website.

name: Himeji
description: Himeji is a city located in Hyōgo Prefecture in the Kansai region. Surrounded by mountains and the sea, the city is most renowned for its iconic landmark, Himeji Castle, which is considered Japan's most beautiful surviving feudal castle. It's designated as the country's national treasure and is also listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site. Memorable for its pristine white color, Himeji Castle boasts a rich history that spans over 600 years. The current castle complex, which was completed in 1609, comprises more than 80 buildings interconnected by a maze of winding paths. The castle's gardens are equally captivating, adorned with cherry blossoms in the spring and flora that complements every season. Beyond the castle, visitors can explore the Koko-En Garden, situated adjacent to the castle, and the Engyoji Temple located on Mount Shosha. Please note that Daytrip recommends verifying opening hours and entrance fees for all third-party activities separately.

name: Sibu
description: Founded as a fort in 1862 to fend of the area's indigenous tribes, Sibu quickly grew into a predominantly Chinese city, earning the nickname the "New Fuzhou". Though many travellers just pass through Sibu on their way to traditional villages, the city offers those who make time to explore it an experience unlike anything else in Sarawak. In a predominantly Chinese city, one of the main landmarks is undoubtedly the Tua Pek Kong Temple - a colorful Buddhist temple with seven-story pagoda. Sibu's Central Market is the largest indoor market in all of Malaysia, and a great place to sample the city's excellent food. Likewise, lively Night Market is streetfood heaven if you're travelling after sundown. To learn about the city's rich cultural history, head to the Sibu Heritage Center, which has informative displays about everything from Chinese ethnic groups to Sarawak's Communist insurgency.
